BMArgus_AGS2D.overview:
The Argus was introduced in 3062, a product of the growing demand for new heavy BattleMech designs in the Federated Suns. Originally conceived as an OmniMech, the design was developed through a joint venture between Achernar BattleMechs of New Avalon and Robinson Standard BattleWorks. When the Armed Forces of the Federated Commonwealth's Department of the Quartermaster rejected the OmniMech proposal due to its prohibitive cost, the two manufacturers retooled the design as a conventional BattleMech, retaining many of the modular features that had made the OmniMech concept attractive.

The Argus fills the role of a versatile heavy brawler, capable of engaging effectively at close and medium ranges while maintaining enough speed to operate alongside cavalry formations. Its modular construction philosophy, a legacy of its OmniMech origins, makes the Argus especially easier to maintain and repair than most contemporary designs, contributing to its rapid adoption by frontline units of the Federated Suns.
BMArgus_AGS2D.capabilities:
Built on a 1A Type 12 Endo Steel chassis and powered by a General Motors 300 XL fusion engine, the Argus achieves a respectable top speed of 86 km/h, sufficient for its intended role as a mobile brawler. The primary production model centers its firepower around a Mydron Model RC Rotary Autocannon/5, a weapon capable of devastating rates of fire at close range. Two Bright-Bloom Extended Range medium lasers complement the autocannon, while a Federated LRM-10 launcher provides limited long-range engagement capability. A Mydron Mini-Gun machine gun rounds out the armament, offering anti-infantry defense. All direct-fire energy and ballistic weapons are linked to an advanced targeting computer, dramatically improving accuracy in close combat.

The Argus carries twelve tons of StarGuard II armor with CASE protection, providing solid survivability for its weight class while safeguarding the MechWarrior from catastrophic ammunition explosions. A Beagle Active Probe grants valuable electronic warfare capability, allowing the Argus to detect hidden units and resist ambush. The design retains its OmniMech heritage in its ease of maintenance, with electronics installed in easy-access modules and standardized connection points throughout the chassis that allow technicians to quickly swap components between damaged units.
BMArgus_AGS2D.history:
The Argus traces its origins to the late 3050s, when the success of Combine-produced OmniMechs inspired manufacturers across the Inner Sphere to develop their own modular designs. Achernar BattleMechs on New Avalon and Robinson Standard BattleWorks independently began work on heavy OmniMech proposals before discovering each other's efforts and entering into a partnership to share research and development costs. Their initial OmniMech submission was rejected by the Department of the Quartermaster, which cited prohibitive production costs. Particularly, the only Federated Suns-exclusive OmniMech to receive approval during this period came from Kallon Industries, and only after Field Marshal Duke George Hasek personally intervened through unofficial channels.

Undeterred, Achernar and Robinson redesigned the chassis as a conventional BattleMech, and the resulting Argus was quickly accepted into service in 3062. The design first saw combat on Kentares IV with the Fifth Donegal Guards, deployed to suppress civil unrest in the turbulent final years of the Federated Commonwealth. The Argus quickly proved its worth across both the Draconis and Crucis Marches, earning particular favor with elite formations such as the First Federated Suns Armored Cavalry.

Production of the Argus was split between both founding manufacturers, though the New Avalon facility appears to have ceased active production following the FedCom Civil War. Robinson Standard BattleWorks has maintained continuous production, introducing several upgraded variants throughout the Jihad and into the Dark Age. The Robinson facility's survival through multiple conflicts has ensured the Argus remains a familiar sight in Federated Suns formations, with the design continuing to evolve through successive technological upgrades to meet the changing demands of the modern battlefield.
BMArgus_AGS2D.deployment: This variant represents the originally planned primary configuration from the Argus's OmniMech development phase, repurposed as a factory variant for conventional production. Stripping the entire close-combat weapon suite, the 2D reconfigures the chassis for long-range fire support. A single Extended Range PPC provides devastating direct fire capability at extreme ranges, while paired LRM-15 launchers fitted with Artemis IV fire control systems deliver accurate indirect fire support. An additional double heat sink helps manage the thermal load of the energy-intensive loadout. Both Achernar BattleMechs and Robinson Standard BattleWorks produce this variant alongside the standard 4D model, and it has gained favor with commanders who value the Argus platform's maintainability but require a fire support role rather than a brawler.

The Argus traces its origins to the late 3050s, when the success of Combine-produced OmniMechs inspired manufacturers across the Inner Sphere to develop their own modular designs. Achernar BattleMechs on New Avalon and Robinson Standard BattleWorks independently began work on heavy OmniMech proposals before discovering each other's efforts and entering into a partnership to share research and development costs. Their initial OmniMech submission was rejected by the Department of the Quartermaster, which cited prohibitive production costs. Particularly, the only Federated Suns-exclusive OmniMech to receive approval during this period came from Kallon Industries, and only after Field Marshal Duke George Hasek personally intervened through unofficial channels.

Undeterred, Achernar and Robinson redesigned the chassis as a conventional BattleMech, and the resulting Argus was quickly accepted into service in 3062. The design first saw combat on Kentares IV with the Fifth Donegal Guards, deployed to suppress civil unrest in the turbulent final years of the Federated Commonwealth. The Argus quickly proved its worth across both the Draconis and Crucis Marches, earning particular favor with elite formations such as the First Federated Suns Armored Cavalry.

Production of the Argus was split between both founding manufacturers, though the New Avalon facility appears to have ceased active production following the FedCom Civil War. Robinson Standard BattleWorks has maintained continuous production, introducing several upgraded variants throughout the Jihad and into the Dark Age. The Robinson facility's survival through multiple conflicts has ensured the Argus remains a familiar sight in Federated Suns formations, with the design continuing to evolve through successive technological upgrades to meet the changing demands of the modern battlefield.
BMArgus_AGS5D.deployment: This variant introduces significant changes to the Argus platform, replacing the entire standard weapon loadout with a Heavy PPC as the primary armament, supplemented by twin Streak SRM-6 launchers and a pair of standard medium lasers. The targeting computer is retained, enhancing accuracy across the new weapon suite. A MASC system grants bursts of speed exceeding 100 km/h, transforming the Argus into a highly mobile striker capable of rapid flanking maneuvers. The addition of a C3 slave unit in the head allows the 5D to share targeting data within a networked lance, making it a valuable component of coordinated combined-arms operations favored by Federated Suns doctrine.

BMArgus_AGS6F.overview:
The Argus was introduced in 3062, a product of the growing demand for new heavy BattleMech designs in the Federated Suns. Originally conceived as an OmniMech, the design was developed through a joint venture between Achernar BattleMechs of New Avalon and Robinson Standard BattleWorks. When the Armed Forces of the Federated Commonwealth's Department of the Quartermaster rejected the OmniMech proposal due to its prohibitive cost, the two manufacturers retooled the design as a conventional BattleMech, retaining many of the modular features that had made the OmniMech concept attractive.

The Argus fills the role of a versatile heavy brawler, capable of engaging effectively at close and medium ranges while maintaining enough speed to operate alongside cavalry formations. Its modular construction philosophy, a legacy of its OmniMech origins, makes the Argus especially easier to maintain and repair than most contemporary designs, contributing to its rapid adoption by frontline units of the Federated Suns.
BMArgus_AGS6F.capabilities:
Built on a 1A Type 12 Endo Steel chassis and powered by a General Motors 300 XL fusion engine, the Argus achieves a respectable top speed of 86 km/h, sufficient for its intended role as a mobile brawler. The primary production model centers its firepower around a Mydron Model RC Rotary Autocannon/5, a weapon capable of devastating rates of fire at close range. Two Bright-Bloom Extended Range medium lasers complement the autocannon, while a Federated LRM-10 launcher provides limited long-range engagement capability. A Mydron Mini-Gun machine gun rounds out the armament, offering anti-infantry defense. All direct-fire energy and ballistic weapons are linked to an advanced targeting computer, dramatically improving accuracy in close combat.

The Argus carries twelve tons of StarGuard II armor with CASE protection, providing solid survivability for its weight class while safeguarding the MechWarrior from catastrophic ammunition explosions. A Beagle Active Probe grants valuable electronic warfare capability, allowing the Argus to detect hidden units and resist ambush. The design retains its OmniMech heritage in its ease of maintenance, with electronics installed in easy-access modules and standardized connection points throughout the chassis that allow technicians to quickly swap components between damaged units.

The original General Motors 300 XL engine is replaced with a Light Fusion Engine, improving survivability at the cost of additional weight. This necessitated a complete weapons overhaul, centering the variant's firepower around a devastating Autocannon/20 mounted in the right arm, capable of crippling most opponents with a single well-placed volley. Light Ferro-Fibrous armor provides comparable protection to the original while saving critical tonnage, and the heat sink count is reduced to ten double heat sinks to accommodate the heavier engine and armament.

BMAssassin_ASN101.overview: The Assassin was introduced in 2676 as the product of corporate ambition rather than military necessity. Maltex Corporation successfully lobbied the Star League to purchase the design as a replacement for the lighter Wasp and Stinger reconnaissance 'Mechs, achieving this through over-hyped performance statistics, fudged budget approximations, and political maneuvering. Despite this inauspicious origin, the forty-ton Assassin proved itself a capable light 'Mech hunter with impressive speed and jumping capability, and its modular design and ease of maintenance allowed it to persist through centuries of warfare long after Maltex's own fortunes had faded. Hellespont 'Mech Works revived the chassis in the late Jihad era, ensuring the Assassin remains a common sight in Capellan and Periphery forces.
BMAssassin_ASN101.capabilities:
The Assassin combines respectable mobility with adequate firepower for its intended role as a reconnaissance platform and light 'Mech hunter. Its VOX 280 fusion engine propels the forty-ton chassis to speeds of 118 kilometers per hour, while seven Lox Lift Series 1 jump jets provide an impressive 210-meter jumping distance that allows pilots to exploit terrain advantages against heavier opponents.

The weapons suite centers on a Holly-5 LRM-5 launcher for long-range harassment, supplemented by a Holly-2 SRM-2 rack and arm-mounted Martell medium laser for close engagements. This combination provides flexibility across engagement ranges, though the design's limited ammunition capacity of just seventy-four total rounds restricts extended operations without resupply. The SRM launcher's ammunition feed system is also prone to jamming in high-heat situations, a persistent concern that has led many operators to adopt conservative firing disciplines during sustained engagements.

The Assassin's most significant weakness lies in its cockpit design. Maltex's cost-cutting measures produced one of the most cramped cockpits in the Inner Sphere, limiting pilot endurance to half that of comparable designs and causing many veterans to develop chronic back problems. Despite numerous redesign attempts over four centuries, this fundamental flaw has never been adequately addressed in standard production models.
BMAssassin_ASN101.history:
The Assassin's troubled history began when Maltex Corporation secured Star League Defense Force contracts through aggressive lobbying rather than superior design. Only several hundred units were produced before quality control investigations slowed production to a crawl, and the design was quietly shuffled to Periphery garrisons and militia markets. The primary manufacturing facility on Errai was destroyed in 2835 during the Second Succession War, further limiting the chassis's availability.

House Marik became the Assassin's most enthusiastic user during the Third Succession War. The 'Mech's impressive performance during the Battle of Rochelle in 2980, where it excelled in muddy conditions that hampered heavier designs, led to widespread adoption in Free Worlds League garrison forces. Marik commanders frequently assigned Assassins to rear-area raiding parties, where their speed and jump capability proved invaluable for hit-and-run operations.

The Capellan Confederation exhausted its Assassin inventory by 3025, and spare parts shortages plagued operators across the Inner Sphere. By 3058, most surviving Assassins had been phased out of frontline service, with the remaining examples typically serving as family heirlooms passed down through MechWarrior dynasties, often sporting extensive field modifications.

The Assassin's fortunes reversed dramatically in late 3067 when Hellespont 'Mech Works acquired the design from Maltex Corporation. Distracted by Jihad-era chaos, tax evasion charges, and suspected Word of Blake connections, Maltex readily surrendered control. Hellespont began producing upgraded variants for the Capellan Confederation Armed Forces, Taurian Defense Force, and Magistracy Armed Forces, using the chassis as an economical means to rebuild shattered formations. The design's shared components with the Raven II further simplified logistics for Capellan operators.

Defiance Industries' attempt to produce the ASN-30 variant for Lyran forces during the FedCom Civil War proved largely unsuccessful, with the radical redesign failing to win acceptance. However, Hellespont's more conservative upgrades have ensured the Assassin remains a common sight in Capellan and Periphery forces well into the thirty-second century.
BMAssassin_ASN101.deployment: This variant was an unofficial variant produced in limited numbers by House Davion during the Succession Wars. Seeking to address the Assassin's ammunition dependency, Davion technicians removed three jump jets and reduced armor protection to mount three Maxell 50 small lasers in the legs and head. The design was considered unsuccessful, sacrificing sixty meters of jumping distance for marginal close-range firepower improvement. Official records indicate only three examples were stationed with the Capellan March Militia, though persistent rumors suggest Prince Hanse Davion maintained a secret facility near Panpour producing additional units. Circumstantial evidence from March Militia wargames supports these claims, though detractors argue the AFFS simply used standard ASN-21s with fake weapon mounts to confuse Maskirovka intelligence.

Hellespont began producing upgraded variants for the Capellan Confederation Armed Forces, Taurian Defense Force, and Magistracy Armed Forces, using the chassis as an economical means to rebuild shattered formations. The design's shared components with the Raven II further simplified logistics for Capellan operators.

Defiance Industries' attempt to produce the ASN-30 variant for Lyran forces during the FedCom Civil War proved largely unsuccessful, with the radical redesign failing to win acceptance. However, Hellespont's more conservative upgrades have ensured the Assassin remains a common sight in Capellan and Periphery forces well into the thirty-second century.
BMAssassin_ASN23.deployment: When Hellespont 'Mech Works began mass production in 3067, this variant became the new standard Assassin variant. Originally developed as a standardized field modification, this upgrade removes the SRM-2 to mount a Magna 400P medium pulse laser and adds an Artemis IV fire control system to the LRM-5 launcher. Within the Capellan Confederation Armed Forces, Taurian Defense Force, and Magistracy Armed Forces, this variant serves primarily in green and reserve formations as an economical means to rebuild shattered units. Capellan commanders frequently employ the variant in fire-support roles for pursuit and strike lances, though chronic shortages of Artemis-compatible ammunition force many pilots to rely on mine-delivery missiles instead.

BMAssassin_ASN30.overview: The Assassin was introduced in 2676 as the product of corporate ambition rather than military necessity. Maltex Corporation successfully lobbied the Star League to purchase the design as a replacement for the lighter Wasp and Stinger reconnaissance 'Mechs, achieving this through over-hyped performance statistics, fudged budget approximations, and political maneuvering. Despite this inauspicious origin, the forty-ton Assassin proved itself a capable light 'Mech hunter with impressive speed and jumping capability, and its modular design and ease of maintenance allowed it to persist through centuries of warfare long after Maltex's own fortunes had faded. Hellespont 'Mech Works revived the chassis in the late Jihad era, ensuring the Assassin remains a common sight in Capellan and Periphery forces.
BMAssassin_ASN30.capabilities:
The Assassin combines respectable mobility with adequate firepower for its intended role as a reconnaissance platform and light 'Mech hunter. Its VOX 280 fusion engine propels the forty-ton chassis to speeds of 118 kilometers per hour, while seven Lox Lift Series 1 jump jets provide an impressive 210-meter jumping distance that allows pilots to exploit terrain advantages against heavier opponents.

The weapons suite centers on a Holly-5 LRM-5 launcher for long-range harassment, supplemented by a Holly-2 SRM-2 rack and arm-mounted Martell medium laser for close engagements. This combination provides flexibility across engagement ranges, though the design's limited ammunition capacity of just seventy-four total rounds restricts extended operations without resupply. The SRM launcher's ammunition feed system is also prone to jamming in high-heat situations, a persistent concern that has led many operators to adopt conservative firing disciplines during sustained engagements.

The Assassin's most significant weakness lies in its cockpit design. Maltex's cost-cutting measures produced one of the most cramped cockpits in the Inner Sphere, limiting pilot endurance to half that of comparable designs and causing many veterans to develop chronic back problems. Despite numerous redesign attempts over four centuries, this fundamental flaw has never been adequately addressed in standard production models.
BMAssassin_ASN30.history:
The Assassin's troubled history began when Maltex Corporation secured Star League Defense Force contracts through aggressive lobbying rather than superior design. Only several hundred units were produced before quality control investigations slowed production to a crawl, and the design was quietly shuffled to Periphery garrisons and militia markets. The primary manufacturing facility on Errai was destroyed in 2835 during the Second Succession War, further limiting the chassis's availability.

House Marik became the Assassin's most enthusiastic user during the Third Succession War. The 'Mech's impressive performance during the Battle of Rochelle in 2980, where it excelled in muddy conditions that hampered heavier designs, led to widespread adoption in Free Worlds League garrison forces. Marik commanders frequently assigned Assassins to rear-area raiding parties, where their speed and jump capability proved invaluable for hit-and-run operations.

The Capellan Confederation exhausted its Assassin inventory by 3025, and spare parts shortages plagued operators across the Inner Sphere. By 3058, most surviving Assassins had been phased out of frontline service, with the remaining examples typically serving as family heirlooms passed down through MechWarrior dynasties, often sporting extensive field modifications.

BMAssassin_ASN30.deployment: Produced under license by Defiance Industries during the FedCom Civil War, this variant represented a radical departure from the classic Assassin formula. The chassis was completely redesigned with endo steel construction and a light fusion engine, allowing installation of an LB-X AC/5 in place of the missile systems, an upgraded ER medium laser, two additional tons of armor, and double heat sinks. Despite these improvements, the variant was widely considered a failure by Lyran commanders, and production numbers remained extremely limited. The ASN-30's poor reception stemmed from its departure from the reconnaissance role, attempting to create a direct combatant from a chassis fundamentally unsuited to sustained engagement.

This modification addresses two of the original design's weaknesses simultaneously, eliminating the ammunition-dependent and jam-prone short-range missile system while improving survivability against the leg attacks common in light 'Mech engagements. The simplicity of the conversion allowed it to spread beyond the Hat-in-the-Ring Battalion to other units with capable technical support.

BMAssassin_Servitor.deployment: The Servitor is a custom variant observed on Solaris VII, piloted by a Solaris VII gladiator. Based on the ASN-99 chassis, this configuration removes the stealth armor and Guardian ECM suite, replacing the head-mounted TAG with a small laser. The most distinctive modifications involve the arm-mounted weapons, with the left arm carrying a small vibroblade and the right mounting a medium X-Pulse laser. Additional small X-Pulse lasers in each leg provide close-range firepower for arena combat. While the Servitor demonstrates the potential for melee-focused Assassin configurations, Hellespont has indicated that mass production of 'Mech-sized vibroblades remains impractical, limiting this variant to one-off custom builds.

BMAtlasIII_AS7D2.overview: The Atlas is perhaps the most recognizable BattleMech in the Inner Sphere. It appears on more recruiting posters, more propaganda films, and in the boxes of more children's toys than any other 'Mech. More than a dozen variants have appeared over the centuries, and Robinson's Atlas III, introduced in 3100, is only the most recent to join the lineage. Rebuilt with cutting-edge technology by Robinson Standard BattleWorks and General Motors, the Atlas III stands as the AFFS' premier assault 'Mech, integrating advanced Clan-specification components into the proven hundred-ton chassis. It serves as a sign of the enduring dominance of the Death's Head design.
BMAtlasIII_AS7D2.capabilities:
The Atlas III represents the most advanced weapons integration ever fitted to an Atlas chassis. A Mydron rotary AC/2 provides sustained suppressive fire at range, while a Clan-specification Streak LRM-20 and Streak SRM-6 ensure that every missile fired finds its target, eliminating the wasteful volleys that plague conventional launchers. Four medium X-pulse lasers deliver punishing close-range damage with improved accuracy, and the entire weapons suite is managed by a radical heat sink flush system that allows the pilot to rapidly shed accumulated heat in controlled bursts.

An Angel ECM suite disrupts enemy targeting and communications, while an armored cockpit provides the pilot with additional survivability befitting the design's intended role as a senior officer's command platform. Custom small shields mounted on each arm offer supplemental protection during close-quarters engagements.

These advantages come at a cost. The rotary AC/2, while versatile, lacks the raw destructive power of the autocannons mounted on earlier Atlas models, forcing pilots to rely on sustained volume of fire rather than single devastating strikes. The radical heat sink flush system, though effective, is mechanically complex and difficult to service in the field. Units operating far from Robinson or El Dorado have reported extended downtime when the flush system requires maintenance. The Atlas III also retains the family's characteristic lack of speed, and the design's heavy reliance on advanced Clan-specification components makes it exceptionally expensive to produce and maintain.
BMAtlasIII_AS7D2.history:
The Atlas III entered service as the most technologically advanced member of the Atlas family, incorporating cutting-edge equipment that pushed the boundaries of what an assault 'Mech could carry. Robinson Standard BattleWorks and General Motors collaborated on the design, producing it at their Robinson and El Dorado facilities respectively. Still rare, Atlas IIIs were reserved for battalion and regimental commanders in the AFFS and RAF, including the personal 'Mech of Exarch Jonah Levin.

The Atlas III earned its reputation in blood during the Capellan assault on Tikonov. Several Atlas IIIs were among the Davion defenders on-planet, and each was targeted by the Capellans for capture, desperate to acquire the design's advanced heat management technology. One of these machines, piloted by Leftenant Nathan Marlowe, fought its way into legend. Attacked outside the city of Salat by a reinforced lance of Capellan 'Mechs, Marlowe called for reinforcements and went on the defensive, engaging at long range with his ballistic weapons. As the Capellans flanked him with their swifter machines, he added his missile systems to the fight, disabling two Anubises and crippling an Agrotera before they could close to effective range. Marlowe continued his fighting retreat, alternating laser fire with heat flushes until only a Vandal and a Lu Wei Bing remained. When the Lu Wei Bing's autocannon disabled his primary ballistic weapon, Marlowe jettisoned the ruined system. Capellan battleROMs clearly show the young warrior flexing the Atlas' great hands and advancing, steam issuing from almost every seam in the 'Mech's armor.

By the time relief arrived from Salat, all the 'Mechs were destroyed. BMAtlasIII_AS7D2.deployment: Intended as a more mainline combatant than the command-oriented D3, this variant sacrificed the radical heat sink system and rotary autocannon in favor of a devastating Hyper-Assault Gauss Rifle/30 paired with a targeting computer. The Streak LRM-20, Streak SRM-6, and medium X-pulse lasers were retained, giving the D2 tremendous firepower across all range brackets. The targeting computer made the HAG/30 particularly lethal, improving accuracy with a weapon system already capable of shredding armor at range. While lacking the D3's heat management and command electronics, the D2 was better suited to front-line assault duty where raw destructive power mattered more than survivability features. Produced at the same General Motors and Robinson Standard BattleWorks facilities as the D3, the D2 saw service with AFFS line units and was occasionally gifted to distinguished militia commanders along the Combine border.

BMAtlasIII_AS7D3.overview: The Atlas is perhaps the most recognizable BattleMech in the Inner Sphere. It appears on more recruiting posters, more propaganda films, and in the boxes of more children's toys than any other 'Mech. More than a dozen variants have appeared over the centuries, and Robinson's Atlas III, introduced in 3100, is only the most recent to join the lineage. Rebuilt with cutting-edge technology by Robinson Standard BattleWorks and General Motors, the Atlas III stands as the AFFS' premier assault 'Mech, integrating advanced Clan-specification components into the proven hundred-ton chassis. It serves as a reflection of the enduring dominance of the Death's Head design.
BMAtlasIII_AS7D3.capabilities:
The Atlas III represents the most advanced weapons integration ever fitted to an Atlas chassis. A Mydron rotary AC/2 provides sustained suppressive fire at range, while a Clan-specification Streak LRM-20 and Streak SRM-6 ensure that every missile fired finds its target, eliminating the wasteful volleys that plague conventional launchers. Four medium X-pulse lasers deliver punishing close-range damage with improved accuracy, and the entire weapons suite is managed by a radical heat sink flush system that allows the pilot to rapidly shed accumulated heat in controlled bursts.

An Angel ECM suite disrupts enemy targeting and communications, while an armored cockpit provides the pilot with additional survivability befitting the design's intended role as a senior officer's command platform. Custom small shields mounted on each arm offer supplemental protection during close-quarters engagements.

These advantages come at a cost. The rotary AC/2, while versatile, lacks the raw destructive power of the autocannons mounted on earlier Atlas models, forcing pilots to rely on sustained volume of fire rather than single devastating strikes. The radical heat sink flush system, though effective, is mechanically complex and difficult to service in the field. Units operating far from Robinson or El Dorado have reported extended downtime when the flush system requires maintenance. The Atlas III also retains the family's characteristic lack of speed, and the design's heavy reliance on advanced Clan-specification components makes it exceptionally expensive to produce and maintain.
BMAtlasIII_AS7D3.history:
The Atlas III entered service as the most technologically advanced member of the Atlas family, incorporating cutting-edge equipment that pushed the boundaries of what an assault 'Mech could carry. Robinson Standard BattleWorks and General Motors collaborated on the design, producing it at their Robinson and El Dorado facilities respectively. Still rare, Atlas IIIs were reserved for battalion and regimental commanders in the AFFS and RAF, including the personal 'Mech of Exarch Jonah Levin.

The Atlas III earned its reputation in blood during the Capellan assault on Tikonov. Several Atlas IIIs were among the Davion defenders on-planet, and each was targeted by the Capellans for capture, desperate to acquire the design's advanced heat management technology. One of these machines, piloted by Leftenant Nathan Marlowe, fought its way into legend. Attacked outside the city of Salat by a reinforced lance of Capellan 'Mechs, Marlowe called for reinforcements and went on the defensive, engaging at long range with his ballistic weapons. As the Capellans flanked him with their swifter machines, he added his missile systems to the fight, disabling two Anubises and crippling an Agrotera before they could close to effective range. Marlowe continued his fighting retreat, alternating laser fire with heat flushes until only a Vandal and a Lu Wei Bing remained. When the Lu Wei Bing's autocannon disabled his primary ballistic weapon, Marlowe jettisoned the ruined system. Capellan battleROMs clearly show the young warrior flexing the Atlas' great hands and advancing, steam issuing from almost every seam in the 'Mech's armor.

By the time relief arrived from Salat, all the 'Mechs were destroyed. The corpse of Leftenant Marlowe's Atlas was found draped across the broken body of the Capellan Vandal, the Lu Wei Bing lying nearby with its head crushed by the Atlas' fists. Marlowe's last stand at Tikonov became an instant recruiting legend for the AFFS and cemented the Atlas III's place in the storied lineage of the Death's Head.
BMAtlasIII_AS7D3.deployment: Produced jointly by General Motors on El Dorado and Robinson Standard BattleWorks on Robinson, this variant remains a rare machine reserved for senior commanders. Atlas IIIs are assigned to battalion and regimental commanders in the AFFS and RAF, with Exarch Jonah Levin's personal machine among the most prominent examples. Production numbers remain low due to the design's reliance on advanced Clan-specification components and the proprietary radical heat sink system. When the Capellan Confederation attacked Tikonov in force, several Atlas IIIs were among the defenders, and each was specifically targeted by the Capellans for capture, reflecting their desperation to reverse-engineer the flush system for their own use.

BMAtlasII_AS7DH.overview: Designed in 2755 to maintain the SLDF's edge over the League's Member States, the AS7-D Atlas remains a formidable assault 'Mech even today. But to General Aleksandr Kerensky that was only the beginning, and an advanced version developed for the Royal BattleMech regiments was just beginning deployment on the eve of the bloody Amaris Coup. At one hundred tons, the Atlas II refined its predecessor's already formidable combination of firepower, protection, and psychological impact, incorporating Star League-era technologies to create what many consider the definitive Royal assault 'Mech. Its extreme rarity and storied lineage have made the Atlas II one of the most sought-after chassis in the Inner Sphere and Clan space alike.
BMAtlasII_AS7DH.capabilities:
An evolution of the iconic AS7-D, the AS7-D-H Atlas II retains the basic structure and electronics. The original missile armament is retained, but a smaller caliber arm-mounted LB 10-X autocannon replaces the heavy autocannon. Installed in a double mount on the left forearm, extended-range large lasers complement the autocannon and LRM launcher. With this heavier arm-mounted weaponry, rear-firing weaponry was deemed redundant and the medium lasers (upgraded to pulse models) were switched to fire forward.

There was no way to surpass the Atlas' legendary armor, but upgrading to ferro-fibrous allowed CASE to be installed. Many of the stylistic alterations in the BattleMech's appearance were made during this change in armor type.

The trade-offs in this redesign are notable. The LB 10-X, while versatile with its cluster and slug ammunition options, lacks the devastating close-range stopping power of the original AC/20 that made the standard Atlas such a fearsome brawler. Additionally, the Atlas II's extreme rarity has always posed significant logistics challenges. Spare parts, particularly for the advanced ferro-fibrous armor and LB 10-X feed system, are difficult to source outside of major manufacturing centers, and field repairs often require cannibalization of other advanced 'Mechs.
BMAtlasII_AS7DH.history:
The Atlas II was still in its first stages of deployment when the New Vandenburg Revolt sparked off the Periphery uprisings in 2765. Facing formidable odds, these few AS7-D-Hs performed magnificently in the hands of their Royal regiment pilots. General Kerensky himself piloted one during his escape from New Vandenburg, proof of the faith the Commanding General placed in his enhanced Atlas design.

With the news that the Terran Hegemony had fallen under Amaris' control, Kerensky led his troops to secure the lightly defended Rim Worlds Republic as a base of operations. Captured Republican factories were repurposed to produce Atlas IIs for Royal commands as they fought the grueling campaign to liberate the Terran Hegemony. When the time came for the Exodus, the Atlas II's fate diverged sharply from its predecessor. While many standard AS7-D Atlas pilots chose to remain in the Inner Sphere, the surviving Atlas II pilots chose almost unanimously to follow their Commanding General into exile. The Atlas II thus vanished from the Inner Sphere entirely, becoming a near-mythical machine known only from old records and fading memories.

In the Clan Homeworlds, the Atlas II became one of the most prized assault 'Mechs. The Clans treasured every example discovered in Brian Caches during their formative years. The most famous Atlas II in Clan history was piloted by ilKhan Nicholas Kerensky himself, eldest son of Aleksandr. Nicholas had followed his father into exile and, after the elder Kerensky's death, forged the scattered exiles into twenty Clans. He led them on a crusade to retake the war-ravaged Pentagon worlds in 2821. Thirteen years later, in 2834, ilKhan Nicholas Kerensky died at the controls of his Atlas II when he intervened in a Trial of Grievance between Widowmaker Khan Cal Jorgensson and Wolf Khan Jerome Winson. The Widowmakers had committed a gross breach of zellbrigen, and when Kerensky stepped between the combatants, Khan Jorgensson fired into the Atlas II's cockpit, killing the ilKhan and sealing Clan Widowmaker's fate. The destruction of the Widowmakers that followed remains one of the most consequential events in Clan history.

The Atlas II returned to the Inner Sphere in dramatic fashion. A single example was sighted among the Jade Falcon Touman during the fighting on Tukayyid in 3052, sending shockwaves through ComStar intelligence analysts who had believed the design extinct. During the Jihad, when the Word of Blake captured Defiance Industries' factories on Hesperus II, they produced several runs of the Atlas II for their forces. The enigmatic Devlin Stone piloted one such machine, the "Phantom," in its distinctive black-and-white skeletal color scheme, as he led his growing coalition against the Blakists. Stone personally commanded from the Atlas II's cockpit during the Trial of Possession against a Star of Ghost Bears on Tukayyid in 3073, and led the flanking maneuver that shattered the Blakist Third Division on Skye in 3074. After the coalition forces evicted the Word of Blake from Hesperus II, Defiance Industries chose to keep the Atlas II in production, finally returning this legendary Royal 'Mech to the Inner Sphere after nearly three centuries of absence.
BMAtlasII_AS7DH.deployment: First fielded in 2765, this variant was developed by the Hegemony Research and Development Department on New Earth exclusively for the SLDF's Royal BattleMech regiments. Production remained extremely limited, with the New Earth facility the sole manufacturer until its destruction during the Amaris Coup in 2767. Captured Republican factories produced small runs during the liberation of the Terran Hegemony. When the Exodus departed the Inner Sphere, virtually every Atlas II pilot followed Kerensky, leaving the design absent from Inner Sphere arsenals for nearly three centuries. The Clans maintained small numbers in their Toumans, treating each as a prized garrison and command asset. After the liberation of Hesperus II from the Word of Blake, Defiance Industries resumed production, distributing new-build Atlas IIs primarily to Lyran Guards and allied coalition commands. Total active numbers remain low, with most formations fielding no more than one or two examples at the regimental level.

Captured Republican factories were repurposed to produce Atlas IIs for Royal commands as they fought the grueling campaign to liberate the Terran Hegemony. When the time came for the Exodus, the Atlas II's fate diverged sharply from its predecessor. While many standard AS7-D Atlas pilots chose to remain in the Inner Sphere, the surviving Atlas II pilots chose almost unanimously to follow their Commanding General into exile. The Atlas II thus vanished from the Inner Sphere entirely, becoming a near-mythical machine known only from old records and fading memories.

In the Clan Homeworlds, the Atlas II became one of the most prized assault 'Mechs. The Clans treasured every example discovered in Brian Caches during their formative years. The most famous Atlas II in Clan history was piloted by ilKhan Nicholas Kerensky himself, eldest son of Aleksandr. Nicholas had followed his father into exile and, after the elder Kerensky's death, forged the scattered exiles into twenty Clans. He led them on a crusade to retake the war-ravaged Pentagon worlds in 2821. Thirteen years later, in 2834, ilKhan Nicholas Kerensky died at the controls of his Atlas II when he intervened in a Trial of Grievance between Widowmaker Khan Cal Jorgensson and Wolf Khan Jerome Winson. The Widowmakers had committed a gross breach of zellbrigen, and when Kerensky stepped between the combatants, Khan Jorgensson fired into the Atlas II's cockpit, killing the ilKhan and sealing Clan Widowmaker's fate. The destruction of the Widowmakers that followed remains one of the most consequential events in Clan history.

The Atlas II returned to the Inner Sphere in dramatic fashion. A single example was sighted among the Jade Falcon Touman during the fighting on Tukayyid in 3052, sending shockwaves through ComStar intelligence analysts who had believed the design extinct. During the Jihad, when the Word of Blake captured Defiance Industries' factories on Hesperus II, they produced several runs of the Atlas II for their forces. The enigmatic Devlin Stone piloted one such machine, the "Phantom," in its distinctive black-and-white skeletal color scheme, as he led his growing coalition against the Blakists. Stone personally commanded from the Atlas II's cockpit during the Trial of Possession against a Star of Ghost Bears on Tukayyid in 3073, and led the flanking maneuver that shattered the Blakist Third Division on Skye in 3074. After the coalition forces evicted the Word of Blake from Hesperus II, Defiance Industries chose to keep the Atlas II in production, finally returning this legendary Royal 'Mech to the Inner Sphere after nearly three centuries of absence.
BMAtlasII_AS7DHTBubbles.deployment: An Atlas II of unknown origins, the only known example of this variant was discovered inside Castle Nautilus, an SLDF Outpost Fortress on the world of Artru in the Aurigan Reach. This seemingly custom variant retained the bulk of the standard Atlas II's weapon loadout but swapped the LB 10-X autocannon for a mammoth AC/20, giving the design devastating short-range firepower more reminiscent of the original AS7-D Atlas. The weapon placement closely resembled the standard Atlas models, suggesting the modification was intended to combine the Atlas II's superior electronics and ferro-fibrous armor with the proven close-combat punch of the original design. The 'Mech saw service during the final defeat of the Aurigan Directorate.

BMAtlas_AS7A.overview: First deployed in 2755, the Atlas was commissioned by General Aleksandr Kerensky as the ultimate expression of assault 'Mech doctrine. He demanded "a 'Mech as powerful as imaginable, as impenetrable as possible, and as foreboding as conceivable, so that fear itself will be our ally." Built by the Hegemony's premier manufacturers, the hundred-ton Atlas was intended to give the Regular Army a decisive advantage over the growing House Lord armies. Despite the upheaval that followed and the abandonment of the Inner Sphere by General Kerensky and most of the SLDF, the Atlas served its purpose and has endured as the most recognized and feared assault 'Mech in existence.
BMAtlas_AS7A.capabilities:
The first impression any spectator gets of the Atlas is its ferocious appearance. Although there are taller 'Mechs on the field, none of them have the sheer presence of the Atlas.

As an assault 'Mech, the Atlas has few peers. The largest long-range missile launcher available sits in the left torso, giving the Atlas a powerful long-range punch. As the 'Mech closes it can bring a bevy of deadly weapons to bear, the most fearsome of which is the massive Defiance 'Mech Hunter Autocannon in the right torso with enough ammunition to decimate a company of 'Mechs. The cannon is backed by a six-tube short-range missile system and two pairs of medium lasers covering all sides of the 'Mech. Twenty heat sinks give the Atlas the freedom to use this firepower, and most MechWarriors are fearful of this 'Mech for very deserved reasons.

Very few if any BattleMechs carry more armor than the Atlas, and a complete set of actuators (including hands) give the 'Mech frightful physical combat capabilities. There are myths among MechWarriors of the Atlas actually picking up lighter 'Mechs and breaking them like toys.

If the Atlas has any weakness it would be its slow speed. Although other assault 'Mechs are as slow, the fact that an Atlas is easily escaped is the hope most MechWarriors have when they face such a machine.
BMAtlas_AS7A.history:
The Atlas was born of necessity. Between 2751 and 2761, the Cameron Edicts passed by the High Council permitted the five House Lords to double the size of their personal armies. The Regular Army needed a weapon that could maintain its supremacy over these swelling forces. General Aleksandr Kerensky himself laid down the specifications, demanding "a 'Mech as powerful as possible, as impenetrable as possible, and as ugly and foreboding as conceivable, so that fear itself will be our ally." Designers took this mandate to heart, spending an entire year perfecting the skull-shaped head that would earn the Atlas its enduring nickname: the "Death's Head."

The Atlas saw its baptism of fire against Stefan the Usurper during the liberation of Terra. In the final battles to secure Earth's major spaceports, the Atlas was instrumental in establishing beachheads that allowed SLDF troops to land safely. General Kerensky's second-in-command, General Aaron DeChavilier, drove the assault on the Usurper's last stronghold, the Imperial City. DeChavilier continually exposed his Atlas to enemy fire, marching forward as if laser bolts, missiles, and cannon shells were nothing more than the annoying buzz of flies. When DeChavilier's Atlas pushed over the concrete outer wall surrounding the Imperial Palace, Kerensky headed for the gates in his Orion. It was a scene that would be immortalized in countless holovids and paintings, forever linking the Atlas to the liberation of humanity's homeworld.

When Kerensky departed on his Exodus, he wanted all Atlases to accompany him. More than two-thirds of Atlas pilots, however, refused to join, perhaps believing they could better their fortunes by remaining in the Inner Sphere. The remaining Atlases and those still rolling off assembly lines on Hesperus II, Al Na'ir, and Quentin continued to inspire terror wherever they walked. As the Succession Wars ravaged the Inner Sphere, the Atlas spread to every major military in limited numbers. Most militaries were loath to tamper with the design for the simple reason that it seemed nearly perfect in its role already, and attempted modifications generally failed since engineers had to make too many concessions to keep the 'Mech functioning.

The Atlas cemented its legend during some of the most crucial moments in Inner Sphere history. On Mallory's World in 3013, First Prince Ian Davion of the Federated Suns held a vital pass against Yorinaga Kurita and the Second Sword of Light while his men made their escape. Although the Kell Hounds and other units pushed forward to support him, Prince Davion fell in battle before help could arrive. A warrior first and a leader second, his sacrifice from the cockpit of an Atlas became one of the most celebrated last stands in military history. Two decades later, the sight of Hanse Davion's Atlases and Victors standing in formation for honors after actions against House Kurita reminded the Inner Sphere that the 'Mech remained the gold standard of assault warfare.

The technological renaissance of the 3040s and 3050s breathed new life into the venerable design. The Draconis Combine debuted the AS7-K variant, transforming the Atlas from a short-ranged brawler into a long-range bombardier. Improved ballistic and energy weapons replaced the original close-quarters armament, extending the 'Mech's reach considerably. Despite being an ancient design, the Atlas' reputation on the battlefield remained unquestioned, and even state-of-the-art machines gave it a wide berth. This was, after all, the flagship of all BattleMechs, and there was still no projected date for it to be replaced.

The Jihad tested the Atlas as never before. On Al Na'ir in early 3069, a lance of corporate-owned Atlases held off wave after wave of Word of Blake troops while defending a dome settlement for several days, eventually succumbing only when penetrating torso hits crippled their powerplants. The Word of Blake's capture of Hesperus II in 3070 temporarily halted Defiance Industries' production lines, a crisis that spurred development of new Atlas variants at secondary facilities. When Hesperus was finally liberated, these newer models entered full production alongside the original.

Through all of this, the Atlas has transcended its role as a mere weapon of war to become a cultural icon. It appears on more recruiting posters, more propaganda films, and in the boxes of more children's toys than any other BattleMech. More than a dozen variants have appeared over the centuries, each one building on a legacy that stretches back to the final days of the Star League. Whether defending a beleaguered colony or leading an assault on a fortified position, the sight of the Death's Head advancing across the battlefield continues to inspire allies and strike fear into enemies, just as General Kerensky intended nearly three centuries ago.
BMAtlas_AS7A.deployment: Developed in 2944 by HildCo Interplanetary on Carver V, this variant was a Capellan Confederation variant that replaced the AC/20 with a Deleon 5 autocannon and mounted five Ceres Arms Sextette SRM racks. This radical departure from the standard loadout shifted the Atlas toward a close-range saturation role, overwhelming targets with massed short-range missile fire. The destruction of House Liao's Atlas factory only twelve years after the variant was introduced ensured this model remained quite rare, with surviving examples highly prized by their Capellan pilots.

As an assault 'Mech, the Atlas has few peers. The largest long-range missile launcher available sits in the left torso, giving the Atlas a powerful long-range punch. As the 'Mech closes it can bring a bevy of deadly weapons to bear, the most fearsome of which is the massive Defiance 'Mech Hunter Autocannon in the right torso with enough ammunition to decimate a company of 'Mechs. The cannon is backed by a six-tube short-range missile system and two pairs of medium lasers covering all sides of the 'Mech. Twenty heat sinks give the Atlas the freedom to use this firepower, and most MechWarriors are fearful of this 'Mech for very deserved reasons.

Very few if any BattleMechs carry more armor than the Atlas, and a complete set of actuators (including hands) give the 'Mech frightful physical combat capabilities. There are myths among MechWarriors of the Atlas actually picking up lighter 'Mechs and breaking them like toys.

If the Atlas has any weakness it would be its slow speed. Although other assault 'Mechs are as slow, the fact that an Atlas is easily escaped is the hope most MechWarriors have when they face such a machine.
BMAtlas_AS7DDC.history:
The Atlas was born of necessity. Between 2751 and 2761, the Cameron Edicts passed by the High Council permitted the five House Lords to double the size of their personal armies. The Regular Army needed a weapon that could maintain its supremacy over these swelling forces. General Aleksandr Kerensky himself laid down the specifications, demanding "a 'Mech as powerful as possible, as impenetrable as possible, and as ugly and foreboding as conceivable, so that fear itself will be our ally." Designers took this mandate to heart, spending an entire year perfecting the skull-shaped head that would earn the Atlas its enduring nickname: the "Death's Head."

The Atlas saw its baptism of fire against Stefan the Usurper during the liberation of Terra. In the final battles to secure Earth's major spaceports, the Atlas was instrumental in establishing beachheads that allowed SLDF troops to land safely. General Kerensky's second-in-command, General Aaron DeChavilier, led the assault on the Usurper's last stronghold, the Imperial City. DeChavilier continually exposed his Atlas to enemy fire, marching forward as if laser bolts, missiles, and cannon shells were nothing more than the annoying buzz of flies. When DeChavilier's Atlas pushed over the concrete outer wall surrounding the Imperial Palace, Kerensky headed for the gates in his Orion. It was a scene that would be immortalized in countless holovids and paintings, forever linking the Atlas to the liberation of humanity's homeworld.

When Kerensky departed on his Exodus, he wanted all Atlases to accompany him. More than two-thirds of Atlas pilots, however, refused to join, perhaps believing they could better their fortunes by remaining in the Inner Sphere. The remaining Atlases and those still rolling off assembly lines on Hesperus II, Al Na'ir, and Quentin continued to inspire terror wherever they walked. As the Succession Wars ravaged the Inner Sphere, the Atlas spread to every major military in limited numbers. Most militaries were loath to tamper with the design for the simple reason that it seemed nearly perfect in its role already, and attempted modifications generally failed since engineers had to make too many concessions to keep the 'Mech functioning.

The Atlas cemented its legend during some of the most decisive moments in Inner Sphere history. On Mallory's World in 3013, First Prince Ian Davion of the Federated Suns held a vital pass against Yorinaga Kurita and the Second Sword of Light while his men made their escape. Although the Kell Hounds and other units pushed forward to support him, Prince Davion fell in battle before help could arrive. A warrior first and a leader second, his sacrifice from the cockpit of an Atlas became one of the most celebrated last stands in military history. Two decades later, the sight of Hanse Davion's Atlases and Victors standing in formation for honors after actions against House Kurita reminded the Inner Sphere that the 'Mech remained the gold standard of assault warfare.

The technological renaissance of the 3040s and 3050s breathed new life into the venerable design. The Draconis Combine debuted the AS7-K variant, transforming the Atlas from a short-ranged brawler into a long-range bombardier. Improved ballistic and energy weapons replaced the original close-quarters armament, extending the 'Mech's reach considerably. Despite being an ancient design, the Atlas' reputation on the battlefield remained unquestioned, and even state-of-the-art machines gave it a wide berth. This was, after all, the flagship of all BattleMechs, and there was still no projected date for it to be replaced.

The Jihad tested the Atlas as never before. On Al Na'ir in early 3069, a lance of corporate-owned Atlases held off wave after wave of Word of Blake troops while defending a dome settlement for several days, eventually succumbing only when penetrating torso hits crippled their powerplants. The Word of Blake's capture of Hesperus II in 3070 temporarily halted Defiance Industries' production lines, a crisis that spurred development of new Atlas variants at secondary facilities. When Hesperus was finally liberated, these newer models entered full production alongside the original.

Through all of this, the Atlas has transcended its role as a mere weapon of war to become a cultural icon. It appears on more recruiting posters, more propaganda films, and in the boxes of more children's toys than any other BattleMech. More than a dozen variants have appeared over the centuries, each one building on a legacy that stretches back to the final days of the Star League. Whether defending a beleaguered colony or leading an assault on a fortified position, the sight of the Death's Head advancing across the battlefield continues to inspire allies and strike fear into enemies, just as General Kerensky intended nearly three centuries ago.
BMAtlas_AS7DDC.deployment: Built in 2776 during the twilight of the Star League, this variant mounted a Command Console in place of one ton of LRM ammunition and the rear-mounted medium lasers. This modification transformed the Atlas into a dedicated command platform, allowing senior officers to coordinate their forces from the cockpit of one of the most heavily protected 'Mechs on the battlefield. The trade-off in firepower was considered acceptable given that commanders rarely operated on the front line, and the Atlas's imposing presence served double duty as both a rallying point and a deterrent.

BMAtlas_AS7DIan.overview: First deployed in 2755, the Atlas was commissioned by General Aleksandr Kerensky as the ultimate expression of assault 'Mech doctrine. He demanded "a 'Mech as powerful as imaginable, as impenetrable as possible, and as foreboding as conceivable, so that fear itself will be our ally." Built by the Hegemony's premier manufacturers, the hundred-ton Atlas was intended to give the Regular Army a decisive advantage over the growing House Lord armies. Despite the upheaval that followed and the abandonment of the Inner Sphere by General Kerensky and most of the SLDF, the Atlas served its purpose and has endured as the most recognized and feared assault 'Mech in existence.

Produced at Yori MechWorks on Al Na'ir and Independence Weaponry on Quentin, the K variant kept sales brisk and maintained the Atlas's status as the flagship of all BattleMechs.

The remaining Atlases and those still rolling off assembly lines on Hesperus II, Al Na'ir, and Quentin continued to inspire terror wherever they walked. As the Succession Wars ravaged the Inner Sphere, the Atlas spread to every major military in limited numbers. A pair of rear-mounted Streak SRM-2 launchers added defensive firepower against flanking attacks. While no longer in production by the Dark Age, many Federated Suns militia units continued to maintain their S variants, often equipping them with advanced autocannon rounds or specialized LRM munitions.

BMAtlas_AS7S2.overview: First deployed in 2755, the Atlas was commissioned by General Aleksandr Kerensky as the ultimate expression of assault 'Mech doctrine. He demanded "a 'Mech as powerful as imaginable, as impenetrable as possible, and as foreboding as conceivable, so that fear itself will be our ally." Built by the Hegemony's premier manufacturers, the hundred-ton Atlas was intended to give the Regular Army a decisive advantage over the growing House Lord armies. Despite the upheaval that followed and the abandonment of the Inner Sphere by General Kerensky and most of the SLDF, the Atlas served its purpose and has endured as the most recognized and feared assault 'Mech in existence.
BMAtlas_AS7S2.capabilities:
The first impression any spectator gets of the Atlas is its ferocious appearance. Although there are taller 'Mechs on the field, none of them have the sheer presence of the Atlas.

As an assault 'Mech, the Atlas has few peers. The largest long-range missile launcher available sits in the left torso, giving the Atlas a powerful long-range punch. As the 'Mech closes it can bring a bevy of deadly weapons to bear, the most fearsome of which is the massive Defiance 'Mech Hunter Autocannon in the right torso with enough ammunition to decimate a company of 'Mechs. The cannon is backed by a six-tube short-range missile system and two pairs of medium lasers covering all sides of the 'Mech. Twenty heat sinks give the Atlas the freedom to use this firepower, and most MechWarriors are fearful of this 'Mech for very deserved reasons.

Very few if any BattleMechs carry more armor than the Atlas, and a complete set of actuators (including hands) give the 'Mech frightful physical combat capabilities. There are myths among MechWarriors of the Atlas actually picking up lighter 'Mechs and breaking them like toys.

If the Atlas has any weakness it would be its slow speed. Although other assault 'Mechs are as slow, the fact that an Atlas is easily escaped is the hope most MechWarriors have when they face such a machine.

BMAvalanche_AVL1O.overview: The Avalanche is a medium Inner Sphere OmniMech introduced in 3133 by Luthien Armor Works on Luthien. Conceived as a joint development between the Draconis Combine and Clan Nova Cat in the aftermath of the Second Combine-Dominion War, the design was intended to rebuild the Clan's depleted touman while providing the DCMS with a cost-effective trooper OmniMech. Built entirely from off-the-shelf Inner Sphere components, the Avalanche fills a niche as an economical medium OmniMech prioritizing reliability and ease of maintenance over raw performance. Production has continued on Luthien through the Dark Age and into the ilClan era, with exports reaching the Capellan Confederation and mercenary markets following Clan Nova Cat's destruction.
BMAvalanche_AVL1O.capabilities:
The Avalanche prioritizes economy and maintainability over cutting-edge performance. Built on a Luthien Class M endo steel chassis, the design employs a standard Hermes 250 fusion engine providing a maximum speed of 86 kilometers per hour, adequate but unexceptional for a fifty-ton platform. Five Icarus Standard jump jets enhance tactical mobility with a jump capacity of 150 meters, while ten tons of Mitchel Argon Standard armor provides reasonable protection, though less than many contemporary medium designs. Ten double heat sinks manage thermal loads across most configurations, and CASE protection in the right torso guards against catastrophic ammunition detonation.

The chassis allocates sixteen tons of pod space, offering decent reconfiguration flexibility for a medium OmniMech. A significant design flaw manifests when Clan-manufactured weapons are installed: the Matabushi Stalker targeting system loses alignment after extended use, with Nova Cat warriors reporting misalignment reaching two full degrees during gunnery exercises, a deficiency that severely undermined confidence in the platform and ultimately led to its abandonment by Clan Nova Cat in favor of the purpose-built Wendigo.
BMAvalanche_AVL1O.history:
The Avalanche emerged from the aftermath of the Second Combine-Dominion War, which ended in 3101 and left Clan Nova Cat's military forces severely depleted. The DCMS granted Luthien Armor Works carte blanche to collaborate with the Clan on a jointly developed OmniMech that would be economical to produce using readily available resources. What followed was one of the longest development cycles in modern BattleMech history, with the project plagued by three decades of false starts, reappropriated funding, and unresolved technical challenges before the first Avalanche rolled off LAW's production line in 3133.

The design was deployed shortly before the Draconis Combine's invasion of the Republic of the Sphere, seeing action with elite formations including the Sword of Light and Benjamin Regulars. A lance of Avalanches from the Sixth Benjamin Regulars participated in a hot-drop onto Shinonoi to secure the primary landing zone, engaging targets from long range with Clan technology before reconfiguring to support capital defense operations. The DCMS found the Avalanche to be a serviceable trooper OmniMech, but Clan Nova Cat's warrior caste was far less satisfied. Persistent targeting system malfunctions with Clan weaponry frustrated Nova Cat warriors to the point where the Clan developed only two mixed-technology configurations before abandoning the platform entirely, opting instead to create the Wendigo, a purely Clan-built OmniMech based on the Avalanche's chassis.

Following the destruction of Clan Nova Cat after its revolt against Coordinator Yori Kurita, the dead Clan's allotment of Avalanches was redistributed. Luthien Armor Works refurbished former Nova Cat machines and channeled them through the Clan's export division, where Clan Sea Fox, the Capellan Confederation, and the Free Worlds League expressed interest. The Confederation purchased a significant number of Avalanches prior to its invasion of the Federated Suns, deploying them extensively in the conquest of Capellan March worlds. Sea Fox merchants resold additional units to mercenary companies, where the solidly-built 'Mech found favor among smaller outfits that valued its reliability and ease of maintenance over raw combat performance.
BMAvalanche_AVL1O.deployment: Introduced in 3133 as the Avalanche's primary configuration, this loadout epitomizes the design's fire support role. Twin LRM-10 launchers mounted in the side torsos deliver coordinated missile volleys at medium to long range, producing the distinctive white smoke clouds that gave the OmniMech its name. Four ER medium lasers distributed across both arms provide accurate secondary fire for closer engagements. Two tons of LRM ammunition stored in the CASE-protected right torso ensure sustained fire capability, though the configuration lacks close-range punch once ammunition is expended.

BMAvatar_AV1O.overview: The Avatar is a seventy-ton Inner Sphere OmniMech born from the Draconis Combine's ambitious effort to reverse-engineer Clan technology following the Battle of Luthien in 3052. Luthien Armor Works began development using captured Mad Dog OmniMechs as the basis for the design, making the Avatar the first Inner Sphere OmniMech conceptualized. Prolonged integration difficulties between Clan and Inner Sphere technologies, however, meant it was among the last of the Combine's first generation OmniMechs to enter production in 3056. Filling the role of a versatile heavy fire support platform, the Avatar leverages a generous thirty-four tons of pod space to accommodate a wide variety of weapon configurations. Licensed production through StarCorps Industries, Victory Industries, and General Motors has spread the design across multiple Successor States, establishing it as one of the most widely manufactured Inner Sphere OmniMechs in service.
BMAvatar_AV1O.capabilities:
The Avatar's chassis mounts a Hermes 280 XL engine, providing a top speed of sixty-four kilometers per hour. While particularly slower than its Clan-designed ancestor, this trade-off in mobility purchases considerably more internal volume and pod capacity than the original Mad Dog offered. With thirty-four tons of available pod space, the Avatar can mount firepower rivaling many assault-weight designs while retaining the tactical flexibility inherent to OmniMech technology. Twelve tons of StarSlab/4 armor provide respectable protection for its weight class, supplemented by CASE systems in both side torsos to mitigate the catastrophic risk of ammunition detonation.

A distinctive feature of the design is its two permanently mounted Victory 23R medium lasers in the center torso. These hardwired weapons trace their origin to early testing phases when OmniPod connector faults risked leaving the entire weapons array disabled. Though the underlying issue was resolved before deployment, the fixed lasers remain as a design vestige ensuring the Avatar is never completely unarmed. In its Prime configuration, the Avatar combines an LB 10-X autocannon with dual LRM-10 launchers equipped with Artemis IV fire control, supplemented by medium pulse lasers and machine guns for a balanced loadout emphasizing ranged engagement with credible close-in capability.
BMAvatar_AV1O.history:
The Avatar's genesis lies in the aftermath of the Battle of Luthien in 3052, when the Draconis Combine Mustered Soldiery found itself in possession of significant Clan salvage but unable to maintain the captured equipment. Within months, the majority of trophy Clan machines in DCMS service were rendered combat ineffective due to maintenance failures. Luthien Armor Works was tasked with finding a practical solution, and their engineers responded by combining captured Vulture components with Inner Sphere technology. The process of melding the two tech bases proved far more difficult than anticipated, and while the Raptor, Owens, and Black Hawk-KU all reached service first, the Avatar's troubled development ultimately produced one of the Combine's most capable and enduring OmniMech designs.

Initial production during the late 3050s went primarily to DCMS units stationed along the Clan border, with limited quantities sold to ComStar and the Federated Commonwealth for deployment in the Lyran half's Clan frontier. The secession of the Lyran Alliance in 3057 prompted the Combine to redirect the reserved FedCom allotment to ComStar instead, an arrangement that persisted through the conclusion of the First Combine-Dominion War. The Davion half of the rump Federated Commonwealth instead received output from locally licensed production, as StarCorps Industries plants on Crofton, Son Hoa, St. Ives, and Loburg brought the Avatar into broader Successor State service during the 3060s. General Motors began production at New Valencia, and Victory Industries on Marduk received a subcontract from Luthien Armor Works, further broadening the manufacturing base within Combine borders.

This distributed production network proved critical when the Word of Blake's assault on Luthien during the opening years of the Jihad resulted in the nuclear destruction of Luthien Armor Works' massive OmniMech production complex. The Guthry Island facility where the Avatar and other OmniMechs were built was reportedly obliterated in the midst of a simultaneous Black Dragon coup, eliminating the design's primary production line along with capacity for several other Combine OmniMechs. The loss was compounded by the destruction of General Motors' facilities on Kathil. However, the surviving StarCorps and Victory Industries lines ensured the Avatar's continued production, albeit at reduced volume.

The Avatar remains in active service across multiple Successor States well into the post-Jihad era. Its widespread distribution across the Draconis Combine, Federated Suns, Lyran Commonwealth, and Capellan Confederation ensures that the design continues to see regular deployment along numerous frontiers, proof of both the robustness of its engineering and the foresight of its licensing arrangements.
BMAvatar_AV1O.deployment: The Prime configuration represents the Avatar's baseline combat loadout, combining an LB 10-X autocannon capable of firing both solid and cluster ammunition with dual LRM-10 launchers equipped with Artemis IV fire control systems for enhanced missile accuracy. Two medium pulse lasers and a pair of machine guns provide close-range firepower, creating a versatile weapons suite capable of engaging targets across multiple range bands. This balanced approach to firepower makes the Prime the most commonly deployed configuration, well-suited to general combat duties where mission parameters may vary.

BMAwesome_AWS10KM.overview: Introduced in 2665 by the Technicron Manufacturing Conglomerate for the Star League Defense Force, the Awesome was designed as a replacement for the aging STR-2C Striker. An eighty-ton assault 'Mech built around a punishing PPC-based armament, the Awesome earned a fearsome reputation as a durable fire-support platform capable of anchoring any battle line. Its near-total independence from ammunition resupply and notoriously difficult-to-kill design have made it one of the most valued assault 'Mechs among logistics officers and field commanders alike. Sought after by every Great House and mercenary command with the means to acquire one, the design has remained a mainstay of assault lances for over four centuries.
BMAwesome_AWS10KM.capabilities:
The standard AWS-8Q carries three Kreuss PPCs as its primary armament: one mounted in the right arm and two split between the left and right torsos. This battery delivers devastating firepower at ranges exceeding five hundred meters, enough to cripple most targets with a single concentrated volley. A Diverse Optics Type 10 Small Laser mounted in the head provides a token close-range weapon, while the left arm terminates in a battlefist for hand-to-hand engagements. A Pitban 240 fusion engine gives the Awesome a top speed of 64.8 kilometers per hour, adequate for an assault 'Mech but insufficient to dictate engagement range against faster opponents.

Twenty-eight standard heat sinks give the Awesome remarkable staying power in prolonged engagements, allowing MechWarriors to maintain a steady two-three-two firing cycle without significant heat buildup. The design carries fifteen tons of standard armor, exceeding even the BattleMaster in total protection, and the placement of critical systems away from explosive components makes the Awesome notoriously difficult to achieve a kill against. Rear armor coverage is among the heaviest found on any assault 'Mech, frustrating attempts by flanking units to exploit the typical weak point.

The Awesome is not without significant drawbacks, however. Its PPCs suffer from the minimum range limitations inherent to the weapon type, making close-quarters combat a serious vulnerability. With only the small laser and a single fist to fall back on at short range, the design is poorly equipped to handle opponents that close inside its effective engagement envelope. The lack of any weapon mount on the left arm further limits its options. The 'Mech's modest ground speed leaves it vulnerable to flanking maneuvers by faster opponents seeking to bypass the forward PPC arc, and commanders who fail to account for these limitations often find their Awesomes isolated and overwhelmed.
BMAwesome_AWS10KM.history:
Technicron Manufacturing developed the Awesome on Savannah in the Free Worlds League, delivering the first production units to the SLDF in 2665 as a direct replacement for the aging Striker. The design proved itself quickly, and by the time of the Amaris Coup the Awesome had secured a place in front-line regiments across the Star League. BMAwesome_AWS10KM.deployment: The 10KM, a joint project between IBMU and Alshain Weaponry, was introduced in 3067. The 'Mech utilizes Irian's compact engine and Compact Gyro to save space at the expense of mass. It retains the speed and ECM of the 9Q, but utilizes an Endo Steel structure. Two Heavy PPCs deal a good amount of damage in each blow, while a Snub-Nose PPC is deadly and accurate at close range. At the time of its introduction the 10KM was reserved for only the elite units of the Free Worlds League and Draconis Combine, and thanks to an iron-clad contract even the wily Irian Technologies had trouble finding a loophole to sell the 'Mech to the other Houses or mercenary units.

BMAwesome_AWS11V.overview: Introduced in 2665 by the Technicron Manufacturing Conglomerate for the Star League Defense Force, the Awesome was designed as a replacement for the aging STR-2C Striker. An eighty-ton assault 'Mech built around a punishing PPC-based armament, the Awesome earned a fearsome reputation as a durable fire-support platform capable of anchoring any battle line. Its near-total independence from ammunition resupply and notoriously difficult-to-kill design have made it one of the most valued assault 'Mechs among logistics officers and field commanders alike. Sought after by every Great House and mercenary command with the means to acquire one, the design has remained a mainstay of assault lances for over four centuries.
BMAwesome_AWS11V.capabilities:
The standard AWS-8Q carries three Kreuss PPCs as its primary armament: one mounted in the right arm and two split between the left and right torsos. This battery delivers devastating firepower at ranges exceeding five hundred meters, enough to cripple most targets with a single concentrated volley. A Diverse Optics Type 10 Small Laser mounted in the head provides a token close-range weapon, while the left arm terminates in a battlefist for hand-to-hand engagements. A Pitban 240 fusion engine gives the Awesome a top speed of 64.8 kilometers per hour, adequate for an assault 'Mech but insufficient to dictate engagement range against faster opponents.

Twenty-eight standard heat sinks give the Awesome remarkable staying power in prolonged engagements, allowing MechWarriors to maintain a steady two-three-two firing cycle without significant heat buildup. The design carries fifteen tons of standard armor, exceeding even the BattleMaster in total protection, and the placement of critical systems away from explosive components makes the Awesome notoriously difficult to achieve a kill against. Rear armor coverage is among the heaviest found on any assault 'Mech, frustrating attempts by flanking units to exploit the typical weak point.

The Awesome is not without significant drawbacks, however. Its PPCs suffer from the minimum range limitations inherent to the weapon type, making close-quarters combat a serious vulnerability. With only the small laser and a single fist to fall back on at short range, the design is poorly equipped to handle opponents that close inside its effective engagement envelope. The lack of any weapon mount on the left arm further limits its options. The 'Mech's modest ground speed leaves it vulnerable to flanking maneuvers by faster opponents seeking to bypass the forward PPC arc, and commanders who fail to account for these limitations often find their Awesomes isolated and overwhelmed.

BMAwesome_AWS11V.deployment: A byproduct of the AWS-11R, the 11V focuses on direct-fire weaponry at the expense of the 11R's LRM capability. An ER PPC with PPC Capacitor provides heavy direct-fire punch, complemented by a Light Gauss Rifle, Extended LRM-15, and ER Medium Laser. An Angel ECM Suite replaces the 11R's Stealth Armor and Guardian ECM for electronic warfare protection. IS Endo Steel and a Compact Gyro provide internal savings, with CASE II protecting the ammunition bays.

BMAwesome_AWS8Q.deployment:
This variant is the standard production model and the most widely encountered variant across the Inner Sphere. Originally fielded by Star League Defense Force line regiments, the base Awesome saw service in every major theater of the Reunification War's aftermath and the early Succession Wars. Its straightforward all-energy loadout made it a natural choice for garrison commands and defensive formations where ammunition resupply was uncertain. SLDF units frequently deployed Awesomes in pairs or lances to create overlapping fields of PPC fire, a tactic adopted by the Successor States and still employed by assault formations to this day.

The Free Worlds League maintained the highest concentration of AWS-8Qs due to its control of the Savannah production lines, and League commanders came to treat the design as the backbone of their heavy assault formations. Other Houses acquired their Awesomes through battlefield salvage, trade, and the occasional raid on League supply depots, ensuring that the 8Q could be found in virtually every major military force across the Inner Sphere.

The variant would never prove to be popular, though, and would finally fall out of usage in the aftermath of the Jihad.
