BMChampion_CHP3P.deployment: Introduced in 3061, this variant is the most extensively redesigned production variant of the Champion. The entire weapons array is replaced: an Ultra autocannon/10 takes the place of the LB-X model, four extended-range medium lasers replace the original laser suite, and an improved Narc missile beacon replaces the SRM launcher. The extralight engine from the CHP-3N is retained, and an improved C3 computer enables the Champion to function within a six-unit C3i network. This configuration emphasizes the Champion's traditional role as a flexible support platform while incorporating modern battlefield networking capabilities.

BMCharger_CGR1A1.overview: Conceived by Wells Technologies on Luthien as an ultra-heavy reconnaissance platform for the Star League Defense Force, the eighty-ton Charger is one of the most maligned BattleMech designs in history. First produced in 2665, the original model could outrun most medium 'Mechs yet mounted only a handful of small lasers, armament that would have been considered inadequate on a 'Mech one-quarter its size. Intended to penetrate defended areas at high speed and withdraw before heavier opponents could engage, the Charger's concept failed to survive contact with reality, and the SLDF quickly sidelined it from frontline service. Despite this ignominious beginning, the Charger eventually found redemption through successive redesigns, proving that even the most flawed chassis can become viable with the right technology and engineering vision.
BMCharger_CGR1A1.capabilities:
The original Charger’s design philosophy (speed and armor over firepower) produced an assault ’Mech whose five small lasers were laughable even to MechWarrior cadets, while its solid Durallex Heavy armor could absorb direct hits from autocannon fire. The massive LTV 400 engine consumed over half the chassis’s mass, leaving virtually nothing for weapons. MechWarriors quickly discovered that the Charger’s only real offensive option was physical combat, using its eighty-ton mass and considerable speed to charge lighter opponents. Against Wasps, Stingers, and ’Mechs whose primary armament had already been destroyed, the Charger was effective; against anything else, it was a liability.

The recovery of Star League technology in the late 3040s finally gave LAW the tools to address the Charger’s fundamental weakness. The CGR-3K replaced the small lasers with four medium pulse lasers and an Artemis IV-enhanced LRM-20, while an XL engine and jump jets gave the design unprecedented tactical flexibility for its weight class. The spacious internal layout (originally a consequence of the oversized engine) proved remarkably adaptable to successive generations of weapons technology, producing variants ranging from urban brawlers to Clan-specification scouts. The same roomy chassis that spawned the Hatamoto-Chi family has ensured the Charger’s continued relevance well into the thirty-second century.
BMCharger_CGR1A1.history:
Wells Technologies built the Charger in 2665, combining heavy Durallex armor with Magna light lasers in a design intended as a high-speed reconnaissance element for the SLDF. The concept (an assault-weight scout that could absorb punishment while gathering intelligence) failed to account for MechWarriors’ natural inclination to engage the enemy, and the Charger’s popgun armament left pilots defenseless when combat proved unavoidable. The Star League withdrew the design from active service, and Wells Technologies found itself wallowing in unsold inventory. Ironically, the fall of the Star League and the First Succession War saved the company from bankruptcy, as the Draconis Combine’s desperate need for ’Mechs led to bulk purchases of the company’s entire overstock.

Most Chargers found their way into DCMS forces, though battlefield salvage eventually distributed the design across every Great House military. Lyran forces adopted the Charger as a heavy reconnaissance element for assault companies, embracing it more warmly than other Houses. When the ISF uncovered Wells Technologies’ covert attempts to sell Chargers to the Lyran Commonwealth in violation of export restrictions, Luthien Armor Works executed an emergency buyout of the company. Wells Technologies closed its doors in 3027, and CGR-1A1 production ceased entirely by 3030.

The Charger’s defining moment came not from any battlefield triumph but from the Hatamoto-Chi program. When ComStar gifted the Draconis Combine with Star League-era BattleMechs in the 3030s, LAW engineers used reverse-engineered Thug technology to transform the despised Charger chassis into the formidable Hatamoto-Chi, an assault ’Mech that would become one of the DCMS’s most iconic designs. The experience gained with lost technology during the crash Hatamoto program led LAW to rework the Charger itself. The CGR-3K debuted in 3049 with ferro-fibrous armor, pulse lasers, and jump jets, earning widespread acceptance from DCMS MechWarriors who had long scorned the design. By 3068, every regular DCMS unit contained at least one post-3050 Charger variant.

The Sapphire Sunset yakuza clan on Shimonita purchased and upgraded a small LAW complex (renamed Sapphire Metals) and began producing CGR-3Ks, CGR-SA5s, and the newer CGR-KMZ design. When the Raven Alliance absorbed the Outworlds Alliance, Raveena Electronics on Ramora (holder of a production license dating back to a LAW legal error) eventually transitioned from Inner Sphere Charger variants to the Clan-specification Charger C, replacing all previous IS-tech production by 3093.
BMCharger_CGR1A1.deployment: The standard production Charger has been manufactured on Luthien since 2665, initially by Wells Technologies and later by Luthien Armor Works following the 3027 buyout. Over a thousand CGR-1A1s were built, roughly five hundred of which survived into the early thirty-first century. Most served with the DCMS, though battlefield salvage distributed them across every Great House military. The design is effective against infantry, light armored vehicles, and ’Mechs whose primary armament has been destroyed, but its five small lasers leave it virtually defenseless against anything heavier. Charger pilots are continually reminded to stay out of heavy combat and to use their speed and mass for physical attacks when engagement is unavoidable.

BMCharger_CGR1A5.capabilities:
The original Charger’s design philosophy (speed and armor over firepower) produced an assault ’Mech whose five small lasers were laughable even to MechWarrior cadets, while its solid Durallex Heavy armor could absorb direct hits from autocannon fire. The massive LTV 400 engine consumed over half the chassis’s mass, leaving virtually nothing for weapons. MechWarriors quickly discovered that the Charger’s only real offensive option was physical combat, using its eighty-ton mass and considerable speed to charge lighter opponents. Against Wasps, Stingers, and ’Mechs whose primary armament had already been destroyed, the Charger was effective; against anything else, it was a liability.

The recovery of Star League technology in the late 3040s finally gave LAW the tools to address the Charger’s fundamental weakness. The CGR-3K replaced the small lasers with four medium pulse lasers and an Artemis IV-enhanced LRM-20, while an XL engine and jump jets gave the design unprecedented tactical flexibility for its weight class. The spacious internal layout (originally a consequence of the oversized engine) proved remarkably adaptable to successive generations of weapons technology, producing variants ranging from urban brawlers to Clan-specification scouts. The same roomy chassis that spawned the Hatamoto-Chi family has ensured the Charger’s continued relevance well into the thirty-second century.

Produced at Sapphire Metals on Shimonita and available as a field refit at various facilities, the variant reflects the Combine’s growing comfort with advanced myomer technology and melee-oriented combat doctrine.

BMCharger_CGRC.overview: Conceived by Wells Technologies on Luthien as an ultra-heavy reconnaissance platform for the Star League Defense Force, the eighty-ton Charger is one of the most maligned BattleMech designs in history. First produced in 2665, the original model could outrun most medium 'Mechs yet mounted only a handful of small lasers, armament that would have been considered inadequate on a 'Mech one-quarter its size. Intended to penetrate defended areas at high speed and withdraw before heavier opponents could engage, the Charger's concept failed to survive contact with reality, and the SLDF quickly sidelined it from frontline service. Despite this ignominious beginning, the Charger eventually found redemption through successive redesigns, proving that even the most flawed chassis can become viable with the right technology and engineering vision.
BMCharger_CGRC.capabilities:
The original Charger’s design philosophy (speed and armor over firepower) produced an assault ’Mech whose five small lasers were laughable even to MechWarrior cadets, while its solid Durallex Heavy armor could absorb direct hits from autocannon fire. The massive LTV 400 engine consumed over half the chassis’s mass, leaving virtually nothing for weapons. MechWarriors quickly discovered that the Charger’s only real offensive option was physical combat, using its eighty-ton mass and considerable speed to charge lighter opponents. Against Wasps, Stingers, and ’Mechs whose primary armament had already been destroyed, the Charger was effective; against anything else, it was a liability.

The recovery of Star League technology in the late 3040s finally gave LAW the tools to address the Charger’s fundamental weakness. The CGR-3K replaced the small lasers with four medium pulse lasers and an Artemis IV-enhanced LRM-20, while an XL engine and jump jets gave the design unprecedented tactical flexibility for its weight class. The spacious internal layout (originally a consequence of the oversized engine) proved remarkably adaptable to successive generations of weapons technology, producing variants ranging from urban brawlers to Clan-specification scouts. The same roomy chassis that spawned the Hatamoto-Chi family has ensured the Charger’s continued relevance well into the thirty-second century.
BMCharger_CGRC.history:
Wells Technologies built the Charger in 2665, combining heavy Durallex armor with Magna light lasers in a design intended as a high-speed reconnaissance element for the SLDF. The concept (an assault-weight scout that could absorb punishment while gathering intelligence) failed to account for MechWarriors’ natural inclination to engage the enemy, and the Charger’s popgun armament left pilots defenseless when combat proved unavoidable. The Star League withdrew the design from active service, and Wells Technologies found itself wallowing in unsold inventory. Ironically, the fall of the Star League and the First Succession War saved the company from bankruptcy, as the Draconis Combine’s desperate need for ’Mechs led to bulk purchases of the company’s entire overstock.

Most Chargers found their way into DCMS forces, though battlefield salvage eventually distributed the design across every Great House military. Lyran forces adopted the Charger as a heavy reconnaissance element for assault companies, embracing it more warmly than other Houses. When the ISF uncovered Wells Technologies’ covert attempts to sell Chargers to the Lyran Commonwealth in violation of export restrictions, Luthien Armor Works executed an emergency buyout of the company. Wells Technologies closed its doors in 3027, and CGR-1A1 production ceased entirely by 3030.

The Charger’s defining moment came not from any battlefield triumph but from the Hatamoto-Chi program. When ComStar gifted the Draconis Combine with Star League-era BattleMechs in the 3030s, LAW engineers used reverse-engineered Thug technology to transform the despised Charger chassis into the formidable Hatamoto-Chi, an assault ’Mech that would become one of the DCMS’s most iconic designs. The experience gained with lost technology during the crash Hatamoto program led LAW to rework the Charger itself. The CGR-3K debuted in 3049 with ferro-fibrous armor, pulse lasers, and jump jets, earning widespread acceptance from DCMS MechWarriors who had long scorned the design. By 3068, every regular DCMS unit contained at least one post-3050 Charger variant.

The Sapphire Sunset yakuza clan on Shimonita purchased and upgraded a small LAW complex (renamed Sapphire Metals) and began producing CGR-3Ks, CGR-SA5s, and the newer CGR-KMZ design. When the Raven Alliance absorbed the Outworlds Alliance, Raveena Electronics on Ramora (holder of a production license dating back to a LAW legal error) eventually transitioned from Inner Sphere Charger variants to the Clan-specification Charger C, replacing all previous IS-tech production by 3093.
BMCharger_CGRC.deployment: A common field refit that trades a medium pulse laser for a C3 slave unit and an additional ton of LRM ammunition, this variant appeared around 3052 as the DCMS embraced C3 networking technology. The modification is performed at various field depots across the Combine, allowing existing CGR-3K Chargers to integrate into combined-arms C3 networks without requiring factory-level work.

BMChimera_CMA1S.overview:
The Chimera is a forty-ton medium BattleMech introduced in 3063, the product of an ambitious collaborative effort between the Draconis Combine, Federated Commonwealth, and Lyran Alliance. Originally conceived as a showcase for the technological advances achieved by all three nations in the years preceding Operations Bulldog and Serpent, the design's development was heavily influenced by Lyran corporate interests before entering full-scale production.

Manufactured by Brigadier Corporation on Oliver, Independence Weaponry on Quentin, and Kressly Warworks on Epsilon Eridani, the Chimera serves as a capable light cavalry and skirmisher platform fielded across multiple successor states, delivering firepower well above what most designs of its weight class can manage.
BMChimera_CMA1S.capabilities:
The Chimera is designed to function within light and cavalry formations, delivering firepower well above what most forty-ton designs can manage while maintaining the speed to keep pace with scouting elements. Built on a Chameleon Light Endo 2 chassis powered by a GM 240 Extra Light engine, the design achieves a top speed of ninety-seven kilometers per hour, further enhanced by six Rawlings 40 jump jets providing a hundred-eighty-meter jump capability.

The armament reflects the Chimera's multinational origins. An arm-mounted ExoStar extended-range large laser provides effective engagement at long ranges, while a Shigunga MRM-20 launcher delivers devastating medium-range volleys that few medium BattleMechs can match. A BrightBloom extended-range medium laser and Scatter Gun light machine gun round out the weapons suite for close-quarters engagements. Despite the concentration of energy weapons, the Chimera manages its heat effectively under normal conditions, though aggressive pilots who push the design to its limits will encounter heat management challenges.

The Chimera's primary weakness lies in its armor protection. Carrying only seven tons of StarGuard CCM armor, the design offers protection comparable to many light BattleMechs rather than its medium-class peers. Its designers accepted this trade-off, reasoning that the 'Mech's speed, jump capability, and firepower would compensate for its thin skin.
BMChimera_CMA1S.history:
The Chimera's development was shaped as much by politics as by engineering. The initial joint venture between the Draconis Combine and Federated Commonwealth was intended as a diplomatic gesture in the lead-up to the campaigns against Clan Smoke Jaguar. When Archon Katherine Steiner-Davion inserted the Lyran Alliance into the project, Lyran corporations rapidly took control of the design process, transforming what had been a cooperative endeavor into something quite different from its original conception.

When the Chimera entered service in 3063, the political situation had deteriorated further. Katherine directed the full production run from Brigadier Corporation's Oliver plant and half of Independence Weaponry's Quentin output to units loyal to her faction. The first deployments went to the Alarion Jaegers, the Tenth Deneb Light Cavalry, and the Third Robinson Rangers, all formations aligned with Katherine. Coordinator Theodore Kurita, recognizing the threat this posed to balanced distribution, responded by licensing production to Kressly Warworks on Epsilon Eridani, ensuring that pro-Victor elements within the Armed Forces of the Federated Commonwealth could also acquire the design.

The C3-equipped variant quickly found its way into several Davion Guards and Crucis Lancers regiments, produced at both the Quentin and Epsilon Eridani facilities. The introduction of the more radical CMA-2K variant in 3069 demonstrated the design's adaptability, trading ranged versatility for close-combat lethality through the integration of Triple Strength Myomer and a melee weapon.

During the Jihad, all three production facilities fell under Word of Blake control, with manufacturing continuing under their direction. The Brigadier and Independence Weaponry plants ceased Chimera production in the post-Jihad era, while the Kressly Warworks facility on Epsilon Eridani transitioned through Republic of the Sphere oversight and has remained the most consistent source of new Chimeras. By the ilClan era, Epsilon Eridani had returned to Capellan Confederation control, with Kressly continuing to produce all three variants.
BMChimera_CMA1S.deployment: The base model Chimera mounts an ExoStar extended-range large laser as its primary long-range weapon, complemented by a Shigunga MRM-20 launcher for devastating medium-range salvos. A BrightBloom extended-range medium laser and Scatter Gun light machine gun provide additional firepower at shorter ranges. This combination allows the design to engage effectively across multiple range brackets, making it a versatile performer in the light cavalry role for which it was intended. Produced at all three Chimera manufacturing facilities, this variant remains the most widely distributed variant.

The first deployments went to the Alarion Jaegers, the Tenth Deneb Light Cavalry, and the Third Robinson Rangers, all formations aligned with Katherine. Coordinator Theodore Kurita, recognizing the threat this posed to balanced distribution, responded by licensing production to Kressly Warworks on Epsilon Eridani, ensuring that pro-Victor elements within the Armed Forces of the Federated Commonwealth could also acquire the design.

The C3-equipped variant quickly found its way into several Davion Guards and Crucis Lancers regiments, produced at both the Quentin and Epsilon Eridani facilities. The introduction of the more radical CMA-2K variant in 3069 demonstrated the design's adaptability, trading ranged versatility for close-combat lethality through the integration of Triple Strength Myomer and a melee weapon.

During the Jihad, all three production facilities fell under Word of Blake control, with manufacturing continuing under their direction. The Brigadier and Independence Weaponry plants ceased Chimera production in the post-Jihad era, while the Kressly Warworks facility on Epsilon Eridani transitioned through Republic of the Sphere oversight and has remained the most consistent source of new Chimeras. By the ilClan era, Epsilon Eridani had returned to Capellan Confederation control, with Kressly continuing to produce all three variants.
BMChimera_CMAC.deployment: This variant represents the most minimal modification possible to the base Chimera design. The Scatter Gun light machine gun and its associated ammunition are removed to make room for a C3 slave unit, allowing the 'Mech to integrate into C3-equipped lances. Produced at both the Quentin and Epsilon Eridani plants, this configuration has found favor with several Davion Guards and Crucis Lancers regiments, where the enhanced targeting data provided by the C3 network maximizes the effectiveness of the Chimera's already potent weapons suite without sacrificing any of its primary armament.

BMCicada_CDA2A.overview:
The Cicada was introduced in 2740 by HartfordCo Industries, a small firm on Bryant whose previous manufacturing experience had been confined to communications and targeting systems. Designed as a supplement or replacement for the popular Locust scout 'Mech, the Cicada was built to compete directly with Bergan Industries' design by matching its speed while doubling its mass, allowing for improved weaponry and an edge in physical combat while keeping costs manageable.

The Star League found sufficient merit in the design to award HartfordCo a limited contract, using the Cicada to replace Locusts lost in fighting along border regions. Though the original factory on Bryant was destroyed during the Succession Wars, stockpiled Cicadas found their way into all five Successor State armies. Production was eventually revived by Free Worlds Defense Industries on Gibson, saving the design from extinction.
BMCicada_CDA2A.capabilities:
The Cicada's prime assets are its speed and freedom from ammunition concerns. A massive Pitban 320 engine, comprising more than half the 'Mech's total mass, propels the forty-ton chassis to speeds approaching 130 kilometers per hour. The standard armament of two medium lasers and one small laser provides sufficient firepower to engage lighter 'Mechs while eliminating logistical dependencies. The lasers are embedded in the armored torso behind the heaviest protection, though this placement creates limited firing arcs that an opponent can exploit by maneuvering behind the 'Mech.

The Cicada's four tons of armor matches that of the much lighter Locust, with the bulk concentrated in the torso. The vestigial arm assemblies and legs carry only minimal protection, making speed the design's primary defense. A well-documented flaw in the original HartfordCo heat sinks caused them to wear out and operate at only sixty percent capacity after extended use, leading to dangerous overheating in combat. While most surviving Cicadas have had their heat sinks replaced with reliable modular units, some examples with defective sinks remained in service until the Free Worlds League Military ordered a comprehensive upgrade program in 3029.
BMCicada_CDA2A.history:
HartfordCo Industries entered the BattleMech market in 2740 amid rising tensions throughout the Inner Sphere. The firm, already known for producing the Von Luckner heavy tank and various electronics packages, sought to challenge Bergan Industries' dominance in the light reconnaissance 'Mech market. The Star League's acceptance of the Cicada, though limited in scope, validated the design and established its reputation as a capable scout platform.

The fall of the Star League and destruction of HartfordCo's Bryant facility during the Succession Wars scattered existing Cicadas across the Inner Sphere. Bryant's central location made it a target for raids by all five Successor States, ensuring the design's widespread distribution. The 'Mech earned a positive reputation in service to the Successor Lords, though this sometimes led to expectations exceeding the design's actual capabilities. By the end of the Fourth Succession War, dwindling numbers threatened the Cicada with extinction.

The discovery of the Helm Memory Core allowed Free Worlds Defense Industries to resurrect production on Gibson, providing the Free Worlds League Military with desperately needed reconnaissance assets following losses in the Andurien conflict. The design proved an excellent platform for recovered lostech, leading to upgraded variants mounting extended-range weapons and improved electronics. Following the ComStar Schism and Word of Blake's relocation to Gibson, Blakist forces became major Cicada users, eventually rivaling the FWLM in numbers deployed.

The Jihad's devastation of Gibson seemed to doom the Cicada once more, but Andurien AeroTech's decision to split from the Blakist-tainted FWDI led to the establishment of Westover BattleMechs. This new subsidiary refurbished an abandoned FWDI facility on Westover, resuming Cicada production and introducing modern variants incorporating variable-speed pulse technology and re-engineered lasers for the reunified Free Worlds League's forces.
BMCicada_CDA2A.deployment: The original production model introduced in 2740, this variant mounts two Magna medium lasers in the side torsos and a single Magna Mk. I small laser in the center torso. This configuration provides adequate firepower for engaging light 'Mechs while maintaining complete independence from supply lines. The design's notorious heat sink defect affected many early production units, though comprehensive replacement programs have addressed this issue in most surviving examples. The 2A remains in service across the Inner Sphere, particularly valued by commands requiring economical reconnaissance platforms.
BMCicada_CDA2A.manufacturer: HartfordCo Industries|Gibson Federated BattleMechs (Free Worlds Defense Industries)

BMCicada_CDA3MA.history:
HartfordCo Industries entered the BattleMech market in 2740 amid rising tensions throughout the Inner Sphere. The firm, already known for producing the Von Luckner heavy tank and various electronics packages, sought to challenge Bergan Industries' dominance in the light reconnaissance 'Mech market. The Star League's acceptance of the Cicada, though limited in scope, validated the design and established its reputation as a capable scout platform.

The fall of the Star League and destruction of HartfordCo's Bryant facility during the Succession Wars scattered existing Cicadas across the Inner Sphere. Bryant's central location made it a target for raids by all five Successor States, ensuring the design's widespread distribution. The 'Mech earned a positive reputation in service to the Successor Lords, though this sometimes led to expectations exceeding the design's actual capabilities. By the end of the Fourth Succession War, dwindling numbers threatened the Cicada with extinction.

The discovery of the Helm Memory Core allowed Free Worlds Defense Industries to resurrect production on Gibson, providing the Free Worlds League Military with desperately needed reconnaissance assets following losses in the Andurien conflict. The design proved an excellent platform for recovered lostech, leading to upgraded variants mounting extended-range weapons and improved electronics. Following the ComStar Schism and Word of Blake's relocation to Gibson, Blakist forces became major Cicada users, eventually rivaling the FWLM in numbers deployed.

The Jihad's devastation of Gibson seemed to doom the Cicada once more, but Andurien AeroTech's decision to split from the Blakist-tainted FWDI led to the establishment of Westover BattleMechs. This new subsidiary refurbished an abandoned FWDI facility on Westover, resuming Cicada production and introducing modern variants incorporating variable-speed pulse technology and re-engineered lasers for the reunified Free Worlds League's forces.
BMCicada_CDA3MA.deployment: Introduced in 3068 as a training variant, this variant was designed to help graduating cadets familiarize themselves with newer weapons technologies. This configuration replaces the Ultra AC/5 of the 3M with a snub-nose PPC while significantly increasing armor protection. The simplified weapons loadout and forgiving nature of the snub-nose PPC make the 3MA an ideal platform for introducing MechWarriors to energy weapon combat before they transition to front-line assignments.
BMCicada_CDA3MA.manufacturer: Gibson Federated BattleMechs (Free Worlds Defense Industries)|Westover BattleMechs

Designed as a supplement or replacement for the popular Locust scout 'Mech, the Cicada was built to compete directly with Bergan Industries' design by matching its speed while doubling its mass, allowing for improved weaponry and an edge in physical combat while keeping costs manageable.

The Star League found sufficient merit in the design to award HartfordCo a limited contract, using the Cicada to replace Locusts lost in fighting along border regions. Though the original factory on Bryant was destroyed during the Succession Wars, stockpiled Cicadas found their way into all five Successor State armies. Production was eventually revived by Free Worlds Defense Industries on Gibson, saving the design from extinction.

The standard armament of two medium lasers and one small laser provides sufficient firepower to engage lighter 'Mechs while eliminating logistical dependencies. The lasers are embedded in the armored torso behind the heaviest protection, though this placement creates limited firing arcs that an opponent can exploit by maneuvering behind the 'Mech.

The Cicada's four tons of armor matches that of the much lighter Locust, with the bulk concentrated in the torso. BMClintIIC.overview:
When the Star League Defense Force departed the Inner Sphere in 2784, they brought several prototype Clints in the original configuration mounting the Armstrong Buster autocannon. These prototypes were placed in a Brian Cache on Circe, where they languished throughout the Exodus Civil War until Clan Snow Raven claimed them following the annihilation of Clan Wolverine and the nuclear attack on their capital of Dehra Dun.

Snow Raven scientists worked to correct the stress problems on the 'Mech's frame caused by the heavier autocannon, and by 2830 had transformed the poorly regarded prototype into a well-armed reconnaissance 'Mech. The design was formally introduced in 2842 and became known as the Clint IIC, serving the Ravens through the Golden Century before production ceased in 2917.
BMClintIIC.capabilities:
The Ravens' key modification was replacing the large Pitban 240 fusion plant with a locally produced Type 81 XL engine. While offering the same output as the Pitban, the Type 81 was much lighter, allowing technicians to reinforce the arm and shoulder skeleton that repeatedly failed on the prototypes. Additional spare mass was used to increase armor protection to seven tons and expand ammunition capacity to four tons.

During the Golden Century, the design was further modified, replacing the Armstrong Buster cannon with a Type KOV LB 10-X autocannon that allowed selectable ammunition loads, and upgrading the lasers to Series 2d extended-range medium variants. All other systems remained as in the original Andoran Industries model, and many retained their SLDF designations. Ironically, the Clint IIC still uses the original Sloane 220 Lockover targeting system, a sign of that component's exceptional quality.

The Clint IIC serves as an effective light 'Mech hunter, capable of ranging far beyond supply lines thanks to its generous ammunition reserves. However, the design retains only ten single heat sinks, limiting sustained fire capability, and its seven tons of standard armor provide adequate but not exceptional protection for a medium 'Mech of its era.
BMClintIIC.history:
Clan Snow Raven used the Clint IIC extensively during the Golden Century, deploying it in many clashes with other Clans. The most notable engagement was the defense of the Hellgate agrodomes in 2897, where the speed and maneuverability of the Clint IIC provided the Ravens with a significant advantage. However, battlefield inexperience cost them the fight, prompting the Clan to abandon the mining colony to the Steel Vipers only two years later.

With the Ravens' acquisition of OmniMech technology, many of their second-line 'Mechs were relegated to rear-echelon duty, including the Clint IIC. Following a policy of quality rather than quantity, by the late thirtieth century the Ravens faced the choice of decommissioning or mothballing the venerable design. The Blood Spirits' offer in 2977 to trade several of their WarShips for Snow Raven 'Mech surplus came at an opportune time, and most Clint IICs were transferred to the Spirits, becoming part of their Omicron Galaxy.

Following the destruction of several Blood Spirit Galaxies in their battles with Clan Star Adder and Clan Burrock, few Clints remained in Spirit service. The waning fortunes of the Clint IIC were reversed in 3052, when the Snow Ravens built the first new units since production ceased in 2917, seeking to exploit the invading Clans' need for equipment to replace their war losses. Clans Wolf and Ghost Bear acquired the largest numbers of the design, trading resources from the Inner Sphere for manufacturing output. The Ravens have refused to trade the design to either the Steel Vipers or Jade Falcons due to ongoing feuds with those Clans.
BMClintIIC.deployment: The standard Clint IIC configuration mounts a Type KOV LB 10-X autocannon as its primary weapon, capable of firing both standard and cluster ammunition from its four-ton supply. Two Series 2d ER medium lasers provide backup firepower at extended ranges. The Type 81 XL engine and Andoran Model JJII jump jets retained from the original design provide excellent mobility for a medium reconnaissance 'Mech, while seven tons of standard armor offers adequate protection. Ten single heat sinks limit sustained fire but prove sufficient for the design's intended hit-and-fade tactics.
BMClintIIC.manufacturer: Clan Snow Raven Industrial Complex Chi|Snow Raven Industrial Complex Alpha

BMClintIIC_2.deployment: Developed during the Jihad in 3073, the Clint IIC 2 adopts an all-energy weapons configuration to eliminate ammunition dependency. Five medium pulse lasers distributed across the center torso, left torso, and right arm provide devastating close-range firepower, while eight improved jump jets greatly enhance tactical mobility beyond the standard configuration. Ten double heat sinks replace the original singles to manage the increased thermal load, and ferro-fibrous armor provides improved protection. An ECM suite mounted in the head offers electronic warfare capability, making this variant particularly effective in disrupting enemy targeting and communications.
BMClintIIC_2.manufacturer: Clan Snow Raven Industrial Complex Chi|Snow Raven Industrial Complex Alpha|Eden Rose [Potemkin Class]/Facility 12-D

BMClint_CLNT12R.overview:
The Clint was commissioned in 2607 by the Star League Defense Force from Andoran Industries Limited, a minor BattleMech firm on Bell that secured the contract under the Star League Armaments Act by undercutting competitors with cost-cutting design features. Mass production of the CLNT-2-3T began in 2608, with over 300 units built before the fall of the Star League and the destruction of Andoran's factories during fighting between House Davion and House Liao.

Designed primarily as an inexpensive reconnaissance unit with the capabilities of a well-armed, low-end medium 'Mech, the Clint fulfilled its intended role admirably despite significant maintenance challenges. The design's non-standard components and shoddy construction made it a technician's nightmare, but its combination of speed, firepower, and an exceptional targeting system ensured its continued service across the Inner Sphere and Periphery for centuries.
BMClint_CLNT12R.capabilities:
The original Clint prototypes mounted a heavier Armstrong Buster-class autocannon, but chassis stress problems during testing forced Andoran to downgrade to the lighter Armstrong J11 autocannon/5. This weapon provides reliable medium-range firepower, complemented by a pair of Martell medium lasers that give the Clint effective close-range punch. The design's limited ammunition supply can force pilots to rely entirely on their lasers during prolonged engagements.

The Clint's Pitban 240 fusion engine propels the 'Mech to speeds approaching 100 kilometers per hour, while Andoran Model JJII jump jets provide 180 meters of jumping capability, allowing it to keep pace with other reconnaissance elements and maneuver effectively through broken terrain. This mobility, combined with the exceptional Sloane 220 Lockover targeting system, compensates significantly for the design's maintenance difficulties.

The Clint exemplifies the adage that one's ride was built by the lowest bidder. Its non-standard components require specific replacements that cannot be easily exchanged with other BattleMech types, and parts rarely lasted a year under normal use. The gyroscope became particularly notorious, with replacement units commanding prices literally worth their weight in gold during the Succession Wars. Despite these flaws, engineers who can look past the poor-quality parts generally agree that the overall design is steady and reliable.
BMClint_CLNT12R.history:
The destruction of Andoran Industries during the First Succession War was comprehensive, eliminating not only the original Clint blueprints but also all records of production numbers and official variants. Houses Davion and Liao took possession of the lion's share of surviving Clints, shipping most to remote locations for garrison duty, though the Capellans maintained several in front-line units. The design proved popular in the Periphery, and Clints could be found throughout the Inner Sphere, though the origins of many machines and whether their differing loadouts represented factory variants or field refits remained unknown.

During the First Succession War, Davion and Liao forces clashed on Bell, with bombing attacks reducing the planet's cities to rubble. House Liao deployed ten Clints in urban centers where they proved their worth. Liao subsequently sent several to the Marik front, where they participated in battles on Pella and Ingersoll against the Free Worlds League's Protectorate Guard. The Arcturan Guard of House Steiner acquired a Clint during a raid on Alula Australis, using it effectively in urban combat on Alexandria and Ryde.

An estimated 200 Clints remained in service through the Clan Invasion, mostly with Capellan forces or scattered along the Federated Suns' border regions. The Capellan Confederation introduced the 2-3U upgrade variant, which was subsequently adopted by the Federated Commonwealth after Bell Refit Yards established operations on the ruins of the original Andoran complex. Using all-new tooling painstakingly reverse-engineered by Defiance Industries from captured examples, the design's blueprints eventually reached Defiance's Furillo facility, which began producing new Clints in 3055 following repeated CCAF raids on Bell.

The FedCom Civil War and Jihad prompted further development, with Defiance releasing the 5U model during the Civil War and the 6S following the fall of Hesperus II to Blakist forces. Word of Blake assistance enabled the Taurian Concordat to establish Clint production at Pinard Protectorates Limited on MacLeod's Land, introducing the 3-3T variant. Production continued into the ilClan era with the 3-4T, a sensible upgrade that shares components with the Cadaver and finally addresses many of the design's troublesome non-standard features.
BMClint_CLNT12R.deployment: The original prototype variant produced for the Star League Defense Force, the 1-2R mounted the heavier Armstrong Buster AC/10 with a single medium laser as secondary armament and lacked jump jets entirely. Only twenty of these prototypes were produced before chassis stress issues forced a redesign. Some departed with General Kerensky during the Exodus, though none have resurfaced in the Inner Sphere. Attempts to emulate the configuration by stripping armor and weapons from standard Clints have appeared, and reports of a similar configuration mounting twin lighter autocannons surfaced along the Kurita-Davion border during the battle for Ronel.

BMCobra_CBR02.overview: The Cobra is a 45-ton medium BattleMech introduced around 3060 by Defiance Industries of Hesperus II. Commissioned by the Lyran Alliance Armed Forces to provide an indigenous fire-support platform, the Cobra was designed to fill a critical gap in the Lyran order of battle without reliance on foreign manufacturing. Its development was a direct response to the Free Worlds League's refusal to export its own missile-centric designs to the newly independent Lyran state. Dubbed the Cobra for its distinctive hood-like targeting array, the design has served as a dependable and affordable missile boat in Lyran formations from its inception through the ilClan era, providing consistent indirect fire capability to commands that might otherwise lack dedicated fire-support assets.
BMCobra_CBR02.capabilities:
The Cobra is purpose-built for the fire-support role, mounting a pair of Coventry Star Fire LRM-15 launchers as its primary armament. Defiance engineers borrowed the Zeus's missile arrangement philosophy, positioning the launcher tubes around and set back from a solid torso core. This configuration allows the Cobra to deliver punishing volleys while maintaining the ability to engage targets across a nearly three-hundred-sixty-degree field of fire through torso rotation, and permits the MechWarrior to throw punches without risking damage to the missile racks. Two Defiance B3M medium lasers mounted in the arms provide adequate close-range self-defense against lighter opponents.

The use of a standard VOX 225 fusion engine keeps production costs down and significantly improves survivability compared to designs relying on extralight powerplants, allowing the Cobra to absorb considerable punishment before losing mobility. However, the design carries notable compromises. Despite using Lexington Ltd. High Grade ferro-fibrous armor, the Cobra's six and a half tons of protection is considered inadequate for a forty-five-ton 'Mech, sacrificing defensive capability for speed. More critically, the design lacks any form of Cellular Ammunition Storage Equipment, making the large ammunition magazine a significant vulnerability that has led some pilots to regard the Cobra as a potential deathtrap.
BMCobra_CBR02.history:
The Cobra's genesis traces directly to the Marik-Liao invasion of the Lyran Alliance in 3057. Lyran commanders, initially caught off guard by the coordinated assault, took careful note of the Free Worlds League Military's fire-support doctrine, particularly the effectiveness of the Apollo BattleMech in suppressing Lyran positions with sustained long-range missile bombardment. When Earthwerks Incorporated refused to sell the Apollo to the Lyran Alliance, extending their Federated Commonwealth embargo to the newly independent Lyran state, the LAAF sought an alternative.

Defiance Industries at Hesperus II eagerly accepted the commission, retaining the Apollo's proven missile-centric philosophy while developing a lighter, faster chassis built around a standard fusion engine to reduce costs and improve survivability. Production of the CBR-02 began around 3060. The design was initially assigned to the Third Donegal Guards for operational testing, and LAAF officials signaled their confidence by authorizing full production even before the testing period concluded. The Free Rasalhague Republic expressed interest in purchasing the design, though neither the Federated Commonwealth nor the St. Ives Compact were expected to receive export authorization.

The Cobra saw service through the Civil War period as a staple of Lyran fire-support lances, but the Jihad brought severe disruption. When the Word of Blake seized control of Hesperus II, production of the CBR-02 halted entirely. Defiance Industries' Furillo facility stepped forward to continue the Cobra line, introducing the improved CBR-03 model that addressed many of the original's shortcomings while maintaining its core fire-support mission.

The CBR-03 has remained in continuous production at Furillo from the Jihad era through the Dark Age and into the ilClan period, ensuring the Cobra's continued presence in Lyran Commonwealth Armed Forces formations. While never achieving the ubiquity of designs like the Zeus or Atlas, the Cobra has carved out a reliable niche as an affordable, effective fire-support platform within the Lyran military-industrial complex.
BMCobra_CBR02.deployment: The original CBR-02 mounts a straightforward fire-support loadout centered on twin long-range missile launchers backed by a pair of medium lasers for close defense. Built on an endo steel frame and protected by ferro-fibrous armor, the design prioritizes speed and firepower over protection. The lack of ammunition storage protection in this configuration remains its most criticized shortcoming, a vulnerability that subsequent variants would address. The CBR-02 saw production at Hesperus II from roughly 3060 until the Jihad-era Word of Blake occupation shut down the line.

While never achieving the ubiquity of designs like the Zeus or Atlas, the Cobra has carved out a reliable niche as an affordable, effective fire-support platform within the Lyran military-industrial complex.
BMCobra_CBR03.deployment: Introduced during the Jihad by Defiance Industries' Furillo plant, this variant stands as a comprehensive upgrade addressing the original Cobra's most criticized weaknesses. A VOX 225 light fusion engine and an extralight gyro free sufficient mass for meaningful improvements while maintaining the same top speed. The standard ferro-fibrous armor is replaced with light ferro-fibrous composite, and the freed weight allows the addition of CASE protection for both ammunition bays, directly answering the most common complaint against the CBR-02. The weapons suite receives significant enhancements: both LRM-15 racks gain Artemis IV fire control systems for improved accuracy, and the standard medium lasers are upgraded to Martell extended-range models, improving the Cobra's defensive reach.

BMColossus_CLP3.overview: The Colossus is a ninety-five-ton assault BattleMech designed by Omnitech Industries exclusively for the Solaris VII arena circuit. Originally completed as the CL-P3 prototype in 3053, the design suffered an inauspicious debut that nearly bankrupted its manufacturer. Over a decade later, a partnership with Bethel Labs and their experimental X-Pulse laser technology revitalized the project, producing the CLS-4S redesign that debuted in 3066. The Colossus fills the role of a heavy close-range brawler, combining an assault-class autocannon with advanced pulse laser technology and innovative arm-mounted shields to devastating effect in arena combat. The design has since become one of the most feared competitors on the Solaris VII fighting circuit.
BMColossus_CLP3.capabilities:
Built on the robust Colossus IXb Endo Steel chassis, the CLS-4S mounts a Pitban 285 engine providing a top speed of fifty-four kilometers per hour, comparable to other assault-weight designs such as the Atlas. The addition of Chilton 600 jump jets provides a ninety-meter jump capability, an unusual feature for a ninety-five-ton design that grants critical tactical mobility in the confined terrain of Solaris arenas. Fourteen and a half tons of Valiant Lamellor armor provide punishing damage absorption, while CASE protection in the torso mitigates the risk of catastrophic ammunition detonation.

The primary armament centers on a dorsal-mounted Defiance Disintegrator LB 20-X autocannon, a devastating weapon well suited to arena combat that can fire both solid slugs and cluster munitions. This is complemented by four Sutel Precision Line pulse lasers fitted with Bethel Labs X-Pulse technology (two large and two medium) distributed across both arms. These X-Pulse lasers bridge much of the range gap between Inner Sphere and Clan pulse weapons, providing a significant technological edge over conventionally armed opponents. Heavily armored shields mounted on each arm protect these valuable weapon systems, a design innovation that replaced the original prototype's less effective coolant pod arrangement. The expanded CASE-protected magazine capacity addresses the ammunition vulnerability that contributed to the prototype's arena failures.
BMColossus_CLP3.history:
The Colossus has one of the more unusual developmental histories among Solaris VII fighting machines. Originally designed by Omnitech Industries as an assault-weight arena combatant, the CL-P3 prototype was completed in 3053 during a period of intense innovation on the Game World. Omnitech's promotional materials ambitiously described the design as combining the King Crab's firepower with the Marauder II's combat flexibility, but reality proved far less flattering. When two of the three prototypes were comprehensively defeated in their inaugural arena fights, the resulting financial losses nearly destroyed Omnitech, and the company hastily shelved the entire Colossus program.

The design languished in obscurity for over a decade until Bethel Labs, a technology firm that had developed experimental X-Pulse laser systems capable of approaching Clan pulse laser ranges, began seeking a suitable demonstration platform. Having reduced the manufacturing costs of their modification kits to well below the price of a complete BattleMech, Bethel Labs approached several Solaris VII manufacturers looking for a willing partner. Omnitech, still stinging from the Colossus debacle but eager for redemption, was the first manufacturer to sign on, offering the mothballed chassis as the test bed for the new technology.

The redesigned CLS-4S made its triumphant debut at the 3066 Class V Championships, where a Starlight Stables entry demonstrated the devastating potential of the X-Pulse upgrades. The design's innovative use of arm-mounted shields to degrade incoming fire while closing to effective X-Pulse range proved a winning tactical combination, and the Colossus claimed the Class V Championship title. The victory generated immediate commercial interest from multiple stables, including White Hand, Overlord, and Gemini, all of whom placed orders with Omnitech.

The subsequent introduction of the CLS-5S variant in 3067, featuring PPC capacitors and a Gauss rifle in place of the X-Pulse armament, further expanded the Colossus's tactical repertoire. Production has remained limited to Omnitech's Solaris VII facility, keeping the design closely associated with the arena circuit where it was born. Despite its niche market, the Colossus represents an important milestone as one of the earliest platforms to demonstrate the viability of X-Pulse laser technology in practical combat applications.
BMColossus_CLP3.deployment: This variant represents the original Colossus prototype completed in 3053. Armed with a standard AC/20 and conventional large and medium pulse lasers in each arm, the prototype relied on six coolant pods distributed across both side torsos rather than the arm-mounted shields that would characterize later production models. Though sharing the same chassis, engine, and jump capability as its successor, this variant's reliance on standard pulse laser technology and its lack of arm protection contributed to its disastrous arena debut, where two of three prototypes were destroyed in their first matches. Omnitech subsequently shelved the design for over a decade before Bethel Labs' X-Pulse technology offered a path to redemption.

The PPC capacitors allow brief power surges approaching Clan-grade output levels, providing devastating alpha-strike capability at range. The dorsal-mounted Defiance Disintegrator is replaced with a Gauss rifle, shifting the design's engagement profile toward longer-range precision fire. Four coolant pods distributed between the side torsos help manage the significant heat load generated by the capacitor-equipped PPCs.

BMCommandoIIC.overview:
The Commando IIC traces its lineage to Lyran volunteers who brought their prized scout 'Mechs into Star League service during the Amaris Civil War. These machines survived the Exodus and became part of Nicholas Kerensky's Clan armies, where they were produced by Clans Smoke Jaguar and Goliath Scorpion.

Upgraded around 2856 by Clan Goliath Scorpion with lighter construction materials and improved weaponry, the Commando IIC emerged as a substantially more lethal platform than its Inner Sphere ancestor. Manufactured solely at the Marshall Light Assembly Station, the design remains rare and is most commonly found in Scorpion second-line and anti-bandit formations.
BMCommandoIIC.capabilities:
The Commando IIC stands as a substantial improvement over its Inner Sphere ancestor, mounting more than twice the weaponry and one-and-a-half times the armor protection. Two Series 2d ER medium lasers provide accurate energy fire, while a Pattern J7 SRM-6 and three SEP Class SRM-4 launchers deliver devastating barrages capable of challenging heavier Clan designs like the Ice Ferret. Pilots of Sharman's Boxers nicknamed the design the "Sucker Punch" for its ability to deliver unexpected damage from such a small chassis.

Ammunition efficiency remains the Commando IIC's most significant weakness. Unlike FedCom-era Inner Sphere variants incorporating Streak and Artemis technologies to improve accuracy, the Clan design relies on unguided launchers that rapidly deplete limited ammunition stores. Warriors must be sparing with their shots when operating far from supply. Despite this limitation, the IIC's responsive controls have earned praise from pilots, though most Scorpion warriors criticize the design for its "plethora of inelegant missile weapons."
BMCommandoIIC.history:
The Commando IIC's combat history began in earnest during the early Clan period, when Clan Goliath Scorpion employed the upgraded design in operations across their Pentagon Worlds holdings. In 2872, Scorpion forces used the 'Mech in a lightning raid against Clan Hell's Horses' weakly defended Tokasha enclave. The Commando IICs outflanked and destroyed the more numerous Horse defenders, winning access to two of that Clan's genetic legacies in the process. This engagement demonstrated the design's effectiveness in the close-quarters, mountainous terrain that characterized much of the Pentagon Worlds.

The proliferation of OmniMechs in the late 2800s fundamentally altered the Commando IIC's role within Clan toumans. As first-line units transitioned to the more flexible OmniMech designs, the Commando IIC was increasingly relegated to reserve formations and second-line duties. The Goliath Scorpions, however, maintained a particular affinity for the design and continued to outfit their pirate hunter units with these 'Mechs, taking advantage of the IIC's reliability and firepower in operations along the fringes of Clan space.

Production has remained limited, with the Marshall Light Assembly Station on Marshall serving as the sole manufacturer. Rare even among the Scorpions, the Commando IIC is often piloted by freeborn soldiers assigned to anti-bandit operations where its heavy short-range armament proves ideal. Several examples have been sighted among the Scorpion's Thirty-third Grenadiers, and the design continues to serve in roles where its proven reliability outweighs the lack of modern OmniMech flexibility.
BMCommandoIIC.deployment: The standard Commando IIC serves primarily in Clan Goliath Scorpion second-line and garrison formations, where its heavy short-range firepower proves ideal for anti-bandit operations along the fringes of Clan space. Rare even among the Scorpions, the design is most often piloted by freeborn soldiers assigned to patrol duties in the Pentagon Worlds. Several examples have been sighted among the Thirty-third Grenadiers, and the design continues to fill roles where proven reliability outweighs the flexibility of modern OmniMech alternatives.

BMCommando_COM1B.overview:
First tested in 2463 by the Coventry Defense Conglomerate, the Commando is a twenty-five ton light BattleMech designed for reconnaissance and raiding. One of the Lyran Commonwealth's earliest homegrown designs, the primitive COM-1A gave way to the definitive COM-2D in 2486, transforming the Commando into a deadly close-range striker that has remained in continuous production for over six centuries.

Manufactured primarily by Coventry Metal Works, the Commando earned a fearsome reputation as a fast, hard-hitting scout capable of punching well above its weight class when deployed in groups. Its widespread production and countless field variants have made it one of the most recognizable light 'Mechs in the Inner Sphere.
BMCommando_COM1B.capabilities:
The standard COM-2D Commando mounts paired short-range missile launchers providing ten tubes of firepower, complemented by an arm-mounted medium laser. This armament allows the twenty-five ton 'Mech to deliver devastating barrages effective against even assault-class machines when deployed in groups. The dual missile system prevents a single lucky hit from disabling all offensive capability, and pilots can concentrate fire on one target or split between two.

This firepower comes at significant cost. Each launcher draws from its own ammunition bin and cannot share reserves, meaning the Commando often exhausts its missiles within minutes of sustained combat. The four tons of armor equals that of lighter scouts, creating fatal vulnerability against heavier opponents. Without jump jets, the design struggles to disengage in rough terrain and cannot escape determined pursuit by larger 'Mechs.

The Commando excels in hit-and-run strikes, scouting in pairs to pin down enemy reconnaissance units, and rapid flanking maneuvers. Against the Draconis Combine's Panther, however, that heavier machine's superior range and jump capability proved an effective counter to Commando hunter-killer groups.
BMCommando_COM1B.history:
The Commando's development was driven by desperation. After Operation Prometheus gave the Lyran Commonwealth stolen Terran Hegemony BattleMech technology in 2455, Kurita raiders struck Coventry in 2461 and secured enough data to jumpstart the Combine's own program. The following year, disgruntled Alarion workers defected to the Free Worlds League with additional plans. Knowing its enemies would soon field their own 'Mechs, the Commonwealth rushed the COM-1A into service in 2463, followed by the definitive COM-2D in 2486 after the original's cooling problems proved insurmountable.

The Commando became a cornerstone of Lyran reconnaissance forces and remained exclusively Commonwealth property for centuries. The Star League attempted repeatedly to acquire the design, but Lyran officials employed clever stalling and subtle deception to keep it from foreign hands. This changed during the Amaris Civil War when Lyran volunteers, disaffected by their government's neutrality, brought Commandos into Star League service with the Loyalist forces that liberated Terra. Some of these 'Mechs accompanied General Kerensky into exile, eventually becoming the basis for the Clan Commando IIC.

The Succession Wars spread the Commando throughout the Inner Sphere as mercenary units acquired examples and developed numerous field modifications. These "dash-seven" variants emerged from refit bays across known space, with Mech-it-Lube franchises becoming particularly associated with Commando modifications. The creation of the Federated Commonwealth finally broke the Lyran monopoly, making the Commando the standard light 'Mech alongside the Valkyrie. Vandenberg Mechanized Industries received license to produce the COM-2D for the Taurian Defense Force, while the Marian Hegemony developed its own rocket-armed COM-4H variant.

Task Force Serpent's campaign against Huntress in 3060 saw extensive use of upgraded dash-seven variants, prompting Coventry Metal Works to dedicate factory space for official recreations of these successful field modifications. The Word of Blake's occupation of Coventry from 3068 to 3074 resulted in the COM-7B variant optimized for hunting Lyran resistance fighters, including the Bradford family forces that continued to defy Blakist rule. The technological recovery of the thirty-first and thirty-second centuries brought further refinements, including the C3-equipped COM-8S spotter and the paradigm-shifting COM-9S long-range harasser.
BMCommando_COM1B.deployment: Developed in 3015, this variant attempted to revive the original large laser concept with modern technology. Lyran engineers mounted a large laser and SRM-2 alongside the medium laser, removing the SRM-6 to accommodate the changes. The design incorporated additional armor and heat sinks to address the problems that plagued the COM-1A. Despite better performance than its primitive ancestor, the variant saw little use as Lyran commanders came to favor the SRM-focused configurations that defined the Commando's tactical role.

BMCommando_COM2D.overview:
First tested in 2463 by the Coventry Defense Conglomerate, the Commando is a twenty-five ton light BattleMech designed for reconnaissance and raiding. One of the Lyran Commonwealth's earliest homegrown designs, the primitive COM-1A gave way to the definitive COM-2D in 2486, transforming the Commando into a deadly close-range striker that has remained in continuous production for over six centuries.

Manufactured primarily by Coventry Metal Works, the Commando earned a fearsome reputation as a fast, hard-hitting scout capable of punching well above its weight class when deployed in groups. Its widespread production and countless field variants have made it one of the most recognizable light 'Mechs in the Inner Sphere.
BMCommando_COM2D.capabilities:
The standard COM-2D Commando mounts paired short-range missile launchers providing ten tubes of firepower, complemented by an arm-mounted medium laser. This armament allows the twenty-five ton 'Mech to deliver devastating barrages effective against even assault-class machines when deployed in groups. The dual missile system prevents a single lucky hit from disabling all offensive capability, and pilots can concentrate fire on one target or split between two.

This firepower comes at significant cost. Each launcher draws from its own ammunition bin and cannot share reserves, meaning the Commando often exhausts its missiles within minutes of sustained combat. The four tons of armor equals that of lighter scouts, creating fatal vulnerability against heavier opponents. Without jump jets, the design struggles to disengage in rough terrain and cannot escape determined pursuit by larger 'Mechs.

The Commando excels in hit-and-run strikes, scouting in pairs to pin down enemy reconnaissance units, and rapid flanking maneuvers. Against the Draconis Combine's Panther, however, that heavier machine's superior range and jump capability proved an effective counter to Commando hunter-killer groups.
BMCommando_COM2D.history:
The Commando's development was driven by desperation. After Operation Prometheus gave the Lyran Commonwealth stolen Terran Hegemony BattleMech technology in 2455, Kurita raiders struck Coventry in 2461 and secured enough data to jumpstart the Combine's own program. The following year, disgruntled Alarion workers defected to the Free Worlds League with additional plans. Knowing its enemies would soon field their own 'Mechs, the Commonwealth rushed the COM-1A into service in 2463, followed by the definitive COM-2D in 2486 after the original's cooling problems proved insurmountable.

The Commando became a cornerstone of Lyran reconnaissance forces and remained exclusively Commonwealth property for centuries. The Star League attempted repeatedly to acquire the design, but Lyran officials employed clever stalling and subtle deception to keep it from foreign hands. This changed during the Amaris Civil War when Lyran volunteers, disaffected by their government's neutrality, brought Commandos into Star League service with the Loyalist forces that liberated Terra. Some of these 'Mechs accompanied General Kerensky into exile, eventually becoming the basis for the Clan Commando IIC.

The Succession Wars spread the Commando throughout the Inner Sphere as mercenary units acquired examples and developed numerous field modifications. These "dash-seven" variants emerged from refit bays across known space, with Mech-it-Lube franchises becoming particularly associated with Commando modifications. The creation of the Federated Commonwealth finally broke the Lyran monopoly, making the Commando the standard light 'Mech alongside the Valkyrie. Vandenberg Mechanized Industries received license to produce the COM-2D for the Taurian Defense Force, while the Marian Hegemony developed its own rocket-armed COM-4H variant.

Task Force Serpent's campaign against Huntress in 3060 saw extensive use of upgraded dash-seven variants, prompting Coventry Metal Works to dedicate factory space for official recreations of these successful field modifications. The Word of Blake's occupation of Coventry from 3068 to 3074 resulted in the COM-7B variant optimized for hunting Lyran resistance fighters, including the Bradford family forces that continued to defy Blakist rule. The technological recovery of the thirty-first and thirty-second centuries brought further refinements, including the C3-equipped COM-8S spotter and the paradigm-shifting COM-9S long-range harasser.
BMCommando_COM2D.deployment: Introduced in 2486, this variant represents the definitive Commando configuration that established the design's reputation as a deadly striker. Six centuries of continuous production have made the 2D the most numerous variant, serving as the baseline from which countless modifications have emerged. Lyran reconnaissance lances relied on the 2D as their standard light 'Mech for generations, and licensed production for the Taurian Defense Force through Vandenberg Mechanized Industries ensured the variant's presence across the Periphery as well.
BMCommando_COM2D.manufacturer: Coventry Defense Conglomerate|Coventry Metal Works|Vandenberg Mechanized Industries|Rim Motors

BMCommando_COM8S.capabilities:
The standard COM-2D Commando mounts paired short-range missile launchers providing ten tubes of firepower, complemented by an arm-mounted medium laser. This armament allows the twenty-five ton 'Mech to deliver devastating barrages effective against even assault-class machines when deployed in groups. The dual missile system prevents a single lucky hit from disabling all offensive capability, and pilots can concentrate fire on one target or split between two.

This firepower comes at significant cost. Each launcher draws from its own ammunition bin and cannot share reserves, meaning the Commando often exhausts its missiles within minutes of sustained combat. The four tons of armor equals that of lighter scouts, creating fatal vulnerability against heavier opponents. Without jump jets, the design struggles to disengage in rough terrain and cannot escape determined pursuit by larger 'Mechs.

The Commando excels in hit-and-run strikes, scouting in pairs to pin down enemy reconnaissance units, and rapid flanking maneuvers. Against the Draconis Combine's Panther, however, that heavier machine's superior range and jump capability proved an effective counter to Commando hunter-killer groups.
BMCommando_COM8S.history:
The Commando's development was driven by desperation. After Operation Prometheus gave the Lyran Commonwealth stolen Terran Hegemony BattleMech technology in 2455, Kurita raiders struck Coventry in 2461 and secured enough data to jumpstart the Combine's own program. The following year, disgruntled Alarion workers defected to the Free Worlds League with additional plans. Knowing its enemies would soon field their own 'Mechs, the Commonwealth rushed the COM-1A into service in 2463, followed by the definitive COM-2D in 2486 after the original's cooling problems proved insurmountable.

The Commando became a cornerstone of Lyran reconnaissance forces and remained exclusively Commonwealth property for centuries. The Star League attempted repeatedly to acquire the design, but Lyran officials employed clever stalling and subtle deception to keep it from foreign hands. This changed during the Amaris Civil War when Lyran volunteers, disaffected by their government's neutrality, brought Commandos into Star League service with the Loyalist forces that liberated Terra. Some of these 'Mechs accompanied General Kerensky into exile, eventually becoming the basis for the Clan Commando IIC.

The Succession Wars spread the Commando throughout the Inner Sphere as mercenary units acquired examples and developed numerous field modifications. These "dash-seven" variants emerged from refit bays across known space, with Mech-it-Lube franchises becoming particularly associated with Commando modifications. The creation of the Federated Commonwealth finally broke the Lyran monopoly, making the Commando the standard light 'Mech alongside the Valkyrie. Vandenberg Mechanized Industries received license to produce the COM-2D for the Taurian Defense Force, while the Marian Hegemony developed its own rocket-armed COM-4H variant.

Task Force Serpent's campaign against Huntress in 3060 saw extensive use of upgraded dash-seven variants, prompting Coventry Metal Works to dedicate factory space for official recreations of these successful field modifications. The Word of Blake's occupation of Coventry from 3068 to 3074 resulted in the COM-7B variant optimized for hunting Lyran resistance fighters, including the Bradford family forces that continued to defy Blakist rule. The technological recovery of the thirty-first and thirty-second centuries brought further refinements, including the C3-equipped COM-8S spotter and the paradigm-shifting COM-9S long-range harasser.
BMCommando_COM8S.deployment: Developed in the early thirty-second century as Boosted C3 technology proliferated to the Lyran Commonwealth, this variant builds upon various dash-seven models to function as a dedicated spotter. An endo steel chassis and XL engine provide improved speed, while paired Streak SRM-2 launchers and ER medium lasers offer defensive capability. The C3 boosted slave unit allows the Commando to share targeting data with friendly forces, transforming the scout into a force multiplier that enhances the accuracy of heavier lance mates.

BMCopperhead_CPRHD002.overview: Introduced in late 3054, the Copperhead is a light BattleMech purpose-built for the arena combat circuits of Solaris VII. Designed and manufactured by Solaris Arms, the thirty-ton 'Mech was conceived to excel in the short-duration, close-quarters engagements that define Solaris arena matches. The design quickly gained prominence after a Silver Dragons Stable pilot elevated it into the prestigious Solaris Top Twenty, establishing the Copperhead as a serious contender despite its light weight class. Following this success, the Silver Dragons commissioned Solaris Arms to develop an advanced variant incorporating experimental weaponry, though the prohibitive cost forced the stable to allow outside sales to recoup development expenses. While primarily an arena machine, the Copperhead attracted limited military interest, with the Draconis Combine Mustered Soldiery acquiring a number of the original production models for battlefield evaluation. The design's specialized nature and single-factory production on Solaris VII have kept overall numbers relatively low compared to mainstream military designs.
BMCopperhead_CPRHD002.capabilities:
The Copperhead's design philosophy centers on maximizing lethality within a thirty-ton frame optimized for arena combat. Built on a Castelli 211CTC chassis and powered by a GM 180 XL engine fitted with a supercharger, the design can achieve burst speeds of one hundred thirty kilometers per hour, allowing pilots to rapidly close distance or disengage in tight arena terrain. A pair of Luxor 2/Q-EX jump jets provide a modest sixty meters of vertical mobility, enough for tactical repositioning over obstacles but criticized by some as insufficient for a light 'Mech. ArcShield reflective armor provides exceptional protection against the energy weapons prevalent in arena combat, though at only four and a half tons the coverage remains thin by military standards. A cramped small cockpit accommodates the design's tight internal space requirements but reduces pilot comfort during prolonged engagements.

The Copperhead's firepower centers on a Sutel Precision Line medium X-pulse laser in the left arm, incorporating Bethel Labs X-pulse technology for devastating accuracy at close range. Three torso-mounted Diverse Optics extended-range medium lasers provide the primary damage output at medium distances, while a Holly Streak SRM-4 rack and head-mounted Poland Main Model C Magshot deliver punishing close-range surprises. Thirteen double heat sinks struggle to manage the heat generated by sustained fire from this advanced laser array, forcing pilots to carefully manage their engagement tempo to avoid potentially catastrophic overheating.
BMCopperhead_CPRHD002.history:
The Copperhead traces its origins to the competitive arena circuits of Solaris VII, where Solaris Arms first produced the design in late 3054. Purpose-built for the gladiatorial combat that defined the Game World's entertainment industry, the original CPR-HD-002 quickly proved itself in Solaris stables. A Silver Dragons Stable pilot drove the design into the prestigious Top Twenty rankings, earning recognition for both the stable and the Copperhead itself. This high-profile success prompted the Silver Dragons to commission a comprehensive upgrade incorporating the latest experimental technologies.

The resulting CPR-HD-003 variant entered production around 3065, featuring advanced weaponry and improved defensive systems. However, the development costs proved so substantial that the Silver Dragons were forced to allow sales to other interested parties, spreading the upgraded Copperhead across multiple Solaris stables. A simplified CPR-HD-004 variant followed shortly after in 3066, trading jump capability for increased armor protection to suit pilots who preferred durability over mobility.

The Clan Invasion's arrival in 3049 had dramatically shifted the Inner Sphere's military priorities, diminishing the role of light BattleMechs in conventional warfare. Despite this trend, the Draconis Combine recognized potential in the original Copperhead and purchased a number of CPR-HD-002 models for battlefield service, representing the design's most significant military adoption. The Combine's interest likely stemmed from the Copperhead's energy-weapon-heavy loadout and arena-proven maneuverability, qualities that translated reasonably well to reconnaissance and harassment duties.

Solaris VII's political control shifted several times over the Copperhead's production history. Originally within Free Worlds League territory during the Star League era, the planet passed through Federated Commonwealth control during the Clan Invasion before falling under Lyran Alliance jurisdiction. These political changes affected but did not halt production, as Solaris Arms continued to operate under successive governments. Production of all Copperhead variants appears to have peaked during the Civil War era before ceasing entirely, likely due to the broader disruptions of the Jihad and the design's inherently limited market appeal beyond the arena circuit. The Copperhead's notoriously high maintenance requirements further constrained its adoption outside the well-equipped workshops of Solaris VII's gaming stables.
BMCopperhead_CPRHD002.deployment: The original production model, this variant first appeared in 3054 and served as the foundation for all subsequent variants. Lacking the supercharger and small cockpit of later models, this version mounts Durallex ferro-fibrous armor and carries twelve double heat sinks. Its weapon array consists of four medium lasers supported by a small pulse laser, with a standard SRM-4 launcher providing close-range firepower and a single-shot Streak SRM-2 offering a one-time surprise punch. While designed for arena combat, the Draconis Combine Mustered Soldiery purchased a quantity of CPR-HD-002 models for conventional military service, making this the only Copperhead variant to see significant battlefield deployment outside Solaris VII.
