BMDevastator_DVS10.overview:
The Devastator was designed by General Aleksandr Kerensky himself to correct perceived flaws in the prototype Titan assault 'Mech. Development halted abruptly when Stefan Amaris seized control of the Terran Hegemony, and resources were redirected to the war effort. The design team remained so dedicated that when Kerensky launched the invasion of Terra, they delivered six prototypes at their own expense for evaluation. None of the Devastator's combat records from that conflict survived, leaving the design lost to the Inner Sphere for over two centuries.

In 3023, Federated Suns troops discovered the original blueprints in a Star League-era facility on Hoff, sparking a decades-long effort to resurrect the design. A low-tech version entered limited production in the mid-3030s, but it was not until 3048 that Norse-Storm BattleMechs produced a fully realized version incorporating the intended Star League technologies. The Devastator has since earned a fearsome reputation as one of the most devastating long-range assault platforms in service, with production eventually expanding to multiple manufacturers across the Federated Suns and Lyran state.
BMDevastator_DVS10.capabilities:
Designed for long-range dominance to compensate for its slow speed, the Devastator mounts two Poland Main Model A Gauss rifles as its primary armament, supplemented by a pair of Donal particle projection cannons in the torsos. This combination delivers punishing firepower at extended ranges, allowing the Devastator to engage and destroy targets well before they can close to effective distance. Conventional wisdom would dictate placing the main guns in the more protected torso locations, but Norse-Storm deliberately mounted the Gauss rifles in the arms. Should a lucky hit cause a rifle to explode, the resulting detonation would not threaten the vulnerable extra-light engine housed in the torso, extending the 'Mech's life expectancy in sustained combat.

Four Intek medium lasers provide close-range defense, with one rear-mounted in the center torso to discourage infantry from approaching the 'Mech's blind spot. The Devastator's heat management is among its most impressive features. Fourteen double heat sinks allow the pilot to move at maximum speed while firing all primary weapons without concern for overheating. Even when doused in inferno gel or suffering multiple engine hits, the pilot need only marginally reduce fire to maintain operational temperatures. Eighteen and a half tons of Durallex Heavy armor provide excellent protection, though the extra-light engine remains a critical vulnerability should torso armor be breached.
BMDevastator_DVS10.history:
The Devastator's origins trace to the final years of the Star League, when General Aleksandr Kerensky personally drafted specifications for a new hundred-ton assault 'Mech to address shortcomings he perceived in the prototype Titan. When Stefan Amaris seized the Terran Hegemony, development stalled as resources were consumed by the war effort. The design team persevered, however, and when Kerensky launched the invasion of Terra in 2777, they delivered six prototypes funded from their own pockets. Only one engagement is recorded in surviving documents, a battle on the Alberta plains where the prototypes acquitted themselves well, but no comprehensive combat records survived the fall of the Star League.

The Devastator remained lost to the Inner Sphere for over two centuries until 3023, when Federated Suns troops uncovered the original blueprints in a Star League facility on Hoff. Initial attempts to reproduce the design proved impossible given the degraded state of Inner Sphere technology. The NAIS constructed a low-tech prototype in 3033, resulting in the downgraded DVS-1D that entered moderate production a few years later. This stopgap variant served until 3048, when Norse-Storm BattleMechs on Loxley began producing the fully realized DVS-2 incorporating the intended Star League technologies. The design was distributed primarily to elite Federated Commonwealth units during the early years of production.

The Devastator saw extensive service during the Clan Invasion and subsequent conflicts, its long-range firepower proving particularly effective against Clan opponents. Many commanders adopted it as a personal bodyguard 'Mech, using batteries of PPCs and Gauss rifles to deter headhunter teams. When the Lyran Alliance seceded in 3057, Archon Katherine stopped all Devastator shipments to the Federated Suns until 3061, when deliveries resumed to loyalist units. The design saw heavy combat throughout the FedCom Civil War, with Norse-Storm's Loxley facility untouched during the fighting and maintaining maximum output to meet the Archon's demands.

In the immediate aftermath of the Civil War, Archon Peter Steiner-Davion placed a massive order for BattleMechs from Norse-Storm. Unlike the Thunder Hawk, the Devastator was cleared for export, and the Armed Forces of the Federated Suns purchased significant numbers to replace assault 'Mechs lost in the fighting. During the Jihad, Norse-Storm became one of the most critical BattleMech industries in the Lyran Alliance, as many competing factories fell under Word of Blake occupation. Corean Enterprises on Augusta later joined production, eventually developing the DVS-10 and DVS-11 variants for Dark Age and ilClan-era service.

Separately from the Inner Sphere's rediscovery, Clan technicians hand-built several Devastators before Operation Klondike using the best available technology. These Early Clan variants were later overhauled with enhanced weapons systems. In a notable legal episode, General Motors attempted to claim ownership of the Devastator design and extract royalties from Norse-Storm. Both Lyran and Federated courts ruled the design had entered the public domain, clearing the way for its widespread production across multiple manufacturers.
BMDevastator_DVS10.deployment: This variant is a production adaptation of the experimental MUSE EARTH project, developed by Corean Enterprises to bring a more practical version of that radical prototype to the battlefield. Retaining the four hundred-rated engine (downgraded from the original's XXL to a more reliable XL) along with the MASC and Supercharger combination, this variant abandoned the MUSE EARTH's heavy PPCs entirely in favor of a suite of re-engineered lasers designed to penetrate advanced armor types. Two large re-engineered lasers in the arms provide primary firepower while two medium re-engineered lasers in the center torso offer close-range coverage. Despite its impressive technology, this variant proved profoundly unpopular throughout the AFFS. MechWarriors despised assignments to the hundred-ton specialist, finding it invariably outranged and outgunned by longer-ranged 'Mechs when attempting to fight outside its narrow niche.

Half a ton of armor was sacrificed to accommodate additional cooling capacity. BMDevastator_DVS2.capabilities:
Designed for long-range dominance to compensate for its slow speed, the Devastator mounts two Poland Main Model A Gauss rifles as its primary armament, supplemented by a pair of Donal particle projection cannons in the torsos. Conventional wisdom would dictate placing the main guns in the more protected torso locations, but Norse-Storm deliberately mounted the Gauss rifles in the arms. Should a lucky hit cause a rifle to explode, the resulting detonation would not threaten the vulnerable extra-light engine housed in the torso, extending the 'Mech's life expectancy in sustained combat.

Four Intek medium lasers provide close-range defense, with one rear-mounted in the center torso to discourage infantry from approaching the 'Mech's blind spot. The Devastator's heat management is among its most impressive features. Fourteen double heat sinks allow the pilot to move at maximum speed while firing all primary weapons without concern for overheating. Even when doused in inferno gel or suffering multiple engine hits, the pilot need only marginally reduce fire to maintain operational temperatures. Eighteen and a half tons of Durallex Heavy armor provide excellent protection, though the extra-light engine remains a critical vulnerability should torso armor be breached.

BMDoloire_DLRO.overview: The Doloire is an eighty-ton assault OmniMech introduced in 3121 as the flagship design of the Republic Armed Forces. Produced by StarCorps Industries on Terra, the Doloire was conceived as a tangible symbol of cooperation between the Republic of the Sphere's Inner Sphere and Clan populations, drawing on scientists from the Clan enclaves within Republican borders to create a design blending both technological traditions. Built with mixed Inner Sphere and Clan technology, the Doloire was intended to serve as a prestigious command platform, frequently assigned to promising young officers seeking to distinguish themselves in battle. Its status as both a military asset and a political statement ensured that the Doloire received attention and resources far exceeding those afforded to more common assault designs.
BMDoloire_DLRO.capabilities:
The Doloire's chassis is built around a Clan-manufactured 320-rated extra-light engine, which provides a respectable top speed of sixty-four kilometers per hour while offering greater survivability than a comparable Inner Sphere XL engine. The use of an endo-composite internal structure saves weight without fully committing to either Clan or Inner Sphere engineering paradigms, freeing up mass for nearly fifteen tons of ArcShield VII Mk.7 standard armor that provides substantial protection across all locations. Twelve double heat sinks handle baseline thermal loads, while thirty-two tons of pod space give technicians considerable latitude in tailoring the design to specific mission profiles.

Two Clan Series 2f extended-range medium lasers are permanently mounted in the center torso, ensuring the Doloire is never completely disarmed regardless of pod configuration. All configurations benefit from integrated actuator enhancement systems built into the arm assemblies, improving weapon accuracy during close engagements. In its Prime configuration, the Doloire carries a pair of Clan large pulse lasers augmented by these actuator enhancements, a Clan Gauss rifle for long-range striking power, and an Angel ECM suite providing electronic warfare capability. This combination of accurate energy weapons, ballistic firepower, and electronic protection makes the Prime a versatile command platform well-suited to leading combined-arms formations.
BMDoloire_DLRO.history:
The Doloire emerged from the Republic of the Sphere's ambitious effort to forge a unified military identity from the diverse populations within its borders. Following the Republic's founding, officials recognized that a prestige OmniMech incorporating both Inner Sphere and Clan technology would serve as a powerful symbol of their cooperative vision. StarCorps Industries on Terra was selected as the manufacturer, leveraging scientists from the Clan enclaves established within Republican territory. When the design entered production in 3121, it represented one of the most sophisticated mixed-technology platforms of its era, and the Republic Armed Forces quickly adopted it as a flagship assault 'Mech assigned to its most promising officers.

The Doloire saw widespread deployment across every regiment of the RAF during the Republic's peak, serving as both a potent battlefield asset and a visible embodiment of Republican ideals. Its status as a command platform made it a high-priority target in engagements, and the design's reputation as both a powerful and prestigious machine ensured that captured examples were highly prized by opposing forces. When Fortress Republic was raised and the Republic withdrew behind its protective barrier, StarCorps continued and even accelerated Doloire production as part of the clandestine military buildup occurring behind the Fortress walls.

Outside the Fortress, the Doloire's fortunes became more fragmented. Republic Remnant units retained several examples, while mercenary commands that had served alongside the RAF managed to hold onto their machines. During the Capellan Confederation's expansion into former Republican territory in the mid-3130s, several engagements featured Doloires on the defensive. The Capellan assault on Azha in 3136, where a small mercenary unit attempted to hold a critical river crossing against advancing Confederation forces, demonstrated both the design's combat effectiveness and the limitations of isolated units facing superior numbers. At least one Doloire was subsequently salvaged by Capellan forces, and the Confederation's growing access to advanced technology ensured these captured machines could be maintained and deployed.

The Blessed Order's revival of ComStar's First Division saw the Doloire adopted in a custom configuration optimized for the Order's networked combat doctrine, further demonstrating the design's adaptability to different organizational philosophies. As the ilClan era dawned and the political environment of the Inner Sphere continued to shift, the Doloire remained a respected if relatively uncommon assault platform, its mixed-technology heritage serving as a lasting reminder of the Republic's attempt to bridge the divide between Inner Sphere and Clan traditions.
BMDoloire_DLRO.deployment: The Prime configuration establishes the Doloire as a versatile command platform capable of engaging targets across multiple range brackets. A pair of Clan large pulse lasers mounted in the arms benefit from integral actuator enhancement systems, delivering exceptional accuracy at medium range. A Clan Gauss rifle in the right torso provides devastating long-range firepower, while an Angel ECM suite disrupts enemy targeting and communications systems. Four additional Clan double heat sinks ensure the configuration can sustain fire without overheating, making the Prime equally effective in prolonged engagements and rapid strikes.

A lance mounted on the left arm provides a melee option against opponents that close to physical combat range, while an extended-range small pulse laser augments the fixed laser array. A C3 master computer fitted in the left torso enables the pilot to coordinate targeting data across a networked lance, making this configuration a natural choice for officers directing combined operations.

Built with mixed Inner Sphere and Clan technology, the Doloire was intended to serve as a prestigious command platform, frequently assigned to promising young officers seeking to distinguish themselves in battle. Its status as both a military asset and a political statement ensured that the Doloire received attention and resources far exceeding those afforded to more common assault designs.
BMDoloire_DLROD.capabilities:
The Doloire's chassis is built around a Clan-manufactured 320-rated extra-light engine, which provides a respectable top speed of sixty-four kilometers per hour while offering greater survivability than a comparable Inner Sphere XL engine. The use of an endo-composite internal structure saves weight without fully committing to either Clan or Inner Sphere engineering paradigms, freeing up mass for nearly fifteen tons of ArcShield VII Mk.7 standard armor that provides substantial protection across all locations. Twelve double heat sinks handle baseline thermal loads, while thirty-two tons of pod space give technicians considerable latitude in tailoring the design to specific mission profiles.

Two Clan Series 2f extended-range medium lasers are permanently mounted in the center torso, ensuring the Doloire is never completely disarmed regardless of pod configuration. All configurations benefit from integrated actuator enhancement systems built into the arm assemblies, improving weapon accuracy during close engagements. In its Prime configuration, the Doloire carries a pair of Clan large pulse lasers augmented by these actuator enhancements, a Clan Gauss rifle for long-range striking power, and an Angel ECM suite providing electronic warfare capability. This combination of accurate energy weapons, ballistic firepower, and electronic protection makes the Prime a versatile command platform well-suited to leading combined-arms formations.

Twin TSEMP cannons mounted in the side torsos can disable enemy electronics and shut down 'Mechs entirely, complementing the fixed extended-range medium lasers. A supercharger allows the Doloire to close distance rapidly, bringing four Streak SRM-4 launchers and a large vibroblade into effective range. Paired Clan extended-range micro lasers in the legs round out the armament, while CASE II protects against ammunition detonation. This configuration represents the most overtly aggressive loadout in the Doloire family, clearly designed for MechWarriors willing to wade into close combat.

BMDragonFire_DGR3F.overview:
The Dragon Fire traces its origins to the twenty-eighth century, conceived as part of the same development project that produced the legendary Marauder. Despite promising specifications, the design never progressed beyond the drawing board during the Star League era, remaining a footnote in General Motors' archives for centuries. The rediscovery of lost Star League technical data in the mid-3050s breathed new life into the dormant blueprint, and General Motors licensed production to J.B. BattleMechs Incorporated rather than undertake the project themselves.

The first Dragon Fire rolled off JBBMI's production lines on Storfors in late 3058, and the seventy-five-ton heavy 'Mech quickly attracted attention from multiple Great Houses. The Dragon Fire established a reputation as a resilient and versatile fire support platform, though corporate upheaval and the Jihad dramatically altered the design's trajectory before new manufacturers eventually restored it to prominence across the Inner Sphere.
BMDragonFire_DGR3F.capabilities:
The Dragon Fire delivers formidable firepower through a carefully balanced weapons array enabled by its Pitban 300 XL engine and Royalstar endo steel chassis. The Zeus Slingshot Gauss rifle serves as the primary weapon, delivering devastating kinetic impacts at extreme range without generating waste heat. A Mydron Excel LB 10-X autocannon complements the Gauss rifle with versatile ammunition options, capable of firing both standard slugs for concentrated damage and cluster rounds effective against vehicles and aerospace fighters. An ExoStar large laser provides reliable energy-based firepower independent of ammunition supplies, while twin Defiance B4M medium pulse lasers deliver accurate close-range fire.

Fourteen and a half tons of ArcShield Maxi II armor provide substantial protection for a heavy 'Mech, and CASE mitigates the risk posed by the design's considerable ammunition stores. The Guardian ECM suite disrupts enemy targeting and electronic warfare systems, a valuable capability that distinguishes the Dragon Fire from many of its contemporaries. The design's primary limitations stem from its reliance on an XL engine, which leaves it vulnerable to side torso damage, and its complete lack of jump jets, restricting maneuverability in rough terrain. The Dragon Fire also bears the dubious distinction of being considered one of the aesthetically least appealing BattleMechs in service, its unsightly weapon bulges and sensor arrays marring the Marauder family's otherwise sleek lines.
BMDragonFire_DGR3F.history:
The Dragon Fire's existence spans centuries of unrealized potential followed by decades of turbulent production history. Originally designed in the late twenty-eighth century alongside the Marauder, the Dragon Fire never achieved production during the Star League era, its blueprints languishing in General Motors' archives through the Succession Wars. The recovery of the Gray Death Memory Core in 3054 brought the design back into consideration, and GM licensed the project to J.B. BattleMechs Incorporated on Storfors for a token fee rather than diverting their own production resources.

The first Dragon Fires entered service in late 3058 and immediately proved their worth. The Draconis Combine became JBBMI's primary customer, and Lyran standing orders reflected unusual cross-faction demand driven by the shared Clan threat. The design's advanced arsenal offered a genuine answer to Clan technology advantages, and its performance during Operation Bulldog and the subsequent Great Refusal cemented its reputation among Inner Sphere militaries.

The mid-3060s brought a dramatic shift when JBBMI signed an exclusive subsidiary contract with the Word of Blake, redesigning the Dragon Fire with improved C-cubed technology. In 3068, a financial crisis saw the company change hands as Blakist-affiliated stockholders acquired controlling interest. Production facilities across the Alliance, Combine, and Federated Suns were shuttered, with new plants opening on Epsilon Eridani, Caph, and New Earth under the renamed J.B. BattleMechs of the Protectorate Ltd. The Dragon Fire became closely associated with the Word of Blake Militia, though a daring raid on the Myer facility on New Earth by Skye Ranger forces resulted in at least six machines being liberated.

The Jihad devastated JBBMI's reputation beyond recovery, and the Dragon Fire spent decades in obscurity following the conflict. The design's fortunes reversed during the Dark Age when General Motors finally took direct interest, producing the radically redesigned DGR-9D as a pocket assault 'Mech from their Kathil facilities. Independence Weaponry on Quentin leveraged their experience with the Fujin to produce the DGR-7K for the Draconis Combine. During the fighting over the Dragon's Tongue, Dragon Fires were fielded in strength by both Houses Davion and Kurita, marking the design's definitive return to frontline service.

The Dragon Fire's combat record includes notable engagements such as Operation Solar Flare, where Davion Assault Guards deployed their Dragon Fires against the mercenary unit Ravannion's Redemption off Euclid. The ensuing engagement saw Davion and Draconis-built Dragon Fires on opposite sides, with the mercenaries' ballistic-reinforced armor variants proving surprisingly effective against the Guards' superior firepower. Persistent rumors from the spinward Periphery describe a nightmarish machine resembling a warped Marauder, speculated to be a heavily modified Dragon Fire, though such reports remain unconfirmed.
BMDragonFire_DGR3F.deployment: The original production model entered service in late 3058 from JBBMI's Storfors facility, representing the first realization of a design conceived centuries earlier. Armed with a Zeus Slingshot Gauss rifle, Mydron Excel LB 10-X autocannon, ExoStar large laser, and twin Defiance medium pulse lasers, the 3F offered a balanced mix of long-range striking power and close-defense capability. The Guardian ECM suite provided electronic warfare protection uncommon in heavy 'Mechs of this era. Initially popular with both Draconis Combine and Lyran forces facing the Clan threat, the 3F saw extensive service during Operation Bulldog and the Great Refusal before JBBMI's association with the Word of Blake redirected production priorities.

Production continued at Storfors alongside the 3F until JBBMI's corporate restructuring under Word of Blake ownership shifted manufacturing priorities.

BMDragonII_DRG11K.overview:
The Dragon II emerged from Luthien Armor Works' post-Jihad efforts to revitalize iconic DCMS designs using advanced technology developed during the devastating conflict. After losing substantial production capacity to Word of Blake attacks, LAW sought to prove the company's continued value through ambitious new designs. The result was a comprehensive reimagining of the Dragon concept, transforming the traditional brawler into an artillery support platform.

Introduced in 3099, the Dragon II represented the DCMS's commitment to technological self-sufficiency under the mandates of Coordinator Urizen II. Every component was manufactured within Combine borders, making it a statement of industrial capability as much as a weapons system. The design found immediate favor among ISF operatives and politically connected officers, who claimed early production runs before regular DCMS units received allocations.
BMDragonII_DRG11K.capabilities:
The Dragon II's combat role differs substantially from its predecessors, emphasizing fire support over close assault. The centerpiece of its armament is the Shigunga Arrow IV Artillery System, capable of delivering precision strikes at extreme ranges or providing area suppression with various ammunition types. Three tons of ammunition storage allows flexibility in loadout selection. The Lord's Light 2 Extended-Range PPC inherited from the Grand Dragon provides all-range direct fire capability, while a Diverse Optics Type 25PX Medium X-Pulse Laser offers close defense.

The shift to artillery support necessitated design compromises in other areas. The Magna 260 engine produces a maximum speed of only 64 kilometers per hour, significantly slower than both the Dragon and Grand Dragon. LAW's engineers compensated through enhanced durability, incorporating a Nykvarn Type 58-66SH Endo Steel chassis and compact gyro. The 12.5 tons of Durallex Guardian II Light Ferro-Fibrous armor provides excellent protection, while CASE II shielding ensures ammunition detonation won't prove immediately catastrophic.
BMDragonII_DRG11K.history:
The Dragon II entered DCMS service during a period of significant political and military transformation within the Draconis Combine. The Republic of the Sphere's formation and subsequent Gray Monday crisis reshaped the strategic sphere, creating both opportunities and challenges for Combine expansion. The Dragon II proved well-suited to this new era of warfare, where combined arms operations and long-range precision strikes often determined battle outcomes.

Early combat deployments demonstrated the Dragon II's effectiveness in coordinated operations. On Palmyra, Dragon IIs of the Seventh New Samarkand Cadre blocked a Davion counterattack outside Sawle, using their Arrow IV systems to break up armored formations while their PPCs engaged survivors. Similar successes on Raman saw Dragon IIs of the Forty-fifth Benjamin Regulars shelling enemy positions across difficult terrain, allowing conventional forces to advance through previously impassable ground.

The Dragon II's association with political appointees and ISF operatives has colored its reputation within the regular DCMS. Veteran MechWarriors often express skepticism toward pilots assigned these machines, viewing their technological advantages as compensation for inferior skill. Despite this tension, the Dragon II has proven its worth repeatedly, earning grudging respect from critics. The experimental DRG-11R variant, equipped with Clan-grade weapons, remains restricted to nobles and the politically connected.
BMDragonII_DRG11K.deployment: The standard Dragon II configuration centers on the Shigunga Arrow IV Artillery System, providing fire support capability unprecedented in the Dragon lineage. The Lord's Light 2 ER PPC inherited from the Grand Dragon ensures direct engagement capability at all ranges, while the Diverse Optics Type 25PX Medium X-Pulse Laser handles close defense. Three tons of Arrow IV ammunition allow loadout flexibility, from standard high-explosive rounds to specialized homing or smoke munitions. The Nykvarn Type 58-66SH Endo Steel chassis and compact gyro maximize internal volume, while CASE II shielding ensures ammunition detonation won't prove immediately catastrophic.

Weight savings from the more efficient Clan technology allow incorporation of MASC, increasing top speed to 86 kilometers per hour. A B-Pod provides last-ditch defense against infantry and battle armor. The variant's restricted availability reinforces perceptions of the Dragon II as a status symbol among DCMS personnel.

BMDragon_DRG1C.overview:
The Dragon was introduced in 2754 during the twilight years of the Star League, designed by Luthien Armor Works as an advanced close assault 'Mech intended to replace the aging Shadow Hawk in SLDF service. Though the design ultimately lost the procurement competition to an upgraded Shadow Hawk variant in what many consider a predetermined contest, the rejection proved fortuitous for the Draconis Combine. LAW pushed the Dragon into full production for the DCMS, where it would become the standard heavy BattleMech for centuries.

Engineered for sustained independent operations, the Dragon's distinctive squat profile and reinforced rear armor reflect its intended role of breaking through enemy formations. Multiple production lines across Luthien and Dieron ensured the Dragon's ubiquity within DCMS forces throughout the Succession Wars.
BMDragon_DRG1C.capabilities:
The Dragon fulfills its close assault role through a combination of respectable firepower, surprising speed, and exceptional durability for extended engagements. Its primary armament centers on an Imperator-A Autocannon/5 mounted in the right arm and a Telos DecaCluster LRM-10 launcher integrated into its protruding chest assembly. This combination provides effective standoff capability as the 'Mech closes with its targets. Two Victory 23R medium lasers round out the weapons suite, with one forward-mounted and another rear-facing to discourage pursuit.

The design philosophy prioritizes sustained combat operations over peak damage output. Forty rounds of autocannon ammunition and a generous missile magazine allow the Dragon to operate independently for extended periods. Ten standard heat sinks prove adequate given the modest thermal demands of its weapons loadout. The ten tons of Starshield armor provide solid protection, particularly around the torso and rear sections. However, the Dragon's most notable characteristic may be its effectiveness in close combat, where MechWarriors frequently employ its reinforced fists and devastating kicks to finish wounded opponents.

By the height of the Succession Wars, the Dragon had achieved legendary status within Combine military culture. Every DCMS battalion included Dragons in significant numbers, with some formations composed entirely of these 'Mechs. The Arm of the Dragon typically employed these machines for softening up barrages before charging to exploit gaps in enemy lines. Such was the Dragon's proliferation that significant numbers fell into enemy hands through salvage, with both the Federated Suns and Lyran Commonwealth fielding captured examples.

Surviving examples found their way into militia formations, where their extended range occasionally proves useful for harassment missions.

BMDragonfly_A.overview: The Viper, known to Inner Sphere forces by its reporting name Dragonfly, is a 40-ton Clan OmniMech first produced in 2940 by Clan Fire Mandrill on the world of Shadow. Conceived as a quick-strike design emphasizing speed and agility over raw firepower, the Viper initially fell out of favor with several Fire Mandrill kindraa due to persistent problems with its omnipod mechanisms. In 3002, the Mandrills traded the design specifications and manufacturing facilities to Clan Ghost Bear in exchange for several production runs of Executioner OmniMechs. The Ghost Bears relocated production to Strana Mechty, developing modular production line technology in the process that would later prove invaluable during their migration to the Inner Sphere. Despite its troubled origins, the Viper has endured as one of the most widely distributed medium OmniMechs in the Clan arsenal, with production eventually spreading to multiple facilities across both the Homeworlds and the Inner Sphere.
BMDragonfly_A.capabilities:
Built on a lightweight Type W2 Endo-steel chassis and powered by a 320-rated XL engine, the Viper achieves a top speed of nearly 130 kilometers per hour, making it one of the fastest medium OmniMechs in any Clan touman. Eight jump jets provide an impressive 240-meter jump capability, granting exceptional tactical flexibility in broken or urban terrain. Seven tons of ferro-fibrous armor provide reasonable protection for its weight class, though the design remains vulnerable to concentrated fire from heavier opponents.

The Viper's primary limitation is its modest 8.5 tons of pod space, which significantly restricts its offensive payload compared to other medium OmniMechs in the 35-to-45-ton range such as the Adder, Shadow Cat, and Grendel. In its Prime configuration, the Viper mounts a pair of medium pulse lasers and an SRM-4 launcher for close-range engagements, supported by twin machine guns for anti-infantry work and an anti-missile system for defensive purposes. While considered undergunned for formal Clan dueling, the Viper excels in the fluid, indirect combat typical of Inner Sphere operations, where its speed allows it to choose engagements and screen for heavier formations.
BMDragonfly_A.history:
The Viper's early history is defined by a pattern of ownership changes that would shape its manufacturing legacy for centuries. Originally produced by Kindraa Sainze of Clan Fire Mandrill on Shadow, the design's troubled relationship with the Fire Mandrills' fractious internal politics led to its transfer to Clan Ghost Bear in 3002. Rather than Trial for land rights on Shadow and become embroiled in inter-Kindraa conflicts, the Ghost Bears restructured the production facility into a modular design and physically relocated the entire manufacturing line to their enclave on Strana Mechty. This innovative modular approach to production would prove to be one of the Viper's most significant, if unintended, legacies. When the Ghost Bears began their migration back to the Inner Sphere in the late 3050s, the modular factory technology developed for the Viper line allowed them to move several other manufacturing operations with relative ease.

Production on Strana Mechty continued under Ghost Bear control until the mid-3060s, when Clan Hell's Horses trialed for and won both production rights and the Upsilon Plant 2J facility. Their tenure was short-lived, however, as Clan Ice Hellion seized the entire plant in early 3068 following a grueling twelve-hour battle between both saKhans. The Ice Hellions immediately put the facility to use, with new configurations being shipped out as quickly as DropShips could be loaded, lending credence to rumors of a planned large-scale operation against their Coyote neighbors on Foster.

Beyond Strana Mechty, additional Viper production existed across the Homeworlds. Clan Coyote maintained a manufacturing line on Delios until 3071, when Clan Goliath Scorpion captured the facility during the opening stages of the Wars of Reaving. The Cloud Cobras operated their own production lines on Homer and at the Albion Armor Works on Albion. Clan Blood Spirit also maintained early production capacity at the Albion facility before the Star Adders assumed control. Following the Wars of Reaving and the destruction or Abjuration of several Clans, the surviving Home Clans continued to field the Viper as the similar Ice Ferret was phased out, possibly due to its association with the departed Spheroid Clans.

Having abandoned their Homeworld production infrastructure, the Ghost Bears, now reorganized as the Rasalhague Dominion, ultimately resumed Viper production at the newly established Dominion Facility Kappa-5 on Thule. This ensured the design remained a fixture within the Dominion's touman well into the Dark Age, where continued deployment in the Inner Sphere demonstrated that the Viper's combination of speed, mobility, and reconfiguration flexibility remained as tactically relevant as ever.
BMDragonfly_A.deployment: Optimized for close-range harassment, the Alternate Configuration A mounts five ER medium lasers alongside an Artemis IV-enhanced SRM-6 launcher. The resulting short-range firepower makes the configuration a dangerous opponent in close combat, though MechWarriors must carefully manage the significant heat generated by sustained alpha strikes to avoid shutdown at critical moments.
BMDragonfly_A.manufacturer: Kindraa Sainze Primary Production Facility|Upsilon Plant 2J|Albion Armor Works Gamma|Largo 'Mech Production Complex|Complex H-1 CCC|Dominion Facility Kappa-5

Seven tons of ferro-fibrous armor provide reasonable protection for its weight class, though the design remains vulnerable to concentrated fire from heavier opponents.

The Viper's primary limitation is its modest 8.5 tons of pod space, which significantly restricts its offensive payload compared to other medium OmniMechs in the 35-to-45-ton range such as the Adder, Shadow Cat, and Grendel. In its Prime configuration, the Viper mounts a pair of medium pulse lasers and an SRM-4 launcher for close-range engagements, supported by twin machine guns for anti-infantry work and an anti-missile system for defensive purposes. While considered undergunned for formal Clan dueling, the Viper excels in the fluid, indirect combat typical of Inner Sphere operations, where its speed allows it to choose engagements and screen for heavier formations.
BMDragonfly_D.history:
The Viper's early history is defined by a pattern of ownership changes that would shape its manufacturing legacy for centuries. Originally produced by Kindraa Sainze of Clan Fire Mandrill on Shadow, the design's troubled relationship with the Fire Mandrills' fractious internal politics led to its transfer to Clan Ghost Bear in 3002. Rather than Trial for land rights on Shadow and become embroiled in inter-Kindraa conflicts, the Ghost Bears restructured the production facility into a modular design and physically relocated the entire manufacturing line to their enclave on Strana Mechty. This innovative modular approach to production would prove to be one of the Viper's most significant, if unintended, legacies. When the Ghost Bears began their migration back to the Inner Sphere in the late 3050s, the modular factory technology developed for the Viper line allowed them to move several other manufacturing operations with relative ease.

Production on Strana Mechty continued under Ghost Bear control until the mid-3060s, when Clan Hell's Horses trialed for and won both production rights and the Upsilon Plant 2J facility. Their tenure was short-lived, however, as Clan Ice Hellion seized the entire plant in early 3068 following a grueling twelve-hour battle between both saKhans. The Ice Hellions immediately put the facility to use, with new configurations being shipped out as quickly as DropShips could be loaded, lending credence to rumors of a planned large-scale operation against their Coyote neighbors on Foster.

Beyond Strana Mechty, additional Viper production existed across the Homeworlds. Clan Coyote maintained a manufacturing line on Delios until 3071, when Clan Goliath Scorpion captured the facility during the opening stages of the Wars of Reaving. The Cloud Cobras operated their own production lines on Homer and at the Albion Armor Works on Albion. Clan Blood Spirit also maintained early production capacity at the Albion facility before the Star Adders assumed control. Following the Wars of Reaving and the destruction or Abjuration of several Clans, the surviving Home Clans continued to field the Viper as the similar Ice Ferret was phased out, possibly due to its association with the departed Spheroid Clans.

Having abandoned their Homeworld production infrastructure, the Ghost Bears, now reorganized as the Rasalhague Dominion, ultimately resumed Viper production at the newly established Dominion Facility Kappa-5 on Thule. This ensured the design remained a fixture within the Dominion's touman well into the Dark Age, where continued deployment in the Inner Sphere demonstrated that the Viper's combination of speed, mobility, and reconfiguration flexibility remained as tactically relevant as ever.
BMDragonfly_D.deployment: Designed to engage at multiple ranges, the Alternate Configuration D carries an LRM-5 for long-range harassment, two ER medium lasers and a Streak SRM-6 for medium-to-close engagement, and an ER small laser for point-blank defense. This mixed-range loadout provides greater tactical flexibility than most Viper configurations, allowing MechWarriors to adapt to changing battlefield conditions without sacrificing effectiveness at any particular range bracket.

When the Ghost Bears began their migration back to the Inner Sphere in the late 3050s, the modular factory technology developed for the Viper line allowed them to move several other manufacturing operations with relative ease.

Production on Strana Mechty continued under Ghost Bear control until the mid-3060s, when Clan Hell's Horses trialed for and won both production rights and the Upsilon Plant 2J facility. Their tenure was short-lived, however, as Clan Ice Hellion seized the entire plant in early 3068 following a grueling twelve-hour battle between both saKhans. The Ice Hellions immediately put the facility to use, with new configurations being shipped out as quickly as DropShips could be loaded, lending credence to rumors of a planned large-scale operation against their Coyote neighbors on Foster.

Beyond Strana Mechty, additional Viper production existed across the Homeworlds. Clan Coyote maintained a manufacturing line on Delios until 3071, when Clan Goliath Scorpion captured the facility during the opening stages of the Wars of Reaving. The Cloud Cobras operated their own production lines on Homer and at the Albion Armor Works on Albion. Clan Blood Spirit also maintained early production capacity at the Albion facility before the Star Adders assumed control. Having abandoned their Homeworld production infrastructure, the Ghost Bears, now reorganized as the Rasalhague Dominion, ultimately resumed Viper production at the newly established Dominion Facility Kappa-5 on Thule. This ensured the design remained a fixture within the Dominion's touman well into the Dark Age, where continued deployment in the Inner Sphere demonstrated that the Viper's combination of speed, mobility, and reconfiguration flexibility remained as tactically relevant as ever.
BMDragonfly_Prime.deployment: The primary configuration balances close-range striking power with defensive capability. A pair of medium pulse lasers and an SRM-4 launcher provide the main offensive punch, while twin machine guns offer anti-infantry suppression and an anti-missile system helps mitigate incoming missile fire. This well-rounded loadout makes this variant configuration a versatile scout and screening platform capable of handling a variety of short-range engagements.

BMDragonfly_U.overview: The Viper, known to Inner Sphere forces by its reporting name Dragonfly, is a 40-ton Clan OmniMech first produced in 2940 by Clan Fire Mandrill on the world of Shadow. Conceived as a quick-strike design emphasizing speed and agility over raw firepower, the Viper initially fell out of favor with several Fire Mandrill kindraa due to persistent problems with its omnipod mechanisms. In 3002, the Mandrills traded the design specifications and manufacturing facilities to Clan Ghost Bear in exchange for several production runs of Executioner OmniMechs. The Ghost Bears relocated production to Strana Mechty, developing modular production line technology in the process that would later prove invaluable during their migration to the Inner Sphere. Despite its troubled origins, the Viper has endured as one of the most widely distributed medium OmniMechs in the Clan arsenal, with production eventually spreading to multiple facilities across both the Homeworlds and the Inner Sphere.
BMDragonfly_U.capabilities:
Built on a lightweight Type W2 Endo-steel chassis and powered by a 320-rated XL engine, the Viper achieves a top speed of nearly 130 kilometers per hour, making it one of the fastest medium OmniMechs in any Clan touman. Eight jump jets provide an impressive 240-meter jump capability, granting exceptional tactical flexibility in broken or urban terrain. Seven tons of ferro-fibrous armor provide reasonable protection for its weight class, though the design remains vulnerable to concentrated fire from heavier opponents.

The Viper's primary limitation is its modest 8.5 tons of pod space, which significantly restricts its offensive payload compared to other medium OmniMechs in the 35-to-45-ton range such as the Adder, Shadow Cat, and Grendel. In its Prime configuration, the Viper mounts a pair of medium pulse lasers and an SRM-4 launcher for close-range engagements, supported by twin machine guns for anti-infantry work and an anti-missile system for defensive purposes. While considered undergunned for formal Clan dueling, the Viper excels in the fluid, indirect combat typical of Inner Sphere operations, where its speed allows it to choose engagements and screen for heavier formations.

BMDuanGung_D9G10.overview: The Duan Gung is a twenty-five-ton light fire support BattleMech introduced in 3058 by Shengli Arms on Victoria for the Capellan Confederation Armed Forces. The design traces its lineage to the Star League-era Sling BattleMech, which also served as a progenitor of the Clan Mist Lynx OmniMech. Named Duan Gung, meaning "Short Bow," the design was developed as part of the Capellan technological renaissance of the late 3050s, filling the light missile support role within the Confederation's military. One of the earliest fruits of the Xin Sheng movement's industrial revitalization, the Duan Gung demonstrated that the Confederation could once again produce competitive new BattleMech designs rather than relying solely on aging Star League-era platforms or foreign imports.
BMDuanGung_D9G10.capabilities:
Approaching speeds of one hundred and twenty kilometers per hour, the Duan Gung presents a minimal target while crossing the battlefield. Its Chilton 360 jump jets provide an impressive one hundred and eighty meters of jump capability, giving it mobility that rivals or exceeds other light BattleMechs in rough and broken terrain. Built on a weight-saving Chariot Type II endo steel chassis and powered by an Omni 175 XL engine, the design devotes its freed tonnage to armament rather than protection.

The primary weapon is a Zeus LRM-10 launcher, providing effective fire support at long range and indirect fire capability when operating as part of a reconnaissance or screening lance. Two Martell medium lasers deliver credible close-range firepower when enemies close the distance. This combination allows the Duan Gung to engage at range before transitioning to direct-fire combat as circumstances dictate.

The design's principal weakness is its thin armor profile. Four tons of Valiant Defco armor leave the Duan Gung vulnerable to concentrated fire, and the exposed XL engine means the loss of a single side torso is catastrophic. When employed as missile support for light or medium lances, however, the design performs admirably, using its speed and jump capability to maintain favorable engagement distances.
BMDuanGung_D9G10.history:
The Duan Gung emerged from Chancellor Sun-Tzu Liao's campaign to restore Capellan military industry during the Xin Sheng movement of the late 3050s. Shengli Arms on Victoria, one of the few Star League-era production facilities to survive the Succession Wars in Capellan space, was refurbished with assistance from technicians and material resources provided through the Confederation's growing ties with the Word of Blake. Engineers based the new design on Sling blueprints found in the facility's archives, and CCAF Strategic Director Talon Zahn shepherded the project through its development phase. A fully functioning prototype walked off the assembly line in late 3057, with limited production beginning the following year and full-scale manufacturing ramping up shortly thereafter.

Trial deployments with the Red Lancers and Warrior House Dai Da Chi validated the design's capabilities. Dai Da Chi was particularly impressed with how the Duan Gung complemented the Raven, the Confederation's primary scout 'Mech. In single-combat tests held in the Da-jiao-tang Mountains on Grand Base, the Duan Gung proved capable of defeating heavier opponents two or even three times its own weight by exploiting its mobility to strike from unexpected angles. In 3059, Chancellor Liao offered the design for sale to current Star League member states and units with ties to the original Star League Defense Force, broadening the Duan Gung's exposure beyond Capellan borders.

The Jihad devastated Shengli Arms when the Word of Blake-aligned Victoria Rangers turned against the factory in December 3068, inflicting crippling damage before being driven off by Sung's Rangers. The company suffered capital and personnel losses of eighty-four percent, though the Duan Gung production line was among the first restored to limited output. A stealth-armored variant emerged from this period of rebuilding as Shengli engineers incorporated the Confederation's latest technologies into the design.

The Victoria War brought further upheaval to the Duan Gung's production history. The Federated Suns briefly captured Victoria, and the retreating CCAF ultimately destroyed the Shengli Arms facility to prevent it from falling into enemy hands. Production continued, however, through Detroit Consolidated MechWorks on Detroit, where a former Stinger production line had been converted to manufacture the Duan Gung following the Capellan Confederation's absorption of that world. This ensured the design remained available to CCAF forces through the Dark Age and into the ilClan era.
BMDuanGung_D9G10.deployment: Introduced during the Jihad, this variant is a significant reconfiguration of the Duan Gung for a direct support role. The Zeus LRM-10 is replaced by a Ceres Arms light PPC, providing superior range and eliminating ammunition dependency. Hellespont Lite stealth armor replaces the standard Valiant Defco plating, supported by a Guardian ECM suite integrated into an enhanced Dian-bao communications system. A Diverse Optics ER small laser supplements the retained Martell medium lasers for anti-infantry work. This variant trades the original's missile support capability for enhanced survivability through reduced sensor signatures, making it well-suited for operating alongside other fast, stealthy Capellan designs.

BMEagle_EGL1M.overview:
The Eagle is Curtiss Militech's entry into the light BattleMech market, introduced in 3058 as a follow-up to their highly successful Wraith medium 'Mech. Designed primarily for the Free Worlds League, the Eagle was conceived as a balanced mix of firepower and mobility on a twenty-five-ton chassis, sacrificing the raw speed typical of its weight class in favor of heavier armament and a valuable target designation role.

The Eagle's practical approach to maintenance and logistics has made it attractive to provincial militia and second-line formations across the Free Worlds League, where reliable supply chains are valued as highly as raw combat performance.
BMEagle_EGL1M.capabilities:
Though not as fast as many 'Mechs in its weight class, the Eagle compensates with considerable firepower at extended ranges. The design mounts a Diverse Optics Sunbeam extended-range large laser as its primary weapon, capable of stripping significant armor from targets at distances exceeding five hundred meters. A Diverse Optics extended-range medium laser provides supplementary fire at closer ranges, giving the Eagle a credible damage output for a twenty-five-ton platform. The inclusion of a Forward-1 TAG laser designator adds a critical force-multiplier role, enabling the Eagle to call in accurate Arrow IV artillery strikes and semi-guided long-range missile fire from supporting units.

Built on a Curtiss Eagle endo steel chassis and powered by a Vlar 125 standard fusion engine, the Eagle achieves a top speed of 86 kilometers per hour with five CurtissJet 55 jump jets providing a hundred and fifty meters of jump capability. The standard engine reduces production costs and improves battlefield survivability compared to extralight alternatives, while simplifying field repair with more readily available replacement parts. Five tons of Kallon FWL armor provide respectable protection against other light 'Mechs, though the design remains vulnerable to concentrated fire from heavier opponents. The design philosophy clearly prioritizes sustained ranged engagement and target designation over the close-range skirmishing role typical of most light designs.
BMEagle_EGL1M.history:
The Eagle's development grew directly from Curtiss Militech's experience with the Wraith, as the company sought to leverage its reputation and manufacturing expertise into the light 'Mech market. The original design, designated EGL-1M, lacked the TAG system that would come to define the Eagle's battlefield role. When the League Central Coordination and Command introduced new semi-guided long-range missiles, Curtiss engineers recognized the opportunity for a fast, light 'Mech capable of designating targets for these munitions and added the TAG system to create the EGL-2M.

Initial sales validated Curtiss's market instincts. Both the Free Worlds League and Capellan Confederation placed substantial orders, with many units coming from formations already familiar with Curtiss-built 'Mechs through their experience with the Wraith. Within the League, various Marik Militia formations received the majority of Eagle shipments, followed by the Fusiliers of Oriente. Smaller numbers were exported to the Capellan Confederation, where the design found a niche in combined-arms formations that valued its target designation capabilities.

During the Jihad, the Eagle saw service across nearly every Marik province, primarily operating in its intended role as a close-in spotter for guided munitions and artillery. The disruption of normal military procurement channels during the conflict created uncertainty for continued production, though officers from both the Fusiliers of Oriente and Regulan Hussars were observed meeting with Curtiss executives on Paradise to secure future deliveries. The Jihad-era EGL-3M variant emerged during this period as Curtiss sought to market a less specialized version of the Eagle for general combat duties.

In the post-Jihad era, Curtiss Militech eventually exited the military market entirely, licensing the Eagle design to Graham-Davis Enterprises on Tamarind. Graham-Davis began production of the EGL-2M and EGL-3M sometime in the mid-3090s under the Duchy of Tamarind-Abbey, ensuring the Eagle's continued availability even as its original manufacturer departed from 'Mech production. The line subsequently passed back to Free Worlds League control as political boundaries shifted during the Dark Age.
BMEagle_EGL1M.deployment: This variant is the original Eagle design, predating the addition of the TAG system that became the hallmark of the EGL-2M. This variant replaces the TAG designator and extended-range medium laser with an anti-missile system backed by a ton of ammunition and an extended-range small laser, trading the force-multiplier role for improved self-defense against missile fire. Few EGL-1M models were produced, with most slated for the Capellan military and the remainder scattered across the Free Worlds League. The variant's scarcity reflects the rapid shift in doctrine toward the TAG-equipped EGL-2M once semi-guided munitions became widely available.

The design philosophy clearly prioritizes sustained ranged engagement and target designation over the close-range skirmishing role typical of most light designs.
BMEagle_EGL3M.history:
The Eagle's development grew directly from Curtiss Militech's experience with the Wraith, as the company sought to leverage its reputation and manufacturing expertise into the light 'Mech market. The original design, designated EGL-1M, lacked the TAG system that would come to define the Eagle's battlefield role. When the League Central Coordination and Command introduced new semi-guided long-range missiles, Curtiss engineers recognized the opportunity for a fast, light 'Mech capable of designating targets for these munitions and added the TAG system to create the EGL-2M.

Initial sales validated Curtiss's market instincts. Both the Free Worlds League and Capellan Confederation placed substantial orders, with many units coming from formations already familiar with Curtiss-built 'Mechs through their experience with the Wraith. Within the League, various Marik Militia formations received the majority of Eagle shipments, followed by the Fusiliers of Oriente. Smaller numbers were exported to the Capellan Confederation, where the design found a niche in combined-arms formations that valued its target designation capabilities.

During the Jihad, the Eagle saw service across nearly every Marik province, primarily operating in its intended role as a close-in spotter for guided munitions and artillery. The disruption of normal military procurement channels during the conflict created uncertainty for continued production, though officers from both the Fusiliers of Oriente and Regulan Hussars were observed meeting with Curtiss executives on Paradise to secure future deliveries. The Jihad-era EGL-3M variant emerged during this period as Curtiss sought to market a less specialized version of the Eagle for general combat duties.

In the post-Jihad era, Curtiss Militech eventually exited the military market entirely, licensing the Eagle design to Graham-Davis Enterprises on Tamarind. Graham-Davis began production of the EGL-2M and EGL-3M sometime in the mid-3090s under the Duchy of Tamarind-Abbey, ensuring the Eagle's continued availability even as its original manufacturer departed from 'Mech production. The line subsequently passed back to Free Worlds League control as political boundaries shifted during the Dark Age.
BMEagle_EGL3M.deployment: Introduced during the Jihad in 3076, this variant emerged from the growing demand across the Free Worlds League for general-purpose combat BattleMechs rather than specialized spotters. This variant replaces all of the EGL-2M's weaponry with a Fusigon light PPC in the left arm and a Diverse Optics medium variable-speed pulse laser in the right, trading the TAG capability and extended-range firepower for more versatile direct-combat armament. The adoption of a Vlar 125 XL engine frees tonnage for the new weapons systems and slightly improved armor distribution, though at the cost of reduced survivability if the engine is breached. Officers of both the Fusiliers of Oriente and Regulan Hussars showed early interest in this variant.

BMEbony_MEB10.overview: The Ebony is a covert operations light BattleMech first appearing in 3081 as a joint product of the Magistracy of Canopus and the Capellan Confederation. Named for the secretive Ebon Magistrate (the Magistracy Intelligence Ministry's ultra-elite covert operations branch) the 25-ton design emerged shrouded in mystery, with even its manufacturing origins initially unknown to foreign intelligence agencies. Jointly produced at Majesty Metals and Manufacturing on Canopus IV and Hellespont 'Mech Works on Sian, the Ebony was designed from the ground up as an intelligence-gathering and surgical strike platform. Leveraging advanced stealth technology and extraordinary speed, the design infiltrates enemy positions while remaining virtually invisible on sensors. Despite limited production numbers, the Ebony quickly established itself as a feared covert operator along the Capellan-Republic border.
BMEbony_MEB10.capabilities:
A massive Magna 250 extralight engine propels the 25-ton Ebony to a cruising speed of 108 kph, placing it among the fastest BattleMechs in production. When running hot enough to activate its triple-strength myomer, the design achieves sustained speeds exceeding 180 kph, making pursuit virtually impossible. The Ebony's sole weapon is a Ceres Arms Thrasher snub-nose PPC, providing highly accurate firepower to a range of 270 meters with maximum engagement out to 450 meters. The Majesty MLIX endo steel chassis keeps structural weight to a minimum, maximizing combat payload.

Five and a half tons of Hellespont Light Stealth armor, powered by an integrated Guardian ECM suite, renders the 'Mech extremely difficult to detect and target. The ECM system also disrupts hostile C3 networks and electronics across a substantial area. Ten double-strength heat sinks manage the thermal load from the stealth armor, PPC, and myomer systems, though activating TSM requires careful heat management by the MechWarrior. While the single weapon limits sustained firepower, the Ebony's combination of stealth, speed, and precision striking creates a formidable covert combatant that excels at hit-and-run operations.
BMEbony_MEB10.history:
The origins of the Ebony are inseparable from the shadowy Ebon Magistrate, the Magistracy of Canopus's ultra-elite covert operations branch that first surfaced shortly before the Jihad. While the Ebon Magistrate's activities remain largely shrouded in secrecy, its namesake 'Mech appeared in both the Magistracy Armed Forces and the Capellan Confederation Armed Forces beginning in 3081, confirming at minimum the existence of the organization.

The circumstances surrounding the Ebony's development remain an enigma. Canopus IV suffered significant damage during the Word of Blake occupation, which lasted until late 3075. Intelligence analysts debated how Majesty Metals could have constructed a new manufacturing line and repaired existing facilities within six years, even with substantial Capellan assistance. Various theories persist, ranging from hidden pre-war facilities on Canopus IV to primary construction occurring within the Confederation itself, with the use of Capellan stealth armor on a Magistracy design lending credence to the latter possibility.

On the Capellan front, intelligence services confirmed construction at Hellespont 'Mech Works on Sian but found deployment patterns considerably harder to track. The Ebony remained especially rare in most Warrior Houses during its early years of service. Significantly, the design was not spotted along the borders of Prefectures V and VI during the tense standoff between the Republic of the Sphere and the Confederation, fueling theories that Capellan forces were being marshaled for eventual military action to reclaim worlds lost during the Blakist occupation.

In the Magistracy, the Ebony found its way into elite formations including the Magistracy Royal Guard, Chasseurs á Cheval, and Canopian Fusiliers. McCarron's Armored Cavalry adopted both the MEB-9 and MEB-10 in reconnaissance lances, further cementing the design's role as a front-line intelligence asset. Within the Warrior Houses, deployment remained limited, with House Imarra receiving confirmed shipments while other surviving Houses were believed to be receiving units as production expanded.

As technology advanced through the Dark Age, the Ebony platform proved adaptable enough to incorporate new weapons systems. The MEB-12 field refit emerged around 3118, introducing TSEMP technology to the chassis, while the factory-produced MEB-13 of 3137 represented a more radical departure with re-engineered laser technology and heat-dissipating armor. These later variants demonstrated the continued relevance of the Ebony even as its role evolved from pure covert operations to broader light combat applications. Production continues at both original facilities, ensuring the design remains a fixture in Canopian and Capellan light 'Mech formations.
BMEbony_MEB10.deployment: Introduced in 3081, this Capellan-oriented modification replaces the snub-nose PPC with an ER large laser, extending effective engagement range considerably. A Capellan-styled dao sword mounted in the left arm provides a devastating melee capability, particularly lethal when combined with active triple-strength myomer. An additional half-ton of armor improves survivability, though these enhancements required exchanging the standard cockpit for a small model, creating somewhat cramped conditions for the pilot. McCarron's Armored Cavalry fields this variant alongside the base model in many of its reconnaissance lances.

A small cockpit creates the necessary internal volume for ammunition storage. The plasma rifle provides flexible tactical options, capable of generating significant heat buildup in enemy 'Mechs while also dealing conventional damage. Among the Warrior Houses, the only confirmed deployment is with the still-rebuilding House Imarra, though it is believed the Ebony is being shipped to all three surviving Houses.

BMEidolon_CEID001.overview:
The Eidolon was a fifty-five-ton medium BattleMech conceived during the final years of the Jihad as an improvised design assembled from surplus Celestial series OmniMech components. First appearing in December 3077, the design was produced by the Martinson Armaments facility on Liberty, built to serve as a broken terrain and urban combat spotter for Word of Blake conventional formations. A true FrankenMech in every sense, the Eidolon reflected the desperate improvisation of the crumbling Blakist Protectorate rather than any coherent long-term development program.

Never more than a stopgap measure, the Eidolon saw extremely limited production, with no more than a single example appearing at any given time. The design's significance ultimately lay not in its own battlefield record but in providing the foundation for the Capellan Confederation's Yao Lien program.
BMEidolon_CEID001.capabilities:
The Eidolon was designed as a broken terrain and urban combat spotter, leveraging improved jump jets to provide an impressive two-hundred-ten-meter jump capability that compensated for its relatively modest ground speed of eighty-six kilometers per hour. While slightly slower than many classic fifty-five-ton designs, the enhanced jump range gave it exceptional tactical mobility in cluttered urban environments and rough terrain.

The 'Mech's armament reflected its grab-bag construction philosophy, mounting a pair of Donal snub-nose PPCs as its sole weaponry. While limited in variety, these weapons provided respectable close-range firepower suitable for the urban engagements the Eidolon was intended to support. Ten tons of medium ferro-fibrous armor provided reasonable protection for a design in its weight class, while ten double heat sinks managed the thermal load of its particle projection cannons adequately. The reliance on surplus components also meant that field maintenance was a persistent challenge, as the hodgepodge of Celestial-derived parts created unique logistical demands that frontline technicians struggled to meet.

The Eidolon's most tactically significant feature was its improved C3 computer, which allowed it to share targeting data with other Blakist units in a network immune to electronic countermeasures. This C3i system made the Eidolon a valuable force multiplier despite its otherwise unremarkable weapons loadout, enabling it to serve as an effective spotter for heavier formations operating in broken terrain.
BMEidolon_CEID001.history:
The Eidolon's brief history is inextricably linked to the internal politics of the Word of Blake during the final years of the Jihad. By late 3077, the Blakist Protectorate was crumbling under the combined onslaught of Stone's Coalition forces, and Cameron St. Jamais recognized the urgent need for additional combat assets. The Celestial OmniMech program had produced more chassis than Apollyon's Manei Domini could crew, yet the cybernetic fanatic refused to release them to conventional formations. St. Jamais found his workaround through the Martinson Armaments facility on Liberty, secretly diverting excess Celestial components to construct a new design from leftover parts.

The Eidolon first appeared in December 3077, though it remained an exceedingly rare sight on the battlefield. Salvaged examples were nearly nonexistent outside Capellan hands, with most recovered units being stripped for parts rather than returned to service. Even before the Confederation began formal production of its successor, the CCAF had amassed the largest collection of salvaged Eidolons, though the design was still considered highly unusual.

The design's true legacy emerged during Operation SCOUR, when Free Worlds Task Force II landed on Liberty. The Capellan Confederation, having already discovered the existence of the hidden Martinson facility during the Jihad, dispatched Warrior House Imarra and supporting forces to secure the planet. After violent clashes with the Free Worlds League's Home Guard and a daring hot drop to seize the island outpost of Quantico, Capellan forces negotiated a ceasefire and later mediation of the planet's ownership.

When House Imarra eventually withdrew, they took with them the true prize: the dismantled remains of the Martinson factory and its BattleMech production lines, which had been hidden among the ruins of a former Star League Defense Force Marine base on Quantico. Capellan intelligence operatives successfully spirited the entire facility away before Coalition forces realized its significance, relocating the production equipment to Ceres Metals Industries on Capella, where the Eidolon would be reborn as the Yao Lien.
BMEidolon_CEID001.deployment: This variant is the sole production variant of the Eidolon, equipped with an improved C3 computer and a pair of Donal snub-nose PPCs. Produced in extremely limited numbers at the Martinson Armaments facility on Liberty, the variant was designed to serve as a networked spotter for conventional Blakist formations operating in broken terrain. The design's reliance on surplus Celestial components made each example essentially unique in its maintenance requirements, ensuring the Eidolon remained a rare and logistically demanding asset throughout its brief service life.

BMEisenfaust_EFT4J.overview:
The Eisenfaust (literally "iron fist" in German) is a forty-five-ton medium BattleMech that entered production during the Jihad, the successful realization of a concept that had eluded Lyran engineers since the earliest days of BattleMech production. Originally commissioned in 2469 as a medium-class siege engine, two separate prototype attempts over the following centuries failed to produce a viable design. It was not until Defiance Industries resurrected the concept with modern technologies that the Eisenfaust finally achieved the balance of firepower, protection, and mobility its designers had always envisioned.

Produced at the Defiance facility on Hesperus II beginning around 3076, the Eisenfaust serves as a capable defensive and urban combat platform for the Lyran Commonwealth. Its long and troubled development history has become a point of pride among Lyran engineers, who view the design as proof that persistence and technological progress can overcome even the most stubborn engineering challenges.
BMEisenfaust_EFT4J.capabilities:
The production Eisenfaust centers its firepower around a Defiance NovaShot Model 2 plasma rifle, a weapon that rivals particle projection cannons in raw damage potential while requiring no field inhibitors. Two tons of ammunition provide adequate supplies for extended engagements, and the weapon proves devastatingly effective against conventional infantry and battle armor formations. Supporting the plasma rifle at range, a Defiance Model 6 extended-range large laser allows the MechWarrior to conserve plasma ammunition for decisive moments.

Close-range defense relies on twin Defiance P5M medium pulse lasers and a Diverse Optics extended-range small laser, providing accurate fire against faster opponents attempting to exploit the Eisenfaust's modest top speed of sixty-four kilometers per hour. The adoption of the Edasich Motors 180 XL engine (the same powerplant mass-produced for the Hatchetman) proved critical to the design's viability, saving enough weight to mount fifteen double heat sinks that allow the Eisenfaust to fire its entire weapons suite without significant heat buildup. The Chariot Type II-B chassis and Durallex Medium armor provide solid protection for a forty-five-ton platform, though the reliance on an extralight engine means torso breaches carry catastrophic risk.
BMEisenfaust_EFT4J.history:
The Eisenfaust endured one of the longest and most troubled development histories of any BattleMech in Lyran service. The LCAF first commissioned a medium-class siege 'Mech in 2469, drawing on early experience with the Commando and Ymir. The Coventry Defense Conglomerate produced a single EFT-2 prototype in 2471 under the direction of engineer Ranomi Ndereba, but the machine's primitive engine could only manage a top speed of thirty-two kilometers per hour, and its thin armor left it hopelessly vulnerable to faster opponents. The LCAF quickly cancelled the project, though the concept continued to percolate through Lyran military planning circles for decades.

In 2512, the LCAF revisited the Eisenfaust concept using improved construction techniques. The resulting EFT-4J prototypes mounted fifty percent more armor and achieved significantly greater speed than the original, but extended combat trials with eight operational units proved that cheaper conventional tanks could still fill the siege role more effectively. The Eisenfaust project was shelved again, and the design rights were eventually transferred to Defiance Industries. The eight EFT-4J prototypes remained in service with the Coventry security garrison for several decades before being scrapped. Particularly, the Eisenfaust's original design concept would later see partial realization in the UrbanMech, which entered service roughly a century and a half later.

The Eisenfaust's resurrection came during the Jihad, when the revitalization of Lyran military production lines encouraged Defiance Industries to revisit previously abandoned designs. The availability of extralight engines, double heat sinks, and advanced weaponry transformed the Eisenfaust from a failed concept into a viable combat platform. After an expedited redesign and review process, the EFT-7X entered production at the Defiance facility on Hesperus II around 3076, making it one of the first new designs to reach Lyran forces in the wake of the Word of Blake's assault against the Lyran Alliance.

Initial production runs went primarily to the Seventh Donegal Guards, with smaller numbers distributed to Royal Guard and Lyrag Regulars formations. The Republic of the Sphere also exercised purchasing options for the design, acquiring Eisenfausts to fill defensive formations. As threats to Hesperus II mounted during the Dark Age (particularly from Clan Wolf and Clan Jade Falcon incursions in the 3140s) StarCorps Industries briefly produced the Eisenfaust under license at their Loburg facility to ensure continuity of supply.
BMEisenfaust_EFT4J.deployment: The second attempt at bringing the Eisenfaust concept to life, this variant emerged in 2515 using significantly improved construction techniques. The redesign achieved roughly fifty percent better armor protection and sixty percent greater top speed than the original EFT-2, addressing the most glaring deficiencies of the earlier prototype. Despite these improvements, extended combat trials with eight operational prototypes demonstrated that cheaper and more readily available conventional tanks could still fulfill the Eisenfaust's intended siege role more effectively. The design rights were sold to Defiance Industries, and the eight prototypes were relegated to the Coventry security garrison before eventually serving as testbed platforms for weapons and equipment configurations that would later inform the EFT-7X production model.
