Four fixed Pryzhok WM 10 jump jets grant the ability to clear one hundred twenty meters of terrain, giving the Executioner agility that belies its ninety-five-ton frame. This emphasis on speed comes at a cost, however, as the engine and mobility systems consume tonnage that might otherwise be devoted to armament, leaving only twenty-six and a half tons of pod space available for weapons and equipment.

Thirteen and a half tons of Arcadia Compound Delta VII ferro-fibrous armor provides adequate protection, though the coverage falls below average for the weight class. The Prime configuration exploits the chassis's mobility by mounting a Gauss rifle for long-range precision strikes alongside dual extended-range large lasers, with a pair of machine guns for anti-infantry work. This loadout favors open-field engagements where the Executioner can dictate range, though the design becomes vulnerable when cornered or facing opponents capable of matching its speed.

The spacious and reliable chassis supports an unusually diverse range of configurations, from energy-heavy brawlers to missile-heavy fire support platforms. While the Executioner carries less raw firepower than the lighter Warhawk, its superior mobility and jump capability make it a highly prized command OmniMech, with multiple Clans leveraging demand for the design as political currency.
BMGladiator_P.history:
The Executioner's origins trace to Clan Ghost Bear's acquisition of Clan Burrock's assault OmniMech schematics through a Trial sometime after the Ghost Bears began developing OmniMech technology in 2873. The ambitious initial plan called for merging the Burrock design with the planned Kodiak platform, creating a totem OmniMech embodying the Ghost Bear spirit. Over twenty prototype trials failed to integrate the MASC system with the hybrid chassis, and Ghost Bear scientists ultimately proposed splitting the effort into two separate platforms. The Clan Council approved, and the first Executioner rolled off the Arcadian production line within three years, entering service in 3001.

Ghost Bear warriors quickly proved the Executioner's worth on the Trial grounds, dominating early Trials of Possession. Clan Smoke Jaguar eventually claimed a Star's worth of the design, and over time every Clan gained access to at least a few examples. The Burrocks and Smoke Jaguars showed the greatest aptitude for developing new configurations, though Ghost Bear remained the sole large-scale producer. Production was centered at the Arcadia BattleMech Plant CM-T02 and later expanded to Alshain BattleWorx following the Clan Invasion, with the Albion Armor Works Alpha facility on Albion also contributing to the production run.

The Battle of Tukayyid in 3052 saw the development of the TC temporary configuration, an energy-focused variant born from ilKhan Ulric Kerensky's push for logistics-minded OmniMech loadouts. Clan Wolf deployed Executioner TCs as fast-response units harassing Com Guard supply lines, while Clan Ghost Bear's Alpha Galaxy used them as shock troopers during the fighting at Spanac and Luk. The TC proved so effective that it became a permanent standard configuration rather than a battlefield expedient, eventually influencing the development of the standardized F configuration.

Following the Wars of Reaving, the Home Clans withdrew the Executioner from service, possibly due to its strong association with the Spheroid Clans. Production still survived the Word of Blake Jihad intact, and the design remained a mainstay of the Rasalhague Dominion touman throughout the Dark Age. During the Second Combine-Dominion War, Ghost Bear Executioners led the assault on the Nova Cat capital of Irece, with Beta Galaxy's charge breaking through the Barcella-LAW manufacturing plant defenses. In the defense of Lambrecht in 3150, Fifth Bear Guards Executioners rallied after a surprise Draconis Combine combat drop to push the Third An Ting Legion from Middle Park and corner them among Castle Brian ruins on Brattanois.
BMGladiator_P.deployment: Alternate Configuration P combines a Hyper-Assault Gauss 30 and an LRM-10 rack for sustained long-range fire support with three heavy medium lasers for close-range defense. A plasma cannon rounds out the loadout, functioning as an oversized flamer that elevates target heat levels while proving devastating against infantry and light vehicles. The P configuration reflects the trend among newer Executioner loadouts toward incorporating HAG technology, offering a middle ground between the extreme HAG 40 of the J variant and the more conservative HAG 20 of the K.
BMGladiator_P.manufacturer: Bergan Industries - Alshain BattleWorx|Albion Armor Works Alpha|Arcadia BattleMech Plant CM-T02

BMGn_GN2O.overview: The Gùn is a twenty-ton light OmniMech introduced in 3134 by Ceres Metals Industries for the Capellan Confederation Armed Forces. Named for the gùn, one of the four traditional Chinese fighting weapons representing the staff, the design was conceived as a dedicated infantry support platform for garrison forces. As one of the lightest OmniMechs ever produced, the Gùn prioritizes tactical flexibility over raw combat power, earning a reputation as an indispensable asset for commanders tasked with holding territory against insurgents and light raiding forces. Production at Ceres facilities on both Capella and Lockton ensures a steady supply for CCAF and allied Magistracy formations throughout the Capellan March.
BMGn_GN2O.capabilities:
Built on a Ceresplex Light Omni endo steel frame powered by a Rawlings 100 fusion engine, the Gùn achieves a respectable top speed of 86 kilometers per hour. The use of a small cockpit and XL gyro frees critical tonnage, granting the chassis ten tons of pod space, an impressive allocation for a design weighing only twenty tons. This flexibility allows garrison commanders to rapidly reconfigure the Gùn based on developing threats, a significant advantage for defensive forces that must counter diverse enemy compositions with limited assets.

The trade-off for this adaptability is protection. Only three and a half tons of Ceres Standard armor shield the chassis, leaving MechWarriors dangerously exposed to anything heavier than small arms fire. The Gùn is emphatically not designed for stand-up engagements with conventional BattleMechs or heavy vehicles. Instead, it excels when operating alongside infantry and battle armor formations, using its speed and firepower to suppress enemy foot soldiers while its own supporting troops close to effective range.

The design's enhanced short-range targeting accuracy further reinforces this close-support doctrine, making the Gùn a lethal threat to infantry at the ranges where engagements against foot troops typically occur.
BMGn_GN2O.history:
The Gùn entered service with the Capellan Confederation Armed Forces in 3134, arriving just as Chancellor Daoshen Liao launched his invasion of the crumbling Republic of the Sphere. Ceres Metals Industries began production at their Capella facility first, with the Lockton plant bringing additional lines online to meet growing demand from both the CCAF and Magistracy Armed Forces.

The design's most notable early deployment came during the Capellan conquest of New Hessen in 3144. A lance of Gùns from the Second McCarron's Armored Cavalry was tasked with establishing a field outpost in a remote mining area following the planet's surrender. When local miners revolted against the new Capellan overseers, the Gùn lance, supported by a company of infantry and a platoon of Arrow IV assault vehicles, suppressed the uprising with devastating efficiency. The combined firepower of the Prime and alternate configurations left the rebel miners with nowhere to hide, with electronic warfare variants flushing insurgents from concealment while their lancemates delivered punishing fire. Two-thirds of the attacking force fell before the remainder scattered.

The Gùn has since seen deployment across CCAF garrison formations, the Magistracy Armed Forces, and the forces of Andurien. Despite years of cooperation between the CCAF and MAF, doctrinal differences remain visible in how each force employs the design. The Confederation primarily deploys the Gùn in support or garrison formations, pairing it with infantry and battle armor for perimeter defense. The MAF, by contrast, values the design as a frontline battle armor transport and combat unit.

Infantry commanders have learned to drill their forces to quickly identify the Gùn's active configuration, as its weapons loadout drastically changes the tactical calculus of any engagement. The presence of an electronic warfare variant in particular frequently indicates supporting artillery assets within range, a combination that has proven devastating to unprepared ground forces.
BMGn_GN2O.deployment: The primary configuration mounts a plasma rifle in the right arm supported by a pair of ER medium lasers, creating a devastating anti-infantry package. The plasma rifle's ability to generate crippling heat buildup in enemy 'Mechs while simultaneously devastating infantry formations makes it the ideal weapon for the Gùn's intended role. Two tons of ammunition provide adequate endurance for garrison patrol duties, though prolonged engagements can quickly exhaust these stores.

Garrison commanders favor this variant when operating in terrain that conceals enemy movement, pairing it with artillery assets for devastating combined-arms effect.

BMGoliath_GOL1H.overview: The Goliath is an eighty-ton quad assault BattleMech introduced in 2652 by Brigadier Corporation. Designed as a larger, more capable successor to the troubled Scorpion, the Goliath overcame the engineering challenges that had plagued earlier four-legged designs to become a quality fire-support platform. Despite its proven performance, the Goliath struggled to find buyers during the Star League era, as the stigma of earlier quad designs made it a hard sell to procurement officers accustomed to bipedal chassis. Production remained limited for over a century before the design earned renewed respect, with multiple manufacturers producing updated variants from the late 3060s onward.
BMGoliath_GOL1H.capabilities:
The Goliath is a steady fire-support unit, with a PPC and dual LRM racks providing good ranged firepower. At 64 kph, it can keep up with heavy units and some lighter 'Mechs, while almost fifteen tons of armor let it take quite a beating. One of the strongest points of the Goliath is the number of heat sinks that allows it to keep up almost a constant rate of fire. Up close, the Goliath suffers. Dual machine guns might be good at fending off infantry, but against armored units they are almost useless, while the long-ranged weaponry is inaccurate.

The quad chassis provides superior stability when firing on the move, reducing the accuracy penalties that plague bipedal designs traversing rough terrain. This makes the Goliath an exceptional platform for sustained bombardment from elevated positions, where its wide stance keeps the weapons array level even on uneven ground. However, the quad layout limits the design's ability to mount arm-based weapons, forcing engineers to concentrate firepower in the torso and head locations. The lack of hands also means the Goliath cannot engage in melee combat or manipulate objects, a significant limitation during urban operations where versatility is prized.
BMGoliath_GOL1H.history:
Brigadier Corporation developed the Goliath in 2652 as the second of their quad BattleMech designs, building on lessons learned from the unsuccessful Scorpion and the Xanthos. While the Scorpion was not a good design, it also had to contend with the fundamental challenges of a four-legged chassis. By learning from their failures, Brigadier's engineers were not only able to overcome many of the problems that the Scorpion suffered from but also to produce a quality design. The questionable reputation of the Scorpion made the Goliath a hard sell, however, and the Star League passed on the design. After over a century of good but limited service in the Periphery and House armies, the League inquired about purchasing some Goliaths, but the deal fell through as the Amaris Coup and the dissolution of the Star League occurred.

The Goliath weighs in at 80 tons, allowing it to carry a much heavier weapons payload and armor than the Scorpion at the cost of mobility. Very few Goliaths remain from the original production run, and most of those are split between Lyran units and the Free Worlds League. The Lyran Commonwealth put a priority on maintaining their Goliaths while Corean manufactures a few new Goliaths each year. Defiance Industries makes spare parts for the Goliath and has discussed manufacturing it, but held out for an upgraded design before beginning production.

Despite the rarity of the 'Mech, it has been involved in many important battles. In a 2901 battle for Sirius, a Marik Goliath was the centerpiece in their attack on a Liao position, disabling a BattleMaster and a pair of Shadow Hawks and pushing the Capellan line back forty kilometers. During the Fourth Succession War, Captain Andrew Redburn's Delta Company annihilated the Fifth Capellan Chargers - 'Cochraine's Goliaths' - on St. Andre.

In the late 3060s the Goliath saw renewed production and renewed popularity and has since become a powerful and respected assault 'Mech. In 3143, the Corean Enterprises - MacAdams-Suharno plant on Stewart was captured by Clan Wolf, and its GOL-6M variant production line was converted to produce a Clan version of the 'Mech.
BMGoliath_GOL1H.deployment: This variant is the original production model of the Goliath, serving as the baseline configuration from which all subsequent variants evolved. Introduced in 2652, the 1H saw service primarily with Periphery and House armies during the Star League era and throughout the Succession Wars. Lyran Commonwealth and Free Worlds League units maintained the largest concentrations, with commanders valuing the design's steady fire-support capabilities and the stability afforded by its quad chassis.

While the Scorpion was not a good design, it also had to contend with the fundamental challenges of a four-legged chassis. By learning from their failures, Brigadier's engineers were not only able to overcome many of the problems that the Scorpion suffered from but also to produce a quality design. The questionable reputation of the Scorpion made the Goliath a hard sell, however, and the Star League passed on the design. After over a century of good but limited service in the Periphery and House armies, the League inquired about purchasing some Goliaths, but the deal fell through as the Amaris Coup and the dissolution of the Star League occurred.

The Goliath weighs in at 80 tons, allowing it to carry a much heavier weapons payload and armor than the Scorpion at the cost of mobility. Very few Goliaths remain from the original production run, and most of those are split between Lyran units and the Free Worlds League. The Lyran Commonwealth put a priority on maintaining their Goliaths while Corean manufactures a few new Goliaths each year. Defiance Industries makes spare parts for the Goliath and has discussed manufacturing it, but held out for an upgraded design before beginning production.

Despite the rarity of the 'Mech, it has been involved in many important battles. In a 2901 battle for Sirius, a Marik Goliath was the centerpiece in their attack on a Liao position, disabling a BattleMaster and a pair of Shadow Hawks and pushing the Capellan line back forty kilometers. During the Fourth Succession War, Captain Andrew Redburn's Delta Company annihilated the Fifth Capellan Chargers - 'Cochraine's Goliaths' - on St. Andre.

In the late 3060s the Goliath saw renewed production and renewed popularity and has since become a powerful and respected assault 'Mech. In 3143, the Corean Enterprises - MacAdams-Suharno plant on Stewart was captured by Clan Wolf, and its GOL-6M variant production line was converted to produce a Clan version of the 'Mech.
BMGoliath_GOL2H.deployment: The 3067 2H is a Periphery upgrade of the 1H model. The 'Mech removes the Machine Guns from the chassis and adds in their place six Rocket Launcher 10s. This gives the Goliath a very powerful close range punch. The upgrade also adds Ferro-Fibrous armor for improved protection without additional weight.

BMGoliath_GOL3L.overview: The Goliath is an eighty-ton quad assault BattleMech introduced in 2652 by Brigadier Corporation. Designed as a larger, more capable successor to the troubled Scorpion, the Goliath overcame the engineering challenges that had plagued earlier four-legged designs to become a quality fire-support platform. Despite its proven performance, the Goliath struggled to find buyers during the Star League era, as the stigma of earlier quad designs made it a hard sell to procurement officers accustomed to bipedal chassis. Production remained limited for over a century before the design earned renewed respect, with multiple manufacturers producing updated variants from the late 3060s onward.
BMGoliath_GOL3L.capabilities:
The Goliath is a steady fire-support unit, with a PPC and dual LRM racks providing good ranged firepower. At 64 kph, it can keep up with heavy units and some lighter 'Mechs, while almost fifteen tons of armor let it take quite a beating. One of the strongest points of the Goliath is the number of heat sinks that allows it to keep up almost a constant rate of fire. Up close, the Goliath suffers. Dual machine guns might be good at fending off infantry, but against armored units they are almost useless, while the long-ranged weaponry is inaccurate.

The quad chassis provides superior stability when firing on the move, reducing the accuracy penalties that plague bipedal designs traversing rough terrain. This makes the Goliath an exceptional platform for sustained bombardment from elevated positions, where its wide stance keeps the weapons array level even on uneven ground. However, the quad layout limits the design's ability to mount arm-based weapons, forcing engineers to concentrate firepower in the torso and head locations. The lack of hands also means the Goliath cannot engage in melee combat or manipulate objects, a significant limitation during urban operations where versatility is prized.

Though the ammo in the side torso is protected by CASE, the ammo in the center torso is not.

For longer-range engagements, the Goliath carries an LRM-10 launcher with an Artemis IV fire control system as well as an ER Large Laser.

Additionally, the 'Mech has a Small Cockpit that is cramped and makes the 'Mech harder to pilot but saves valuable weight. The 'Mech also has an Improved C3 computer, allowing it to share targeting telemetry with similarly equipped units.

The Compact Gyro and standard 240 engine reduce speed but free tonnage for the turret system. Anyone marking the 6M as easy to flank is in for a surprise.

BMGoshawkII.overview: The Goshawk II is a forty-five-ton Clan medium BattleMech developed by Clan Snow Raven in the mid-3080s, drawing inspiration from the heavier Vapor Eagle that the Ravens had long operated. Produced at Snow Raven Industrial Complex Alpha on the Inner Sphere world of Dante, the Goshawk II was designed specifically as a second-line combat platform for exclusive use by Raven Alliance forces. Ten tons lighter than its progenitor, the Goshawk II compensates with significantly greater speed and agility, incorporating an ECM suite to counter the increasingly sophisticated electronic warfare capabilities encountered in Inner Sphere service. Clan Sea Fox later began producing their own variant at facilities in the Chain Cluster, expanding the design's availability beyond its original Raven Alliance exclusivity.
BMGoshawkII.capabilities:
Built on a weight-saving GS-2E endo steel chassis, the Goshawk II mounts a 315-rated extralight fusion engine that pushes the forty-five-ton 'Mech to an impressive 118.8 km/h, substantially faster than the Vapor Eagle it descends from. Seven jump jets provide an equally impressive leap capability of two hundred and ten meters, exceeding even its larger ancestor's mobility. Nine tons of standard armor offer adequate protection for a design intended to operate at high speed, and an integral ECM suite helps neutralize the electronic warfare advantages that Inner Sphere opponents increasingly bring to the battlefield.

The Goshawk II's armament centers on a right-arm ER large laser as its sole long-range weapon, capable of engaging targets at significant distances with precision. Close-range firepower comes from a pair of small pulse lasers and six micro pulse lasers distributed across the arms and head, all guided by a targeting computer that maximizes their effectiveness. This energy-only configuration eliminates ammunition dependency, granting extended operational endurance well suited to the Raven Alliance's expeditionary doctrine. The design excels in high-speed slashing attacks, closing rapidly to deliver precise fire before withdrawing beyond effective retaliation range.
BMGoshawkII.history:
The Goshawk II's development reflects Clan Snow Raven's pragmatic approach to rebuilding their military strength following their relocation to the Outworlds Alliance. Having operated the larger Vapor Eagle since before the Clan Invasion, Raven engineers leveraged their deep familiarity with the design to produce a lighter, faster derivative better suited to their new operational reality as a Clan operating within the Inner Sphere. Production began at Snow Raven Industrial Complex Alpha on Dante in 3086, with the design designated exclusively for Raven second-line formations.

The Ravens' close commercial relationship with Clan Sea Fox eventually brought the design to wider distribution. Sea Fox merchants, recognizing the Goshawk II's export potential, began manufacturing their own variant at Manufacturing Plant SFF-AL1 on Alnabog in the Chain Cluster. This Sea Fox-produced Goshawk II 4 incorporated more advanced technology including an XXL engine, and was marketed to various buyers including the Republic of the Sphere.

The Republic's acquisition of Sea Fox-built Goshawk IIs led directly to the experimental RISC variant. In 3136, the Republic Institute of Strategic Combat at their Sandhurst proving grounds on Terra attempted to install an experimental emergency coolant system into the platform. The project yielded only four converted test units before disastrous field trials ended the program. Three of four test units were destroyed within three months, including two from catastrophic coolant system failures that went undetected due to falsely reassuring temperature readouts. RISC shelved the project permanently, and Sea Fox component codes found on recovered wreckage successfully deflected media scrutiny away from the Republic's covert involvement.
BMGoshawkII.deployment: The standard Goshawk II serves as the backbone of Raven Alliance second-line formations, combining exceptional speed and jump capability with an ECM suite that provides a significant electronic warfare advantage over most opponents. Its array of micro and small pulse lasers guided by a targeting computer makes it highly effective in close-range engagements, while the ER large laser provides a credible ranged threat. The design's improved life support systems and nimble jump characteristics reflect its origins as a platform intended for extended operations in demanding environmental conditions.

BMGoshawk_3.overview: The Vapor Eagle, known to Inner Sphere intelligence services by its reporting name Goshawk, is a fifty-five-ton Clan medium BattleMech introduced in 2863 by Clan Steel Viper. Designed principally as a dueling platform rather than a line combat unit, the Vapor Eagle was built to excel in the one-on-one Trials so prevalent in Clan warrior culture. Its distinctive arm baffles, which lend the design its Inner Sphere codename, serve a functional role in stabilizing jump jet flight rather than merely deflecting exhaust. First appearing in the Inner Sphere with Steel Viper forces during the Clan Invasion, ComStar operatives initially struggled to understand the close-combat garrison 'Mech's intended purpose until Clan society became better understood. Production of the Vapor Eagle has been maintained across multiple Clan Homeworld factories and, following the relocation of Clan Snow Raven to the Inner Sphere, at facilities in the Raven Alliance.
BMGoshawk_3.capabilities:
The Vapor Eagle's chassis mounts a 330-rated extralight fusion engine driving the fifty-five-ton 'Mech to speeds of 97.2 km/h, while six jump jets provide a leap capability of one hundred and eighty meters. Built on an endo steel frame and clad in nine tons of ferro-fibrous armor, the design achieves an impressive balance of protection, speed, and firepower for its weight class. The most distinctive feature of the Vapor Eagle is its large arm baffles, reminiscent of the venerable Griffin's blast deflectors but functioning as stabilizing wings. By diverting thrust from the torso-mounted jump jets over their surfaces, these baffles grant the Vapor Eagle exceptionally smooth and controllable jump flight, allowing precision landings that few 'Mechs of comparable mass can match.

The standard weapons configuration emphasizes devastating close-range firepower suitable for formal dueling. A large pulse laser serves as the primary weapon in the right arm, supported by three medium pulse lasers split between the side torsos and a quartet of machine guns. Two Streak SRM-2 launchers round out the armament, while a targeting computer enhances the accuracy of the entire loadout. This configuration makes the Vapor Eagle lethal within its engagement envelope, though it lacks any meaningful long-range capability, leaving it vulnerable to opponents who can dictate engagement distances.
BMGoshawk_3.history:
The Vapor Eagle originated with Clan Steel Viper as a dedicated dueling design, seeing its earliest service in the garrison formations that defended Viper holdings across the Clan Homeworlds. Produced primarily at New Kent Armorworks on New Kent and at facilities on Hellgate, the design became a staple of Steel Viper second-line forces throughout the Golden Century and into the Political Century. Additional production was established by Clan Ice Hellion on Hector and Clan Goliath Scorpion on Roche, giving the Vapor Eagle a broad manufacturing base among the Homeworld Clans.

When Clan Steel Viper seized the Hellgate enclave from Clan Snow Raven in 2899, the conquest brought the facility under Viper control. Ironically, the Snow Ravens' long familiarity with the design from their time on Hellgate would later enable them to establish their own production. The Vapor Eagle saw little notice from the Inner Sphere until the Clan Invasion, where Steel Viper garrison forces brought it to the Occupation Zones. ComStar operatives puzzled over the close-range dueling 'Mech until Clan culture became better understood.

The Hegira War proved a turning point for the design. After Clan Jade Falcon ejected the Steel Vipers from the Inner Sphere, Viper leadership undertook a broad reconfiguration program to produce variants better suited to larger, more fluid engagements. These updated models filled gaps in frontline formations during the Vipers' campaigns against Clans Snow Raven and Star Adder in the Homeworlds. The progression to increasingly heavy ballistic armament in later Clan refits of the Vapor Eagle has drawn comparisons to similar trends in Phoenix Hawk lineage designs, casting the Vapor Eagle as a conceptual bridge between upgraded SLDF chassis and the monstrously upsized Phoenix Hawk IIC.

The Wars of Reaving devastated many Homeworld Clans, and the destruction of Clan Steel Viper scattered surviving production among successor factions including Clan Coyote and the remnants of other Homeworld powers. The New Kent facilities fell silent as the Steel Vipers were annihilated, while factories on Hector and Roche passed through Goliath Scorpion and eventually Coyote control. Meanwhile, Clan Snow Raven's relocation to the Outworlds Alliance saw the design take on new life, with Snow Raven Industrial Complex Alpha on Dante establishing production for the Raven Alliance military. Salvaged Viper-made Vapor Eagles also appeared in Jade Falcon garrisons and on Solaris VII's arena circuit, where the design's dueling pedigree found an appreciative audience among holovid broadcasters. In the Dark Age, reports surfaced of rare Vapor Eagle variants appearing on contested worlds near the Fortress Republic, with structural analysis suggesting custom refits of older Steel Viper airframes connected to forces behind the Fortress Wall.
BMGoshawk_3.deployment: Developed by Clan Steel Viper scientists in response to the changing nature of Clan warfare following contact with the Inner Sphere, the Vapor Eagle 3 is a complete weapons overhaul while retaining the proven chassis. An extended-range PPC provides the long-range striking power the original design sorely lacked, supported by an ATM-3 launcher that offers tactical flexibility despite being limited to a single ton of ammunition. Three heavy medium lasers deliver punishing close-range firepower, while a pair of standard SRM-2 launchers add further damage potential. This variant filled an increasingly critical role in Steel Viper frontline formations during their campaigns in the Homeworlds prior to the Wars of Reaving.

BMGrandCrusaderII_GRND03.overview: The Grand Crusader II is an 80-ton assault BattleMech that is a comprehensive redesign of the original Grand Crusader, developed on Terra during the Word of Blake's occupation. Commissioned in 3065 by Precentor Martial Cameron St. Jamais as part of a broader effort to streamline Terra's manufacturing capacity, the redesign leveraged shared components with other Blakist assault platforms to accelerate production. The first Grand Crusader II rolled off the line in early March 3066, and the redesign so thoroughly altered the 'Mech's armor profile and appearance that it was designated as a distinct chassis from its predecessor. The Grand Crusader II represented a marked improvement in survivability and mobility over the original design.
BMGrandCrusaderII_GRND03.capabilities:
The Grand Crusader II addresses the two most significant criticisms of the original design: limited long-range firepower and the vulnerability inherent in its XL engine. Engineers replaced the Hermes 240 XL with a Pitban 320 Light Fusion engine, dramatically improving survivability while simultaneously increasing the 'Mech's top speed to 64 kilometers per hour. The incorporation of triple-strength myomer further enhances ground speed to over 86 kilometers per hour when the 'Mech runs hot, giving the Grand Crusader II a burst mobility unusual for an assault platform. Four CurtissJet 80 jump jets provide additional tactical flexibility, allowing the design to navigate terrain that would stymie its predecessor.

Built on a Skobel Template 8 Endo Steel chassis and protected by fifteen tons of Aldis Plate armor with CASE, the Grand Crusader II trades the original's missile-heavy loadout for a more balanced direct-fire arsenal. An improved C3 computer allows the design to share targeting data with lance mates, strengthening Level II coordination and fire control. The streamlined production process, sharing components with other Blakist assault designs, gave the Grand Crusader II an ease of maintenance that its predecessor lacked, though the 'Mech's stable firing platform and improved survivability are what most distinguish it from the original Grand Crusader.

BMGrandCrusaderII_GRND03.history:
The Grand Crusader II emerged directly from the Word of Blake's aggressive military expansion on Terra following Operation Odysseus. With Cameron St. Jamais driving production quotas beyond what Terra's factories could sustain, the involvement of Vicore Industries proved critical to both increasing output and improving the design. The shared component philosophy with the Vanquisher and Legacy programs enabled rapid manufacturing ramp-up across Skobel MechWorks and Krupp Armament Works facilities in Russia and Germany.

All Blakist divisions received the Grand Crusader II as it entered production, with older Grand Crusader models being rotated out of frontline service. The 'Mech saw extensive action throughout the Jihad, serving in garrison and offensive operations across the Word of Blake Protectorate. The Grand Crusader II's improved survivability compared to the XL-engine original proved its worth in the brutal close-quarters fighting that characterized much of the conflict.

Following the Coalition's liberation of Terra and the destruction of the Word of Blake, both Skobel MechWorks and Krupp Armament Works fell under Republic of the Sphere control. While the factories themselves survived the Jihad, production of the Grand Crusader II appears to have been discontinued, with the Republic showing little interest in perpetuating Blakist designs. The schematics for a proposed Grand Crusader OmniMech, which the Word of Blake had been developing before the Jihad erupted, were never completed and the project was abandoned in favor of the Celestial series. However, copies of these incomplete plans would later surface in unexpected hands, ultimately giving rise to the Scorpion Empire's Star Crusader.
BMGrandCrusaderII_GRND03.deployment: This variant introduces the Pitban 320 Light Fusion engine, triple-strength myomer, and CurtissJet 80 jump jets that define the Grand Crusader II platform. Armed with two extended-range large lasers as primary weapons, the variant supplements its direct-fire capability with an LRM-15 launcher equipped with Artemis IV fire control and a Streak SRM-6 for close-range engagements. Three extended-range medium lasers round out the weapons array. The incorporation of an improved C3 computer allows this variant to function as a networked fire-support node, sharing targeting data with lance mates to improve overall formation accuracy.

The shared component philosophy with the Vanquisher and Legacy programs enabled rapid manufacturing ramp-up across Skobel MechWorks and Krupp Armament Works facilities in Russia and Germany.

All Blakist divisions received the Grand Crusader II as it entered production, with older Grand Crusader models being rotated out of frontline service. The 'Mech saw extensive action throughout the Jihad, serving in garrison and offensive operations across the Word of Blake Protectorate. The Grand Crusader II's improved survivability compared to the XL-engine original proved its worth in the brutal close-quarters fighting that characterized much of the conflict.

Following the Coalition's liberation of Terra and the destruction of the Word of Blake, both Skobel MechWorks and Krupp Armament Works fell under Republic of the Sphere control. While the factories themselves survived the Jihad, production of the Grand Crusader II appears to have been discontinued, with the Republic showing little interest in perpetuating Blakist designs. The schematics for a proposed Grand Crusader OmniMech, which the Word of Blake had been developing before the Jihad erupted, were never completed and the project was abandoned in favor of the Celestial series. However, copies of these incomplete plans would later surface in unexpected hands, ultimately giving rise to the Scorpion Empire's Star Crusader.
BMGrandCrusaderII_GRND04.deployment: This variant reconfigures the Grand Crusader II as a dedicated long-range sniper platform, mounting a Krupp Strumfurer light Gauss rifle as its primary weapon for extreme-range engagement. A Blankenburg extended-range particle projection cannon adds devastating energy firepower at long range, while two Diverse Optics Sunbeam extended-range medium lasers and a Guided Technologies 2nd Gen Streak SRM-6 provide credible close-range defense. Like the GRN-D-03, this variant carries an improved C3 computer for networked targeting, and its Aldis Plate armor includes CASE to protect against ammunition explosions. The GRN-D-04's radically altered armor profile gave the Grand Crusader II a distinctly different silhouette from its predecessor, abandoning the barrel-chested look for a more streamlined appearance influenced by the Legacy.

BMGrandCrusader_GRND01.overview: The Grand Crusader is an 80-ton assault BattleMech commissioned in 3052 by Word of Blake Precentor Martial Trent Arian following the schism with ComStar. Named for a passage in the writings of Jerome Blake extolling those who fight to preserve technology and knowledge, the design is unrelated to the venerable Crusader despite frequent confusion caused by its name. Produced by Gibson Federated BattleMechs on Gibson, the Grand Crusader was developed to address the fledgling Word of Blake Militia's acute shortage of BattleMech assets after their flight to the Free Worlds League. The first examples reached the Blakist First Division in 3053, quickly becoming a signature design of the Word of Blake's early military buildup.
BMGrandCrusader_GRND01.capabilities:
Built around a weight-saving Crucis-ES Endo Steel chassis and a Hermes 240 XL engine, the Grand Crusader trades speed for devastating firepower. Its top speed of only 54 kilometers per hour makes it one of the slower assault designs of its era, but the tonnage freed by its lightweight internal structure allows it to carry an impressive weapons array and over fifteen tons of Maximillian 45 armor protection. The distinctive barrel-chested profile, reminiscent of designs like the Awesome and Mackie, houses twin Holly LRM-20 launchers fed from six tons of ammunition and linked to Artemis IV fire control systems for enhanced accuracy. These missile racks deploy from innovative slide-up housings on the 'Mech's back, granting superior firing arcs.

For engagements at medium range, two Tronel PPL-20 large pulse lasers provide accurate and punishing firepower, while a pair of Intek medium pulse lasers handle close-range threats. An LFN Lindblad Shotgun anti-missile system mounted atop the cockpit provides limited defense against incoming missiles, though its elevated placement creates blind spots along the lower legs and rear arc that leave the Grand Crusader vulnerable to battle armor attacks. The Word of Blake accepted this limitation, confident that years would pass before their forces encountered Clan Elementals in significant numbers.
BMGrandCrusader_GRND01.history:
The Grand Crusader's origins lie in the tumultuous aftermath of the ComStar Schism. When Trent Arian assumed command of the newly formed Word of Blake Militia in 3052, the organization possessed very few BattleMechs, as most Com Guard MechWarriors who defected to the Word were unable to bring their machines with them. Arian negotiated directly with Gibson Federated BattleMechs to produce the Grand Crusader, underwriting production costs and permitting open-market sales to offset expenses. Despite this arrangement, the Blakists acquired virtually every unit produced, making it a signature design of their early military buildup.

The Grand Crusader saw steady production throughout the late Clan Invasion and Civil War eras, with Gibson Federated BattleMechs serving as the sole manufacturer. The design earned a reputation as a capable fire-support platform, though its association with the Word of Blake also gave it a stigma that discouraged widespread adoption by other factions. The few examples that reached FWLM commands were generally viewed with a mixture of respect for their firepower and suspicion of their origins.

Following the Blakist seizure of Terra during Operation Odysseus, the Grand Crusader program underwent a dramatic transformation under Precentor Martial Cameron St. Jamais. Seeking to expand Militia capabilities, St. Jamais enlisted Vicore Industries to streamline production across Terra's manufacturing base. This effort produced the Grand Crusader II, a comprehensive redesign manufactured by Skobel MechWorks and Krupp Armament Works beginning in 3066. The original Grand Crusader also served as the foundation for the Word of Blake's early OmniMech research, though that project was ultimately shelved in favor of the Celestial series. With the fall of the Word of Blake during the Jihad, surviving Grand Crusaders became rare trophies scattered across the Inner Sphere, their presence raising suspicion wherever they appeared due to their unmistakable Blakist heritage.
BMGrandCrusader_GRND01.deployment: The original production model of the Grand Crusader entered service in 3053, built around the Hermes 240 XL engine that gives the design its characteristic slow but heavily armed profile. Optimized as a combined-arms fire-support platform, this variant pairs twin LRM-20 launchers with Artemis IV fire control for long-range bombardment, supported by large and medium pulse lasers for medium-range engagements. The anti-missile system provides some protection against return fire. This variant formed the backbone of Word of Blake assault lances throughout the Clan Invasion and Civil War eras, with virtually all production allocated to Blakist formations.
BMGrandCrusader_GRND01.manufacturer: Gibson Federated BattleMechs (A Division of Free Worlds Defense Industries)

BMGrandDragon_DRG10K.overview:
The Grand Dragon emerged from Luthien Armor Works' efforts to modernize the venerable Dragon chassis using newly recovered Star League technology. What began as a simple field modification replacing the autocannon with a particle projection cannon evolved into a full production model by 3040. Over the following fifteen years, LAW systematically converted Dragon production lines at Luthien, Dieron, Saffel, and Yorii to Grand Dragon manufacture, completely phasing out the original by 3055.

The Grand Dragon represented the Combine's technological renaissance following the recovery of the Helm Memory Core. The design maintained the Dragon's characteristic speed and versatility while incorporating significant improvements. Production continued until the Word of Blake's devastating 3068 attacks on LAW facilities, though rapid establishment of new factories ensured the Grand Dragon's continued service.
BMGrandDragon_DRG10K.capabilities:
The Grand Dragon's combat effectiveness stems from its successful integration of advanced technology without sacrificing the original Dragon's core strengths. The Hermes 360 XL engine pushes the sixty-ton chassis to a maximum speed of 97 kilometers per hour, making it one of the faster heavy 'Mechs in DCMS service. This mobility combines with the Lord's Light 2 Extended-Range PPC to create a highly effective skirmisher capable of dictating engagement ranges. The Telos DecaCluster LRM-10 provides supplementary firepower, while three Victory 23R medium lasers handle close defense.

Thirteen double heat sinks manage the thermal load efficiently, allowing sustained fire with the primary weapons. CASE-protected ammunition storage demonstrates LAW's attention to survivability. The enhanced hip and torso assembly developed at Nykvarn increased torso rotation from 250 degrees to nearly 300 degrees, substantially improving the 'Mech's ability to engage targets across wider firing arcs. This modification became standard on all Grand Dragons produced after the Jihad. However, the XL engine that enables the Grand Dragon's impressive speed also serves as a significant vulnerability, as penetrating damage to either torso section can disable the 'Mech entirely.
BMGrandDragon_DRG10K.history:
The Grand Dragon's development traces back to the waning years of the Fourth Succession War, when DCMS commanders began experimenting with field modifications to their Dragon 'Mechs. The most successful of these swapped the autocannon for a particle projection cannon, creating what would become the DRG-1G configuration. Initial reception proved enthusiastic enough that LAW formalized the design for production in 3040.

Acceptance within the DCMS came rapidly as the Grand Dragon reached line units throughout the 3040s and 3050s. The 'Mech's effective combination of speed, firepower, and heat management made it popular with MechWarriors who appreciated its versatility. Nearly every DCMS line unit eventually fielded a company of Dragons or Grand Dragons. The Grand Dragon also saw extensive use during the Clan Invasion, where its mobility proved valuable against technologically superior Clan opponents.

The Jihad brought severe disruption when Word of Blake forces struck LAW's primary facilities between 3068 and 3070. LAW's resilience proved equal to the challenge, as the company established new manufacturing capacity within two years. The Nykvarn facility earned the honor of restarting Grand Dragon production, followed by rebuilt facilities on Abiy Adi and Savinsville. Post-Jihad variants continued the chassis's evolution, incorporating C3 networks, improved missiles, and eventually Clan-grade technology.
BMGrandDragon_DRG10K.deployment: A thirty-second century derivative of the DRG-7K, this variant incorporates Anti-Penetrative Ablation armor to maintain the Grand Dragon's battlefield relevance against increasingly powerful weaponry. The protective technology disperses incoming energy weapon damage across a wider area, reducing penetration depth. Otherwise maintaining the 7K's general configuration with Endo Steel chassis and XL engine, the 10K carries paired ER medium lasers, a Snub-Nose PPC, and an MRM-20 with Apollo fire control. The variant ensures the Grand Dragon remains competitive in an era of proliferating advanced weapons technology.

The experimental C3 system provides improved data sharing at the cost of increased maintenance requirements, reflecting the Combine's willingness to field cutting-edge technology despite reliability concerns.

BMGrandDragon_DRG9KC.overview:
The Grand Dragon emerged from Luthien Armor Works' efforts to modernize the venerable Dragon chassis using newly recovered Star League technology. What began as a simple field modification replacing the autocannon with a particle projection cannon evolved into a full production model by 3040. Over the following fifteen years, LAW systematically converted Dragon production lines at Luthien, Dieron, Saffel, and Yorii to Grand Dragon manufacture, completely phasing out the original by 3055.

The Grand Dragon represented the Combine's technological renaissance following the recovery of the Helm Memory Core. The design maintained the Dragon's characteristic speed and versatility while incorporating significant improvements. Production continued until the Word of Blake's devastating 3068 attacks on LAW facilities, though rapid establishment of new factories ensured the Grand Dragon's continued service.
BMGrandDragon_DRG9KC.capabilities:
The Grand Dragon's combat effectiveness stems from its successful integration of advanced technology without sacrificing the original Dragon's core strengths. The Hermes 360 XL engine pushes the sixty-ton chassis to a maximum speed of 97 kilometers per hour, making it one of the faster heavy 'Mechs in DCMS service. This mobility combines with the Lord's Light 2 Extended-Range PPC to create a highly effective skirmisher capable of dictating engagement ranges. The Telos DecaCluster LRM-10 provides supplementary firepower, while three Victory 23R medium lasers handle close defense.

Thirteen double heat sinks manage the thermal load efficiently, allowing sustained fire with the primary weapons. CASE-protected ammunition storage demonstrates LAW's attention to survivability. The enhanced hip and torso assembly developed at Nykvarn increased torso rotation from 250 degrees to nearly 300 degrees, substantially improving the 'Mech's ability to engage targets across wider firing arcs. This modification became standard on all Grand Dragons produced after the Jihad. However, the XL engine that enables the Grand Dragon's impressive speed also is a significant vulnerability, as penetrating damage to either torso section can disable the 'Mech entirely.
BMGrandDragon_DRG9KC.history:
The Grand Dragon's development traces back to the waning years of the Fourth Succession War, when DCMS commanders began experimenting with field modifications to their Dragon 'Mechs. The most successful of these swapped the autocannon for a particle projection cannon, creating what would become the DRG-1G configuration. Initial reception proved enthusiastic enough that LAW formalized the design for production in 3040.

Acceptance within the DCMS came rapidly as the Grand Dragon reached line units throughout the 3040s and 3050s. The 'Mech's effective combination of speed, firepower, and heat management made it popular with MechWarriors who appreciated its versatility. Nearly every DCMS line unit eventually fielded a company of Dragons or Grand Dragons. The Grand Dragon also saw extensive use during the Clan Invasion, where its mobility proved valuable against technologically superior Clan opponents.

The Jihad brought severe disruption when Word of Blake forces struck LAW's primary facilities between 3068 and 3070. LAW's resilience proved equal to the challenge, as the company established new manufacturing capacity within two years. The Nykvarn facility earned the honor of restarting Grand Dragon production, followed by rebuilt facilities on Abiy Adi and Savinsville. Post-Jihad variants continued the chassis's evolution, incorporating C3 networks, improved missiles, and eventually Clan-grade technology.
BMGrandDragon_DRG9KC.deployment: Produced at the Nykvarn facility beginning in 3071, this variant addresses DCMS commanders' desire for Grand Dragon-pure C3 networks. Based on the 5K chassis but lacking CASE protection, the variant replaces one rear-facing laser with an MML-5 and swaps the ER PPC for a Snub-Nose PPC optimized for closer engagements. Light ferro-fibrous armor enhances survivability, while the inclusion of a C3 master computer enables the 'Mech to serve as a network coordinator. Though designed for standoff engagement, the configuration proves effective at close range where the Snub-Nose PPC's damage maximizes.

BMGrandTitan_TITN10M.overview:
The Grand Titan is a hundred-ton assault BattleMech introduced in 3054 by Earthwerks Incorporated, based on a design created by Vining Engineering and Salvage Team. The 'Mech traces its lineage to the Titan, an abandoned Star League Defense Force prototype recovered by the Armed Forces of the Federated Suns in 3023. Rather than simply modernizing the original, VEST's engineers used the recovered specifications as a springboard for an entirely new design intended to challenge Clan OmniMechs on equal terms.

VEST sold the completed design to Earthwerks, whose Keystone facility produces the Grand Titan primarily for the Free Worlds League, with the Word of Blake historically purchasing significant numbers of each production run.
BMGrandTitan_TITN10M.capabilities:
Built on a Corean Model 101BLP Endo Steel chassis and powered by an LTV 400 XL fusion engine, the Grand Titan achieves a respectable top speed of sixty-five kilometers per hour for its weight class. The use of an extralight engine saves considerable tonnage but creates a well-known vulnerability to torso damage, a trade-off VEST's designers accepted to maximize the 'Mech's offensive payload. Eighteen tons of Durallex Heavy armor provide solid protection across the frame.

The Grand Titan's weapons suite is optimized for short-to-medium range engagements. Twin Diverse Optics Type 20 large pulse lasers serve as the primary striking weapons, complemented by a Holly LRM-15 launcher for longer-range fire. At close quarters, paired Holly SRM-6 racks and medium pulse lasers deliver devastating salvos, with all missile systems linked to Artemis IV fire control for improved accuracy. A pair of rear-mounted small pulse lasers and a McArthur anti-missile system round out the defensive package. While effective as a brawler, the design's reliance on the vulnerable XL engine and its troubled development history have earned it a reputation as a maintenance-intensive machine.

BMGrandTitan_TITN10M.history:
The Grand Titan's story begins not with VEST or Earthwerks but with the recovery of the original Titan prototype specifications by Federated Suns forces in 3023. The Titan had been an ambitious Star League Defense Force assault 'Mech project that was abandoned during the upheaval of the Amaris Civil War. When VEST's engineers obtained access to the recovered data, they embarked on what would become one of the more eventful development programs in recent BattleMech history.

VEST's ambitions exceeded their discipline. The engineering team, already plagued by technical difficulties, faced constantly changing project requirements that ballooned the design well beyond its weight budget. By the time the Grand Titan was ready for production, VEST's marketing department had already sold the design to Earthwerks Incorporated, which found itself manufacturing a 'Mech significantly different from what had been originally promised. The removal of missile ammunition and one-shot Streak launchers, along with resolution of engine teething problems, ultimately produced a more focused if less versatile machine.

Production began at Earthwerks' Keystone Plant #3 in 3054, with the Free Worlds League Military claiming the majority of each production run. The Word of Blake became the second-largest customer, purchasing significant numbers for their growing military forces. The Knights of the Inner Sphere adopted the Grand Titan as a prestige assault platform, while white-painted Grand Titans serving in the Word of Blake's First Division became among the most feared sights on the battlefield.

During the Jihad, the Grand Titan saw extensive combat on multiple fronts. On Epsilon Eridani, Word of Blake forces demonstrated the 'Mech's devastating close-range firepower against both civilian infrastructure and opposing military forces. When Wolf's Dragoons arrived under the Allied Mercenary Command banner, they faced an assault company anchored by three Grand Titans in the Ruger Badlands, ultimately being forced to withdraw in what became a significant Blakist propaganda victory. The design continued in service following the Jihad, with the N13M variant becoming a popular choice among Republic, Free Worlds League, and mercenary forces through the Dark Age era.
BMGrandTitan_TITN10M.deployment: The base T-IT-N10M is the original production model that established the Grand Titan on the battlefield. Its combination of pulse lasers, Artemis-guided missiles, and an anti-missile system makes it a formidable close-range combatant, though the 'Mech's dependence on its XL engine for the speed needed to close with opponents has drawn criticism from assault 'Mech purists who prefer more durable powerplants. The Free Worlds League Military and Word of Blake have been the primary operators since production began in 3054.

Armored components protect the heavy-duty gyro, cockpit, and all limb actuators, making the 'Mech exceptionally resilient in close quarters. Its combination of a Heavy PPC, ER Large Laser, and assorted energy weapons provides effective firepower at multiple ranges. The T-IT-N13M has become a popular commander's 'Mech among Republic, Free Worlds League, and mercenary forces.

BMGrasshopper_GHR5H.overview: The Grasshopper entered service in 2780 as a heavy close-range BattleMech designed for the Star League Defense Force. Originally conceived as a stealthy hunter-killer of light and medium 'Mechs, difficulties integrating experimental stealth systems with the chassis delayed the design past the end of the Amaris Civil War, and the troublesome technology was ultimately stripped from the final production model. The untested and unorthodox 'Mech was distributed throughout the Regular Army rather than the more prestigious Royal divisions, and within four years Grasshoppers could be found in most SLDF regiments. As the Star League dissolved, the chaos of Operation EXODUS and the defection of SLDF units carried the design into virtually every Successor State army. Manufactured by Lantren Corporation on Bryant, the Grasshopper earned an enduring reputation as a mobile, self-reliant heavy 'Mech capable of operating far from established supply lines, and its rugged construction kept the design on battlefields for centuries despite severely limited production numbers.
BMGrasshopper_GHR5H.capabilities:
The Grasshopper combines heavy 'Mech firepower with mobility typically associated with lighter designs. Its VOX 280 engine provides a ground speed of sixty-four kilometers per hour, while four Leviathon Lifter jump jets grant a jump capability of one hundred and twenty meters, remarkable for a seventy-ton chassis. This combination allows the Grasshopper to close rapidly with enemy formations, appearing suddenly in the midst of tightly-packed units where its predominantly short-ranged armament is most devastating.

The primary weapon, a Diplan HD large laser mounted in the center torso, ensures the Grasshopper remains combat-capable even after suffering crippling limb damage, earning it the classification of a "zombie" 'Mech among field commanders. Four Diplan M3 medium lasers spread across the torso and arms allow return fire from virtually any angle, while a single Conan/S LRM-5 provides token long-range harassment primarily used to soften targets before the lasers come to bear. Twenty-two heat sinks give the design superior thermal management compared to other heavy 'Mechs, and its near-exclusive reliance on energy weapons frees it from ammunition dependency, a critical advantage during extended independent operations.

Thirteen tons of Durallex Heavy armor provides respectable protection for the design's weight class, though the Grasshopper can be outgunned by dedicated fire-support platforms of similar tonnage. The design philosophy accepts this trade-off, relying instead on mobility and endurance to dictate the terms of engagement.
BMGrasshopper_GHR5H.history:
The Grasshopper's history is inextricably linked to the fall of the Star League. Designed by Lantren Corporation on Bryant for the SLDF, the 'Mech entered service in 2780, too late for the Amaris Civil War it was originally intended to fight in. Problems integrating experimental stealth systems had delayed production by years, and when those systems were ultimately abandoned, the resulting conventional design was distributed to Regular Army formations rather than the elite Royal divisions. This widespread distribution proved fateful; as the Star League dissolved and SLDF units defected to the Successor States during Operation EXODUS, Grasshoppers were carried into virtually every House army.

The First Succession War proved the crucible that forged the Grasshopper's reputation. Its mobility and endurance made it a premier 'Mech for storming fortifications, and it frequently led assaults that exploited its jump capability to bypass defensive positions. The Grasshopper also served effectively as a backup brawler in companies of light and medium 'Mechs, and its self-reliance made it prized by mercenary commands. However, the design remained an uncommon sight during the Succession Wars, causing many commanders to mistakenly treat it as just another heavy 'Mech until it leapt into their midst and disrupted their formations. ComStar's publication of Technical Readout: 3025 finally brought wider awareness of the Grasshopper's true capabilities.

The Second Succession War dealt a severe blow to production when the Lantren Corporation factory on Bryant was destroyed in 2843 by a Free Worlds League raiding force that damaged the facility's protective domes, exposing it to the planet's worsening global storms. New production ceased entirely for over two centuries. Despite this, the Grasshopper's rugged construction meant that most of the original production run survived through careful maintenance, with many units prioritizing Grasshopper repairs over even a commander's personal 'Mech.

The technological renaissance of the thirty-first century breathed new life into the design. Lantren Corporation introduced the GHR-5J upgrade in 3049, incorporating recovered Star League technology, though the original 5H remained so popular it outnumbered the upgrade three to one for decades. Only when the Draconis Combine introduced its C3-equipped variants did this trend begin to reverse. LexaTech Industries of Hun Ho recognized the growing demand and began production of the completely redesigned GHR-6K in 3064, establishing a new production line that would generate several further variants including the Jihad-era GHR-7K. Jalastar Aerospace on Panpour later secured a license to produce the 6K for the Federated Suns.

During the Jihad, Arc-Royal MechWorks developed experimental prototypes incorporating cutting-edge technology, eventually producing the refined GHR-7P in 3081 primarily for the mercenary market. Rumors also circulated that the Word of Blake had reopened the original Lantren factory on Bryant, supported by higher-than-expected concentrations of Grasshoppers observed in Blakist forces. The Grasshopper has continued to serve across every major conflict of the thirty-first century and beyond, with LexaTech's GHR-8K representing the design's continued evolution in the ilClan era.
BMGrasshopper_GHR5H.deployment: Introduced in 2780, this variant is the original production model of the Grasshopper. Armed with a center-torso-mounted Diplan HD large laser, four Diplan M3 medium lasers, and a Conan/S LRM-5, the design emphasized close-range energy combat with minimal ammunition dependency. Twenty-two heat sinks managed the thermal load effectively, while four Leviathon Lifter jump jets provided exceptional mobility for a seventy-ton chassis. The 5H proved so reliable and well-regarded that it remained the most common Grasshopper variant for centuries, outnumbering even its Star League-technology successor by a ratio of three to one well into the Clan Invasion era.

Twenty-two heat sinks managed the thermal load effectively, while four Leviathon Lifter jump jets provided exceptional mobility for a seventy-ton chassis. The 5H proved so reliable and well-regarded that it remained the most common Grasshopper variant for centuries, outnumbering even its Star League-technology successor by a ratio of three to one well into the Clan Invasion era.

BMGrasshopper_GHR5J.overview: The Grasshopper entered service in 2780 as a heavy close-range BattleMech designed for the Star League Defense Force. Originally conceived as a stealthy hunter-killer of light and medium 'Mechs, difficulties integrating experimental stealth systems with the chassis delayed the design past the end of the Amaris Civil War, and the troublesome technology was ultimately stripped from the final production model. The untested and unorthodox 'Mech was distributed throughout the Regular Army rather than the more prestigious Royal divisions, and within four years Grasshoppers could be found in most SLDF regiments. As the Star League dissolved, the chaos of Operation EXODUS and the defection of SLDF units carried the design into virtually every Successor State army. Manufactured by Lantren Corporation on Bryant, the Grasshopper earned an enduring reputation as a mobile, self-reliant heavy 'Mech capable of operating far from established supply lines, and its rugged construction kept the design on battlefields for centuries despite severely limited production numbers.
BMGrasshopper_GHR5J.capabilities:
The Grasshopper combines heavy 'Mech firepower with mobility typically associated with lighter designs. Its VOX 280 engine provides a ground speed of sixty-four kilometers per hour, while four Leviathon Lifter jump jets grant a jump capability of one hundred and twenty meters, remarkable for a seventy-ton chassis. This combination allows the Grasshopper to close rapidly with enemy formations, appearing suddenly in the midst of tightly-packed units where its predominantly short-ranged armament is most devastating.

The primary weapon, a Diplan HD large laser mounted in the center torso, ensures the Grasshopper remains combat-capable even after suffering crippling limb damage, earning it the classification of a "zombie" 'Mech among field commanders. Four Diplan M3 medium lasers spread across the torso and arms allow return fire from virtually any angle, while a single Conan/S LRM-5 provides token long-range harassment primarily used to soften targets before the lasers come to bear. Twenty-two heat sinks give the design superior thermal management compared to other heavy 'Mechs, and its near-exclusive reliance on energy weapons frees it from ammunition dependency, a critical advantage during extended independent operations.

Thirteen tons of Durallex Heavy armor provides respectable protection for the design's weight class, though the Grasshopper can be outgunned by dedicated fire-support platforms of similar tonnage. The design philosophy accepts this trade-off, relying instead on mobility and endurance to dictate the terms of engagement.
BMGrasshopper_GHR5J.history:
The Grasshopper's history is inextricably linked to the fall of the Star League. Designed by Lantren Corporation on Bryant for the SLDF, the 'Mech entered service in 2780, too late for the Amaris Civil War it was originally intended to fight in. Problems integrating experimental stealth systems had delayed production by years, and when those systems were ultimately abandoned, the resulting conventional design was distributed to Regular Army formations rather than the elite Royal divisions. This widespread distribution proved fateful; as the Star League dissolved and SLDF units defected to the Successor States during Operation EXODUS, Grasshoppers were carried into virtually every House army.

The First Succession War proved the crucible that forged the Grasshopper's reputation. Its mobility and endurance made it a premier 'Mech for storming fortifications, and it frequently directed assaults that exploited its jump capability to bypass defensive positions. The Grasshopper also served effectively as a backup brawler in companies of light and medium 'Mechs, and its self-reliance made it prized by mercenary commands. However, the design remained an uncommon sight during the Succession Wars, causing many commanders to mistakenly treat it as just another heavy 'Mech until it leapt into their midst and disrupted their formations. ComStar's publication of Technical Readout: 3025 finally brought wider awareness of the Grasshopper's true capabilities.

The Second Succession War dealt a severe blow to production when the Lantren Corporation factory on Bryant was destroyed in 2843 by a Free Worlds League raiding force that damaged the facility's protective domes, exposing it to the planet's worsening global storms. New production ceased entirely for over two centuries. Despite this, the Grasshopper's rugged construction meant that most of the original production run survived through careful maintenance, with many units prioritizing Grasshopper repairs over even a commander's personal 'Mech.

The technological renaissance of the thirty-first century breathed new life into the design. Lantren Corporation introduced the GHR-5J upgrade in 3049, incorporating recovered Star League technology, though the original 5H remained so popular it outnumbered the upgrade three to one for decades. Only when the Draconis Combine introduced its C3-equipped variants did this trend begin to reverse. LexaTech Industries of Hun Ho recognized the growing demand and began production of the completely redesigned GHR-6K in 3064, establishing a new production line that would generate several further variants including the Jihad-era GHR-7K. Jalastar Aerospace on Panpour later secured a license to produce the 6K for the Federated Suns.

During the Jihad, Arc-Royal MechWorks developed experimental prototypes incorporating cutting-edge technology, eventually producing the refined GHR-7P in 3081 primarily for the mercenary market. Rumors also circulated that the Word of Blake had reopened the original Lantren factory on Bryant, supported by higher-than-expected concentrations of Grasshoppers observed in Blakist forces. The Grasshopper has continued to serve across every major conflict of the thirty-first century and beyond, with LexaTech's GHR-8K representing the design's continued evolution in the ilClan era.
BMGrasshopper_GHR5J.deployment: Introduced in 3049 by Lantren Corporation, this variant stands as a straightforward upgrade of the venerable 5H using recovered Star League technology. The Diplan large laser gives way to a Diverse Optics Sunbeam extended-range model, improving the primary weapon's reach by over twenty-five percent. The Conan/S LRM-5 is replaced with a Hovertec Streak SRM-2, and the two torso-mounted medium lasers are exchanged for a SureFire 444 anti-missile system. These changes modernize the design while preserving its hallmark ammunition independence, as the Streak launcher's inherent efficiency means the reduction in missile stores has no practical impact on field endurance.

Problems integrating experimental stealth systems had delayed production by years, and when those systems were ultimately abandoned, the resulting conventional design was distributed to Regular Army formations rather than the elite Royal divisions. This widespread distribution proved fateful; as the Star League dissolved and SLDF units defected to the Successor States during Operation EXODUS, Grasshoppers were carried into virtually every House army.

The First Succession War proved the crucible that forged the Grasshopper's reputation. Its mobility and endurance made it a premier 'Mech for storming fortifications, and it frequently directed assaults that exploited its jump capability to bypass defensive positions. The Grasshopper also served effectively as a backup brawler in companies of light and medium 'Mechs, and its self-reliance made it prized by mercenary commands. However, the design remained an uncommon sight during the Succession Wars, causing many commanders to mistakenly treat it as just another heavy 'Mech until it leapt into their midst and disrupted their formations. ComStar's publication of Technical Readout: 3025 finally brought wider awareness of the Grasshopper's true capabilities.

The Second Succession War dealt a severe blow to production when the Lantren Corporation factory on Bryant was destroyed in 2843 by a Free Worlds League raiding force that damaged the facility's protective domes, exposing it to the planet's worsening global storms. New production ceased entirely for over two centuries. Despite this, the Grasshopper's rugged construction meant that most of the original production run survived through careful maintenance, with many units prioritizing Grasshopper repairs over even a commander's personal 'Mech.

The technological renaissance of the thirty-first century breathed new life into the design. Lantren Corporation introduced the GHR-5J upgrade in 3049, incorporating recovered Star League technology, though the original 5H remained so popular it outnumbered the upgrade three to one for decades. Only when the Draconis Combine introduced its C3-equipped variants did this trend begin to reverse. LexaTech Industries of Hun Ho recognized the growing demand and began production of the completely redesigned GHR-6K in 3064, establishing a new production line that would generate several further variants including the Jihad-era GHR-7K. Jalastar Aerospace on Panpour later secured a license to produce the 6K for the Federated Suns.

During the Jihad, Arc-Royal MechWorks developed experimental prototypes incorporating cutting-edge technology, eventually producing the refined GHR-7P in 3081 primarily for the mercenary market. Rumors also circulated that the Word of Blake had reopened the original Lantren factory on Bryant, supported by higher-than-expected concentrations of Grasshoppers observed in Blakist forces. The Grasshopper has continued to serve across every major conflict of the thirty-first century and beyond, with LexaTech's GHR-8K representing the design's continued evolution in the ilClan era.
BMGrasshopper_GHR7KGravedigger.deployment: This custom variant originated as a captured Kuritan GHR-7K prototype that underwent testing and modification at the New Avalon Institute of Science. The C3 slave and ER medium laser were removed to accommodate a pair of center-torso-mounted medium pulse lasers, while the Guardian ECM was relocated to the left torso. The defining modification is the integration of triple strength myomer, transforming the Grasshopper into an exceptionally dangerous brawler capable of devastating physical attacks when elevated heat levels activate the enhanced musculature. Fourteen double heat sinks maintain sufficient cooling to keep the TSM engaged during sustained combat. This variant saw extensive use during the Word of Blake's occupation of New Avalon, terrorizing Blakist patrols through ambushes and commando-style raids across the planet's cities and woodlands.

The untested and unorthodox 'Mech was distributed throughout the Regular Army rather than the more prestigious Royal divisions, and within four years Grasshoppers could be found in most SLDF regiments. As the Star League dissolved, the chaos of Operation EXODUS and the defection of SLDF units carried the design into virtually every Successor State army. Manufactured by Lantren Corporation on Bryant, the Grasshopper earned an enduring reputation as a mobile, self-reliant heavy 'Mech capable of operating far from established supply lines, and its rugged construction kept the design on battlefields for centuries despite severely limited production numbers.
BMGrasshopper_GHRC.capabilities:
The Grasshopper combines heavy 'Mech firepower with mobility typically associated with lighter designs. Its VOX 280 engine provides a ground speed of sixty-four kilometers per hour, while four Leviathon Lifter jump jets grant a jump capability of one hundred and twenty meters, remarkable for a seventy-ton chassis. This combination allows the Grasshopper to close rapidly with enemy formations, appearing suddenly in the midst of tightly-packed units where its predominantly short-ranged armament is most devastating.

The primary weapon, a Diplan HD large laser mounted in the center torso, ensures the Grasshopper remains combat-capable even after suffering crippling limb damage, earning it the classification of a "zombie" 'Mech among field commanders. Four Diplan M3 medium lasers spread across the torso and arms allow return fire from virtually any angle, while a single Conan/S LRM-5 provides token long-range harassment primarily used to soften targets before the lasers come to bear. Twenty-two heat sinks give the design superior thermal management compared to other heavy 'Mechs, and its near-exclusive reliance on energy weapons frees it from ammunition dependency, a critical advantage during extended independent operations.

Thirteen tons of Durallex Heavy armor provides respectable protection for the design's weight class, though the Grasshopper can be outgunned by dedicated fire-support platforms of similar tonnage. The design philosophy accepts this trade-off, relying instead on mobility and endurance to dictate the terms of engagement.
