A 240-rated XL engine maintains the chassis's baseline speed of 64 kilometers per hour with MASC providing brief sprints to 86 kph. Each side torso mounts an SRM-6 launcher for close-range punch, while each arm carries an ER flamer, a standard flamer, and a pair of plasma cannons. This configuration transforms the Hellfire into a devastating close-range combatant specializing in thermal warfare, capable of overwhelming enemy 'Mechs through sheer heat saturation. Fifteen double heat sinks struggle to manage the enormous heat generation of the plasma cannons and flamers, demanding careful fire discipline.

BMHellhound_2.overview:
The Conjurer, designated the Hellhound by Inner Sphere intelligence agencies, is in every practical sense a Wolverine IIC, a comprehensive Clan technology rebuild of the venerable Inner Sphere design. Introduced in 2829, the Conjurer was developed from the WVR-7H Wolverine II, the Star League Defense Force's Royal variant of the standard Wolverine chassis. Despite the clear lineage, the Clans refused to retain the original name due to the stigma associated with the Not-Named Clan, instead designating the rebuilt 'Mech the Conjurer.

Built on an endo steel internal structure and protected by eight and a half tons of ferro-fibrous armor, the fifty-ton Conjurer served primarily as a second-line combatant throughout much of Clan history. The design gained renewed prominence when Clan Nova Cat established manufacturing on Irece following the Clan's Abjurement, and later when the Wolf Empire converted the Thermopolis Wolverine production lines to Conjurer manufacture in 3142, granting Clan Wolf a manufacturing capacity that exceeded their most ambitious projections.
BMHellhound_2.capabilities:
The Conjurer combines respectable speed with a potent short-to-medium range weapons suite, making it an effective skirmisher and raider. Powered by a standard Hermes 300 fusion engine, the design achieves a top speed of 96.6 kilometers per hour, a notable improvement over its Wolverine ancestor. Six BMP Mk. XXI jump jets provide a 180-meter jump capability, granting exceptional tactical mobility that allows the Conjurer to dominate broken terrain and exploit flanking opportunities.

The base configuration mounts a Kolibri Delta Series large pulse laser as its primary weapon, delivering accurate and devastating fire at medium range. Two Series 2b extended-range medium lasers provide supporting firepower, while a pair of Pattern J2 Streak SRM-2 launchers add close-range punch with the efficiency of Streak technology ensuring every missile finds its mark. This all-energy primary armament, supplemented by the ammunition-efficient Streak systems, gives the Conjurer excellent operational endurance, a quality particularly valued in the independent raiding operations for which second-line Clan units are frequently tasked.

The use of a standard fusion engine rather than the extra-light designs favored in frontline OmniMechs reflects the Conjurer's second-line status, but also grants superior survivability when absorbing torso damage. The endo steel chassis and ferro-fibrous armor maximize protection without sacrificing payload capacity, resulting in a well-balanced medium 'Mech that has consistently exceeded expectations throughout its long service history.
BMHellhound_2.history:
The Conjurer emerged during the early years of Clan civilization, when the descendants of Kerensky's Exodus fleet were establishing their military doctrines and rebuilding their arsenals with newly developed technology. The design was created in 2829 as part of the broader Clan effort to upgrade proven Star League designs, with the WVR-7H Wolverine II serving as the foundation for the rebuild. ComStar intelligence initially reported the design as a modified Wolverine before recognizing it as a distinct Clan variant and assigning the reporting name Hellhound.

For centuries, the Conjurer served as a reliable second-line combatant across the Clan homeworlds. With the advent of OmniMech technology, frontline Galaxies transitioned to more flexible designs, but the Conjurer retained a valued role in garrison and second-line formations. Its standard engine construction and logistical simplicity made it particularly well-suited for independent operations, and warriors assigned to the design found it an effective platform for reconnaissance and special operations. When the Clans invaded the Inner Sphere, Great House military analysts came to respect the Conjurer's combat capabilities, noting that its combination of speed, firepower, and ruggedness made it a more dangerous opponent than its second-line designation might suggest.

The Conjurer's fortunes shifted dramatically following Clan Nova Cat's Abjurement from Clan society and resettlement in the Draconis Combine. Facing the need to rebuild their depleted touman, the Nova Cats negotiated a complex exchange with Clan Diamond Shark, trading three Carrack-class merchant vessels and manufacturing rights to the Hellhound in return for raw materials and access to factory facilities on Irece and Avon. The Nova Cat variants that emerged from this arrangement demonstrated considerable innovation, and the Diamond Sharks' own Spina Galaxies began fielding their version of the design. The Nova Cat rebuilds honored the sacrifice of allied Draconis Combine units, particularly the Second Arkab Legion and the Ryuken-ni, who had fought alongside the Clan during the Ghost Bear-Combine War.

The Wolf Empire's conquest of Thermopolis in 3142 opened an entirely new chapter in the Conjurer's production history. Clan Wolf converted the existing Kallon Industries Wolverine manufacturing lines to produce the Conjurer, initially assembling a stopgap variant from available Inner Sphere components, including spare engines and autocannons from the Shockwave production line, supplemented by MASC systems already being manufactured at the facility. This Conjurer 8, originally intended as a temporary measure while full Clan-specification manufacturing was established, proved popular enough with warriors that it continued production alongside standard Clan-technology models. The first Conjurer 8 units saw combat during a raid on Asellus Australis, where they engaged the First Nova Cat Regulars in what served as an effective shakedown for the new variant.
BMHellhound_2.deployment: Following the devastating Combine-Ghost Bear War, Clan Nova Cat faced the critical challenge of rebuilding its shattered touman without the Clan Homeworld industrial base it had been Abjured from. Khan Santin West negotiated an arrangement with Clan Diamond Shark, trading three Carrack-class merchant vessels and rights to the rebuilt design in exchange for materials and construction assistance at factories on Irece and Avon. The resulting Conjurer 2 was almost completely rebuilt from the ground up, sharing little beyond its silhouette with the original. A Consolidated 350 extra-light engine pushes the top speed to an impressive 119 kilometers per hour, while upgraded BMP Mk. XXI jump jets extend the jumping distance to 210 meters. The entire weapons suite was replaced with an ATM-9 launcher carrying three tons of ammunition for maximum tactical flexibility, supplemented by two medium pulse lasers linked to a targeting computer for precision fire. An additional half-ton of armor brings protection to the maximum the fifty-ton chassis can sustain. Fielded across all Nova Cat Galaxies, with limited numbers in Diamond Shark and Wolf-in-Exile formations, the Conjurer 2 also saw the rare honor of being gifted to select Draconis Combine units.

XXI jump jets provide a 180-meter jump capability, granting exceptional tactical mobility that allows the Conjurer to dominate broken terrain and exploit flanking opportunities.

Two Series 2b extended-range medium lasers provide supporting firepower, while a pair of Pattern J2 Streak SRM-2 launchers add close-range punch with the efficiency of Streak technology ensuring every missile finds its mark. This all-energy primary armament, supplemented by the ammunition-efficient Streak systems, gives the Conjurer excellent operational endurance, a quality particularly valued in the independent raiding operations for which second-line Clan units are frequently tasked.

The endo steel chassis and ferro-fibrous armor maximize protection without sacrificing payload capacity, resulting in a well-balanced medium 'Mech that has consistently exceeded expectations throughout its long service history.

Three additional double heat sinks beyond the base model's complement manage the substantial heat generated by the heavy laser battery. The variant retains the original's speed, jump capability, and armor protection, making it a straightforward upgrade that enhances striking power without sacrificing the mobility that defines the Conjurer line. Its relative simplicity compared to the more extensively reworked Conjurer 2 made it an attractive option for Clan quartermasters seeking improved combat performance without the logistical complications of a completely new design.

BMHellion_A.overview: The Hellion is a 30-ton Clan OmniMech introduced in 3059 by Clan Ice Hellion, embodying that Clan's deep-seated philosophy of swift, decisive warfare. Designed by the Hector MechWorks Facility Alpha as a heavier evolution of the proven Mist Lynx chassis, the Hellion was intended to fill the role of a fast striker and headhunter capable of keeping pace with the Ice Hellions' aggressive doctrines. The design achieves a remarkable balance of speed, protection, and pod space for its weight class, incorporating endo steel construction and ferro-fibrous armor to maximize payload capacity. Following the destruction of Clan Ice Hellion during Operation ICE STORM, the Hellion has proliferated widely among the Successor Clans, with production lines established on Valencia by the Scorpion Empire and on Svarstaad by Clan Hell's Horses.
BMHellion_A.capabilities:
The Hellion is built around a 210-rated XL engine that propels the thirty-ton OmniMech to a cruising speed of 75 kph, with a maximum sprint of 118 kph. The integration of a myomer acceleration signal circuitry system allows the Hellion to achieve burst speeds of up to 151 kph, enabling it to outrun many designs in its weight class and even keep pace with lighter 'Mechs. Five and a half tons of Compound Gamma ferro-fibrous armor provide exceptional survivability for a light OmniMech, making the Hellion especially difficult to bring down compared to its peers.

With 11.5 tons of available pod space, the Hellion offers more flexibility than many competing designs of similar or even greater mass, including the Ice Ferret and Viper. The Prime configuration exemplifies the design's versatility, mounting four ER medium lasers and a trio of Streak SRM-2 launchers for devastating close-range headhunter engagements, while an LRM-10 provides the ability to harass targets at longer ranges. This combination of speed, durability, and reconfigurable firepower has made the Hellion a preferred command unit for light Stars, where its superior toughness relative to other light OmniMechs provides an important measure of survivability for Star Commanders leading from the front.
BMHellion_A.history:
The Hellion was born from Clan Ice Hellion's relentless pursuit of speed as a battlefield virtue. Produced at the Hector MechWorks Facility Alpha beginning in 3059, the design quickly became one of the most popular 'Mechs in the Ice Hellion touman, prized both for its performance and its symbolic connection to the Clan's namesake predator. The honor of piloting a Hellion was fiercely contested through Trials, and the design became synonymous with Ice Hellion combat doctrine.

The Hellion saw its most significant early combat during Operation ICE STORM in 3071, when Clan Ice Hellion launched its ill-fated invasion of the Inner Sphere. On Romulus, Hellions of the Seventh Attack Cluster employed their signature speed and aggression against the First Falcon Hussars, executing slashing hit-and-run attacks in and around Remus City. The light OmniMechs proved devastatingly effective in headhunter operations, eliminating key Jade Falcon officers and forcing the disorganized Hussars to retreat off-world. Despite these tactical successes, Operation ICE STORM ultimately led to the destruction of Clan Ice Hellion as a political entity.

The Hellion survived its parent Clan's demise, however. As the Ice Hellions were absorbed by Clan Goliath Scorpion (later the Escorpion Imperio and then the Scorpion Empire) the design remained deeply popular among former Hellion warriors, particularly within the Hellion Galaxy. Manufacturing was eventually established at the Prosoma War Works on Valencia, ensuring continued production for the Empire's military. Simultaneously, large numbers of Hellions were seized as isorla by Clan Jade Falcon and Clan Hell's Horses during the chaos of Operation ICE STORM. The Horses proved particularly fond of the design, finding its speed and agility perfectly suited to their combined-arms Mongol horde tactics.

Clan Hell's Horses eventually established their own Hellion production line at the Svarstaad Industriplex Alpha, developing new configurations optimized for their distinctive combat doctrine. By 3147, during Operation Noyan, packs of Horse Hellions were employed against Jade Falcon garrisons on Colmar, racing ahead of the main body to skirmish enemy outriders and disrupt communications with ECM while unleashing devastating close-range laser fusillades. When encountering entrenched defenses, the Hellions called in massed artillery strikes from supporting Stars, demonstrating the design's evolution from a pure headhunter into an integral element of combined-arms operations. A surprising number of Hellions have also surfaced in the Clan Occupation Zones through commercial channels, likely stemming from the loss of an entire shipment from Hector to the Diamond Sharks.
BMHellion_A.deployment: Alternate Configuration A transforms the Hellion into a dedicated mobile harassment platform. Three LRM-10 launchers provide substantial long-range missile firepower, allowing the configuration to saturate targets with sustained barrages while exploiting the chassis's speed to remain outside effective return fire range. A single ER medium laser provides token close defense. The configuration becomes particularly devastating when operating alongside Narc-equipped lancemates, as the homing-capable LRM volleys achieve dramatically improved accuracy against tagged targets. Ice Hellion commanders originally developed this configuration to fulfill a fire support role that the Clan's speed-centric doctrine typically neglected.

BMHellion_G.history:
The Hellion was born from Clan Ice Hellion's relentless pursuit of speed as a battlefield virtue. Produced at the Hector MechWorks Facility Alpha beginning in 3059, the design quickly became one of the most popular 'Mechs in the Ice Hellion touman, prized both for its performance and its symbolic connection to the Clan's namesake predator. The honor of piloting a Hellion was fiercely contested through Trials, and the design became synonymous with Ice Hellion combat doctrine.

The Hellion saw its most significant early combat during Operation ICE STORM in 3071, when Clan Ice Hellion launched its ill-fated invasion of the Inner Sphere. On Romulus, Hellions of the Seventh Attack Cluster employed their signature speed and aggression against the First Falcon Hussars, executing slashing hit-and-run attacks in and around Remus City. The light OmniMechs proved devastatingly effective in headhunter operations, eliminating key Jade Falcon officers and forcing the disorganized Hussars to retreat off-world. Despite these tactical successes, Operation ICE STORM ultimately led to the destruction of Clan Ice Hellion as a political entity.

The Hellion survived its parent Clan's demise, however. As the Ice Hellions were absorbed by Clan Goliath Scorpion (later the Escorpion Imperio and then the Scorpion Empire) the design remained deeply popular among former Hellion warriors, particularly within the Hellion Galaxy. Manufacturing was eventually established at the Prosoma War Works on Valencia, ensuring continued production for the Empire's military. Simultaneously, large numbers of Hellions were seized as isorla by Clan Jade Falcon and Clan Hell's Horses during the chaos of Operation ICE STORM. The Horses proved particularly fond of the design, finding its speed and agility perfectly suited to their combined-arms Mongol horde tactics.

Clan Hell's Horses eventually established their own Hellion production line at the Svarstaad Industriplex Alpha, developing new configurations optimized for their distinctive combat doctrine. By 3147, during Operation Noyan, packs of Horse Hellions were employed against Jade Falcon garrisons on Colmar, racing ahead of the main body to skirmish enemy outriders and disrupt communications with ECM while unleashing devastating close-range laser fusillades. When encountering entrenched defenses, the Hellions called in massed artillery strikes from supporting Stars, demonstrating the design's evolution from a pure headhunter into an integral element of combined-arms operations. A surprising number of Hellions have also surfaced in the Clan Occupation Zones through commercial channels, likely stemming from the loss of an entire shipment from Hector to the Diamond Sharks.
BMHellion_G.deployment: Alternate Configuration G introduces Inner Sphere-sourced technology to the Hellion platform, most particularly a TSEMP One-Shot cannon capable of disrupting enemy electronics and potentially shutting down a target's systems entirely. Three improved heavy medium lasers provide the primary sustained offensive capability, while an LRM-10 offers ranged fire support. The inclusion of the TSEMP system reflects an increasing willingness among Clan warriors to adopt effective Inner Sphere technologies, and the one-shot nature of the weapon encourages aggressive tactics, close rapidly, disable a priority target with the TSEMP, then finish it with concentrated laser fire before withdrawing.

BMHellspawn_HSN10G.overview:
The Hellspawn was developed by General Motors in response to a 3056 call from the Armed Forces of the Federated Commonwealth for a modern, highly mobile fire support BattleMech to replace the aging Dervish. As the flagship design of GM's newly opened production facility on Talcott, the Hellspawn was awarded its contract by the Department of the Quartermaster in October 3060 and first entered service in 3062.

At 45 tons, the Hellspawn carries the same primary firepower as the Dervish in a package ten tons lighter, trading armor protection and structural durability for dramatically increased speed and maneuverability. The design incorporates advanced technologies including an endo steel chassis, extralight engine, and integrated Guardian ECM suite, positioning it as a next-generation fire support platform for Federated Suns forces. Despite its technological sophistication, the Hellspawn has earned a mixed reputation, praised for its agility but criticized for its fragility.
BMHellspawn_HSN10G.capabilities:
The Hellspawn is built on a GM Fury-M endo steel chassis powered by a GM 270 XL extralight engine, achieving a top speed of 97.2 kph, significantly faster than the Dervish it was designed to replace. Six Rawlings 80 jump jets provide an impressive 180 meters of jumping capability, making the Hellspawn one of the most mobile fire support platforms in active service. A Dalban SuperMicronics communications system integrated with a Guardian ECM suite provides protection against enemy electronic warfare systems such as C3 networks and Artemis IV fire control.

Twin Federated 10-Shot LRM-10 launchers deliver effective ranged fire support, while three RAMTech 800P medium pulse lasers provide accurate close-range defense that actually improves upon the Dervish's short-range capability while reducing ammunition dependency. However, the design's most significant weakness is its armor protection. Six and a half tons of StarGuard III armor represents less than seventy percent of the chassis' theoretical maximum, leaving the Hellspawn dangerously vulnerable to concentrated fire. The decision to forgo CASE protection for the left torso ammunition bins compounds this fragility, and the XL engine amplifies the vulnerability further, any side torso breach results in a catastrophic combat kill, leading some pilots to label the 'Mech a deathtrap.
BMHellspawn_HSN10G.history:
The Hellspawn's development was driven by the devastation inflicted upon the Armed Forces of the Federated Commonwealth during the Clan Invasion and its aftermath. Department of the Quartermaster reports estimated that the AFFC would require as long as two decades to return to its pre-3049 readiness levels, a timeline that failed to account for the conflicts of subsequent years. In 3056, the AFFC released requirements for several new combat units with contracts to be awarded by 3060, and General Motors responded with the Hellspawn from its newly opened Talcott production lines, winning the contract in October of that year.

The Hellspawn was first shipped to the Crucis Lancers in September 3062, allowing them to retire their ancient Dervishes to garrison units or scrap heaps. Distribution quickly expanded, with units from the Deneb Light Cavalry to the Robinson Rangers receiving the new design. The Second Ceti Hussars and Davion Light Guards employed Hellspawns to particularly devastating effect on New Syrtis, ravaging the lightest elements of the Fourth Donegal Guards' reconnaissance force using combined direct fire and Thunder munitions.

Despite its combat successes, the Hellspawn has struggled to fully escape its poor reputation among MechWarriors, a consequence of its thin armor, exposed ammunition bins, and vulnerable XL engine that has made many pilots wary of the assignment. General Motors has continued developing improved variants to address these criticisms, with proposals ranging from enhanced fire control systems to completely redesigned weapons loadouts emphasizing close combat capability. The Jihad and its aftermath saw several of these variants enter production, as the desperate demand for any available combat units overrode lingering concerns about the chassis' survivability limitations.
BMHellspawn_HSN10G.deployment: Introduced in 3076, this variant adopted a more versatile weapons configuration built around paired MML-7 launchers that can fire both long-range and short-range missiles depending on the tactical situation. Two medium pulse lasers and a light PPC round out the armament, providing energy backup at multiple range brackets. This variant sacrifices one jump jet, reducing jump capability to 150 meters, but offers greater tactical flexibility than earlier Hellspawn models. The design was produced at GM's Talcott facility and also adopted through field modifications across various commands.

BMHellstar.overview: Following the success of the Cygnus, the Hellstar emerged from the joint production efforts of Clan Wolf-in-Exile and Clan Hell's Horses as another collaborative assault BattleMech, first appearing in 3079 during the closing stages of the Jihad. Drawing inspiration from the Annihilator and the venerable Awesome, the Hellstar was designed as a sustained-fire platform built for extended campaigns rather than the quick, decisive engagements favored by most Clan doctrines. While sharing a large number of components with the Cygnus, the design is a ground-up effort tailored specifically for its all-energy arsenal. The Wolves-in-Exile and Hell's Horses maintained exclusive production of the ninety-five-ton design, making the Hellstar one of the more tightly controlled assault platforms of its era.
BMHellstar.capabilities:
The Hellstar is built around a devastating all-energy armament of four Ripper Series A1 Extended-Range Particle Projector Cannons, mounted in reinforced housings in the arms and torsos. This weapons battery gives the ninety-five-ton 'Mech the capability to destroy or cripple anything less than another assault BattleMech with a single salvo. An unprecedented thirty double heat sinks allow the Hellstar to maintain this punishing rate of fire indefinitely without heat buildup, a remarkable engineering achievement that sets it apart from most energy-heavy designs.

The Type MA-58 Endo Steel chassis and GM 380 XL engine provide a top speed of sixty-four kilometers per hour, impressive mobility for an assault 'Mech of its tonnage. Maximum defense is provided by over eighteen tons of Royal-7 Standard armor, the most protection the chassis can carry. The design deliberately sacrifices secondary weaponry and close-range versatility for sustained long-range firepower and endurance, making the Hellstar an ideal platform for extended campaigns.

The large reinforced weapon housings have drawn speculation regarding their true purpose. BMHellstar.history:

Republic Armed Forces analysts initially questioned why the designers chose to create a fixed-configuration BattleMech rather than simply modifying the Cygnus into an all-energy variant, but given the extensive changes required, building a new design from the ground up proved more practical.

Production was established at two facilities: WC Site 1 on Arc-Royal under the Wolves-in-Exile, and the Csesztreg Industriplex Alpha on Csesztreg under Clan Hell's Horses. The Hellstar appeared equally in the Toumans of both Clans, with all production dedicated to replenishing their forces damaged during the Jihad. The Republic of the Sphere managed to salvage a few badly-damaged examples from Jihad battlefields, and polite overtures made through the Lyran Commonwealth regarding the possibility of acquiring additional units were firmly rebuffed.

More significantly, the Hellstar's design philosophy and particularly the documented use of its reinforced arm housings as improvised melee weapons suggested a broader shift in Clan tactical thinking. Combined with reports of Clan Jade Falcon testing dedicated melee weapons during the same period, the Hellstar represented a wider trend of Clan forces adapting to the unconventional tactics employed by the Word of Blake and Inner Sphere militaries.

Through the Republic Era and into the Dark Age, the Hellstar remained in continuous production at both Arc-Royal and Csesztreg. Ownership of the Csesztreg facility transitioned fully to Clan Hell's Horses following the Jihad, while WC Site 1 on Arc-Royal continued under joint Lyran and Wolf-in-Exile control. Both Clans maintained the design as one of their premier assault platforms, valued for its sustained firepower and reliability in extended operations.

The absence of any secondary weapons makes the design entirely dependent on its PPC battery, leaving pilots with no fallback if forced into extreme close quarters. However, the combination of sustained firepower, heavy armor, and respectable assault-class mobility makes the base configuration a formidable anchor for extended operations where attrition favors energy-dependent designs over ammunition-reliant opponents.

BMHellstar_3.deployment: Also developed during the Jihad, this variant replaces the four ER PPCs with Series 7Ja ER Large Lasers and retains the Targeting Computer, transforming the Hellstar into a highly mobile long-range sniper platform. The reduced heat generation allows a reduction to twenty-eight double heat sinks while still enabling heat-neutral operation, and the freed tonnage supports an active probe and ECM suite, reflecting hard-won lessons from exposure to the electronic warfare tactics employed by the Word of Blake and Inner Sphere during the Jihad.

BMHercules_HRCLS9000.overview: The Hercules was introduced in 3054 by Kali Yama/Alphard Trading Corporation and Kali Yama Weapons Industries in response to a Free Worlds League request for a heavy BattleMech combining balanced mobility with substantial firepower. Designed from the outset as a versatile trooper capable of filling multiple combat roles, the seventy-ton Hercules mounts a diverse weapons array covering engagement ranges from extreme distance to point-blank. Powered by a Magna 350 XL engine that propels the chassis to speeds unusual for its weight class, the design fills the gap between slower assault platforms and lighter, less well-armed heavy designs. Production at facilities on Kendall and Kalidasa ensured steady supply to Free Worlds League Military formations, and the chassis quickly earned a reputation as a reliable all-around performer suited to missions ranging from air defense to direct fire support.
BMHercules_HRCLS9000.capabilities:
The Hercules is primarily intended as a mobile firing platform. Its Magna 350 XL fusion engine drives the seventy-ton chassis to a cruising speed of fifty-four kilometers per hour, with a flank speed of eighty-six, making it one of the faster designs in its weight class. This speed comes at the cost of jump capability, leaving the Hercules reliant on open terrain or careful route planning to avoid being outmaneuvered by lighter opponents. Eleven tons of Aldis Heavy ferro-fibrous armor provide protection sufficient to weather volleys from Clan OmniMechs and Inner Sphere opponents alike, giving MechWarriors confidence in sustained engagements.

The weapons loadout emphasizes versatility across all ranges. A Fusigon Model XI extended-range PPC serves as the primary weapon, capable of reaching targets at extreme distance. An Imperator Code Red LB 10-X autocannon supplements this at intermediate ranges, with the ability to switch between standard slugs and cluster munitions for anti-aircraft or anti-infantry work. Close-range defense falls to a Holly Streak SRM-2 launcher, an Aberdovey medium pulse laser, and two rear-mounted Martell small pulse lasers, the latter added specifically to counter Elemental swarming attacks. A Burow anti-missile system in the center torso provides additional protection against incoming missile fire. The design's primary weakness is a known electrical overload when struck by PPC fire, a flaw that has persisted despite the addition of damper circuits.
BMHercules_HRCLS9000.history:
The Hercules emerged from House Marik's desire for a new generation of heavy BattleMechs that could match the technological resurgence sweeping the Inner Sphere during the mid-thirty-first century. Kali Yama/Alphard Trading Corporation on Kendall and Kali Yama Weapons Industries on Kalidasa both commenced production in 3054, with the design entering Free Worlds League Military service shortly thereafter. The dual production lines ensured a steady supply of frames, and the Hercules quickly became a common sight in FWLM heavy and assault lances.

The Outworlds Alliance proved an unexpectedly significant customer, purchasing two dozen Hercules chassis, making the Periphery state the third-largest buyer after the FWLM and various mercenary commands. Given the higher cost of the Hercules compared to the older-technology designs typically sold to Periphery governments, the purchases attracted scrutiny. Suggestions that the Alliance intended to reverse-engineer the advanced technology proved unfounded, though especially only nineteen of the twenty-four units shipped were accounted for.

Operation Bulldog provided the Hercules its first major combat test against Clan forces, where it proved its worth against the Smoke Jaguars. The combination of long-range energy and ballistic weapons with close-range missile and laser systems proved devastating in the varied engagements of the campaign. Earlier, during Operation Guerrero, the design had performed satisfactorily but without particular distinction. It was in engagements against Clan opponents that the Hercules truly demonstrated its design philosophy, the mixed weapons array allowed MechWarriors to engage at whatever range the tactical situation demanded.

The Hercules also found success in the Solaris VII arenas, where representatives from Kali Yama Weapons Industries persuaded several stables and cooperatives to adopt the design. The chassis fared well in arena competition, further boosting its reputation and commercial appeal. During the Jihad, the Kalidasa facility fell under Word of Blake control while the Kendall plant continued production under Free Worlds League authority. Post-Jihad, the Kendall facility briefly operated under independent management before the reconstituted Free Worlds League reasserted control, introducing upgraded variants including the -9003 and -9004 models during the Dark Age era.
BMHercules_HRCLS9000.deployment: The base HRC-LS-9000 represents the standard production model of the Hercules as it entered service in 3054. Mounting the full complement of weapons from extended-range PPC to anti-missile system, this configuration embodies the Free Worlds League's design philosophy of maximum versatility in a single chassis. The combination of speed, armor, and diverse armament makes the base model effective across a broad range of tactical situations, from long-range fire support duels to close-quarters brawls against Elemental-supported Clan formations.
BMHercules_HRCLS9000.manufacturer: Kali Yama Weapons Industries Inc.|Kali Yama/Alphard Trading Corp.

BMHermesII_HER2MMercury.overview:
The Hermes II was introduced in 2798 by Irian BattleMechs Unlimited as a heavier successor to the original Star League-era Hermes. Designed as a heavy scout for the Free Worlds League Military, the forty-ton 'Mech combined respectable firepower with superior armor protection and reliable communications capabilities, filling a critical reconnaissance role in the post-Star League era. Early prototypes suffered from a flawed autocannon placement spread across the center torso, prompting a temporary laser-armed replacement while engineers consolidated the weapon into its final mounting.

The design earned the nickname "Old Reliable" for its exceptional ease of field maintenance, making it one of the most serviceable medium 'Mechs of its time. Production continued throughout the Succession Wars and beyond, with the Hermes II becoming a signature design of House Marik's military forces. The distinctive wing-like protrusions on the 'Mech's ankles, often mistaken for heat sinks, are purely cosmetic elements linking the design to its Hermes predecessor.
BMHermesII_HER2MMercury.capabilities:
The Hermes II excels in restrictive terrain such as cities and forests, where its combination of speed, armor, and firepower gives it decisive advantages over lighter scouts. The Oriente autocannon provides reliable long-range firepower, while the Irian Weapons Works medium laser handles anti-'Mech duties at closer ranges. The Olympian flamer serves both anti-infantry purposes and enables the 'Mech's signature escape tactic, igniting surrounding terrain to blind enemy thermal sensors and discourage pursuit through the resulting inferno.

BMHermesII_HER6D.overview:
The Hermes II was introduced in 2798 by Irian BattleMechs Unlimited as a heavier successor to the original Star League-era Hermes. Designed as a heavy scout for the Free Worlds League Military, the forty-ton 'Mech combined respectable firepower with superior armor protection and reliable communications capabilities, filling a critical reconnaissance role in the post-Star League era. Early prototypes suffered from a flawed autocannon placement spread across the center torso, prompting a temporary laser-armed replacement while engineers consolidated the weapon into its final mounting.

The design earned the nickname "Old Reliable" for its exceptional ease of field maintenance, making it one of the most serviceable medium 'Mechs of its time. Production continued throughout the Succession Wars and beyond, with the Hermes II becoming a signature design of House Marik's military forces. The distinctive wing-like protrusions on the 'Mech's ankles, often mistaken for heat sinks, are purely cosmetic elements linking the design to its Hermes predecessor.
BMHermesII_HER6D.capabilities:
The Hermes II excels in restrictive terrain such as cities and forests, where its combination of speed, armor, and firepower gives it decisive advantages over lighter scouts. The Oriente autocannon provides reliable long-range firepower, while the Irian Weapons Works medium laser handles anti-'Mech duties at closer ranges. The Olympian flamer serves both anti-infantry purposes and enables the 'Mech's signature escape tactic, igniting surrounding terrain to blind enemy thermal sensors and discourage pursuit through the resulting inferno.

Seven and a half tons of Riese armor provides protection superior to most light 'Mechs the Hermes II is likely to encounter, allowing pilots to trade fire with enemy scouts or survive initial contact with heavier opponents long enough to withdraw. The Hermes 240 engine delivers a top speed of 97 kilometers per hour, sufficient to stay ahead of most pursuit.

The heart of the design is its Irian E.A.R. communications system, capable of direct satellite uplinks and tight-beam data bursts. This advanced system requires considerable surface area on the chassis, but grants reconnaissance teams exceptional coordination capabilities that have made the Hermes II invaluable for intelligence-gathering operations throughout its service history.

While the RAC/5 offers devastating burst damage potential, the variant retains only a single ton of ammunition, forcing MechWarriors to exercise careful fire discipline to avoid running dry during extended engagements.

BMHermes_HER1A.overview:
The Hermes was commissioned in 2632 by the Star League Defense Force as a high-speed reconnaissance platform capable of outrunning virtually any other BattleMech of its era. Rushed through development and into service by Irian BattleMechs Unlimited, the thirty-ton design entered regular deployment with numerous electronic glitches and design flaws that plagued early production runs. The SLDF's technicians spent years implementing field repairs to resolve these issues, though by the time the problems were addressed, the Hermes had earned a reputation for unreliability that made it unpopular with pilots who questioned the wisdom of taking such a lightly-armed scout into combat.

The Hermes served only nineteen years on the front lines before being relegated to second-line units and eventually mothballed. The Succession Wars brought the design out of storage to serve the Successor States, though the advanced technology that made it exceptional gradually became lostech. Irian BattleMechs Unlimited eventually resumed production of an upgraded model incorporating recovered technology, restoring the Hermes to its original reconnaissance role.
BMHermes_HER1A.capabilities:
Speed has always been the Hermes' greatest asset, and often its only real defense. The massive GM 270 fusion engine occupies nearly half the 'Mech's total mass, granting a top speed exceeding 150 kilometers per hour that few designs can match. This extraordinary swiftness comes at significant cost: the chassis can mount only minimal armor and a modest weapons array, forcing pilots to rely on evasion rather than protection or firepower when confronted by enemy forces.

The original Hermes mounted an advanced Alexis Photon Target Acquisition System that used computer controls and ranging lasers to optimize weapon accuracy, automatically holding fire orders until achieving proper target lock. This sophisticated system became one of the first casualties of the Succession Wars' technological decline, with no operational examples surviving outside ComStar's secret stockpiles. Modern variants have replaced these systems with contemporary electronics, including Beagle active probes and Guardian ECM suites that restore the Hermes' reconnaissance superiority.

The standard armament of twin Hellion-V medium lasers provides adequate firepower for engaging light targets, while the Olympian flamer allows pilots to create diversionary fires or discourage infantry attacks. The flamer's napalm-based fuel system, while complex, is considered among the safest designs ever produced due to its separation of fuel storage from the ignition mechanism.
BMHermes_HER1A.history:
The Hermes emerged from Irian BattleMechs Unlimited's attempt to create the fastest scout BattleMech possible for the Star League Defense Force. Commissioned in 2632, the design achieved its speed goals but suffered from rushed development that introduced persistent electronic problems. Despite years of field corrections, the damage to the Hermes' reputation proved impossible to repair, and it served only nineteen years before being reassigned to militia units and eventually decommissioned entirely.

The Succession Wars resurrected the mothballed Hermes as desperate Successor States pressed every available chassis into service. Without the infrastructure to maintain its advanced systems, surviving examples became increasingly degraded, their endo-steel structures replaced with heavier standard materials and their sophisticated electronics cannibalized for parts. By the end of the Third Succession War, operational Hermes outside the Com Guards' secret arsenal were barely recognizable shadows of their original specifications. When IBMU reopened the Hermes production line in 2798, it was to build the heavier Hermes II instead, offering only refit services for remaining Hermes chassis.

When the Helm Memory Core enabled technological recovery, Irian BattleMechs Unlimited selected the Hermes as their first test platform for refitting obsolete designs with recovered lostech. The project succeeded in 3047 with the HER-3S, incorporating MASC systems and advanced sensors that restored (and in some ways exceeded) the original design's reconnaissance capabilities. Post-Clan Invasion export restrictions eventually relaxed, though bureaucratic complications prevented sales to the Federated Commonwealth and Draconis Combine for nearly a decade, ensuring the Free Worlds League Military's exclusive use of the upgraded Hermes through Operation Guerrero.

New variants continued development through the Civil War era, with the Word of Blake acquiring significant numbers for their growing military forces. The Jihad saw Hermes employed by both Blakist forces and their opponents, with rumors of stealth-armored variants closely guarded by the Word. Production continues at Irian, maintaining the design's role as the Free Worlds League's premier light scout platform centuries after its troubled introduction.
BMHermes_HER1A.deployment: Introduced in 2856, this variant represents the Succession Wars downgrade of the original Star League Hermes. The advanced endo-steel structure and ferro-fibrous armor were replaced with standard materials as the technology to maintain them became unavailable, resulting in armor protection reduced by half compared to the original specification. The sophisticated Alexis Photon targeting system gave way to a Wasat Aggressor, eliminating the automated fire control that distinguished the original design. Despite these compromises, the 1A retained the Hermes' exceptional speed and basic armament, allowing it to continue serving as a scout throughout the Succession Wars era.

BMHighlanderIIC.overview:
One of the most popular Star League BattleMechs, many Highlanders accompanied General Aleksandr Kerensky into exile during the Exodus. Some were mothballed, but many found their way into the toumans of the Clans. As Clan technology advanced over the subsequent centuries, weapons systems were progressively upgraded until the design known as the Highlander IIC finally emerged around 2858 during the Golden Century. By the Civil War era, though no new Highlander IICs had been produced since the thirtieth century, several hundred remained in scattered use throughout the touman of every Clan.

The Jihad and subsequent conflicts revitalized production. Clan Wolf established refit facilities on Weingarten to convert salvaged Inner Sphere Highlander chassis into IIC-standard machines, an operation that continued for seventy years. When Clan Hell's Horses captured Weingarten in 3142, they discovered the intact refit line and further enhanced it to produce entirely new Highlander IIC variants, demonstrating the enduring appeal of this venerable assault design.
BMHighlanderIIC.capabilities:
The Highlander IIC retains the fundamental design philosophy of its Inner Sphere ancestor while dramatically upgrading its combat potential through Clan technology. The primary armament centers on an EMRG "Captain" Series Gauss rifle and a Type XXVI "Great Bow" LRM-20 launcher for devastating long-range engagements. At closer distances, a pair of MPA-14 Mod. 12a Streak SRM-6 launchers ensure that every missile finds its target, while three Series PPS-VIII Medium Pulse Lasers provide accurate close-range fire. With the use of newer, lighter Clan weapons, the damage potential of the Highlander has roughly doubled compared to the original design.

Fourteen and a half tons of Arcadia Compound Delta VII ferro-fibrous armor represent the maximum protection that can be crammed onto the frame, making the IIC exceptionally durable in prolonged engagements. Twelve double heat sinks manage thermal output adequately, though aggressive alphas can still tax the cooling system. The retention of three Prentiss-IIIA jump jets preserves the hallmark ninety-meter jumping capability, allowing Clan MechWarriors to execute the infamous Highlander Burial just as effectively as their Inner Sphere predecessors. The generous ammunition supply means the IIC rarely needs to conserve rounds even during extended Trials.

BMHighlanderIIC.history:
The Highlander IIC traces its origins to the Golden Century, when Clan scientists methodically upgraded the surviving Highlander chassis brought on the Exodus with progressively more advanced Clan technology. The Arcadia BattleMech Plant CM-T15, operated by Clan Star Adder on Arcadia in the Rechlan system, served as the primary production facility, and the design saw widespread adoption across nearly every Clan touman. Production eventually tapered off, and by the thirty-first century no new Highlander IICs had been built for over a hundred years, though hundreds remained in scattered service.

The Word of Blake Jihad prompted Clan Wolf to revive the design through an innovative approach. Operating out of an extensive boneyard on Weingarten, the Wolves established the W-7 Facilities refit line to convert purchased, scavenged, or salvaged Inner Sphere Highlander chassis into updated Clan-specification IICs. This operation sustained Wolf production for seventy years, during which new combat variants including the IIC 2 and IIC 3 were developed to address evolving battlefield requirements.

When Clan Wolf abandoned Weingarten during the Dark Age upheavals, Clan Hell's Horses occupied the planet in 3142 and discovered the intact W-7 refit facilities. However, the post-Blackout hunger for military hardware had dried up all sources of spare Inner Sphere Highlander chassis. Undaunted, the Horses enhanced the production line to build the required SL-XT chassis on-site, sourcing parts from their facilities on New Oslo and the Clan Sea Fox line on Alnabog. The resulting Highlander IIC 4 proved a formidable weapon during Operation Noyan, demonstrating that the ancient assault design still had much to offer on the modern battlefield.
BMHighlanderIIC.deployment: The base Highlander IIC represents the standard Clan upgrade of the original Star League design, mounting an EMRG Gauss rifle, Type XXVI LRM-20, dual Streak SRM-6 launchers, and three Medium Pulse Lasers. Fourteen and a half tons of ferro-fibrous armor and three jump jets preserve the original Highlander's hallmark combination of protection and mobility. First produced at the Arcadia BattleMech Plant CM-T15 by Clan Star Adder during the Golden Century, the base configuration remained in scattered service across every Clan touman for centuries, with Clan Wolf later establishing refit production on Weingarten.

The combination of the HAG/20's high rate of fire and the ECM's defensive properties makes the IIC 3 particularly effective in combined-arms operations where disrupting enemy coordination is as valuable as raw firepower.

BMHighlander_HGN694.overview:
The Highlander is one of the most iconic assault BattleMechs in the history of the Inner Sphere, first entering service with the Star League Defense Force in 2592. Designed by StarCorps Industries as a dedicated city and installation defender, the ninety-ton design combined a versatile weapons mix, heavy ferro-fibrous armor protection, and an unusual feature for an assault chassis: jump jets that granted it tactical mobility unmatched by its peers. This agility proved so effective that within decades of its introduction, nearly every Regular and Royal Army BattleMech regiment featured Highlanders in their ranks.

Perhaps more than any other single design, the Highlander is defined by the infamous "Highlander Burial", a death-from-above attack in which the 'Mech leaps onto a lighter opponent and literally drives it into the ground. So popular was this devastating tactic that StarCorps reengineered the Highlander's legs specifically to withstand repeated such attacks, transforming a desperation move into a signature combat technique feared across every battlefield in the Inner Sphere and beyond.
BMHighlander_HGN694.capabilities:
The Highlander carries a weapons mix optimized for ranged engagements that remains effective when ranges close. The primary weapon of the original HGN-732 is an M-7 Gauss rifle capable of delivering devastating kinetic impacts at extreme range, backed by a Holly LRM-20 launcher for sustained long-range fire support. At closer distances, a Holly SRM-6 rack and a pair of Harmon Starclass medium lasers provide significant short-range firepower. Two tons of ammunition for each launcher system and the Gauss rifle provide excellent battlefield endurance, while CASE protects the MechWarrior from catastrophic ammunition explosions.

Fifteen and a half tons of Grumman-3 ferro-fibrous armor make the Highlander exceptionally well protected for its class, while three HildCo Model 10 jump jets grant it a mobility advantage that most assault 'Mechs cannot match. This combination of firepower, protection, and mobility allows the Highlander to control engagement ranges, pursue fleeing opponents, and execute the feared Highlander Burial with devastating effect. The design's relatively low heat output allows pilots to maintain a near-continuous barrage, though sustained use of all weapons systems simultaneously still demands thermal discipline.
BMHighlander_HGN694.history:
Designed for the Star League Defense Force in 2592, the Highlander was an instant success with both Regular and Royal regiments. Its wide variety of weapons and jump jets allowed it to take on any situation, and the design rapidly became one of the most common assault 'Mechs in the SLDF order of battle. The Highlander saw extensive service through the final decades of the Star League era, and many accompanied General Aleksandr Kerensky on the Exodus, where Clan scientists would eventually upgrade surviving chassis into the formidable Highlander IIC using advanced Clan technology.

The Succession Wars devastated Highlander production in the Inner Sphere. StarCorps' factory on Son Hoa was destroyed toward the end of the Second Succession War, driving the original HGN-732 to virtual extinction. An agreement between Hollis Incorporated and StarCorps to rebuild destroyed chassis from scratch using readily available technology produced the downgraded HGN-733, which Hollis continued to custom-build on Corey until the Fourth Succession War when the licensing arrangement was revoked. By the mid-3030s, StarCorps had managed to restart limited production on Son Hoa, producing barely a dozen new 'Mechs per year.

Throughout the Succession Wars, ComStar secretly maintained a large stock of original Highlanders inherited from the Star League. During the War of 3039, ComStar provided both HGN-733s and a few advanced HGN-732s to the Draconis Combine, shocking Lyran forces who encountered what they believed to be extinct Star League-era technology. The Northwind Highlanders also maintained a disproportionate number of operational Highlanders through the Succession Wars, many with original Star League-era components, and their skill with the Highlander Burial became legendary.

By 3057, StarCorps' Son Hoa factory had returned to full production, producing original-specification HGN-732 Highlanders for Lyran units of the Federated Commonwealth. The FedCom Civil War spurred the development of multiple advanced variants, including the urban-combat focused HGN-734 and the ComStar-enhanced HGN-736. The HGN-734's debut in 3062 also had an unexpected civilian legacy: the production changeover left a surplus of older-specification components, which StarCorps repurposed to create the St. Florian FireMech, one of the most advanced IndustrialMechs introduced since the fall of the Star League. Post-Civil War production continued to diversify, with the HGN-738 introducing Heavy Gauss Rifle technology and the experimental HGN-641-X-2 pushing the boundaries of what the venerable chassis could accommodate.

The Word of Blake Jihad severely disrupted Highlander production when Blakist forces attacked the Son Hoa factories in 3074, rendering them temporarily inoperable. Meanwhile, Clan Wolf had established its own Highlander legacy on Weingarten, converting salvaged Inner Sphere chassis into Highlander IICs at the W-7 Facilities, an operation that would eventually pass to Clan Hell's Horses when they captured the planet in 3142. Production of new Inner Sphere variants eventually resumed on Son Hoa, and designs such as the HGN-740 continued to emerge well into the Dark Age. The Highlander's long and distinguished service record, combined with its association with the famed Northwind Highlanders mercenary brigade, has cemented its place as one of the most recognized and respected assault 'Mechs in the history of mechanized warfare.
BMHighlander_HGN694.deployment: Introduced during the FedCom Civil War, this variant takes a radical approach to the Highlander platform by replacing the missile launchers, medium lasers, and jump jets with two large lasers and a Heavy Gauss Rifle while retaining the standard M-7 Gauss Rifle. The result is a devastating long-range fire-support platform with enormous alpha-strike potential, though the sacrifice of the Highlander's signature jump capability means this variant cannot perform the feared Highlander Burial. Production at Son Hoa was brief, as the design was soon superseded by the HGN-738.

BMHitman_HM1.overview:
The Hitman is a thirty-ton light BattleMech introduced in 3055 by Diplan 'Mechyards for the Draconis Combine Mustered Soldiery. Designed as a dedicated spotter for Arrow IV artillery systems, the Hitman fills a specialized niche that few other light 'Mechs can match. DCMS analysts identified the need for a fast scout capable of carrying Target Acquisition Gear after observing the Clans' minimal reliance on artillery, recognizing that precision-guided munitions could help offset the enemy's technological superiority in direct engagements.

Once famous for their Jenner and Mongoose designs, Diplan 'Mechyards had fallen on hard times during the Succession Wars but returned to full-scale BattleMech production with the Hitman. The design gave the DCMS a purpose-built artillery coordination platform at a time when few manufacturers were producing dedicated spotter chassis.
BMHitman_HM1.capabilities:
The Hitman is built around speed and electronic warfare rather than raw firepower. Its GM 210 XL engine propels the thirty-ton chassis to a top speed of nearly 119 kilometers per hour, while an integrated MASC system enables bursts exceeding 151 kilometers per hour when the situation demands it. This exceptional mobility allows the Hitman to close rapidly to effective TAG range, designate targets for Arrow IV artillery batteries and semi-guided LRM fire, and withdraw before enemy forces can effectively respond.

The Hitman's electronic warfare suite is comprehensive for its weight class. An Apple Churchill Guardian ECM suite provides concealment from enemy sensors, while a Wunderland Beagle active probe detects hidden units that might threaten the 'Mech during its approach runs. Should the Hitman encounter a foe it cannot outpace, three Argra 3L medium lasers provide solid defensive firepower, and a Thunderstroke-L LRM-5 launcher linked to an Artemis IV fire control system offers engagement capability at longer ranges.

Five tons of Starshield A armor provide reasonable protection for a light 'Mech, though the fragile XL engine makes concentrated fire a serious threat. The Hitman's designers clearly prioritized its spotter role over survivability in a stand-up fight, a trade-off that makes the design far more valuable when properly paired with Arrow IV-equipped support elements than its modest armament might suggest.

BMHitman_HM1.history:
Diplan 'Mechyards had been reduced to little more than a holding company during the Succession Wars as their manufacturing plants were destroyed. Following the Clan Invasion, Diplan secured financial backing from Hachiman Taro Electronics Limited and upgraded their component manufacturing plant on Aix-la-Chapelle into a full BattleMech production facility. After extensive testing on the training grounds of New Samarkand's Sun Zhang Academy, the Hitman entered widespread deployment with the DCMS for the drive against Clan Smoke Jaguar.

With large numbers of Arrow IV-equipped vehicles and 'Mechs finally reaching front-line units, the DCMS began teaming them with Hitman scouts to devastating effect during Operation Bulldog. The Ryuken regiments used this new equipment combination against the Jaguars, and the perfected artillery coordination tactics served the DCMS well when Clan Ghost Bear later launched their own assault on the Combine.

The DCMS initially limited Hitman deployment to formations possessing the necessary artillery missile systems to fully exploit the design's TAG capability. Not wishing to waste the 'Mech's other considerable capabilities, the DCMS created the HM-2 field modification for units lacking artillery assets but fielding C3-equipped lances. The Seventeenth Recon Regiment, better known as Camacho's Caballeros, especially deployed Hitman scouts on Luzerne during the Ghost Bear incursion. When the First Bear Regulars crossed the border, the regiment's scout elements called in a withering artillery barrage that gutted an entire Ghost Bear Cluster.

Production continued at Diplan 'Mechyards on Aix-la-Chapelle through the Jihad era, which saw the introduction of the HM-1r variant as a more versatile direct-combat platform. The Hitman also served as the foundation for Diplan's later Kabuto light 'Mech, which adapted the successful chassis into a close-range striker role. From the Clan Invasion through the ilClan era, the Hitman has remained in continuous production, evidence of both the design's enduring utility and Diplan 'Mechyards' successful return to full-scale BattleMech manufacturing.
BMHitman_HM1.deployment: The base HM-1 model represents the Hitman's original design intent as an artillery spotter and electronic warfare platform. Armed with a Forward 1 TAG system, Guardian ECM suite, Beagle active probe, and MASC for high-speed ingress runs, this variant is optimized for designating targets for Arrow IV batteries and semi-guided LRM fire. Three medium lasers and an Artemis-linked LRM-5 launcher provide self-defense capability, though the design's true value lies in its ability to multiply the effectiveness of supporting artillery formations.

Engineers stripped all original armament and replaced the standard gyroscope with an XL gyro to free internal space. The new weapons suite centers on an MML-7 launcher capable of firing both LRM and SRM ammunition, paired with dual ER medium lasers that extend the 'Mech's effective engagement envelope beyond the original's medium laser range. While sacrificing the specialized electronic warfare capability that defined the original Hitman, this variant offers greater tactical flexibility as a fast striker that can contribute meaningful firepower independent of supporting artillery assets.

BMHitman_HM2.overview:
The Hitman is a thirty-ton light BattleMech introduced in 3055 by Diplan 'Mechyards for the Draconis Combine Mustered Soldiery. Designed as a dedicated spotter for Arrow IV artillery systems, the Hitman fills a specialized niche that few other light 'Mechs can match. DCMS analysts identified the need for a fast scout capable of carrying Target Acquisition Gear after observing the Clans' minimal reliance on artillery, recognizing that precision-guided munitions could help offset the enemy's technological superiority in direct engagements.

Once famous for their Jenner and Mongoose designs, Diplan 'Mechyards had fallen on hard times during the Succession Wars but returned to full-scale BattleMech production with the Hitman. The design gave the DCMS a purpose-built artillery coordination platform at a time when few manufacturers were producing dedicated spotter chassis.
BMHitman_HM2.capabilities:
The Hitman is built around speed and electronic warfare rather than raw firepower. Its GM 210 XL engine propels the thirty-ton chassis to a top speed of nearly 119 kilometers per hour, while an integrated MASC system enables bursts exceeding 151 kilometers per hour when the situation demands it. This exceptional mobility allows the Hitman to close rapidly to effective TAG range, designate targets for Arrow IV artillery batteries and semi-guided LRM fire, and withdraw before enemy forces can effectively respond.

The Hitman's electronic warfare suite is comprehensive for its weight class. An Apple Churchill Guardian ECM suite provides concealment from enemy sensors, while a Wunderland Beagle active probe detects hidden units that might threaten the 'Mech during its approach runs. Should the Hitman encounter a foe it cannot outpace, three Argra 3L medium lasers provide solid defensive firepower, and a Thunderstroke-L LRM-5 launcher linked to an Artemis IV fire control system offers engagement capability at longer ranges.

Five tons of Starshield A armor provide reasonable protection for a light 'Mech, though the fragile XL engine makes concentrated fire a serious threat. The Hitman's designers clearly prioritized its spotter role over survivability in a stand-up fight, a trade-off that makes the design far more valuable when properly paired with Arrow IV-equipped support elements than its modest armament might suggest.

BMHitotsumeKozo_HKZ1F.overview: The Hitotsume Kozo is a fifty-five-ton medium BattleMech introduced in 3136 by Luthien Armor Works on New Samarkand. Conceived during the Draconis Combine's unofficial cultural rebirth, LAW engineers designed the chassis as a stylized homage to ancient Japanese samurai, channeling the aggressive close-combat philosophy that had come to define a new generation of Combine war machines. Similar in doctrine to the Rokurokubi, the Hitotsume Kozo fills the role of a medium striker capable of devastating enemies at range before closing to deliver punishing melee attacks. Initially unpopular among front-line formations due to its demanding heat management, the design ultimately earned a fearsome reputation in the hands of the Ghost Regiments and other aggressive units within the Draconis Combine Mustered Soldiery.
BMHitotsumeKozo_HKZ1F.capabilities:
The Hitotsume Kozo's primary weapon is a shoulder-mounted Lord's Light 3 heavy particle projection cannon, capable of delivering devastating fire at range while building the heat necessary to activate the 'Mech's Triple Strength Myomer. A pair of Diverse Optics Type 20X extended-range medium lasers provide supplementary firepower from the left arm, while a stylized hatchet (fashioned to resemble an ancient Japanese double-ended sickle) gives the design its signature melee capability. When the myomer bundles reach optimal operating temperature, the Hitotsume Kozo transforms from a moderately fast skirmisher into a terrifyingly quick close-quarters killer.

A Hermes 330 XL engine provides respectable speed for a medium 'Mech, while four Icarus 81 jump jets grant tactical flexibility on broken terrain. The chassis mounts an impressive fourteen and a half tons of New Samarkand Teppeki hardened armor, granting exceptional resilience against ballistic and physical attacks at the cost of additional weight. This protection philosophy reflects the design's intended role: close with the enemy and endure return fire while delivering melee strikes.

The Hitotsume Kozo's greatest weakness is its challenging heat management. Only twelve double heat sinks struggle to dissipate the output of its energy weapons, forcing pilots to carefully manage their firing patterns. In inexperienced hands, the 'Mech can quickly overheat and shut down at the worst possible moment, a vulnerability that contributed to its initial unpopularity among conventional formations.
BMHitotsumeKozo_HKZ1F.history:
The Hitotsume Kozo emerged during the turbulent 3130s, a period when the Draconis Combine experienced an unofficial cultural renaissance that deeply influenced military procurement. Luthien Armor Works, already producing the Rokurokubi and other culturally-inspired designs, developed the Hitotsume Kozo as a heavier complement to their existing lineup of Japanese-styled BattleMechs. Named after a mythological one-eyed dwarf from ancient Terran folklore, the design entered production at LAW's New Samarkand facility in 3136.

The 'Mech's early service history was marked by rejection from mainstream DCMS formations. Front-line commanders considered the design too temperamental, its heat management too demanding, and its advanced systems too difficult to maintain for conventional units. The Procurement Department redirected production to the Ghost Regiments and other formations considered expendable by the Combine's military establishment. This decision proved serendipitous, enthusiastic officers and the yakuza-samurai who populated these units embraced the Hitotsume Kozo's aggressive design philosophy wholeheartedly.

Through extensive practice and raiding operations, Ghost Regiment warriors transformed the Hitotsume Kozo into an efficient killing machine. Paired with Rokurokubis and other fast close-quarters 'Mechs, Hitotsume Kozos provided ranged cover fire before closing to deliver devastating melee attacks. One notable engagement on the world of Mara demonstrated the design's effectiveness when a mixed Ghost company assaulted a fortified bunker network. Five Hitotsume Kozos blasted distant fortifications with their heavy PPCs before sprinting forward to wade into the defensive complex, using their hatchets to cut through the remaining defenders and breach the bunker line for the assault force.

By the ilClan era, the Hitotsume Kozo had firmly established itself within the DCMS, with LAW continuing production at New Samarkand. The design's reputation had evolved considerably from its inauspicious beginnings, earning grudging respect even among formations that had initially rejected it. The introduction of the HKZ-1P variant provided a more accessible option for conventional units, while the original HKZ-1F remained the preferred choice of veteran warriors who had mastered its demanding heat curve.
BMHitotsumeKozo_HKZ1F.deployment: The base HKZ-1F is the standard production model and the most widely fielded configuration of the Hitotsume Kozo. Its combination of a heavy PPC, extended-range medium lasers, triple strength myomer, and a melee weapon gives it a distinctive tactical profile among Combine medium 'Mechs. Pilots who have mastered the heat curve use the heavy PPC to soften targets at range before sprinting in under myomer-enhanced speed to deliver devastating hatchet strikes. The HKZ-1F has found particular favor among the Ghost Regiments, where warriors pair it with lighter Rokurokubis and Panthers to form aggressive combined-arms lances.

The ultra autocannon provides reliable damage output at medium range, and the pulse lasers offer improved accuracy during close-quarters engagements. This variant has been positively received by MechWarriors in the Ghost Regiments who prefer a more conventional combat approach.

BMHollanderIII_BZKD1.overview: The Hollander III is a thirty-second-century reimagining of the Hollander concept, developed by General Motors at their Kathil facility and entering production in 3114. Rather than a direct evolution of Coventry Metal Works' original design, the Hollander III represents an independent effort to recapture the Hollander's signature combination of outsized firepower on a lightweight, affordable chassis. General Motors' engineers adopted a fundamentally different technical approach, creating a fast-striking light combatant that trades the original's long-range sniping role for aggressive hit-and-run tactics. First adopted by the Armed Forces of the Federated Suns, the design attracted interest from the Lyran Commonwealth Armed Forces and the mercenary market, spawning two additional variants to serve different tactical doctrines.
BMHollanderIII_BZKD1.capabilities:
The Hollander III returns to the original Hollander's thirty-five-ton weight class but takes a dramatically different design approach. Built on a GM BZK-III endo-steel chassis and powered by a GM 175 XL engine, the design incorporates a supercharger that allows brief bursts of speed up to one hundred and eight kilometers per hour, far exceeding the original Hollander's pedestrian pace. A compact gyro frees internal space for the supercharger system, while six tons of StarGuard Reflec armor with CASE II provides meaningful protection against energy weapons, the most common threat in the Dark Age battlefield environment.

The primary armament, a GM Nova-10 Ultra Class 10 autocannon with three tons of ammunition, trades the original Hollander's extreme range for a higher rate of fire and sustained combat capability. The ultra-class weapon's double-tap capability gives the pilot significant burst damage potential, particularly effective during the high-speed attack runs the supercharger enables. A full-head ejection system on the base model provides an additional margin of safety, acknowledging the risks inherent in combining an XL engine with light armor. The overall design philosophy prioritizes aggressive mobility over the original Hollander's patient, standoff approach.
BMHollanderIII_BZKD1.history:
The Hollander III emerged from General Motors' initiative to revive the Hollander concept for a new era. By the early thirty-second century, the original Hollander line had been out of production for decades, its Coventry factories never having fully recovered from the Jihad. General Motors, recognizing the enduring demand for an affordable light 'Mech with heavy firepower, developed the Hollander III at their established Kathil facility, leveraging existing production infrastructure rather than attempting to rebuild Coventry's manufacturing capability.

Production began in 3114, with the Armed Forces of the Federated Suns receiving the first BZK-D1 models. The design quickly found favor in Periphery March garrisons, where its firepower and speed made it an effective deterrent against pirate raids. Hollander IIIs became common throughout the Capellan March as well, frequently serving as ambush elements against raiders attempting to exploit the region's long borders.

The Lyran Commonwealth Armed Forces expressed interest almost immediately, leading to the BZK-D2 variant in 3115, while General Motors expanded their market by offering the energy-focused BZK-D3 to mercenary buyers beginning in 3118. The design's versatility and General Motors' reputation for reliable production ensured steady sales across multiple factions.

Hollander IIIs gained broader notoriety through several high-profile engagements, including the defense against pirate raids on Bastille and the ill-fated defense of Abruzzi in 3145, where a mercenary company of Hollander IIIs was overwhelmed by a Capellan Hussars task force in a brutally one-sided engagement that illustrated both the design's firepower and its vulnerability when employed as a line combat unit rather than in its intended hit-and-run role.
BMHollanderIII_BZKD1.deployment: The base Hollander III model entered production in 3114 at General Motors' Kathil facility, built around the GM Nova-10 Ultra Class 10 autocannon as its primary weapon. The design incorporates a supercharger for high-speed strike operations, reflective armor optimized against energy weapons, and a full-head ejection system acknowledging the risks of its XL engine. Three tons of autocannon ammunition provide sustained combat endurance significantly exceeding the original Hollander's limited Gauss rounds, making this variant better suited to the extended engagements common in Periphery patrol and garrison operations.
