However, with only four tons of StarGuard I armor, the design is ill-suited for prolonged firefights or hand-to-hand combat, and commanders typically withdraw their Javelins once ammunition is expended.
BMJavelin_JVN11P.history:
Stormvanger Assemblies introduced the Javelin in 2751 as an export design for Star League member states seeking a capable light reconnaissance platform. The Federated Suns emerged as the largest customer, and House Davion took particular interest in the design's development. By the opening shots of the First Succession War, the Javelin had been integrated into most Federated Suns regiments, its sudden battlefield appearances catching many enemy combatants off guard.

The Javelin earned its reputation for ambush tactics during numerous engagements throughout the Succession Wars. During the long Battle of Kentares, a lance of Javelins and a Wasp from the Second Crucis Lancers executed a devastating rear attack against Kurita forces, destroying a Phoenix Hawk and damaging several other 'Mechs before using leapfrogging tactics to withdraw to friendly lines. The Second Battle of Cylene II in December 3002 demonstrated even more innovative usage, when recon lances composed mostly of Javelins hid beneath thirty meters of water in Waterhole Number Nine. When Kurita assault regiments entered the lake, the concealed Javelins surfaced and unleashed devastating point-blank missile barrages, contributing to the Combine's subsequent withdrawal from the planet.

The destruction of Stormvanger's Caph factory in 2774 during the Amaris Civil War ended original production. Despite this, the Javelin remained in widespread service, particularly with the Armed Forces of the Federated Suns. During the War of 3039, elements of the Tenth Deneb Light Cavalry on Marduk employed Javelins in aggressive anti-armor tactics, charging through Combine Demolisher formations while delivering full salvos of missiles.

Following the Clan Invasion, the Federated Commonwealth initiated upgrade programs incorporating recovered lostech. Jalastar Aerospace began producing new Javelins in 3055 at the behest of AFFC High Command, with the JVN-11D becoming the primary production variant during the Jihad era. The ilClan period has seen Jalastar return the Javelin to its classic missile-armed striker role with the JVN-12N, now featuring Clan-specification weaponry and enhanced mobility for continued service alongside Stingers and Wasps in AFFS reconnaissance lances.
BMJavelin_JVN11P.deployment: Produced by Coalition Armory Inc. for the Filtvelt Coalition, this variant incorporates ferro-fibrous armor matching modern standards while accommodating the realm's technological limitations. Four Streak SRM-2 launchers provide ammunition-efficient firepower without overtaxing the single heat sinks that remain standard in Filtvelt's limited industrial base. The design demonstrates effective adaptation of the Javelin platform to peripheral state production capabilities.

BMJennerIIC_4.overview:
Despite a somewhat enigmatic origin, the Jenner IIC is a powerful and fast light striker 'Mech. Serving with distinction during Operation Revival among the forces of Clan Nova Cat, the Jenner IIC caused confusion among Inner Sphere observers as the original Jenner was first fielded in September 2784, the same year the Exodus fleet left the Inner Sphere in November.

Pre-production Jenners were newly deployed when the SLDF left the Inner Sphere to the suffering of the Succession Wars. The Clans were only reintroduced to the BattleMech through isorla Jenners that Wolf's Dragoons returned with on their second supply run. Guided by visions of future doom, the Nova Cats claimed the Kuritan 'Mech as their own and turned what was one of the Inner Sphere's best light strikers into one of the fastest 'Mechs of its time.
BMJennerIIC_4.capabilities:
The Jenner IIC takes the original Jenner concept to the extreme, being fast and well-armed but ill-suited for prolonged engagements. While massing the same as its progenitor, the IIC mounts a more powerful extralight engine. It is ideal for fast striking, scouting, scout-hunting, and head-hunting operations. Jenner IICs are often some of the first 'Mechs off the DropShip, clearing out scouts and other threats early in a battle.

The base configuration mounts a Pattern C4 Streak SRM-4 in the center torso and a Pattern J7 SRM-6 launcher in each arm, carrying one ton of reloads for each missile rack. Though vulnerable to anti-missile systems and heavily dependent on supply lines, the hail of missiles the Jenner IIC can unleash makes it ideal for eliminating light threats such as scouts and combat vehicles.

To achieve this firepower on a light chassis, the Jenner IIC uses a 315-rated XL engine, endo steel structure, and three and a half tons of ferro-fibrous armor. It also carries enough jump jets to leap 210 meters, giving it exceptional mobility.
BMJennerIIC_4.history:
Though the original version is used by a number of Clans, the Nova Cats fielded multiple Jenner IIC variants as well as continuing its development after their Abjurement. Considerable resources were spent to bring new production online of visually refreshed versions at their Irece Alpha facility to help fill out their rebuilding touman.

Ultimately, the Jenner IIC outlasted the Clan that designed it. During the final battles for Irece in late 3142, Jenner IICs acted as sentries and early-warning scouts, protecting civilian and military transports evacuating before the Dragon's wrath fell upon them. Several Stars of factory-fresh Jenner IICs and Arbalests screened the spaceport near the Irece Alpha production facilities, but the Gunji-no-Kanrei's forces steamrolled the spaceport and only a handful of DropShips managed to reach orbit.

With the acquisition of Irece Alpha following the Nova Cats' fall, Clan Sea Fox took over production of the Jenner IIC, proliferating it throughout the Inner Sphere. Clan Wolf continues to be the largest customer, forcing mercenaries to pay a premium for this premiere striker. The agreement with the Draconis Combine has the Jenner IIC openly available to all purchasers willing to meet Sea Fox prices.
BMJennerIIC_4.deployment: Developed by Clan Nova Cat to modernize both visual appearance and abilities as well as demonstrate their retained strength following Abjurement, the 4 model retains the Streak SRM-4 but replaces the standard SRM launchers with a pair of ATM-3s, each accompanied by a ton of ammunition. This allows greater tactical flexibility with standard, extended-range, or high-explosive munitions.

BMJenner_JR7A.overview:
The Jenner is a relatively modern design, first constructed in 2784 by Diplan Mechyards of Ozawa under contract to House Kurita. Originally developed for the Star League Defense Force, the design was secretly acquired by the Draconis Combine after Kerensky's Exodus. Designed as a fast, hit-and-run guerrilla fighter, the Jenner would form the foundation for highly mobile lances that became a hallmark of DCMS doctrine.

Faster than most opponents while carrying respectable firepower for its weight class, the Jenner became synonymous with Combine military power, remaining the exclusive property of House Kurita for over fifty years. However, the Jenner's reputation was forever tarnished by its prominent role in the Kentares Massacre of 2796, when waves of Jenners carried out Coordinator Jinjiro Kurita's infamous directive.
BMJenner_JR7A.capabilities:
Among the fastest 'Mechs of its era, the Jenner packs impressive firepower at close range. Its optimum engagement range is 30 to 90 meters, and its speed and jump capability make it exceptionally hard to hit. The Jenner can move in quickly, deliver its attack, and retreat before sustaining serious damage. Because the Argra 3L medium lasers are the primary armament, the 'Mech can operate for extended periods without ammunition concerns during deep raids.

The Thunderstroke SRM-4 provides additional hitting power for decisive moments, though the limited ammunition supply requires careful management during prolonged operations. Combined, these weapons give the Jenner more firepower than most light BattleMechs and several medium designs as well. Though an alpha strike generates significant heat, pilots use their impressive jump capability to buy cooling time between engagements.

The Jenner lacks arms for physical attacks, a deliberate design choice given its low tonnage. The four tons of armor provide only light protection compared to similar weight classes, making pilot skill and mobility essential to survival in sustained combat.
BMJenner_JR7A.history:
Diplan was originally contracted by the SLDF to produce Jenners, with the first models joining the Exodus fleet in 2784. Once Kerensky disappeared, Kurita agents secretly negotiated with Diplan to continue the contract under the noses of FedSuns peacekeepers on Ozawa. When the DCMS began its offensive in 2786, Kurita MechWarriors infiltrated under civilian cover launched the first wave directly from Diplan's warehouses.

Despite the outbreak of the First Succession War, construction continued at Diplan Mechyard's factory on Ozawa until a raw materials shortage halted assembly in 2815, though chassis production continued. In 2823, production resumed on Ozawa, with some 3,000 chassis shipped to a Diplan subsidiary on Luthien for final fittings and assembly. By 2830, both production lines were producing 1,350 Jenners a year. The sheer destruction of the Succession Wars took their toll when the Ozawa facilities were destroyed in 2837, and unexplained explosion destroyed the remaining assembly plant on Luthien in 2848, ending Jenner production.

By 2840, the Federated Suns and Lyran Commonwealth had obtained operational Jenners through battlefield salvage. By 2845, all Successor States had access to the design, although it continued to be primarily a Kurita 'Mech. Despite the huge production volumes of the era, the Jenner never became very prevalent beyond the Draconis Combine. A favorite tactic of Jenner lances was to gang up on larger 'Mechs and unleash a devastating alpha strike, often with one or two 'Mechs equipped with inferno rounds.

Rebuilding a Jenner production line on Luthien became a top priority under Gunji-no-Kanrei Theodore Kurita. With ComStar aid, Luthien Armor Works finally reopened the line in 3046. The recovery of lost technology made the Jenner a prime candidate for upgrades, though LAW deliberately avoided radical changes to preserve the original's core advantages. The spectacularly brutal start to the Jihad led many units to return to stockpiles of once-shunned Jenners for replacement machines, proving their value once again.
BMJenner_JR7A.deployment: An early Star League-era variant, this variant replaced all other weapons with a single large laser supported by extra heat sinks. Similar to the prototype JR7-X configuration, this refit was an attempt to address the original design's weapons problems while maintaining the chassis and mobility advantages. Like the prototype, few of these variants survived the Succession Wars.

Its optimum engagement range is 30 to 90 meters, and its speed and jump capability make it exceptionally hard to hit. The Jenner can move in quickly, deliver its attack, and retreat before sustaining serious damage. Because the Argra 3L medium lasers are the primary armament, the 'Mech can operate for extended periods without ammunition concerns during deep raids.

The Thunderstroke SRM-4 provides additional hitting power for decisive moments, though the limited ammunition supply requires careful management during prolonged operations. Combined, these weapons give the Jenner more firepower than most light BattleMechs and several medium designs as well. Though an alpha strike generates significant heat, pilots use their impressive jump capability to buy cooling time between engagements.

The Jenner lacks arms for physical attacks, a deliberate design choice given its low tonnage. The four tons of armor provide only light protection compared to similar weight classes, making pilot skill and mobility essential to survival in sustained combat.
BMJenner_JR7DWebster.history:
Diplan was originally contracted by the SLDF to produce Jenners, with the first models joining the Exodus fleet in 2784. Once Kerensky disappeared, Kurita agents secretly negotiated with Diplan to continue the contract under the noses of FedSuns peacekeepers on Ozawa. When the DCMS began its offensive in 2786, Kurita MechWarriors infiltrated under civilian cover launched the first wave directly from Diplan's warehouses.

Despite the outbreak of the First Succession War, construction continued at Diplan Mechyard's factory on Ozawa until a raw materials shortage halted assembly in 2815, though chassis production continued. In 2823, production resumed on Ozawa, with some 3,000 chassis shipped to a Diplan subsidiary on Luthien for final fittings and assembly. By 2830, both production lines were producing 1,350 Jenners a year. The sheer destruction of the Succession Wars took their toll when the Ozawa facilities were destroyed in 2837, and unexplained explosion destroyed the remaining assembly plant on Luthien in 2848, ending Jenner production.

By 2840, the Federated Suns and Lyran Commonwealth had obtained operational Jenners through battlefield salvage. By 2845, all Successor States had access to the design, although it continued to be primarily a Kurita 'Mech. Despite the huge production volumes of the era, the Jenner never became very prevalent beyond the Draconis Combine. A favorite tactic of Jenner lances was to gang up on larger 'Mechs and unleash a devastating alpha strike, often with one or two 'Mechs equipped with inferno rounds.

Rebuilding a Jenner production line on Luthien became a top priority under Gunji-no-Kanrei Theodore Kurita. With ComStar aid, Luthien Armor Works finally reopened the line in 3046. The recovery of lost technology made the Jenner a prime candidate for upgrades, though LAW deliberately avoided radical changes to preserve the original's core advantages. The spectacularly brutal start to the Jihad led many units to return to stockpiles of once-shunned Jenners for replacement machines, proving their value once again.
BMJenner_JR7DWebster.deployment: This custom variant, nicknamed 'Crow', features a distinctive black paint scheme and is optimized for aggressive Death from Above attacks. A swap to double heat sinks allows several to be removed and replaced with additional jump jets, giving the pilot exceptional vertical mobility for devastating physical attacks from above. The enhanced jump capacity transforms the Jenner from a conventional striker into a terrifying close-assault platform that can drop onto opponents from unexpected angles, exploiting the thirty-five-ton chassis as a weapon in its own right.

Few if any of these prototype Jenners survived into the thirty-first century.

BMJinggau_JNG7L.overview: The Jinggau emerged from the Shengli Arms facility on Victoria in early 3059, a product of the Capellan Confederation's Xin Sheng revitalization movement and the unlikely assistance of the Word of Blake's Toyama faction. The sixty-five-ton heavy cavalry design was one of several BattleMechs developed using the old Star League-era production infrastructure on Victoria, with Blake technicians helping to refurbish the facility as repayment of a personal debt owed to Chancellor Sun-Tzu Liao. The name Jinggau, reportedly meaning "siren," proved apt, the design was built to announce its presence on the battlefield with devastating force rather than operate from the shadows. Despite early complications during development, the Jinggau would prove itself a formidable combatant and a cornerstone of the modern Capellan Confederation Armed Forces.
BMJinggau_JNG7L.capabilities:
The Jinggau is designed to wade into the thick of combat rather than skulk at the edges of an engagement. Built on a lightweight Chariot Type II Endo Steel chassis and powered by a VOX 325 XL engine, the design achieves a top speed exceeding eighty-six kilometers per hour while five Hellespont Leaper jump jets provide one hundred and fifty meters of jump capability, allowing it to close rapidly across almost any terrain. Over eleven tons of armor give the Jinggau excellent survivability for its weight class, ensuring it can absorb punishment while pressing the attack.

The primary weapon is the formidable Zhi-tong-yao Gauss rifle, capable of striking targets at extreme range and delivering punishing kinetic impacts that can stagger even assault-class machines. Sixteen rounds of ammunition allow the Jinggau to sustain fire through several engagements before requiring resupply. As the range closes, four Diverse Optics extended-range medium lasers and a precise Raker-IV medium pulse laser provide withering close-range firepower that exploits any weakened armor the Gauss rifle has already compromised.

The reliance on an XL engine represents the design's primary vulnerability, a penetrating hit to the side torso can prove catastrophic. Additionally, the two-ton ammunition bay for the Gauss rifle presents an explosion risk if the internal structure is breached, though the weapon itself does not generate waste heat. Thirteen double heat sinks manage the thermal load effectively under normal combat conditions.
BMJinggau_JNG7L.history:
The Jinggau's origins are inextricably linked to the Capellan Confederation's Xin Sheng movement and the restoration of the Star League-era production facility on Victoria that became Shengli Arms. Toward the end of 3058, the Word of Blake's Toyama faction began providing Chancellor Sun-Tzu Liao with technicians and material resources to finish overhauling the facility, reportedly as repayment of a personal debt. This assistance accelerated the development of several new designs, with the Jinggau walking off the assembly line in early 3059. Production was halted for over a year after the initial run revealed that both arm sections required extensive redesign, but by 3060 the line had resumed in limited numbers.

The Jinggau quickly proved its worth during the Capellan-St. Ives War, where its combination of speed, firepower, and armor made it an ideal spearhead for Capellan offensive operations. As production increased, the design saw service with elite units including the Tau Ceti Rangers, Warrior Houses, and the Death Commandos. The Shengli Arms facility continued to develop variants through the Civil War period, introducing the plasma rifle-armed JN-G7L and the stealth-capable JN-G9CC during the Jihad. However, the Word of Blake Jihad inflicted devastating damage on Shengli Arms when renegade elements attacked in late 3068, crippling production lines and causing an estimated eighty-four percent loss of capital and personnel. The facility eventually restored Jinggau production to limited capacity, operating at roughly sixty-three percent output by 3079.

The design's fortunes shifted dramatically during the Victoria War when the Federated Suns invaded Victoria in 3103. The Fifth Capellan Defense Force, unwilling to let Shengli Arms fall to the enemy, razed the facility entirely. The Federated Suns subsequently sold the gutted plant to Kallon Industries, which refurbished it to produce Davion designs instead. For over four decades, no new Jinggaus left the Victoria production lines, though significant numbers remained in service across multiple nations through salvage, battlefield capture, and the Clan Hell's Horses refit programs that emerged after Operation SCOUR in 3078.

The Jinggau's renaissance came in 3145 when the CCAF recaptured Victoria. Shengli's engineers initially presented a modernized design under the "Jinggau II" designation, but Capellan officials quashed the name in favor of continuity, preferring to frame the return to Jinggau production as a restoration of normalcy rather than a new beginning. The resulting JN-G9B incorporated Clan Sea Fox-supplied technology alongside domestic innovations, producing a formidable modern combatant that surprised Republic Armed Forces defenders during Operation Clarity with its triple-strength myomer-enhanced speed and increased survivability. By the ilClan era, the Jinggau had become a truly multi-national design, with original Capellan production models, Clan-technology refits, and mixed-tech conversions serving across the Inner Sphere in the forces of the Confederation, Federated Suns, Free Worlds League, Republic remnants, and Clan Hell's Horses alike.
BMJinggau_JNG7L.deployment: Introduced during the Jihad in 3068, this variant applies advanced Capellan weapons technology to the proven Jinggau chassis. The Gauss rifle and laser array are replaced with a pair of plasma rifles mounted in the right arm and six standard medium lasers in the left arm, creating a devastating close-range combatant capable of inflicting severe thermal damage on enemy machines while maintaining respectable direct-fire capability. The heat sink count is increased to fifteen double heat sinks to cope with the substantially higher thermal output, though aggressive use of both plasma rifles simultaneously can still overwhelm the cooling system.

The primary weapon is the formidable Zhi-tong-yao Gauss rifle, capable of striking targets at extreme range and delivering punishing kinetic impacts that can stagger even assault-class machines. Sixteen rounds of ammunition allow the Jinggau to sustain fire through several engagements before requiring resupply. As the range closes, four Diverse Optics extended-range medium lasers and a precise Raker-IV medium pulse laser provide withering close-range firepower that exploits any weakened armor the Gauss rifle has already compromised.

The reliance on an XL engine represents the design's primary vulnerability, a penetrating hit to the side torso can prove catastrophic. Additionally, the two-ton ammunition bay for the Gauss rifle presents an explosion risk if the internal structure is breached, though the weapon itself does not generate waste heat. Thirteen double heat sinks manage the thermal load effectively under normal combat conditions.
BMJinggau_JNG9CC.history:
The Jinggau's origins are inextricably linked to the Capellan Confederation's Xin Sheng movement and the restoration of the Star League-era production facility on Victoria that became Shengli Arms. Toward the end of 3058, the Word of Blake's Toyama faction began providing Chancellor Sun-Tzu Liao with technicians and material resources to finish overhauling the facility, reportedly as repayment of a personal debt. This assistance accelerated the development of several new designs, with the Jinggau walking off the assembly line in early 3059. Production was halted for over a year after the initial run revealed that both arm sections required extensive redesign, but by 3060 the line had resumed in limited numbers.

The Jinggau quickly proved its worth during the Capellan-St. Ives War, where its combination of speed, firepower, and armor made it an ideal spearhead for Capellan offensive operations. As production increased, the design saw service with elite units including the Tau Ceti Rangers, Warrior Houses, and the Death Commandos. The Shengli Arms facility continued to develop variants through the Civil War period, introducing the plasma rifle-armed JN-G7L and the stealth-capable JN-G9CC during the Jihad. However, the Word of Blake Jihad inflicted devastating damage on Shengli Arms when renegade elements attacked in late 3068, crippling production lines and causing an estimated eighty-four percent loss of capital and personnel. The facility eventually restored Jinggau production to limited capacity, operating at roughly sixty-three percent output by 3079.

The design's fortunes shifted dramatically during the Victoria War when the Federated Suns invaded Victoria in 3103. The Fifth Capellan Defense Force, unwilling to let Shengli Arms fall to the enemy, razed the facility entirely. The Federated Suns subsequently sold the gutted plant to Kallon Industries, which refurbished it to produce Davion designs instead. For over four decades, no new Jinggaus left the Victoria production lines, though significant numbers remained in service across multiple nations through salvage, battlefield capture, and the Clan Hell's Horses refit programs that emerged after Operation SCOUR in 3078.

The Jinggau's renaissance came in 3145 when the CCAF recaptured Victoria. Shengli's engineers initially presented a modernized design under the "Jinggau II" designation, but Capellan officials quashed the name in favor of continuity, preferring to frame the return to Jinggau production as a restoration of normalcy rather than a new beginning. The resulting JN-G9B incorporated Clan Sea Fox-supplied technology alongside domestic innovations, producing a formidable modern combatant that surprised Republic Armed Forces defenders during Operation Clarity with its triple-strength myomer-enhanced speed and increased survivability. By the ilClan era, the Jinggau had become a truly multi-national design, with original Capellan production models, Clan-technology refits, and mixed-tech conversions serving across the Inner Sphere in the forces of the Confederation, Federated Suns, Free Worlds League, Republic remnants, and Clan Hell's Horses alike.
BMJinggau_JNG9CC.deployment: An advanced-technology variant that also emerged during the Jihad in 3072, this configuration trades the Jinggau's jump jets for MASC and replaces the standard armor with Stealth Armor paired with a Guardian ECM suite, fundamentally altering the design's tactical profile. The weapons loadout is completely reworked around a Snub-Nose PPC and Large Variable Speed Pulse Laser as primary armament, supported by three Small Variable Speed Pulse Lasers. A Beagle active probe enhances the already formidable electronic warfare capabilities, while an XL gyro frees the tonnage required for these systems. The result is a sophisticated electronic warfare platform that can close rapidly under stealth protection before unleashing precise, punishing fire at short range.

BMJuggernaut_JGR9T1.overview: The Juggernaut is a ninety-ton assault BattleMech produced by Solaris Arms exclusively for the arena combat circuit on Solaris VII. First entering production in 3053, the design was conceived as a dedicated gladiatorial machine, optimized for the close-quarters engagements that define the Game World's most popular arena formats. Unlike military assault 'Mechs designed around combined-arms doctrine, the Juggernaut was engineered from the ground up for one-on-one dueling, where its measured advance and devastating short-range firepower proved decisive. The design earned a fearsome reputation across multiple arenas despite its deliberate lack of speed and long-range capability, qualities that would be liabilities on a conventional battlefield but serve as acceptable trade-offs in the controlled confines of arena combat.
BMJuggernaut_JGR9T1.capabilities:
Built around a GM 270 fusion engine, the Juggernaut moves at a top speed of fifty-four kilometers per hour, respectable for a ninety-ton design but hardly nimble. What it lacks in mobility it compensates for with devastating close-range firepower. The primary armament of the definitive JG-R9T2 consists of three Sutel Precision Line Large X-Pulse Lasers and three Medium X-Pulse Lasers utilizing Bethel Labs technology, providing accurate and punishing fire at typical arena engagement distances. A battery of twelve LFN Lindblad machine guns, six mounted in each side torso, delivers a withering hail of fire at point-blank range, particularly effective against lighter-armored opponents in the final moments of arena bouts.

The Juggernaut's sixteen double heat sinks cannot fully manage the waste heat generated by its advanced laser systems, a significant design compromise that Solaris Arms attempted to mitigate with four volatile coolant pods mounted in the torso. Sixteen and a half tons of Valiant Chainmail armor provide excellent protection, essential for a design built on a Castelli chassis that deliberately sacrifices hand actuators in favor of additional weapon capacity. The lack of hands is of little concern in arena formats where ranged firepower decides most engagements.
BMJuggernaut_JGR9T1.history:
Solaris Arms introduced the original JG-R9T1 in 3053, entering a competitive market for dedicated gladiatorial BattleMechs. While flashier designs grabbed headlines, the Juggernaut quietly accumulated an impressive record of victories, particularly in open terrain arenas such as the Boreal Reaches and the Steiner Coliseum where its measured advance could not be easily flanked.

Major stables took notice of the Juggernaut's growing catalogue of wins. Bromley Stables became one of the design's most prominent operators, fielding Juggernauts in mid-tier and championship-level bouts throughout the late 3050s and 3060s. The improved JG-R9T2, introduced in 3057, addressed persistent complaints about the original's sensor placement and incorporated improved laser technology, significantly boosting the design's competitive viability. The JG-R9T3 followed around 3065, adopting ballistic sidearms better suited to penetrate the increasingly heavy armor fielded by rival arena 'Mechs.

The Word of Blake's invasion of Solaris VII during the Jihad devastated the planet's arena infrastructure and disrupted Solaris Arms' production operations. Several prominent stables collapsed in the aftermath, scattering their MechWarriors and surviving machines across the Inner Sphere. Some Juggernauts resurfaced on secondary game worlds such as Noisiel, where displaced arena fighters continued to ply their trade far from the wreckage of Solaris City.

Ownership of Solaris VII (and with it, Solaris Arms) has shifted multiple times throughout the planet's tumultuous history, passing from Free Worlds League sovereignty through Lyran and Federated Commonwealth control, back to Lyran hands, and eventually falling under Clan Wolf's dominion during the ilClan era. Despite these political upheavals, the Juggernaut has remained a fixture of the arena circuit wherever organized gladiatorial combat continues to draw crowds and C-bills.
BMJuggernaut_JGR9T1.deployment: The original JG-R9T1 mounts conventional pulse lasers rather than the advanced X-Pulse variants of later production runs. Compensating for the reduced heat output, the design carries fewer double heat sinks while adding small pulse lasers and additional machine guns for a staggering close-range battery. Ammunition bins are protected with CASE, reflecting early lessons learned from arena losses. The original model drew persistent criticism for its poorly placed outboard sensor arrays, which proved vulnerable to damage and hampered targeting reliability, shortcomings that would drive the comprehensive redesign of the JG-R9T2.

BMJuliano_JLN5A.overview: The Juliano was the Marik-Stewart Commonwealth's signature assault BattleMech, introduced in 3116 as the culmination of that realm's longstanding ambition to develop a native assault-weight design. Named after Juliano Marik, the first Captain-General of the Free Worlds League, the ninety-ton 'Mech was produced by Irian BattleMechs Unlimited at their Angell II facility. Designed as an all-purpose combatant capable of filling virtually any tactical role demanded of an assault 'Mech, the Juliano employs a distinctive mix of Inner Sphere and Clan technologies to achieve an excellent balance of firepower, protection, and mobility. Following twenty years of distinguished service as the signature unit of the Marik-Stewart Commonwealth, the Juliano was inherited by the reformed Free Worlds League Military, where it has become a mainstay of assault lances across the League's front-line formations.
BMJuliano_JLN5A.capabilities:
The Juliano achieves its versatility through an Irian Tonans Endo-Composite chassis powered by a Hermes 360 XL engine, giving the ninety-ton machine a respectable top speed of 64 kph for its weight class. Protection comes from over sixteen tons of Durallex Guardian II Light Ferro-Fibrous armor supplemented by CASE II equipment in both arms, ensuring ammunition detonations do not prove fatal. Engineers further reinforced the cockpit armor to improve pilot survivability in prolonged engagements.

The 'Mech's primary firepower centers on three Diverse Optics Sunbeam Extended-Range Large Lasers distributed across the torso sections, providing devastating long-range striking power. These are complemented by three Diverse Optics Sunfire Extended-Range Medium Lasers for intermediate engagements and four arm-mounted Clan-specification Pattern J6 Streak SRM-6 launchers that deliver punishing close-range salvos with exceptional ammunition efficiency. A specialized combat computer was installed on the advice of prototype test pilots to manage the significant heat generated by the laser battery, though inexperienced MechWarriors can still push the design to critical overheat by firing too aggressively. This combination of weapons allows the Juliano to remain effective across all engagement ranges and continue fighting long after ammunition-dependent opponents have exhausted their stores.
BMJuliano_JLN5A.history:
The Juliano's history is inextricably linked to the political fortunes of the Free Worlds League's successor states. Development began in the early thirty-second century within the Marik-Stewart Commonwealth, one of several states that emerged following the dissolution of the Free Worlds League during the Jihad. The Commonwealth's leadership sought to establish military self-sufficiency by producing a native assault BattleMech, and Irian BattleMechs Unlimited's facility on Angell II was tasked with the project.

Production commenced around 3116, and the Juliano quickly earned its place as the signature 'Mech of the realm. The Commonwealth jealously guarded its new creation, forbidding all export of the design. For roughly twenty years, the Juliano served as a symbol of Marik-Stewart military power and was deployed exclusively within Commonwealth forces.

The reformation of the Free Worlds League in the early 3140s brought the Juliano into broader service. The new FWLM inherited the design and maintained the export ban while assigning new-build Julianos to front-line formations, particularly the Tamarind Regulars tasked with operations along the Lyran border. The Eighth Tamarind Regulars particularly received large numbers of the design, pairing them with Awesomes in assault lance formations.

The Fourth Battle of Tamarind in 3142 provided the Juliano's first major combat debut under League colors. During fighting along the Zanzibar River at Point Bravo, a mixed assault lance of the Eighth Regulars equipped with Julianos engaged a Lyran Guards assault lance whose 'Mechs had already expended much of their ammunition in sustained combat. The engagement demonstrated the Juliano's defining tactical advantage: its ability to sustain combat long after ammunition-dependent opponents had spent their stores, tearing apart the Lyran formation in a devastating combination of laser and missile fire.

Beyond the League, Clan Wolf acquired a limited number of Julianos as salvage during its invasion of Marik-Stewart territory, assigning these captured machines to second-line Clusters. The introduction of the JLN-5B and JLN-5C variants in 3146 expanded the Juliano family, with Irian BattleMechs Unlimited demonstrating both the ability to simplify the design for increased production and to push it to its technological limits with full Clan-specification armament.
BMJuliano_JLN5A.deployment: The base JLN-5A represents the original production configuration fielded exclusively by the Marik-Stewart Commonwealth beginning in 3116. Its mixed-technology weapons suite pairs Inner Sphere lasers with Clan-specification Streak missile launchers, a combination that proved highly effective at sustaining combat after ammunition-dependent opponents had exhausted their stores. Export was forbidden by the Commonwealth and remains restricted under the reformed Free Worlds League. By 3140, the design was being assigned in large numbers to the Tamarind Regulars to support operations against the Lyran Commonwealth. Outside the League, only Clan Wolf fields substantial numbers, having acquired salvaged units during its invasion of Marik-Stewart territory.

The result is the most devastating variant in the Juliano family, a reflection of Irian BattleMechs Unlimited's growing capability to produce full Clan-technology weapon systems for the reformed Free Worlds League.

BMJupiter.overview:
The Jupiter was developed by Clan Jade Falcon during the waning years of the Civil War era, intended to serve as a cost-effective complement to the Turkina assault OmniMech. Khan Pryde directed the Falcon's Scientist and Technician Castes to design a new second-line assault 'Mech that could form the backbone of garrison Clusters, with a mandate for resource efficiency and rapid deployment. The design emerged from CJF Factory Zone 4 on Erewhon with suspicious speed, fueling rumors that the Scientist Caste had been developing the 'Mech covertly before revealing it to the warrior caste in late 3067.

Production began in 3068, with Jupiters appearing in large quantities along the Periphery border almost immediately. Built entirely from locally available components, the Jupiter proved a rugged and easily maintained assault platform, qualities that would later see it spread beyond Jade Falcon forces into mercenary and House armies throughout the post-Jihad Inner Sphere.
BMJupiter.capabilities:
The Jupiter is a 100-ton assault 'Mech designed around a long-range fire paradigm that allows its pilots to engage targets well before closing to direct combat range. The heart of this philosophy is a weapon suite combining two Type XX Extended Range PPCs with four Type DL Ultra-5 autocannons, providing a devastating volume of fire at extended distances. Two Series IV LRM-15 launchers add indirect fire capability and sustained pressure on advancing enemies. The "spike collar" Goshawk E-Series sensor suite, which can be raised or lowered depending on battlefield conditions, gives the Jupiter enhanced targeting data that makes the most of its ranged weaponry.

A Gorvachs 300 XL engine propels the massive design to a top speed of 54 km/h, trading speed for the ability to carry nineteen and a half tons of Raydient Series 5 armor, protection rivaled by few other designs in its weight class. The reliance on an extralight engine does create vulnerability to flanking attacks, but the Jupiter's arsenal ensures that few opponents survive long enough to exploit this weakness at range.

The design's deliberate emphasis on locally sourced, commonly available components gives it a logistical advantage that many more complex assault 'Mechs cannot match, allowing field technicians to keep Jupiters operational with minimal supply chain dependencies.
BMJupiter.history:
The Jupiter's development traces back to the eve of the Jihad, when Clan Jade Falcon sought to bolster its garrison forces with a capable assault 'Mech that could be produced without straining already-committed supply lines. CJF Factory Zone 4 on Erewhon was tasked with the design, and production commenced in 3068 with the 'Mech appearing along the Falcon's Periphery borders in significant numbers. The timing proved fortuitous, as second-line warriors defending Falcon worlds eagerly adopted the design.

The Jupiter's first major test came during the Hellion Tantrum of 3071–3072, when Clan Ice Hellion launched its ill-fated invasion of the Jade Falcon Occupation Zone. Before the assault, Jupiters had been concentrated among garrison Clusters, but the conflict demonstrated the design's combat effectiveness so convincingly that demand surged across all Falcon forces. Provisional Garrison Clusters equipped with Jupiters saw their firepower increase dramatically, delivering devastating defensive fire that helped break the Hellion advance.

Throughout the Jihad era, the Jupiter remained primarily a Jade Falcon weapon. The Clan successfully defended its exclusive possession through Trials of Possession, though reports from August 3073 placed Jupiters among Clan Hell's Horses forces during an attack on Thule, an acquisition the Falcons vigorously denied sanctioning. How the Horses obtained the assault design remains a matter of speculation among intelligence analysts.

The factory on Erewhon continued production through the early Dark Age, with newer variants entering service to keep the design relevant against evolving battlefield threats. In 3144, the factory was relocated from Erewhon to Alyina, though whether production continued uninterrupted at the new site remains uncertain. By the ilClan era, Clan Hell's Horses had assumed control of the facility, ensuring the Jupiter's continued service even as its original Falcon stewards saw their fortunes change dramatically.

The design's rugged construction and relatively simple logistics have also seen it spread beyond Clan forces, with mercenary commands and House armies acquiring examples through battlefield salvage and the post-Jihad arms trade. This proliferation stands as reflection of the Falcon Scientist Caste's original mandate: build something tough, effective, and easy to keep running.
BMJupiter.deployment: The standard Jupiter carries the original long-range weapons suite that defined the chassis from its introduction, combining heavy energy weapons with rapid-firing ballistic autocannons and missile launchers to create a devastating engagement platform at extended distances. The retractable sensor suite gives pilots enhanced targeting data to make the most of this arsenal. Jade Falcon garrison Clusters equipped with the standard Jupiter found it ideally suited to defensive operations where the design could exploit its weapons reach from prepared positions, delivering punishing fire on approaching enemies long before they could close to effective range.

BMKabuto_KBO7A.overview: The Kabuto is a twenty-ton BattleMech introduced in 3059 by Diplan 'Mechyards on Aix-la-Chapelle for the Draconis Combine Mustered Soldiery. Designed to fill the Combine's critical shortage of effective light BattleMechs, the Kabuto was purpose-built for fast reconnaissance, lightning raids, and flanking attacks in support of the combined-arms doctrine the DCMS adopted following the Clan Invasion. Named for the elaborate helmet-like armor encasing the 'Mech's head assembly, the Kabuto delivered exceptional speed and maximum armor protection at a cost of under 2.5 million C-bills, making it one of the most affordable front-line light designs in DCMS service. The design has remained a fixture of Combine light reconnaissance lances from the Civil War era through the ilClan period.
BMKabuto_KBO7A.capabilities:
The Kabuto achieves its remarkable performance through a combination of advanced materials and focused design philosophy. A Chariot Type 1a endo steel chassis saves critical weight while maintaining structural integrity, and a Leenex 140 XL extralight engine propels the twenty-ton 'Mech to a top speed exceeding 118 kilometers per hour. This weight-saving approach allows the Kabuto to mount four and a half tons of Starshield A armor (the maximum possible for its tonnage class) making it exceptionally difficult to disable for a light 'Mech.

The Kabuto's armament consists of a pair of Guided Technologies 2nd Gen Streak SRM-4 launchers, providing devastating close-range firepower with near-perfect accuracy courtesy of the Streak targeting system. This simplified weapons loadout is a deliberate design choice, dramatically easing field maintenance and logistics by requiring only a single ammunition type. A Sipher CommCon SCU-4 communications suite and Cat's Eyes 5 targeting system provide solid battlefield awareness.

The Kabuto's primary weakness lies in its ammunition dependency and the short effective range of its missile systems, which can limit tactical flexibility in prolonged engagements or when facing opponents that maintain stand-off distance. The lack of jump jets further restricts the design's ability to exploit complex terrain for flanking maneuvers.
BMKabuto_KBO7A.history:
The Kabuto's development traces directly to the cultural and military upheaval caused by the Clan Invasion. Prior to 3049, the Draconis Combine's warrior culture dismissed light BattleMechs as beneath the honor of a proper MechWarrior. Bushido demanded toe-to-toe combat, and machines that could not stand against heavier opponents were considered unworthy. The devastating Clan offensives shattered this orthodoxy, as Combine warriors found themselves outmatched in traditional engagements by opponents with superior technology and training. Only by embracing Theodore Kurita's combined-arms reforms could the DCMS hope to contest the Clan advance, and light 'Mechs became essential for fast reconnaissance, raids, and flanking attacks in coordination with all available assets.

Diplan 'Mechyards, already producing the successful Hitman BattleMech on Aix-la-Chapelle, adapted its existing chassis design for the Kabuto program. The design teams deliberately modeled their development process on the Hitman's success, even arranging for student MechWarriors at the Sun Zhang Military Academy on New Samarkand to field-test the prototype in the same fashion that had validated the Hitman years earlier. Production commenced at the Aix-la-Chapelle facility, with initial units issued to DCMS formations that had suffered light 'Mech losses during Operation Bulldog in 3059.

The Kabuto proved popular with DCMS light BattleMech pilots throughout the Civil War era and into the Jihad, its combination of speed, protection, and low cost ensuring a steady demand from front-line commands. During the Ghost Bear-Combine War, however, frontline experience revealed the limitations of its missile armament against Clan OmniMechs. Warriors who grew weary of circling opponents while waiting for missile locks began modifying their Kabutos in the field, most commonly swapping the launchers for light energy weapons to gain range and eliminate ammunition dependency.

Production at Aix-la-Chapelle continued through the Dark Age and into the ilClan era, with the Kabuto remaining a fixture of DCMS light reconnaissance lances. The design's affordability and ease of maintenance ensured that even during periods of industrial disruption, the Kabuto could be kept operational in large numbers, fulfilling the combined-arms role that Theodore Kurita's reforms had originally envisioned for Combine light 'Mechs.
BMKabuto_KBO7A.deployment: This variant is the original production model of the Kabuto line, mounting twin Streak SRM-4 launchers as its sole armament. This focused missile loadout gives the design devastating close-range alpha strikes with near-perfect accuracy, but limits its tactical flexibility to engagements within short range brackets. DCMS commanders typically deploy this variant in pairs or full lances, using the design's exceptional speed to execute flanking runs against heavier targets before withdrawing to reload. The variant saw extensive service replacing light 'Mechs lost during Operation Bulldog and remained the standard Kabuto configuration through the Civil War era until frontline experience during the Ghost Bear-Combine War prompted widespread field modifications.

This widespread refit replaces both Guided Technologies Streak launchers with a pair of Lord's Light light particle projection cannons, one mounted in each side torso. The light PPCs offer comparable damage concentration at twice the effective range while eliminating ammunition dependency entirely. The freed tonnage from the removed ammunition bin accommodates an additional heat sink in the head to manage the energy weapons' thermal output.

BMKarhu_A.overview: The Karhu was introduced in 3079 as the first Clan-technology OmniMech produced by Odin Manufacturing for the Ghost Bear Dominion. Named after the Finnish word for "bear," the sixty-five-ton heavy OmniMech was designed to fill the Dominion's need for a fast cavalry platform built with the latest Clan technology. Odin Manufacturing, based on the former Free Rasalhague Republic world of Orestes, won a competitive contract against their chief rival Bergan Industries in 3077, delivering a design that earned a fierce reputation as a frontline cavalry 'Mech despite lingering questions about its electronics reliability. The Karhu remains a symbol of the Dominion's industrial ambitions and a mainstay of its frontline clusters.
BMKarhu_A.capabilities:
The Karhu is built around a Beowulf 4 Enhanced endo steel chassis powered by a Pitban 325-rated extra-light engine, giving the sixty-five-ton OmniMech a respectable top speed of eighty-six kilometers per hour. Ten and a half tons of Compound A2F ferro-fibrous armor provide solid protection for its weight class, while twelve fixed double heat sinks manage baseline waste heat across its varied configurations. This combination of speed, protection, and Clan-grade construction leaves an impressive thirty tons of available pod space for mission-specific equipment.

The Prime configuration reflects the design's appeal to the KungsArmé tradition of physical combat, mounting a retractable blade sculpted into a fearsome three-pronged claw alongside a plasma cannon in the right arm. An ER PPC and ER medium laser in the left arm provide ranged firepower, while improved jump jets grant exceptional battlefield mobility. However, Odin's relative inexperience with Clan technology has manifested in documented electronics reliability issues. The firm reused the Beowulf's proven Dash-2 Standard communications system and Blade 12 targeting computer to save development time, but intermittent compatibility glitches with Clan-manufactured components have plagued the design in the field, a problem technicians attribute to fundamental incompatibilities between Inner Sphere electronics architectures and Clan equipment.
BMKarhu_A.history:
The Karhu's development was born from the merger of the Free Rasalhague Republic and the Ghost Bear Dominion, which opened Clan technology to Inner Sphere manufacturers for the first time. For Odin Manufacturing, the merger represented both opportunity and challenge. Their Orestes production facility had been damaged by Word of Blake raids in the late 3060s, and the demands of the Jihad forced them to continue producing existing Inner Sphere designs while simultaneously planning their transition to Clan-technology manufacturing. By 3077, when the Dominion announced a competition for a new heavy OmniMech, Odin was finally ready to make the leap.

The competition between Odin and their rival Bergan Industries proved fierce. Odin identified Bergan as their primary competitor and designed the Karhu specifically to outperform whatever Bergan produced, while simultaneously launching a marketing campaign rooted in Rasalhagian nationalism aimed at former KungsArme officers within the Dominion touman. This strategy proved effective, and Odin won the contract in 3079 with a design that was widely acknowledged as technologically superior to Bergan's competing entry, the Arcas.

First deployed in 3079, the Karhu arrived too late to participate in Operation SCOUR but rapidly became a fixture in the Dominion's frontline clusters. Paired frequently with the Ursus II, the Karhu earned a reputation as a cavalry 'Mech, flanking opponents while heavier designs drew fire at close range. During the Jihad's final stages and the early Republic era, Karhus were concentrated in frontline formations alongside Vultures and other OmniMechs, forming the mobile striking arm of Dominion combined-arms doctrine.

The design's success has not been without controversy. Competition between Odin and Bergan Industries has grown increasingly bitter, with Odin officials publicly disparaging Bergan as "that Capellan company with their Combine workers." Requests for Orestes-built 'Mechs are noticeably higher among Rasalhagian warriors as a result of this rivalry. The Ghost Bear Council has expressed concern over this infighting and has requested that representatives of both companies exercise restraint, though reports suggest the merchants are too deeply engaged in their competition to easily comply.

The Karhu's documented electronics reliability issues have been a persistent concern throughout its service history. Technicians have traced the intermittent glitches to fundamental incompatibilities between the Inner Sphere-designed communications and targeting systems and the Clan-manufactured components they interface with, citing similar problems on Beowulfs retrofitted with Clan equipment. BMKatanaCrockett_CRK50032.overview: The Katana is an eighty-five-ton assault BattleMech derived from the Star League-era Crockett, created when ComStar transferred a cache of downgraded Crocketts to the Draconis Combine as part of Operation Rosebud in 3035. The 'Mechs were delivered through the Blankenburg Technologies storage facility on Soul, which Primus Myndo Waterly handed over to Independence Weaponry under the guise of a lease agreement. After examining and making minor modifications to the Crocketts, IW rechristened them as Katanas and deployed them to replace Chargers in several DCMS line units. The Katana quickly established itself as a valued heavy assault platform, particularly after the development of C3 computer technology enabled coordinated lance operations. When the Soul facility's lease expired and reverted to Blankenburg Technologies, the company retained the former IW engineering team and entered into a technology-sharing agreement to continue Katana production and development.
BMKatanaCrockett_CRK50032.capabilities:
The Katana shares the fundamental design architecture of its Crockett parent, retaining the same Geometric 530 Hard Core chassis, Strand 255 fusion engine, and Geotec 300 jump jets. This provides identical ground speed of fifty-four kilometers per hour and ninety meters of jumping capability. Twelve and a half tons of CarboStrand armor matches the protection level of the original Crockett design, and the same GRPNTR Groundpainter 5 communications system and Scope 30 RNDST targeting-tracking system handle battlefield awareness.

Where the Katana diverges from its predecessor is in its weapons fit and heat management. The extended-range large lasers are replaced with standard Magna Mk III large lasers, a practical concession to the Combine's manufacturing capabilities in the 3030s. The Blankenburg LB 10-X autocannon is retained in the left torso, fed by a two-ton ammunition bin, preserving the versatility of standard and cluster munitions. Twin Holly SRM-6 launchers in the side torsos and two Dodd small lasers mounted co-axially with the large lasers round out the armament. The most significant compromise is the substitution of twenty standard heat sinks for the original fifteen double units, substantially reducing the 'Mech's ability to sustain high rates of fire and forcing pilots to manage their heat output more carefully during extended engagements.
BMKatanaCrockett_CRK50032.history:
The Katana's origins trace directly to ComStar's Operation Rosebud, a diplomatic initiative designed to strengthen ties with the Draconis Combine during the 3030s. Primus Myndo Waterly authorized the transfer of the Blankenburg Technologies storage facility on Soul to the Combine in 3035 as a gesture of good faith. The facility, nominally leased to Independence Weaponry to maintain appearances, contained not only a cache of Crocketts but also a trove of lostech weapons and components that IW reverse-engineered for distribution to other Combine manufacturers.

Independence Weaponry spent several months examining the Crocketts before making minor modifications and redesignating them as Katanas. The rechristening served the dual purpose of obscuring the 'Mechs' ComStar origins and asserting Combine ownership of the design. Deployed to replace underperforming Chargers in several DCMS mobile line units, the Katana proved effective enough that it quickly became a mainstay in heavier formations throughout the Combine's military structure.

The introduction of C3 computer technology prompted Independence Weaponry to develop specialized variants in 3057, including the CRK-5003-C with a C3 slave unit and the CRK-5003-CM carrying a C3 master computer. These configurations enhanced the Katana's value as a lance coordination platform within the DCMS's increasingly network-centric doctrine. When the lease on the Soul facility expired and Blankenburg Technologies resumed direct control, the company recognized the value of IW's work and hired the entire Katana engineering team, entering into a technology-sharing agreement to ensure continuity of production.

This arrangement bore fruit during the Jihad era with the CRK-5003-CJ variant in 3071, which upgraded the design with improved jump jets and double heat sinks, finally restoring the thermal management capabilities lost when the original Crocketts were downgraded. The Katana continued to evolve well into the Dark Age, with the CRK-5006-1 variant fielded by the secretive Hikage, the Combine's shadowy special operations unit. This advanced configuration incorporated a Gauss rifle, Streak SRM-6 launchers with CASE II protection, and improved jump jets, representing a substantial capability leap that demonstrated the Draconis Combine's ongoing commitment to developing the Katana as a distinct platform rather than merely a derivative of the Crockett.
BMKatanaCrockett_CRK50032.deployment: This variant is the base Katana configuration, representing the modified Crocketts transferred to the Draconis Combine through Operation Rosebud in 3035. This variant substitutes standard Magna Mk III large lasers for the Crockett's extended-range models and replaces the fifteen double heat sinks with twenty single units, reflecting the Combine's manufacturing constraints of the era. The LB 10-X autocannon, SRM-6 launchers, jump jets, and armor protection remain unchanged from the parent design. The Katana designation and these modifications effectively created a distinct identity for the Combine's version of the venerable Crockett assault 'Mech.

BMKheper_KHP7R.overview: The Kheper is a fifty-five-ton medium BattleMech secretly developed in the mid-thirty-second century by the Blessed Order, a renegade faction within ComStar led by Malcolm Buhl. Designed as a frontline combatant for the clandestine resurrection of the Com Guard's First Division, the 'Mech was manufactured by the New Earth Trading Company, a corporate front operated by ComStar since the early Succession Wars. Production began around 3135, with construction lines concealed among NETC's extensive civilian manufacturing operations on New Earth. The Kheper was engineered as a versatile generalist intended for ease of maintenance and logistical simplicity, and it has since gone on to serve multiple masters as control of its production facility has changed hands.
BMKheper_KHP7R.capabilities:
Built around a Core Tek 275 XL engine mounted in a NETC Kappa endo steel frame, the Kheper achieves a respectable top speed of eighty-six kilometers per hour for a fifty-five-ton design. Nine tons of Wall Type 8 light ferro-fibrous armor provide solid protection while maintaining the design's emphasis on weight efficiency, and CASE II systems in the right arm and left torso safeguard against catastrophic ammunition detonation.

The Kheper's weapons suite reflects its generalist philosophy, covering engagement ranges from long to close quarters. An M-7 Gauss rifle mounted in one arm serves as the primary weapon, delivering devastating kinetic impacts at range, while a Holly multi-missile launcher in the opposing arm provides flexible fire support with both long-range and short-range missile loads. For closer engagements, a Martell extended range medium laser and Martell-X medium X-pulse laser deliver concentrated energy fire, supplemented by a Blankenburg small variable-speed pulse laser for point defense and anti-infantry work.

The absence of jump jets represents the design's primary limitation, restricting the Kheper's tactical flexibility in broken or urban terrain where vertical mobility would otherwise allow it to exploit cover and elevation advantages.
BMKheper_KHP7R.history:
The Kheper's origins trace to a crucial moment in the twilight of ComStar's existence as a military power. In 3128, agents of the Blessed Order infiltrated a Republic of the Sphere data depot on Terra and stole advanced technical specifications from the Word of Blake's Manei Domini program, including extensive data on the Celestial series OmniMechs. Malcolm Buhl, the Blessed Order's leader, commissioned the New Earth Trading Company to develop new BattleMech designs from this stolen data, exploiting NETC's long history as a ComStar-controlled corporate front to conceal military production within the company's vast civilian manufacturing operations.

The Kheper and its heavier counterpart, the Uraeus, were the primary fruits of this clandestine program. The Com Guard's rebuilt First Division deployed both designs as core components when it took the field, fighting alongside the division until its final engagement against the Republic Armed Forces on Epsilon Eridani. The Com Guards' defeat there brought the Kheper to the Republic's attention, and the subsequent seizure of NETC's New Earth facilities placed the production line firmly under RAF control. The Republic nationalized the company, folding Kheper production into its own military infrastructure.

Re-staffed under new management, NETC continued producing the Kheper for the Republic Armed Forces. RAF strategists quickly recognized the design's value for raiding operations beyond the Fortress Republic's walls, as the 'Mech's obscurity meant opponents had virtually no intelligence on its capabilities. The Kheper proved a popular machine among raiding parties, its straightforward construction keeping it operational even during extended deployments far from Republic supply lines.

NETC's New Earth facility has a long and complex ownership history stretching back to the Star League era, when it operated under the Terran Hegemony. The factory passed through independent control during the early Succession Wars before being absorbed into the Lyran Commonwealth and later the Federated Commonwealth. The Word of Blake seized the facility during the Jihad, and though it was believed destroyed during New Earth's liberation in 3078, the factory was rebuilt under Republic of the Sphere control. With the collapse of Fortress Republic and the rise of the ilClan era, the facility and its Kheper production line have passed into the hands of Clan Jade Falcon, ensuring this once-secret design continues to see service under new masters.
BMKheper_KHP7R.deployment: This variant is the sole production variant of the Kheper. The design entered service with the Com Guard's rebuilt First Division and saw its first combat during operations on Epsilon Eridani. Following the Republic Armed Forces' acquisition of the production line, this variant proved well suited to the RAF's operational needs, where its straightforward maintenance requirements and reliance on widely sourced parts kept it operational during extended deployments far from established supply lines. No additional factory variants have been produced.

BMKingCrab_KGC000.overview:
The King Crab was designed in 2741 by Cosara Weaponries at the direct request of General Aleksandr Kerensky for an assault 'Mech capable of crippling or destroying another BattleMech in a single salvo. Filling the role of a devastating close-range combatant, the hundred-ton King Crab earned its fearsome reputation through the raw destructive power of its twin super-heavy autocannons, mounted in distinctive claw-like arm housings that gave the design its name. Though initially envisioned as a potential command vehicle, the King Crab proved less suited to that capacity than expected, a role ultimately filled by the Atlas.

Production was centered at Cosara facilities on Mars and Northwind under Star League authority, with the design seeing widespread service in the SLDF. The devastation of the Succession Wars reduced the King Crab to near-extinction, but ComStar's secret preservation of the Mars factory ensured the design's survival and eventual return to mass production in the thirty-first century.
BMKingCrab_KGC000.capabilities:
The King Crab's tactical doctrine is straightforward: close with the enemy and deliver overwhelming firepower. Its primary armament of twin Deathgiver Autocannon/20s represents one of the most destructive weapon pairings ever mounted on a BattleMech, capable of stripping the armor from virtually any opponent in a few devastating salvos. The autocannons are housed within reinforced arm assemblies fitted with simple hand actuators that function as protective cowlings, giving the 'Mech its distinctive crab-like silhouette and the appearance of pincers opening and closing in combat. A Simpson-15 LRM launcher and Exostar large laser provide secondary fire support at longer ranges, ensuring the King Crab is not entirely helpless during its approach to engagement range.

Sixteen tons of Aldis X ferro-fibrous armor provide solid, evenly distributed protection across the chassis, with CASE safeguarding the ammunition stores from catastrophic detonation. The arms represent a notable vulnerability, however, as an internal hit to either limb can knock an autocannon out of the fight entirely. The King Crab's most significant limitation is its dependence on ammunition; each autocannon draws from a mere five-round magazine, giving pilots limited sustained firepower before running dry. Combined with a modest top speed of 54 kilometers per hour and a well-earned reputation as a maintenance-intensive design, the King Crab demands careful tactical employment and reliable logistics to realize its devastating potential.
BMKingCrab_KGC000.history:
The King Crab's origins trace to 2741, when General Aleksandr Kerensky personally commissioned Cosara Weaponries to design an assault 'Mech of unmatched destructive power. The resulting design exceeded expectations, and production commenced at Cosara's facilities on Mars and Northwind. The King Crab served with distinction in the SLDF throughout the final decades of the Star League, though it never displaced the Atlas as the preferred command vehicle for senior officers. When the Amaris Civil War erupted in 2767, Republican forces destroyed the Mars factory, leaving only the Northwind facility operational.

The Exodus of 2784 dealt the King Crab a severe blow, as General Kerensky's departing forces took the vast majority of existing King Crabs with them, including the entire production run of the prototype KGC-010. The Northwind factory's destruction in 2786, an early casualty of the First Succession War, effectively ended new production in the Inner Sphere. The King Crab's relatively simple construction meant surviving examples were easier to maintain than many Star League-era designs, but attrition took its toll. By the close of the Third Succession War, only a handful remained in active service with the Great Houses, each one a prized and jealously guarded asset.

ComStar's seizure of Terra through Operation Silver Shield proved critical to the King Crab's survival. The order's technicians repaired and mothballed the damaged Mars factory, secretly stockpiling King Crabs for future use. By the early thirty-first century, ComStar contracted Cosara Weaponries to quietly resume production to replenish their aging reserves, equipping the Com Guards with refurbished and newly built King Crabs. The looming threat of the Clan Invasion spurred the development of the KGC-001 "Clanbuster" variant in 3052, which proved so successful at the Battle of Tukayyid that ComStar authorized general market sales from both the Mars and Northwind plants, with Cosara receiving a share of profits.

The Word of Blake's conquest of Terra and subsequent seizure of the Northwind factory in 3069 upended King Crab production once again. The Blakists retooled the Northwind line to produce their own variants, including the jump-capable KGC-008 for Protectorate forces. ComStar responded with an uncharacteristically bold move, dispatching a mercenary espionage team to infiltrate the Northwind facility and steal the new design specifications. These plans were then offered to StarCorps Industries, who eagerly began producing the KGC-007 at their Son Hoa plant for ComStar, the Lyran Alliance, and the Federated Suns alike.

The post-Jihad era saw continued evolution of the King Crab. StarCorps relocated their production line from Son Hoa to Loburg in the late 3090s, introducing the modernized KGC-009 in 3104 to meet the demands of the Lyran Commonwealth Armed Forces. The design proved popular with senior Lyran officers despite its continued ammunition dependency. Cosara Weaponries eventually returned the Mars facility to active production under Republic of the Sphere oversight, developing the KGC-011 with its revolutionary XXL engine for dramatically improved battlefield mobility. By the ilClan era, the King Crab remained a respected and feared assault platform, its production split between Cosara's historic Mars facility and StarCorps' Loburg plant, ensuring the design's continued presence on battlefields across the Inner Sphere.
BMKingCrab_KGC000.deployment: The original production model of the King Crab, this variant entered service in 2743 as the definitive expression of General Kerensky's vision for a single-salvo assault 'Mech. Armed with twin Deathgiver Autocannon/20s backed by a Simpson-15 LRM launcher and Exostar large laser, the design delivered devastating short-range firepower while maintaining modest long-range capability. Sixteen tons of Aldis X ferro-fibrous armor with CASE provided excellent protection for its era. Production ceased when the Mars factory was destroyed in 2767 and the Northwind facility followed in 2786, though ComStar preserved and later reactivated the Mars line for Com Guard service.

BMKingCrab_KGC0000Toro.overview:

BMKingCrab_KGC0000Toro.capabilities:
The King Crab's tactical doctrine is straightforward: close with the enemy and deliver overwhelming firepower. Its primary armament of twin Deathgiver Autocannon/20s represents one of the most destructive weapon pairings ever mounted on a BattleMech, capable of stripping the armor from virtually any opponent in a few devastating salvos. The autocannons are housed within reinforced arm assemblies fitted with simple hand actuators that function as protective cowlings, giving the 'Mech its distinctive crab-like silhouette and the appearance of pincers opening and closing in combat. A Simpson-15 LRM launcher and Exostar large laser provide secondary fire support at longer ranges, ensuring the King Crab is not entirely helpless during its approach to engagement range.

Sixteen tons of Aldis X ferro-fibrous armor provide solid, evenly distributed protection across the chassis, with CASE safeguarding the ammunition stores from catastrophic detonation. The arms represent a notable vulnerability, however, as an internal hit to either limb can knock an autocannon out of the fight entirely. The King Crab's most significant limitation is its dependence on ammunition; each autocannon draws from a mere five-round magazine, giving pilots limited sustained firepower before running dry. Combined with a modest top speed of 54 kilometers per hour and a well-earned reputation as a maintenance-intensive design, the King Crab demands careful tactical employment and reliable logistics to realize its devastating potential.

BMKingCrab_KGC007.overview:
The King Crab was designed in 2741 by Cosara Weaponries at the direct request of General Aleksandr Kerensky for an assault 'Mech capable of crippling or destroying another BattleMech in a single salvo. Filling the role of a devastating close-range combatant, the hundred-ton King Crab earned its fearsome reputation through the raw destructive power of its twin super-heavy autocannons, mounted in distinctive claw-like arm housings that gave the design its name. Though initially envisioned as a potential command vehicle, the King Crab proved less suited to that capacity than expected, a role ultimately filled by the Atlas.

Production was centered at Cosara facilities on Mars and Northwind under Star League authority, with the design seeing widespread service in the SLDF. The devastation of the Succession Wars reduced the King Crab to near-extinction, but ComStar's secret preservation of the Mars factory ensured the design's survival and eventual return to mass production in the thirty-first century.
BMKingCrab_KGC007.capabilities:
The King Crab's tactical doctrine is straightforward: close with the enemy and deliver overwhelming firepower. Its primary armament of twin Deathgiver Autocannon/20s represents one of the most destructive weapon pairings ever mounted on a BattleMech, capable of stripping the armor from virtually any opponent in a few devastating salvos. The autocannons are housed within reinforced arm assemblies fitted with simple hand actuators that function as protective cowlings, giving the 'Mech its distinctive crab-like silhouette and the appearance of pincers opening and closing in combat. A Simpson-15 LRM launcher and Exostar large laser provide secondary fire support at longer ranges, ensuring the King Crab is not entirely helpless during its approach to engagement range.

Sixteen tons of Aldis X ferro-fibrous armor provide solid, evenly distributed protection across the chassis, with CASE safeguarding the ammunition stores from catastrophic detonation. The arms represent a notable vulnerability, however, as an internal hit to either limb can knock an autocannon out of the fight entirely. The King Crab's most significant limitation is its dependence on ammunition; each autocannon draws from a mere five-round magazine, giving pilots limited sustained firepower before running dry. Combined with a modest top speed of 54 kilometers per hour and a well-earned reputation as a maintenance-intensive design, the King Crab demands careful tactical employment and reliable logistics to realize its devastating potential.
