Production began in 3064, initially yielding the LGH-4Y model without the advanced targeting computer that would later define the design. Almost immediately, the intelligence operation that would transform the Lightray was underway. Taking advantage of the chaos created by the FedCom Civil War, Word of Blake ROM agents stole targeting computer technology from the Federated Suns, itself reverse-engineered from captured Clan equipment. The Precentor Martial wasted no time ordering the Lightray production lines retooled, and the LGH-4W with its integrated targeting computer became the standard production model from 3065 onward.

The Lightray saw its primary service during the Jihad, when the Word of Blake unleashed its forces across the Inner Sphere. As a Blakist-exclusive design produced solely on Terra, the Lightray equipped Militia divisions across multiple fronts, with its high speed and accurate weaponry proving well-suited to the hit-and-run tactics employed by Word of Blake forces. Later variants incorporating C3i and improved C3 computers reflected the Blakists’ emphasis on networked warfare doctrines.

The design’s fortunes declined sharply with the fall of the Word of Blake at the conclusion of the Jihad. With Martinson Armaments’ Terra-based production facilities falling under Republic of the Sphere control, Lightray production appears to have ceased entirely. The Republic showed no interest in continuing manufacture of the distinctly Blakist design, and the factory’s production lines were not reactivated for the Lightray. Surviving examples continued to serve in scattered former-Blakist units and the occasional mercenary command, but the design effectively became extinct as a production ’Mech following the establishment of the Republic.
BMLightray_LGH4Y.deployment: This variant is the original Lightray configuration produced in 3064, predating the ROM intelligence operation that secured targeting computer technology from the Federated Suns. Without the targeting computer, the available weight was instead allocated to a pair of SRM-2 launchers and a single ton of ammunition, supplementing the same laser array found on later models. MechWarriors quickly noted the variant’s limited effective engagement range, and the design was soon superseded once the retooled LGH-4W entered production.

BMLightray_LGH5W.overview:
The Lightray is a Word of Blake medium BattleMech designed by Martinson Armaments at their Australia facility on Terra. Commissioned by the Precentor Martial in the early 3060s, the fifty-five-ton design originated as a heavy scout platform capable of extreme speeds while carrying meaningful armor protection and weaponry. Martinson Armaments, already experienced with BattleMech production through the Spartan and Initiate designs, produced the first Lightrays in 3064.

The Lightray's incorporation of an advanced targeting computer, acquired through a Word of Blake intelligence operation, significantly enhanced the design's combat effectiveness and became its defining feature. Produced exclusively on Terra, the Lightray became a signature medium-weight design of the Word of Blake Militia during the late Civil War era and throughout the Jihad.
BMLightray_LGH5W.capabilities:
The Lightray's defining characteristic is its exceptional speed for a fifty-five-ton BattleMech. Powered by an enormous LTV 385 XL extralight engine (the largest that can possibly be fitted to a chassis of its weight class) the design achieves a top speed of nearly 120 kilometers per hour in open terrain. This extraordinary mobility makes it one of the fastest medium 'Mechs ever fielded, easily outpacing most designs in its weight category. The trade-off for this speed is the absence of jump jets, limiting the Lightray's maneuverability in close terrain.

The 'Mech's armament centers on a Tronel XIII large pulse laser linked to a Scope 3580 targeting computer, making it devastatingly accurate even at high speeds. Two Diverse Optics extended-range medium lasers and a single extended-range small laser supplement this primary weapon, all benefiting from the targeting computer's enhanced accuracy. While the Lightray carries fewer weapons than many medium designs, its hit rate is significantly higher than its peers. The Geometric 33B endo steel frame and over ten tons of Strasbourg Armaments ferro-fibrous armor provide solid protection, ensuring the 'Mech can survive the engagements its speed brings it into.

BMLinebacker_A.overview: The Linebacker was commissioned in 3052 by Clan Wolf Khans to address a critical gap in their heavy OmniMech roster. The venerable Timber Wolf, while devastating in stand-up engagements, struggled to keep pace with lighter Star-mates during running battles, limiting the tactical flexibility of front-line Clusters. Designed to pair the firepower expected of a sixty-five-ton OmniMech with the speed of designs ten tons lighter, the Linebacker was intended to supplement and eventually replace the Timber Wolf in Wolf offensive formations. Its distinctive hunched profile, said to resemble the players of ancient Terran American Football, earned it the codename that became its official designation. Though its Warden origins initially limited acceptance among Crusader Wolves, the Linebacker has proven itself across multiple theaters and Clans, establishing a reputation as one of the fastest heavy OmniMechs in production.
BMLinebacker_A.capabilities:
The Linebacker achieves its remarkable speed through a Heavy Force 390-rated XL engine, propelling the sixty-five-ton OmniMech to a top speed of ninety-seven kilometers per hour. This engine choice is the defining trade-off of the design, consuming significant mass that would otherwise be available for weapons and equipment. The result is 17.5 tons of pod space, roughly ten tons less than the Timber Wolf it was designed to complement. The Type W4 Endo Steel frame provides structural savings, while ten tons of Composite A-4 ferro-fibrous armor delivers respectable protection for a 'Mech expected to operate at the leading edge of an advance.

In its primary configuration, the Linebacker mounts a pair of ER PPCs that deliver devastating firepower at extreme range, backed by an LRM-5 launcher for supplementary bombardment. A Streak SRM-4 provides efficient close-range punch, while a rear-mounted ER Small Laser discourages pursuit. This loadout allows the Linebacker to engage effectively while maintaining the speed to choose its engagements. The low-slung, hunched torso profile provides an exceptionally stable firing platform, enabling accurate fire even at high speeds. Common configurations either exploit the Linebacker's speed to maintain standoff range while sniping, or leverage that same velocity to rapidly close distance and overwhelm enemy positions.
BMLinebacker_A.history:
The Linebacker was born from battlefield necessity during the Clan Invasion. Commissioned by Khans Ward and Kerensky in 3052, the design entered production at Wolf Clan Site 2 on Strana Mechty and WC Site 1 on Arc-Royal. A Trinary formed from the first production run deployed to Tukayyid with Gamma Galaxy, where the Linebacker saw its baptism of fire against ComStar defenders. Though the design performed admirably, the upheaval of the Refusal War and the Crusader Wolves' disdain for what they viewed as a Warden creation prevented the Linebacker from appearing in significant numbers until the mid-3060s.

Before the Refusal War, the Wolves had shared the Linebacker design with Clans Snow Raven and Coyote. As Wolf combat losses mounted in the years that followed, the design spread further through Clan politics and warfare. Clan Hell's Horses and the Jade Falcons acquired Linebackers through various means, while fighting on Lum allowed the Steel Vipers to seize several examples, many of which later fell to the Cloud Cobras following the Viper absorption on Homer.

Clan Wolf proper did not replace Linebackers lost during the Jihad, and the design became a common sight only among the Wolves-in-Exile, who maintained constant production at their Arc-Royal facilities. The loss of Arc-Royal to the Jade Falcons forced the Exiles to scramble, eventually relocating production to fall-back facilities on Donegal under the Assault Tech Industries banner.

The Linebacker experienced a dramatic resurgence when Khan Alaric Ward ordered the design back into mass production for the Wolf Empire. W-12 Facilities on Zosma joined the production effort as the Linebacker was recast as a mainstay of the Wolf Empire's heavy BattleMech forces, serving alongside the Timber Wolf, Warwolf, and Crossbow as the spearpoint of the Empire's advance toward Terra. During the conquest of the Republic Remnant, Linebackers of the 103rd Wolf Guard Striker Cluster played a decisive role in the May 3149 Battle of Alhena, where their superior speed allowed them to outflank Republic artillery positions and overrun defensive emplacements that had stalled a conventional assault.
BMLinebacker_A.deployment: Alternate Configuration A mirrors the armament philosophy of the Timber Wolf Prime, mounting paired ER Large Lasers as primary weapons alongside LRM-5 and LRM-15 launchers for sustained long-range bombardment. Two ER Medium Lasers round out the loadout for closer engagements. This configuration delivers considerable long-distance damage through a missile-heavy approach, though the increased heat burden of sustained fire requires careful management. The A configuration is frequently deployed in fire support Stars where the Linebacker's speed allows rapid repositioning between bombardment positions.
BMLinebacker_A.manufacturer: WC Site 1|Wolf Clan Site 2|Assault Tech Industries|W-12 Facilities

This loadout allows the Linebacker to engage effectively while maintaining the speed to choose its engagements. The low-slung, hunched torso profile provides an exceptionally stable firing platform, enabling accurate fire even at high speeds. Common configurations either exploit the Linebacker's speed to maintain standoff range while sniping, or leverage that same velocity to rapidly close distance and overwhelm enemy positions.
BMLinebacker_E.history:
The Linebacker was born from battlefield necessity during the Clan Invasion. Commissioned by Khans Ward and Kerensky in 3052, the design entered production at Wolf Clan Site 2 on Strana Mechty and WC Site 1 on Arc-Royal. A Trinary formed from the first production run deployed to Tukayyid with Gamma Galaxy, where the Linebacker saw its baptism of fire against ComStar defenders. Though the design performed admirably, the upheaval of the Refusal War and the Crusader Wolves' disdain for what they viewed as a Warden creation prevented the Linebacker from appearing in significant numbers until the mid-3060s.

Before the Refusal War, the Wolves had shared the Linebacker design with Clans Snow Raven and Coyote. As Wolf combat losses mounted in the years that followed, the design spread further through Clan politics and warfare. Clan Hell's Horses and the Jade Falcons acquired Linebackers through various means, while fighting on Lum allowed the Steel Vipers to seize several examples, many of which later fell to the Cloud Cobras following the Viper absorption on Homer.

Clan Wolf proper did not replace Linebackers lost during the Jihad, and the design became a common sight only among the Wolves-in-Exile, who maintained constant production at their Arc-Royal facilities. The loss of Arc-Royal to the Jade Falcons forced the Exiles to scramble, eventually relocating production to fall-back facilities on Donegal under the Assault Tech Industries banner.

The Linebacker experienced a dramatic resurgence when Khan Alaric Ward ordered the design back into mass production for the Wolf Empire. W-12 Facilities on Zosma joined the production effort as the Linebacker was recast as a mainstay of the Wolf Empire's heavy BattleMech forces, serving alongside the Timber Wolf, Warwolf, and Crossbow as the spearpoint of the Empire's advance toward Terra. During the conquest of the Republic Remnant, Linebackers of the 103rd Wolf Guard Striker Cluster played a decisive role in the May 3149 Battle of Alhena, where their superior speed allowed them to outflank Republic artillery positions and overrun defensive emplacements that had stalled a conventional assault.
BMLinebacker_E.deployment: Alternate Configuration E leverages the flexibility of Advanced Tactical Missile technology, mounting a pair of ATM-6 launchers with magazine capacity for multiple ammunition types. An ER Large Laser provides consistent direct fire support, while a Light Active Probe enhances the configuration's reconnaissance capability. The ATM launchers allow MechWarriors to select ammunition optimized for the engagement range, from extended-range bombardment to devastating short-range high-explosive salvos, making this configuration exceptionally adaptable to changing battlefield conditions.
BMLinebacker_E.manufacturer: WC Site 1|Wolf Clan Site 2|Assault Tech Industries|W-12 Facilities

BMLinebacker_H.overview: The Linebacker was commissioned in 3052 by Clan Wolf Khans to address a critical gap in their heavy OmniMech roster. The result is 17.5 tons of pod space, roughly ten tons less than the Timber Wolf it was designed to complement. BMLineholder_KW1LH2.overview:
The Lineholder was introduced in 3058 as the first BattleMech design produced by Kressly Warworks on Epsilon Eridani. Created using a set of "Common Sense Design" guidelines, the fifty-five-ton 'Mech was developed by a Kressly think tank to meet self-imposed standards for speed, heat management, weapons-to-heat-sink ratios, and damage bracket projections. The result is a medium-weight platform that balances firepower, protection, and mobility at a price point attractive to small commands, minor nobles, and garrison forces throughout the Chaos March.

In its first year of production, the Lineholder achieved remarkable commercial success compared to other designs in its weight class, rapidly becoming the garrison machine of choice for factions able to afford newly manufactured BattleMechs. The design's affordable price point and reliance on easy-to-source components have kept it in production across multiple political upheavals, a sign of the enduring appeal of Kressly's common-sense engineering philosophy.
BMLineholder_KW1LH2.capabilities:
The Lineholder is built around a philosophy of reliability and simplicity. A standard Kressly GRF1A-MDX chassis carries a Core Tek 275 fusion engine, giving the 'Mech a top speed of 86 kilometers per hour, sufficient to keep pace with all but the fastest light and medium designs. Ten tons of Kressly Stoneskin 30M armor provide above-average protection for its weight class, reinforcing the 'Mech's intended role as a dependable workhorse rather than a specialized combatant.

The Lineholder's weapons suite emphasizes versatility across engagement ranges. A pair of LongFire V LRM-5 launchers provide long-range fire support and limited indirect capability, while a BlazeFire Systems large laser delivers accurate damage at medium ranges. Four Intek medium lasers round out the arsenal, creating a formidable close-range deterrent. Fourteen heat sinks manage the thermal load effectively, allowing sustained fire in all but the most prolonged engagements.

The design's reliance on proven, off-the-shelf components is both its greatest strength and its principal limitation. While the Lineholder is remarkably easy to maintain and repair (a quality reinforced by its widely recognized Easy to Maintain design quirk) it lacks the specialized edge of more expensive competitors. Many commands assign the Lineholder as the damage dealer in a medium attack lance or as the quick-response element of a heavier assault company, roles that play to its combination of speed, firepower, and endurance.
BMLineholder_KW1LH2.history:
The Lineholder emerged in 3058 from Kressly Warworks, an independent manufacturer operating on Epsilon Eridani in the contested Chaos March. Kressly's think tank developed the design using their "Common Sense Design" guidelines, a set of self-imposed engineering principles governing speed, thermal management, and weapons effectiveness. The result was a medium BattleMech that offered solid performance at a highly competitive price, a combination that proved irresistible to the minor factions, garrison commands, and independent units that formed the bulk of Kressly's target market.

The Lineholder's commercial success in its first years of production was remarkable by any standard for a new design. Its affordable price point and reliance on common, easy-to-source components made it the garrison machine of choice across the Chaos March, and demand quickly spread to the Federated Suns, the Word of Blake, and even Periphery states such as the Circinus Federation. This early success encouraged Kressly to invest in variant development, producing upgraded models targeting higher-paying customers.

The relationship between Kressly Warworks and the Word of Blake proved particularly significant. When the Blakists gained control of Epsilon Eridani during the late Civil War era, Kressly came under Word of Blake ownership, resulting in the development of the advanced KW2-LHW variant with integrated C3i networking. Simultaneously, Kressly produced the Linebreaker variant exclusively for the Federated Suns, until production was abruptly suspended following the dissolution of the second Star League, apparently as Blakist retaliation for the Federated Suns' no-confidence vote.

During the Jihad, Kressly Warworks continued operations under Word of Blake control, producing the LHW and base Lineholder variants for Blakist forces. Following the liberation of Epsilon Eridani and the establishment of the Republic of the Sphere, the factory transitioned to Republic oversight, resuming broader production including the previously suspended Linebreaker. The Republic era also saw the introduction of the KW2-LH10, a thoroughly modernized variant incorporating plasma weaponry and C3 emergency master technology that proved popular in command lances.

With the collapse of the Republic and the rise of the ilClan era, Epsilon Eridani passed to Capellan Confederation control, and Kressly Warworks continues to produce the Lineholder under its latest owners, proof of the enduring commercial viability of a design built from the start on principles of affordability, simplicity, and common sense.
BMLineholder_KW1LH2.deployment: The base Lineholder model can be found in almost every garrison within the Chaos March and beyond. Its low cost and ease of repair have made it highly desirable among small and medium-sized units, from minor planetary militia to independent mercenary companies. Demand for the design has reached as far as Periphery states such as the Circinus Federation. In both its intended roles (as the damage dealer in a medium attack lance or as the quick ready-response 'Mech of a heavier assault company) the Lineholder's reputation for dependable, solid performance remains well-deserved.

With the collapse of the Republic and the rise of the ilClan era, Epsilon Eridani passed to Capellan Confederation control, and Kressly Warworks continues to produce the Lineholder under its latest owners, proof of the enduring commercial viability of a design built from the start on principles of affordability, simplicity, and common sense.
BMLineholder_KW2LH10.deployment: Introduced in the early 3130s under Republic of the Sphere production, this variant stands as a significant departure from earlier Lineholder designs. It replaces all previous weaponry with a plasma rifle for primary firepower, supported by MML-5 launchers providing flexible missile capability and medium pulse lasers for close defense. The addition of a C3 emergency master computer made this variant particularly popular in command lances, allowing it to serve as a network coordination node while maintaining respectable combat capability. The design reflects the Republic's emphasis on networked warfare doctrine and multi-role flexibility.

BMLineholder_KW2LHW.overview:
The Lineholder was introduced in 3058 as the first BattleMech design produced by Kressly Warworks on Epsilon Eridani. Created using a set of "Common Sense Design" guidelines, the fifty-five-ton 'Mech was developed by a Kressly think tank to meet self-imposed standards for speed, heat management, weapons-to-heat-sink ratios, and damage bracket projections. The result is a medium-weight platform that balances firepower, protection, and mobility at a price point attractive to small commands, minor nobles, and garrison forces throughout the Chaos March.

In its first year of production, the Lineholder achieved remarkable commercial success compared to other designs in its weight class, rapidly becoming the garrison machine of choice for factions able to afford newly manufactured BattleMechs. The design's affordable price point and reliance on easy-to-source components have kept it in production across multiple political upheavals, evidence of the enduring appeal of Kressly's common-sense engineering philosophy.
BMLineholder_KW2LHW.capabilities:
The Lineholder is built around a philosophy of reliability and simplicity. A standard Kressly GRF1A-MDX chassis carries a Core Tek 275 fusion engine, giving the 'Mech a top speed of 86 kilometers per hour, sufficient to keep pace with all but the fastest light and medium designs. Ten tons of Kressly Stoneskin 30M armor provide above-average protection for its weight class, reinforcing the 'Mech's intended role as a dependable workhorse rather than a specialized combatant.

The Lineholder's weapons suite emphasizes versatility across engagement ranges. A pair of LongFire V LRM-5 launchers provide long-range fire support and limited indirect capability, while a BlazeFire Systems large laser delivers accurate damage at medium ranges. Four Intek medium lasers round out the arsenal, creating a formidable close-range deterrent. Fourteen heat sinks manage the thermal load effectively, allowing sustained fire in all but the most prolonged engagements.

The design's reliance on proven, off-the-shelf components is both its greatest strength and its principal limitation. While the Lineholder is remarkably easy to maintain and repair (a quality reinforced by its widely recognized Easy to Maintain design quirk) it lacks the specialized edge of more expensive competitors. Many commands assign the Lineholder as the damage dealer in a medium attack lance or as the quick-response element of a heavier assault company, roles that play to its combination of speed, firepower, and endurance.
BMLineholder_KW2LHW.history:
The Lineholder emerged in 3058 from Kressly Warworks, an independent manufacturer operating on Epsilon Eridani in the contested Chaos March. Kressly's think tank developed the design using their "Common Sense Design" guidelines, a set of self-imposed engineering principles governing speed, thermal management, and weapons effectiveness. The result was a medium BattleMech that offered solid performance at a highly competitive price, a combination that proved irresistible to the minor factions, garrison commands, and independent units that formed the bulk of Kressly's target market.

The Lineholder's commercial success in its first years of production was remarkable by any standard for a new design. Its affordable price point and reliance on common, easy-to-source components made it the garrison machine of choice across the Chaos March, and demand quickly spread to the Federated Suns, the Word of Blake, and even Periphery states such as the Circinus Federation. This early success encouraged Kressly to invest in variant development, producing upgraded models targeting higher-paying customers.

The relationship between Kressly Warworks and the Word of Blake proved particularly significant. When the Blakists gained control of Epsilon Eridani during the late Civil War era, Kressly came under Word of Blake ownership, resulting in the development of the advanced KW2-LHW variant with integrated C3i networking. Simultaneously, Kressly produced the Linebreaker variant exclusively for the Federated Suns, until production was abruptly suspended following the dissolution of the second Star League, apparently as Blakist retaliation for the Federated Suns' no-confidence vote.

During the Jihad, Kressly Warworks continued operations under Word of Blake control, producing the LHW and base Lineholder variants for Blakist forces. Following the liberation of Epsilon Eridani and the establishment of the Republic of the Sphere, the factory transitioned to Republic oversight, resuming broader production including the previously suspended Linebreaker. The Republic era also saw the introduction of the KW2-LH10, a thoroughly modernized variant incorporating plasma weaponry and C3 emergency master technology that proved popular in command lances.

With the collapse of the Republic and the rise of the ilClan era, Epsilon Eridani passed to Capellan Confederation control, and Kressly Warworks continues to produce the Lineholder under its latest owners, a reflection of the enduring commercial viability of a design built from the start on principles of affordability, simplicity, and common sense.
BMLineholder_KW2LHW.deployment: The most extensive modification of the Lineholder chassis, this variant was produced exclusively for the Word of Blake. Building on the structural innovations of the Linebreaker, it uses the same endo steel chassis and ferro-fibrous armor while mounting an entirely upgraded weapons suite: an extended-range large laser, twin LRM-5 launchers, and four extended-range medium lasers, all supported by double heat sinks. The centerpiece of the design is its C3i computer, which allows the Lineholder to share targeting data with up to five other units in a networked Level II formation. This integration capability made it one of the more advanced Blakist garrison designs prior to the Jihad.

BMLobo.overview: The Lobo was conceived in the late 3050s by Clan Wolf as a lighter, faster companion to the venerable Timber Wolf. Introduced around 3059, the forty-ton medium BattleMech was designed to complement Clan Wolf's frontline OmniMechs with a focus on missile and energy firepower. The incorporation of newly acquired Advanced Tactical Missile technology drove the design's development, though the cost of these systems necessitated weight-saving measures throughout the chassis. At forty tons, the Lobo fills the role of a fast skirmisher capable of outpacing the Timber Wolf, aligning with Clan Wolf's shift toward faster, harder-hitting designs during the late thirty-first century.
BMLobo.capabilities:
Built on a Type-A endo steel chassis and powered by a General Systems 240 XL engine, the Lobo achieves a top speed of ninety-seven kilometers per hour, making it one of the faster medium 'Mechs in Clan Wolf's touman. The design mounts a single Volt-7 extended range large laser in the chest for long-range jousting, while twin CC 6-rack Advanced Tactical Missile launchers provide exceptional flexibility through standard, extended-range, and high-explosive munition types. Paired General Systems heavy medium lasers and a single heavy small laser deliver devastating close-range firepower. Four tons of ATM ammunition supply adequate stores for sustained engagements.

Defensively, seven tons of Type-1 ferro-fibrous armor provide reasonable protection for the weight class, supplemented by a Shield-3 anti-missile system that offers some defense against incoming missile fire. However, the Lobo suffers from significant heat management problems. With only ten double heat sinks, the design cannot sustain fire from its full arsenal without risking shutdown. MechWarriors have adapted by employing an aggressive hit-and-fade doctrine, engaging at full output before withdrawing to dissipate accumulated heat during weapons-free cooling periods.
BMLobo.history:
The Lobo's development traces directly to Khan Vladimir Ward's dissatisfaction with the Linebacker OmniMech, a design championed by his predecessors Natasha Kerensky and Phelan Ward. Seeking a 'Mech that better aligned with his vision for Clan Wolf's evolving tactical doctrine, Ward directed his scientists to develop a lighter, faster companion to the Timber Wolf that emphasized missile firepower over the Linebacker's generalist pod-based approach. Early prototypes proved disappointing until Clan Coyote unveiled the Advanced Tactical Missile system, which Khan Ward secured through a brief and bloody batchall, neatly solving the design's primary weapons dilemma.

Production of the Lobo began at W-7 Facilities on Tranquil around 3059, establishing the design as Clan Wolf's primary ATM testbed. The Lobo quickly demonstrated its worth in border skirmishes during the Civil War era, engaging Jade Falcon and Ghost Bear forces along the Occupation Zone boundaries. Its combination of speed and flexible missile loadout proved particularly effective in the rapid strike-and-fade operations favored by Wolf commanders. Engagements against Clan Wolf-in-Exile and probing attacks on ComStar positions further validated the design, though extended combat revealed the heat management limitations inherent in its weapons configuration.

The Word of Blake's devastating nuclear attack on Tamar in 3070 crippled much of Clan Wolf's industrial infrastructure. Production continued at the Tranquil facility through the Civil War period, and around 3075, the newly established W-8 Facilities on Tamar began assembling Lobos from components shipped from the W-7 plants on Weingarten. This expansion coincided with the introduction of two new variants specifically developed for the anti-infantry and anti-battle armor roles that had become critical during the Jihad campaigns.

The Lobo continued to serve in Clan Wolf's touman through the Republic era and into the Dark Age. When Clan Hell's Horses seized portions of the former Wolf Occupation Zone, control of the Tamar production facility eventually transferred to the Horses, who maintained Lobo production alongside their own designs. Despite its origins as a Clan Wolf exclusive and Khan Ward's ambitions to develop it into an OmniMech platform, the Lobo ultimately remained a standard BattleMech, one whose practical battlefield performance ensured its continued relevance even as it passed into new hands.
BMLobo.deployment: Deployed exclusively within Clan Wolf's touman following its introduction in 3059, the Lobo saw action primarily in border skirmishes against Clan Jade Falcon and Clan Ghost Bear during the Civil War era. A notable distance-strike engagement against Clan Wolf-in-Exile and several probing attacks against ComStar positions provided additional combat data. The design earned commendable marks in these engagements, though encounters with ComStar forces revealed a tendency toward vulnerability in prolonged combat where the constrained heat management forced MechWarriors into extended cooling periods. However, the Lobo's heavy laser armament consistently allowed it to prevail when pilots managed their thermal profile effectively.

BMLobo_3.deployment: First produced in 3077, this later Jihad-era variant takes the anti-infantry role to its extreme. A pair of machine gun arrays, each mounting four machine guns, occupy the arms, providing withering antipersonnel fire at close range. Twin anti-personnel Gauss rifles in the side torsos add further capability against soft targets. For engagements with heavier opposition, an extended range PPC serves as the primary weapon, supported by a medium pulse laser and a pair of Streak SRM-4 launchers that ensure reliable hits against more mobile targets. An extra double heat sink helps manage the thermal load. This configuration proved particularly suited to the urban pacification and counter-insurgency operations that characterized the later stages of the Jihad.

BMLocustIIC_4.overview:
Clan Mongoose unleashed the Locust IIC in 2832, an upgraded version of the venerable Inner Sphere Locust designed to complement the Clan's fast-strike tactics during the Golden Century. The speedy design enabled Mongoose warriors to win numerous Trials before Clan Smoke Jaguar absorbed the Mongooses and inherited the production line on Circe. Following the de facto annihilation of the Jaguars during Operation Bulldog, Clan Jade Falcon claimed the Circe facility, while Clan Wolf maintained separate production as a garrison unit. Designed for reconnaissance and fast-strike raids, the Locust IIC offered MechWarriors comparable speed to the original Locust with significantly greater protection and offensive capability.

Though rendered largely obsolete by OmniMechs for front-line service, the design's simplicity, low cost, and ease of maintenance ensured its continued place in second-line Clusters across multiple Clans. The relocation of Clan production to Inner Sphere worlds following the invasion brought renewed interest in the chassis, with facilities on Sudeten, New Oslo, Satalice, and Stewart all producing new variants to meet the demands of occupation warfare and garrison duty.
BMLocustIIC_4.capabilities:
The original inspiration for the Locust IIC was a dwindling supply of SLDF Royal Locusts, long beloved by MechWarriors for their exceptional battlefield performance. The 'Mech that walked off the production lines on Circe boasted exponentially greater firepower and survivability over its namesake. The main armament consists of a medium pulse laser flanked by eight extended-range small lasers, allowing the Locust IIC to serve as an excellent anti-infantry platform with the capability to harass heavier 'Mechs. Powered by a standard 200-rated fusion engine, the chassis achieves a top speed of 129.6 kilometers per hour while carrying significantly more armor protection through ferro-fibrous plating over an endo steel frame. Ten double heat sinks manage the considerable waste heat generated by the energy weapon array.

The Locust IIC's larger size makes it a more durable weapon platform than the original Locust, and a far more difficult enemy to neutralize. Its narrow, low-profile silhouette complicates targeting solutions for enemy gunners, while the straightforward engineering makes field repairs manageable even with limited resources. However, the design retains the original Locust's chronic vulnerability in its leg actuators, which remain undersized relative to the stresses of high-speed maneuvering over rough terrain. Despite this weakness, the Locust IIC has proven its value repeatedly as a second-line combatant, and inner Sphere production has only expanded the design's reach and tactical flexibility.
BMLocustIIC_4.history:
Clan Mongoose first fielded the Locust IIC during the Golden Century, and the design served with distinction across multiple Clans as it changed hands through absorption and Trials of Possession. Clan Smoke Jaguar operated the primary facility on Circe for centuries, while production spread to Homeworld sites on Ironhold, Niles, Sheridan, Strana Mechty, and York under Jade Falcon, Hell's Horses, Star Adder, Coyote, Wolf, and Blood Spirit ownership respectively. The design's proliferation across so many Clans testified to its reliability and low cost of operation.

The Clan Invasion brought the Locust IIC to the Inner Sphere in significant numbers, and it quickly became one of the most recognizable Clan second-line designs. Locust IICs from the Wolf Empire and Clan Jade Falcon saw heavy fighting in the Lyran Commonwealth as their toumans ravaged the LCAF. While the speed and ferocity of these operations often caught LCAF forces wrong-footed, even Clan forces occasionally suffered stinging defeat under withering Lyran firepower. During the fighting on Tharkad in 3143, an overconfident Locust IIC MechWarrior in Clan Wolf's Beta Galaxy led his combined-arms recon Star too far ahead and blundered into a lightning company of the Second Royal Guards, with BattleROM footage of a Guards Gauntlet overtaking the fleeing Locust IIC becoming a fixture in Lyran propaganda holovids.

In the Deep Periphery, the Locust IIC played a part in the Scorpion Empire's conquest of the Hanseatic League in 3140. After merchant-employed mercenaries crushed the Thirty-Fifth Scorpion Cuirassiers on Königsberg, Khan Magon Scott reassigned warriors to form a Star of Locust IICs to replace OmniMech losses in scouting units. Their firepower proved devastating against League 'Mechs, and their speed enabled them to outmaneuver better-equipped mercenaries, sweeping into the rear areas of Regional Defense Force 2 and effectively ending its ability to repair damaged equipment.

Hell's Horses began producing the Locust IIC 7 from their captured facility on New Oslo in 3076, employing it in a supporting role for armor and infantry operations. During the campaign to liberate Terra from the Word of Blake, the Nova Cats' Eleventh Mechanized Cavalry fielded several Locust IIC 7s, where their targeting computer-backed AP Gauss rifles proved highly effective in the tunneled warrens of Kyoro Dome against experienced battle armor defenders. Most recently, the relocated Wolves refurbished the ancient Locust production lines on Stewart to produce the Locust IIC 10, ensuring the design will continue to serve well into the ilClan era.
BMLocustIIC_4.deployment: Almost completely redesigned for Inner Sphere production by Clan Jade Falcon, this variant replaced the extended-range small lasers with six heavy small lasers and swapped the medium pulse laser for an extended-range medium laser. Two additional double heat sinks were added to manage the increased thermal load. Produced at Olivetti Weaponry on Sudeten and at the W-7 Facilities on Weingarten, the design proved popular enough to spawn several derivative variants including the Locust IIC 6 and 7.

BMLocustIIC_9.deployment: The Jade Falcons' most ambitious Locust IIC variant features an experimental 350-rated XXL engine paired with an XL gyro, pushing the chassis to extraordinary speeds at the cost of increased fragility. The primary armament of two improved heavy medium lasers delivers substantial firepower for a twenty-five-ton design. Produced exclusively at Olivetti Weaponry on Sudeten, the Locust IIC 9 is a bold experiment in maximizing light 'Mech performance through advanced technology.

BMLocust_LCT1E.overview: The Locust stands as one of the most enduring and ubiquitous BattleMech designs in history, with continuous production spanning over five centuries since Bergan Industries first introduced the chassis in 2499. Designed exclusively for reconnaissance and quick strike missions, this twenty-ton light 'Mech relies on exceptional speed to outpace threats rather than armor to absorb them. The Locust's compact frame and narrow profile make it a difficult target, though these same characteristics leave little room for heavy weaponry or substantial protection. Within its weight class, the design excels as a scout, overshadowed only by 'Mechs equipped with jump jets. The sheer number of manufacturers producing the Locust across the Inner Sphere and Periphery has kept production costs low and replacement parts readily available, ensuring the design's continued relevance on battlefields from the Age of War through the ilClan era.
BMLocust_LCT1E.capabilities: The Locust's primary asset has always been speed. Powered by a 160-rated fusion engine in its base configuration, the chassis achieves a cruising speed of 86.4 km/h and a maximum velocity of 129.6 km/h, with later variants pushing these figures even higher through extralight engines and myomer accelerator signal circuitry. This mobility proves essential to the 'Mech's survival, as four tons of standard armor provides minimal protection against direct hits from battlefield weapons. The original LCT-1V mounted a chin-turret medium laser supported by two arm-mounted machine guns, a loadout adequate for deterring infantry and engaging targets of opportunity but wholly insufficient for sustained combat against heavier opponents. The design's lack of hand actuators and jump jets limits its effectiveness in close-quarters engagements and restrictive terrain. When forced into combat, Locust pilots typically fight holding actions until reinforcements arrive or operate in groups of three to encircle isolated enemy 'Mechs. Few MechWarriors relish extended assignments in a Locust, though those who master its capabilities often develop exceptional piloting skills born of necessity.
BMLocust_LCT1E.history:
Bergan Industries operated eight factories producing Locusts during the Star League era, supplying member states through the Amaris Civil War. The Succession Wars saw manufacturing expand to nearly a dozen facilities, including several in the Periphery, as the design's simplicity and low cost made it attractive to powers lacking sophisticated industrial bases. Everyone from pirates to corporate security forces purchased Locusts in substantial numbers, leading to an explosion of variants as different manufacturers and field technicians modified the chassis to meet local needs.

During the Second Hidden War, also called the War of Davion Succession, General Kessem of House Davion demonstrated the Locust's strategic potential on Ludwig, organizing five lances of fast-moving units to penetrate Kurita lines and draw crack units away from the front. Though losses proved staggering, the gambit slowed Ludwig's fall by months. House Marik's 10th Militia Regiment showed the design's urban combat potential during city-fighting on Callison in 3020, where Locust recon lances navigated narrow streets to devastating effect against defending infantry. The battle for Royal in 3020 illustrated both the Locust's strengths and weaknesses when detachments from the 8th Deneb Light Cavalry successfully flanked Kurita positions while three companies of the 10th Deneb blundered into an ambush of heavy and assault 'Mechs and were nearly annihilated. That same engagement saw House Davion introduce a new Locust variant mounting a heavy Magna PPC, but difficulties with the O/P 911 targeting system and massive overheating made it an utter failure, the recoil from firing the PPC actually knocked down these small 'Mechs in combat.

As the Succession Wars wound down, manufacturers within the Successor States began experimenting with rediscovered technology. The Capellan Confederation modified the Ares facility to produce the LCT-1L with improved Triple Strength Myomer, while Achernar, Corean, and Defiance introduced upgraded variants incorporating endo steel, ferro-fibrous armor, and advanced weapons systems. The Clan Invasion prompted further development, with the LCT-3D, 3M, and 3S entering service just in time to face the invaders. The Word of Blake later commissioned Corean Enterprises to develop the LCT-5M for their militia, purchasing the entire first production run. Even into the thirty-second century, the Locust continues rolling off production lines across the Periphery, with Bergan and Defiance introducing the LCT-7V and 7S variants during the ilClan era. The Marian Hegemony's assault on Marantha in 3150 demonstrated the design's continued vulnerability when a century of Locusts charging an entrenched militia position was cut down by field guns and portable missiles, the survivors posted to the Cohors Morituri for their failure.
BMLocust_LCT1E.deployment: Introduced in 2811 at the request of the Capellan Confederation, this variant replaced the machine guns and medium laser with an all-energy weapons configuration: two arm-mounted medium lasers and two small lasers. This arrangement eliminated ammunition dependency and allowed MechWarriors to flip their weapons between forward and rearward firing arcs at will. Among the least-produced variants, the "Energy" Locust saw limited adoption outside Capellan service, though surviving examples remain in use across the Inner Sphere.

Everyone from pirates to corporate security forces purchased Locusts in substantial numbers, leading to an explosion of variants as different manufacturers and field technicians modified the chassis to meet local needs.

During the Second Hidden War, also called the War of Davion Succession, General Kessem of House Davion demonstrated the Locust's strategic potential on Ludwig, organizing five lances of fast-moving units to penetrate Kurita lines and draw crack units away from the front. Though losses proved staggering, the gambit slowed Ludwig's fall by months. House Marik's 10th Militia Regiment showed the design's urban combat potential during city-fighting on Callison in 3020, where Locust recon lances navigated narrow streets to devastating effect against defending infantry. The battle for Royal in 3020 illustrated both the Locust's strengths and weaknesses when detachments from the 8th Deneb Light Cavalry successfully flanked Kurita positions while three companies of the 10th Deneb blundered into an ambush of heavy and assault 'Mechs and were nearly annihilated. That same engagement saw House Davion introduce a new Locust variant mounting a heavy Magna PPC, but difficulties with the O/P 911 targeting system and massive overheating made it an utter failure, the recoil from firing the PPC actually knocked down these small 'Mechs in combat.

As the Succession Wars wound down, manufacturers within the Successor States began experimenting with rediscovered technology. The Capellan Confederation modified the Ares facility to produce the LCT-1L with improved Triple Strength Myomer, while Achernar, Corean, and Defiance introduced upgraded variants incorporating endo steel, ferro-fibrous armor, and advanced weapons systems. The Clan Invasion prompted further development, with the LCT-3D, 3M, and 3S entering service just in time to face the invaders. The Word of Blake later commissioned Corean Enterprises to develop the LCT-5M for their militia, purchasing the entire first production run. Even into the thirty-second century, the Locust continues rolling off production lines across the Periphery, with Bergan and Defiance introducing the LCT-7V and 7S variants during the ilClan era. The Marian Hegemony's assault on Marantha in 3150 demonstrated the design's continued vulnerability when a century of Locusts charging an entrenched militia position was cut down by field guns and portable missiles, the survivors posted to the Cohors Morituri for their failure.
BMLocust_LCT1L.deployment: Introduced in 3030 as a testbed for Triple Strength Myomer technology at Bergan Industries' Ares facility, this variant retained the standard LCT-1V weapons loadout while incorporating experimental myomer bundles designed to operate at higher temperatures without catching fire. When properly heated, the TSM allows the Locust to achieve even greater speeds and enhanced close-combat capability, though few pilots willingly engage in physical combat with such a lightly armored chassis.

BMLocust_LCT1M.overview: The Locust stands as one of the most enduring and ubiquitous BattleMech designs in history, with continuous production spanning over five centuries since Bergan Industries first introduced the chassis in 2499. Designed exclusively for reconnaissance and quick strike missions, this twenty-ton light 'Mech relies on exceptional speed to outpace threats rather than armor to absorb them. The Locust's compact frame and narrow profile make it a difficult target, though these same characteristics leave little room for heavy weaponry or substantial protection. Within its weight class, the design excels as a scout, overshadowed only by 'Mechs equipped with jump jets. The sheer number of manufacturers producing the Locust across the Inner Sphere and Periphery has kept production costs low and replacement parts readily available, ensuring the design's continued relevance on battlefields from the Age of War through the ilClan era.
BMLocust_LCT1M.capabilities: The Locust's primary asset has always been speed. Powered by a 160-rated fusion engine in its base configuration, the chassis achieves a cruising speed of 86.4 km/h and a maximum velocity of 129.6 km/h, with later variants pushing these figures even higher through extralight engines and myomer accelerator signal circuitry. This mobility proves essential to the 'Mech's survival, as four tons of standard armor provides minimal protection against direct hits from battlefield weapons. The original LCT-1V mounted a chin-turret medium laser supported by two arm-mounted machine guns, a loadout adequate for deterring infantry and engaging targets of opportunity but wholly insufficient for sustained combat against heavier opponents. The design's lack of hand actuators and jump jets limits its effectiveness in close-quarters engagements and restrictive terrain. When forced into combat, Locust pilots typically fight holding actions until reinforcements arrive or operate in groups of three to encircle isolated enemy 'Mechs. Few MechWarriors relish extended assignments in a Locust, though those who master its capabilities often develop exceptional piloting skills born of necessity.

BMLocust_LCT1Y2.overview: The Locust stands as one of the most enduring and ubiquitous BattleMech designs in history, with continuous production spanning over five centuries since Bergan Industries first introduced the chassis in 2499. Designed exclusively for reconnaissance and quick strike missions, this twenty-ton light 'Mech relies on exceptional speed to outpace threats rather than armor to absorb them. The Locust's compact frame and narrow profile make it a difficult target, though these same characteristics leave little room for heavy weaponry or substantial protection. Within its weight class, the design excels as a scout, overshadowed only by 'Mechs equipped with jump jets. The sheer number of manufacturers producing the Locust across the Inner Sphere and Periphery has kept production costs low and replacement parts readily available, ensuring the design's continued relevance on battlefields from the Age of War through the ilClan era.
BMLocust_LCT1Y2.capabilities: The Locust's primary asset has always been speed. Powered by a 160-rated fusion engine in its base configuration, the chassis achieves a cruising speed of 86.4 km/h and a maximum velocity of 129.6 km/h, with later variants pushing these figures even higher through extralight engines and myomer accelerator signal circuitry. This mobility proves essential to the 'Mech's survival, as four tons of standard armor provides minimal protection against direct hits from battlefield weapons. The original LCT-1V mounted a chin-turret medium laser supported by two arm-mounted machine guns, a loadout adequate for deterring infantry and engaging targets of opportunity but wholly insufficient for sustained combat against heavier opponents. The design's lack of hand actuators and jump jets limits its effectiveness in close-quarters engagements and restrictive terrain. When forced into combat, Locust pilots typically fight holding actions until reinforcements arrive or operate in groups of three to encircle isolated enemy 'Mechs. Few MechWarriors relish extended assignments in a Locust, though those who master its capabilities often develop exceptional piloting skills born of necessity.
BMLocust_LCT1Y2.history:
Bergan Industries operated eight factories producing Locusts during the Star League era, supplying member states through the Amaris Civil War. The Succession Wars saw manufacturing expand to nearly a dozen facilities, including several in the Periphery, as the design's simplicity and low cost made it attractive to powers lacking sophisticated industrial bases. Everyone from pirates to corporate security forces purchased Locusts in substantial numbers, leading to an explosion of variants as different manufacturers and field technicians modified the chassis to meet local needs.

During the Second Hidden War, also called the War of Davion Succession, General Kessem of House Davion demonstrated the Locust's strategic potential on Ludwig, organizing five lances of fast-moving units to penetrate Kurita lines and draw crack units away from the front. Though losses proved staggering, the gambit slowed Ludwig's fall by months. House Marik's 10th Militia Regiment showed the design's urban combat potential during city-fighting on Callison in 3020, where Locust recon lances navigated narrow streets to devastating effect against defending infantry. The battle for Royal in 3020 illustrated both the Locust's strengths and weaknesses when detachments from the 8th Deneb Light Cavalry successfully flanked Kurita positions while three companies of the 10th Deneb blundered into an ambush of heavy and assault 'Mechs and were nearly annihilated. That same engagement saw House Davion introduce a new Locust variant mounting a heavy Magna PPC, but difficulties with the O/P 911 targeting system and massive overheating made it an utter failure, the recoil from firing the PPC actually knocked down these small 'Mechs in combat.

The Clan Invasion prompted further development, with the LCT-3D, 3M, and 3S entering service just in time to face the invaders. This configuration pushed the chassis's heat management to its limits but provided substantially improved firepower for pilots willing to manage their thermal buildup carefully.

Everyone from pirates to corporate security forces purchased Locusts in substantial numbers, leading to an explosion of variants as different manufacturers and field technicians modified the chassis to meet local needs.

During the Second Hidden War, also called the War of Davion Succession, General Kessem of House Davion demonstrated the Locust's strategic potential on Ludwig, organizing five lances of fast-moving units to penetrate Kurita lines and draw crack units away from the front. Though losses proved staggering, the gambit slowed Ludwig's fall by months. House Marik's 10th Militia Regiment showed the design's urban combat potential during city-fighting on Callison in 3020, where Locust recon lances navigated narrow streets to devastating effect against defending infantry. The battle for Royal in 3020 illustrated both the Locust's strengths and weaknesses when detachments from the 8th Deneb Light Cavalry successfully flanked Kurita positions while three companies of the 10th Deneb blundered into an ambush of heavy and assault 'Mechs and were nearly annihilated. That same engagement saw House Davion introduce a new Locust variant mounting a heavy Magna PPC, but difficulties with the O/P 911 targeting system and massive overheating made it an utter failure, the recoil from firing the PPC actually knocked down these small 'Mechs in combat.

As the Succession Wars wound down, manufacturers within the Successor States began experimenting with rediscovered technology. The Capellan Confederation modified the Ares facility to produce the LCT-1L with improved Triple Strength Myomer, while Achernar, Corean, and Defiance introduced upgraded variants incorporating endo steel, ferro-fibrous armor, and advanced weapons systems. The Clan Invasion prompted further development, with the LCT-3D, 3M, and 3S entering service just in time to face the invaders. The Word of Blake later commissioned Corean Enterprises to develop the LCT-5M for their militia, purchasing the entire first production run. Even into the thirty-second century, the Locust continues rolling off production lines across the Periphery, with Bergan and Defiance introducing the LCT-7V and 7S variants during the ilClan era. The Marian Hegemony's assault on Marantha in 3150 demonstrated the design's continued vulnerability when a century of Locusts charging an entrenched militia position was cut down by field guns and portable missiles, the survivors posted to the Cohors Morituri for their failure.
BMLocust_LCT5V.deployment: Built in 3068 for Periphery powers, this variant combined the LCT-3V's dual laser configuration with modern technology. Two ER medium lasers and two RL-10 rocket launchers provided improved firepower while ferro-fibrous armor enhanced protection. The original LTV 160 engine maintained traditional Locust performance. Both the Magistracy of Canopus and Taurian Concordat produce this variant, with Majesty Metals and Manufacturing, Pinard Protectorates Limited, and Taurus Territorial Industries maintaining active production lines.

BMLocust_LCT5W.overview: The Locust stands as one of the most enduring and ubiquitous BattleMech designs in history, with continuous production spanning over five centuries since Bergan Industries first introduced the chassis in 2499. Designed exclusively for reconnaissance and quick strike missions, this twenty-ton light 'Mech relies on exceptional speed to outpace threats rather than armor to absorb them. The Locust's compact frame and narrow profile make it a difficult target, though these same characteristics leave little room for heavy weaponry or substantial protection. Within its weight class, the design excels as a scout, overshadowed only by 'Mechs equipped with jump jets. The sheer number of manufacturers producing the Locust across the Inner Sphere and Periphery has kept production costs low and replacement parts readily available, ensuring the design's continued relevance on battlefields from the Age of War through the ilClan era.
BMLocust_LCT5W.capabilities: The Locust's primary asset has always been speed. Powered by a 160-rated fusion engine in its base configuration, the chassis achieves a cruising speed of 86.4 km/h and a maximum velocity of 129.6 km/h, with later variants pushing these figures even higher through extralight engines and myomer accelerator signal circuitry. This mobility proves essential to the 'Mech's survival, as four tons of standard armor provides minimal protection against direct hits from battlefield weapons. The original LCT-1V mounted a chin-turret medium laser supported by two arm-mounted machine guns, a loadout adequate for deterring infantry and engaging targets of opportunity but wholly insufficient for sustained combat against heavier opponents. The design's lack of hand actuators and jump jets limits its effectiveness in close-quarters engagements and restrictive terrain. When forced into combat, Locust pilots typically fight holding actions until reinforcements arrive or operate in groups of three to encircle isolated enemy 'Mechs. Few MechWarriors relish extended assignments in a Locust, though those who master its capabilities often develop exceptional piloting skills born of necessity.

BMLokiMkII_A.overview: The Hel is a 65-ton Clan Heavy OmniMech introduced in 3121, developed by Clan Jade Falcon as a successor to the venerable Hellbringer originally designed by Clan Hell's Horses scientists in 2926. Known to the Inner Sphere as the Loki Mk II, the Hel was created in the years preceding Gray Monday to address the aging Hellbringer's longstanding deficiencies in armor protection and equipment capacity. Manufactured jointly by Olivetti Weaponry on Sudeten and Csesztreg Industriplex Alpha on Csesztreg, the design has become most common in the Jade Falcon and Hell's Horses toumans, where it serves as a versatile heavy fire platform capable of fulfilling roles ranging from long-range sniping to close-quarters brawling.
BMLokiMkII_A.capabilities:
The Hel achieves its remarkable forty tons of pod space through a combination of engineering trade-offs that fundamentally distinguish it from its predecessor. A 260-rated XL fusion engine provides a maximum speed of only 64 kilometers per hour, a significant reduction from the Hellbringer's 86 kph top speed that has earned the design the unflattering nickname "Slowki" among Spheroid detractors. This sacrifice in mobility is offset by the installation of a small cockpit and Compound H17 ferro-fibrous armor, which together provide approximately fifty percent more protection than the notoriously thin-skinned original Hellbringer. The T-E H65 Omni chassis utilizes an endo steel internal structure to maximize available tonnage.

The Prime configuration exemplifies the design's long-range philosophy, mounting paired Gauss rifles and ER large lasers in its arms for devastating firepower at extended distances. A torso-mounted Streak SRM-4 provides limited close-range defense when engagement distances collapse. The Multi-Trac targeting system allows MechWarriors to effectively track multiple targets simultaneously, a critical advantage when exploiting the Hel's enormous weapon loadouts. While the small cockpit limits pilot comfort during extended operations, the sheer volume of pod space available ensures that configurations can be tailored to virtually any tactical requirement.
BMLokiMkII_A.history:
The Hel emerged from Clan Jade Falcon's recognition that the original Hellbringer, despite its iconic status as a Clan Invasion-era heavy OmniMech, suffered from fundamental design limitations that no amount of reconfiguration could overcome. Development began prior to Gray Monday in 3132, with Olivetti Weaponry on Sudeten and Csesztreg Industriplex Alpha collaborating on a design that would retain the Hellbringer's flexibility while dramatically improving survivability. The resulting chassis entered production in 3121 and spread quickly through both the Jade Falcon and Hell's Horses toumans.

The Hel saw significant combat during the Clan invasions of the Republic of the Sphere and Lyran Commonwealth in the 3140s. A notable early deployment occurred on Sargasso in July 3142, when the Ninth Talon Cluster of Clan Jade Falcon deployed a Binary of Hels fitted with B configurations to suppress resistance in the city of Salicastrum on the southern continent of Perusalem. The Long Tom cannons proved devastatingly effective against rebel positions, though a subsequent ambush by a Nova of Wolf-in-Exile forces destroyed half the Binary. The surviving Star regrouped and ultimately forced a Clan Wolf retreat, preventing the world from falling back into Commonwealth hands.

The divergence between Hell's Horses and Jade Falcon tactical philosophies became apparent during Operation Noyan on Biota in 3142, where the Eighty-Second Mechanized Cavalry under Star Colonel Waylon Mehta overran the Falcons' Fifth Mixed Cluster. Both Clans fielded Hels extensively during the engagement, with kinsmen from opposing forces dueling in extended single combat that highlighted the chassis's versatility in different doctrinal approaches.

As combat experience accumulated, the two primary operators developed the Hel along divergent paths. The Hell's Horses focused on leveraging the massive pod space for long-range firepower delivery, producing configurations emphasizing Gauss rifles, missile systems, and energy weapons optimized for standoff engagement. The Jade Falcons, meanwhile, worked to address the "Slowki" reputation by developing configurations incorporating improved jump jets and superchargers to enhance battlefield mobility. This dual development philosophy has produced a diverse stable of configurations that ensure the Hel remains a cornerstone of both toumans well into the ilClan era.
BMLokiMkII_A.deployment: Alternate Configuration A presents a more balanced weapons mix designed to handle both armored vehicles and infantry formations. Each arm carries an ER PPC paired with a medium pulse laser, while the right torso houses twin improved heavy medium lasers and a pair of AP Gauss rifles for anti-infantry work. An LB 10-X autocannon in the left torso provides flexible direct fire capability with both slug and cluster ammunition options. An Angel ECM suite mounted in the right torso enhances survivability by disrupting enemy targeting systems. With fourteen double heat sinks managing the substantial energy weapon load, the A configuration operates effectively at medium ranges where its diverse weapon systems can be brought to bear simultaneously.

BMLoki_A.overview: The Hellbringer was introduced in 2926 by Clan Hell's Horses as a heavy OmniMech born from necessity. Following the loss of Tokasha MechWorks to Clan Ghost Bear in the Battle of Tokasha, the Horses launched several ambitious development programs to rebuild their OmniMech capabilities using heavy, cost-effective designs that maximized firepower. Only the Hellbringer achieved lasting success, with development time reduced through creative reuse of structural molds from the Summoner. The Horses promptly lost their primary production facility for the design, and chose to leverage their remaining manufacturing capacity by gifting and trading the Hellbringer to other Clans to secure political favors. This deliberate dissemination resulted in the design spreading throughout nearly every Clan's touman. The Inner Sphere first encountered the Hellbringer during Clan Jade Falcon's invasion, where AFFC officer Galen Cox assigned it the reporting name "Loki" after declaring each configuration "utterly mad."

BMLongbow_LGB0W.overview:
The Longbow is one of the longest-serving fire support BattleMechs in the Inner Sphere, with a production history spanning more than six centuries. First designed in 2480 by Lockenburg-Holly Industries on Emris IV for the Free Worlds League Military, the eighty-five-ton assault 'Mech drew heavy inspiration from the Terran Hegemony's Archer, scaling the proven fire support concept up by fifteen tons and relocating its missile launchers to the arms for wider firing arcs. The Longbow's success secured Lockenburg-Holly's future, and the company's subsequent merger into StarCorps Industries made the design available to militaries across the Inner Sphere.

Despite never being a popular assignment among MechWarriors due to its vulnerability relative to its tonnage, the Longbow has remained in continuous production through centuries of conflict. StarCorps has produced no fewer than three visually distinct generations of the design (the original Star League model, the Clan Invasion-era 7Q, and the 3061 "Phoenix" redesign) each reflecting the evolving technology and combat doctrine of its era.
BMLongbow_LGB0W.capabilities:
The Longbow's design philosophy has remained remarkably consistent across its many iterations: deliver overwhelming long-range missile fire while remaining safely behind the front lines. The LGB-7Q model, representative of the post-Star League standard, mounts a pair of Holly LRM-20 launchers in its iconic barrel-shaped arms complemented by two torso-mounted Delta Dart LRM-5 launchers, enabling a devastating barrage of up to fifty missiles per salvo at ranges exceeding six hundred meters. Twenty-two single heat sinks allow the 'Mech to sustain this rate of fire indefinitely, a critical consideration for extended bombardment operations. Two Ceres Arms medium lasers provide a token close-range defense, though the Longbow is poorly equipped for direct engagement.

The 7Q's Strand 255 engine limits top speed to fifty-four kilometers per hour, sacrificing the mobility of the older 0W model for fourteen and a half tons of StarSlab armor, a significant improvement in survivability. The AntiAir Flak Systems-1 targeting system gives the Longbow an exceptional ability to engage fast-moving aerospace targets, a niche capability that has kept the design relevant in combined-arms operations well beyond what its raw specifications might suggest. The lack of CASE in the standard model remains the design's most criticized vulnerability, as an ammunition explosion can destroy the 'Mech outright despite its otherwise robust construction.
BMLongbow_LGB0W.history:
The Longbow traces its origins to the early BattleMech age, when the Free Worlds League Military identified fire support as a critical capability gap in its expanding forces. Lockenburg-Holly Industries answered this need in 2480 with the LGB-0C, a primitive eighty-five-ton design that paired twin LRM-20 launchers with the widest firing arcs of any assault 'Mech then in service. Despite thin armor and primitive technology, the Longbow proved the viability of dedicated missile support platforms and quickly became a fixture in League formations.

The design's success attracted wider attention during the Star League era. The merger of Lockenburg-Holly into the multinational StarCorps Industries opened production to all Great Houses, much to the Free Worlds League's displeasure. The upgraded LGB-0W, introduced in 2529 with a larger Strand 340 engine for improved mobility, became the definitive Star League model, with factories on Crofton, Emris IV, Fletcher, and Loburg producing the design for armies across the Inner Sphere. The subsequent LGB-7Q traded speed for heavier armor and an improved targeting system, establishing the template that would define the Longbow for centuries.

The Succession Wars devastated StarCorps' production network. Anton Marik's revolt in 3014 destroyed the original Emris IV facility, and by 3039 only the Crofton and Loburg plants remained fully operational, with Emris IV undergoing decades of reconstruction. Despite these losses, the Longbow's widespread proliferation ensured that spare parts and salvageable chassis remained available throughout the Inner Sphere, and the design continued to see extensive service in every major conflict of the era.

The recovery of lostech during the Clan Invasion prompted StarCorps to revitalize the Longbow, but the resulting LGB-7V proved disastrous. Designed to give the 'Mech close-range capability with an XL engine, pulse lasers, and an ER large laser, the expensive variant was misused as a frontline brawler by commanders and pilots, suffering excessive losses. Every major military that fielded it eventually sold its stocks to mercenaries and purchased alternative designs like the Naginata and Salamander. Recognizing the failure, StarCorps introduced the visually refreshed LGB-12C "Phoenix" model in 3061, returning to the Longbow's fire support roots with enhanced LRM capacity and Artemis IV fire control across all launchers. The Phoenix models were manufactured across StarCorps' fully rebuilt production network on Crofton, Emris IV, Loburg, St. Ives, and Terra.

The Jihad and its aftermath brought further evolution. The Son Hoa facility, initially limited to refits producing the popular LGB-10C, gained full production capability when the planet achieved independence in the early thirty-second century. StarCorps moved its King Crab line to the more defensible Loburg and upgraded the Son Hoa Longbow refit line to produce complete 'Mechs, resulting in several new models that combined the classic Star League-era appearance with advanced technology. These included the LGB-14V medium-range combatant and the devastating LGB-10K autocannon variant. Meanwhile, the Crofton, Loburg, and St. Ives plants continued producing Phoenix-lineage models for Federated Suns, Lyran, and Capellan buyers, while the LGB-12C also found a place in the militaries of the former St. Ives Compact and even the Word of Blake during its occupation of Terra.

By the ilClan era, the Longbow's six-century legacy showed no signs of ending. Production lines on multiple worlds continued to turn out new variants for an ever-changing battlefield, and the design remained one of the most common assault 'Mechs across the Inner Sphere. The sheer number of surviving chassis (including Star League-era 0W models still operational in Periphery states) ensured the Longbow would continue to serve for generations to come.
BMLongbow_LGB0W.deployment: The standard Star League-era Longbow introduced in 2529, this variant replaced the primitive 0C with a larger Strand 340 engine that boosted top speed to sixty-four kilometers per hour, allowing it to keep pace with most heavy 'Mechs. This speed came at the cost of five tons of armor and reduced heat dissipation, with only a single ChisComp 32 small laser backing up the four LRM launchers. The trade-off made the 0W a powerful but risky fire support platform that demanded careful positioning. The model saw production across multiple StarCorps facilities and became the most widely distributed Longbow variant during the Age of War and Succession Wars.

BMLongbow_LGB7Q.history:
The Longbow traces its origins to the early BattleMech age, when the Free Worlds League Military identified fire support as a critical capability gap in its expanding forces. Lockenburg-Holly Industries answered this need in 2480 with the LGB-0C, a primitive eighty-five-ton design that paired twin LRM-20 launchers with the widest firing arcs of any assault 'Mech then in service. Despite thin armor and primitive technology, the Longbow proved the viability of dedicated missile support platforms and quickly became a fixture in League formations.

The design's success attracted wider attention during the Star League era. The merger of Lockenburg-Holly into the multinational StarCorps Industries opened production to all Great Houses, much to the Free Worlds League's displeasure. The upgraded LGB-0W, introduced in 2529 with a larger Strand 340 engine for improved mobility, became the definitive Star League model, with factories on Crofton, Emris IV, Fletcher, and Loburg producing the design for armies across the Inner Sphere. The subsequent LGB-7Q traded speed for heavier armor and an improved targeting system, establishing the template that would define the Longbow for centuries.

The Succession Wars devastated StarCorps' production network. Anton Marik's revolt in 3014 destroyed the original Emris IV facility, and by 3039 only the Crofton and Loburg plants remained fully operational, with Emris IV undergoing decades of reconstruction. Despite these losses, the Longbow's widespread proliferation ensured that spare parts and salvageable chassis remained available throughout the Inner Sphere, and the design continued to see extensive service in every major conflict of the era.

The recovery of lostech during the Clan Invasion prompted StarCorps to revitalize the Longbow, but the resulting LGB-7V proved disastrous. Designed to give the 'Mech close-range capability with an XL engine, pulse lasers, and an ER large laser, the expensive variant was misused as a frontline brawler by commanders and pilots, suffering excessive losses. Every major military that fielded it eventually sold its stocks to mercenaries and purchased alternative designs like the Naginata and Salamander. Recognizing the failure, StarCorps introduced the visually refreshed LGB-12C "Phoenix" model in 3061, returning to the Longbow's fire support roots with enhanced LRM capacity and Artemis IV fire control across all launchers. The Phoenix models were manufactured across StarCorps' fully rebuilt production network on Crofton, Emris IV, Loburg, St. Ives, and Terra.

The Jihad and its aftermath brought further evolution.
