The remaining secondary weapons are removed to accommodate the C3 computer. When operating within a C3 lance, the KC's high speed and active probe make it an ideal forward node, feeding precise targeting data to heavier lance mates while remaining fast enough to disengage before the enemy can pin it down.

BMNightWolf.overview: The Night Wolf is a ninety-ton assault BattleMech developed by Clan Wolf in the aftermath of the Jihad. Introduced in 3085, the design was conceived as a practical response to two simultaneous crises facing the Wolves: the severing of their supply lines to the Kerensky Cluster during the Word of Blake Jihad, and the growing effectiveness of combined-arms doctrines employed by their adversaries. Produced at W-7 Facilities on Weingarten, which had become the administrative capital of the Wolf Occupation Zone following Tamar's irradiation in 3070, the Night Wolf was intended to replenish aging second-line assault formations with a purpose-built standard BattleMech. The design represented a departure from the Wolves' traditional reliance on OmniMech superiority, instead embracing a more pragmatic philosophy of fielding a capable and self-sufficient assault platform manufactured entirely from resources available within the Occupation Zone.
BMNightWolf.capabilities:
For a Clan-made assault 'Mech, the Night Wolf presents a deliberately balanced profile rather than pursuing excellence in any single area. Its Light Force 360 XL engine drives the ninety-ton chassis to a modest sixty-four kilometers per hour, while four Grandthrust Mk. 5 jump jets provide a hundred and twenty meters of jump capability, sufficient to maintain tactical positioning against most contemporary opponents. The DSAM Endo 4 internal structure saves critical tonnage for the design's diverse weapons suite.

The armament reflects a combined-arms philosophy well suited to garrison and second-line duty. Twin Type 9 Series 1 ATM 9 launchers provide flexible engagement capability at any range through their selectable munitions, while a Series 4D-2 Heavy Large Laser delivers punishing direct-fire damage at medium range. A Zeta-series X Plasma Cannon in the left arm proves especially effective against conventional vehicles and infantry formations, and a Series 2b ER Medium Laser supplements the energy weapons. A targeting computer helps offset the Heavy Large Laser's inherent accuracy difficulties, while a TJ6 "Bell" Mark II ECM suite and a Shield 3A Anti-Missile System provide layered defensive countermeasures against electronic warfare and missile-heavy opponents.

The fifteen and a half tons of Compound 12B2 standard armor provide adequate protection for most encounters, though noticeably less than ferro-fibrous alternatives could offer at equivalent weight. This trade-off reflects the design's emphasis on manufacturing simplicity within the Wolf Occupation Zone's industrial constraints.
BMNightWolf.history:
The Night Wolf's development is inseparable from the upheavals that reshaped Clan Wolf during the Jihad era. When the Word of Blake's campaign severed the Wolves' year-long supply lines to the Kerensky Cluster, the Clan was forced to confront the inadequacy of its homeworld-dependent logistics. Compounding this crisis, the combined-arms philosophies championed by enemies like the Word of Blake and the returning Hell's Horses challenged traditional Clan combat doctrines, demanding a more flexible battlefield response. The Night Wolf emerged from this dual crisis as a practical, indigenously produced assault 'Mech.

W-7 Facilities on Weingarten (a complex that had grown from a series of smaller industrial sites near accessible resources into a significant military manufacturing hub) began Night Wolf production around 3084. Weingarten's elevation to the administrative capital of the Wolf Occupation Zone after Tamar's irradiation by the Word of Blake in 3070 ensured the planet received priority allocation of resources and technical expertise, making it a natural home for new weapons programs.

Clan Wolf deployed the Night Wolf primarily in its second-line assault formations, where it gradually replaced aging designs such as the Highlander IIC and the Supernova that the Clan could no longer readily acquire from the Homeworlds. Many Night Wolves appeared among forces stationed along the shared border with Clan Hell's Horses, forming a key part of the defensive cordon against inter-Clan raids and territorial disputes in the former Lyran and Free Rasalhague Republic worlds.

The Night Wolf's production run proved relatively brief. When Clan Wolf abandoned its Occupation Zone in the late 3130s to pursue its march toward Terra, the departing Wolves systematically destroyed the Night Wolf production line at W-7 Facilities rather than allow it to fall into enemy hands. Clan Hell's Horses annexed Weingarten in 3138, but the destruction of the sole manufacturing facility effectively ended Night Wolf production. Only existing units remain in service, primarily with Hell's Horses garrison forces that inherited the remnants of the former Wolf Occupation Zone.
BMNightWolf.deployment: Clan Wolf has employed the Night Wolf primarily to replenish losses in its second-line assault formations, where it has gradually replaced more venerable designs that the Clan can no longer readily acquire from the Homeworlds, including the Highlander IIC and the Supernova. Significant numbers of Night Wolves have appeared among forces arrayed along the Wolves' shared border with Clan Hell's Horses, forming a key component of the defensive cordon against inter-Clan territorial disputes. No factory variants of the Night Wolf have been produced; the design entered service in its sole configuration, reflecting the pragmatic priorities of a wartime development program.

BMNightsky_NGS4S.overview: The Nightsky was introduced in 3053 by Defiance Industries on Hesperus II as the next evolution of the Federated Commonwealth's signature hatchet-wielding BattleMech lineage. Building on the success of the Hatchetman and Axman, the fifty-ton Nightsky was designed to provide an experienced MechWarrior with a powerful and heat-efficient close-combat platform capable of engaging Clan opponents in the one arena where Inner Sphere forces held a decisive advantage: physical combat. The LCAF's request for the design was driven by the realization that while Clan technology outclassed Inner Sphere weapons at range, a fast, well-armed melee 'Mech could close the gap and turn engagements into brutal close-quarters brawls. Produced exclusively at Defiance's Hesperus II facility, the Nightsky quickly became a staple of Lyran and later Federated Commonwealth forces, earning a fearsome reputation among units that favored aggressive assault tactics.
BMNightsky_NGS4S.capabilities:
The Nightsky is built around a Vlar 300 XL engine that propels the fifty-ton chassis to speeds approaching one hundred kilometers per hour, an exceptional pace for a medium 'Mech of its weight class. Six HildCo Model 13 jump jets further enhance its mobility with a jump capability of one hundred and eighty meters, allowing the design to traverse broken terrain and close rapidly with its targets. The Dorwinion Standard chassis carries nine and a half tons of Kallon Royalstar armor, providing solid protection for a 'Mech that is expected to absorb punishment during its approach to melee range.

The centerpiece of the Nightsky's arsenal is a four-ton hatchet mounted in the right arm, capable of cleaving through armor plating with devastating force. Supporting this primary weapon is a quartet of Sutel Precision Line pulse lasers (one large, two medium, and one small) that provide accurate firepower at close to medium ranges. The pulse laser suite's enhanced accuracy compensates for the chaotic conditions of close-quarters combat, ensuring the pilot can soften targets before delivering a killing blow with the hatchet. The reliance on energy weapons eliminates ammunition dependency, though the Vlar XL engine is a significant vulnerability; a critical hit to either side torso will disable the 'Mech entirely, a risk inherent to all XL-powered designs.
BMNightsky_NGS4S.history:
The Nightsky emerged during one of the most turbulent periods in Inner Sphere history. Introduced in 3053, just as the Clan Invasion was reshaping the strategic arena, the design was Defiance Industries' answer to the LCAF's urgent need for 'Mechs that could exploit the one tactical domain where Inner Sphere forces could compete with Clan warriors on more equal footing. The success of the Hatchetman had proven the viability of dedicated melee 'Mechs, and the Nightsky built upon that foundation with superior speed, armor, and firepower.

Nightskys proliferated rapidly throughout the Federated Commonwealth after their introduction, with many units replacing aging Hatchetmen and Axmen in frontline formations. The design became particularly popular among lightning company commanders who valued its combination of speed and devastating close-range striking power. By the time of the Lyran secession from the Federated Commonwealth, the Nightsky had spread widely enough that both the Lyran Alliance and Federated Suns fielded significant numbers, with examples appearing in pro-Victor Davion formations as well as pro-Katherine Steiner forces during the FedCom Civil War.

The Jihad inflicted significant damage on Defiance's Hesperus II facilities, disrupting Nightsky production and forcing the company to establish a refit line at their Furillo plant to handle the complex conversion work required by newer variants. Despite these setbacks, the design endured, with the venerable NGS-5T remaining in active production through the early Dark Age. Defiance continued to evolve the design, with the NGS-6T entering production during the Jihad era and becoming one of the company's most enduring Nightsky variants, remaining in active manufacture well into the ilClan era.

At the turn of the thirty-second century, the LCAF requested that Defiance develop a new Nightsky model incorporating the latest technologies. This led to the NGS-7S, which featured advanced armor composites and improved actuator systems while maintaining the design's characteristic ease of upgrade from older models using standardized upgrade kits. The 7S entered production during the Dark Age and continued into the ilClan period, ensuring the Nightsky lineage remained relevant on battlefields more than a century after the original design first drew its hatchet.
BMNightsky_NGS4S.deployment: The base model Nightsky establishes the design's core philosophy of speed and close-quarters lethality. Armed with a Sutel Precision Line large pulse laser for medium-range engagements, two medium pulse lasers and a small pulse laser for close-in work, and the signature four-ton hatchet, this variant is a pure brawler that excels at closing with its targets and dismantling them in melee combat. Full-head ejection capability and a switchable hatchet arm that can accommodate left-handed MechWarriors round out a design built for aggressive pilots.

BMNightsky_NGS6S.overview: The Nightsky was introduced in 3053 by Defiance Industries on Hesperus II as the next evolution of the Federated Commonwealth's signature hatchet-wielding BattleMech lineage. Building on the success of the Hatchetman and Axman, the fifty-ton Nightsky was designed to provide an experienced MechWarrior with a powerful and heat-efficient close-combat platform capable of engaging Clan opponents in the one arena where Inner Sphere forces held a decisive advantage: physical combat. The LCAF's request for the design was driven by the realization that while Clan technology outclassed Inner Sphere weapons at range, a fast, well-armed melee 'Mech could close the gap and turn engagements into brutal close-quarters brawls. Produced exclusively at Defiance's Hesperus II facility, the Nightsky quickly became a staple of Lyran and later Federated Commonwealth forces, earning a fearsome reputation among units that favored aggressive assault tactics.
BMNightsky_NGS6S.capabilities:
The Nightsky is built around a Vlar 300 XL engine that propels the fifty-ton chassis to speeds approaching one hundred kilometers per hour, an exceptional pace for a medium 'Mech of its weight class. Six HildCo Model 13 jump jets further enhance its mobility with a jump capability of one hundred and eighty meters, allowing the design to traverse broken terrain and close rapidly with its targets. The Dorwinion Standard chassis carries nine and a half tons of Kallon Royalstar armor, providing solid protection for a 'Mech that is expected to absorb punishment during its approach to melee range.

The centerpiece of the Nightsky's arsenal is a four-ton hatchet mounted in the right arm, capable of cleaving through armor plating with devastating force. Supporting this primary weapon is a quartet of Sutel Precision Line pulse lasers (one large, two medium, and one small) that provide accurate firepower at close to medium ranges. The pulse laser suite's enhanced accuracy compensates for the chaotic conditions of close-quarters combat, ensuring the pilot can soften targets before delivering a killing blow with the hatchet. The reliance on energy weapons eliminates ammunition dependency, though the Vlar XL engine serves as a significant vulnerability; a critical hit to either side torso will disable the 'Mech entirely, a risk inherent to all XL-powered designs.

BMNightstar_NSR9FC.overview: The Nightstar was born in 2767 during the Amaris Civil War, commissioned by the Star League Defense Force after battlefield analysis revealed that unit commanders (particularly those piloting Marauder BattleMechs) were being systematically targeted by Amaris loyalist forces. Designed jointly by General Motors and Norse-Storm Technologies as a ninety-five-ton heavy support and command platform, the Nightstar entered production just eight months after its initial commission, a reflection of the urgency of the SLDF's need. The design saw distinguished service during the liberation of Terra before becoming an early casualty of the technological regression that followed the Star League's collapse. It would take nearly three centuries before the Federated Commonwealth restored the Nightstar to active production, returning one of the Star League's most formidable assault 'Mechs to the battlefield.
BMNightstar_NSR9FC.capabilities:
The Nightstar shares a number of design features with its Marauder lineage, but at twenty tons heavier and powered by a Pitban 285-rated extralight fusion engine, the chassis carries over fifty tons of weapons and equipment atop eighteen tons of Kallon Royalstar heavy armor. This combination of firepower and protection makes the Nightstar one of the most dangerous stand-off combatants in the Inner Sphere, capable of engaging and destroying opponents at virtually any range bracket.

The primary armament consists of twin Norse-Storm Model 7D Gauss rifles mounted in each arm, backed by a Defiance 1001 extended-range PPC in the right torso. This trio of weapons delivers devastating long-range firepower, with each Gauss rifle capable of stripping nearly a ton of armor per shot. For close-range defense, a pair of Defiance P5M medium pulse lasers and a head-mounted ExoStar small laser provide supplemental firepower. Fourteen double heat sinks manage the thermal load with minimal difficulty.

Beyond its weapons array, the Nightstar's electronics suite is exceptional. The Tek BattleCom communications system provides superior command-and-control capability, while the DLK Phased Array Sensor System (widely regarded as the finest stock targeting and tracking system available prior to the development of dedicated targeting computers) grants pilots extraordinary accuracy. This combination of firepower, protection, and sophisticated electronics firmly establishes the Nightstar's role as a premier command assault 'Mech, though its modest top speed of fifty-four kilometers per hour leaves it vulnerable to faster opponents that can dictate engagement range.
BMNightstar_NSR9FC.history:
The Nightstar's origins trace directly to the chaos of the Amaris Civil War, when Stefan Amaris's forces made a deliberate practice of targeting SLDF unit commanders in their distinctive Marauder BattleMechs. The SLDF's response was swift, within eight months of commissioning, the first Nightstars rolled off production lines at General Motors on Kathil and Norse Technologies on Afleir, providing commanders with a vastly more survivable platform from which to lead their forces. The design saw distinguished service during the liberation of Terra and the final campaigns against Amaris.

The Nightstar became one of the earliest victims of the First Succession War. In 2786, a Free Worlds League raid savaged the Norse Technologies factory on Afleir, while a freak accident killed the General Motors engineering team on Kathil. With both production lines silenced and the technological expertise to rebuild them lost, the Nightstar joined the growing list of Star League designs that slipped beyond the Inner Sphere's ability to manufacture. Surviving examples became increasingly rare prizes, fought over by Successor State militaries desperate for any edge.

Nearly three centuries later, in 3057, the recovery of lostech and advances in manufacturing enabled both halves of the fracturing Federated Commonwealth to restart Nightstar production. General Motors reopened its Kathil line, while Norse-Storm Technologies (the corporate successor to Norse Technologies) established production on Solaris VII. The timing proved fortuitous, as the Nightstar entered service just as the Clan threat and internal divisions within the Federated Commonwealth created enormous demand for heavy assault platforms.

During the FedCom Civil War, the Nightstar served on both sides of the conflict, with its presence on the battlefield often marking the location of senior commanders. Reports from the war include accounts of Nightstar pilots employing extreme measures in the bitter fighting (including the use of atomic weapons on worlds such as Axton and Marlette) illustrating the desperate intensity of that conflict. The Lyran Alliance permitted mercenary sales early on, particularly to units deployed along the Clan Occupation Zones, while the Federated Suns restricted sales to its most trusted mercenary commands only after line units like the Davion Assault Guards received adequate numbers.

The design has continued to see active production and deployment through the Jihad and into the Dark Age. General Motors leveraged its experience with the successful Marauder MAD-9D to restart an updated Nightstar production line on Kathil, producing the NSR-10D variant beginning around 3144. The Nightstar remains a symbol of battlefield command authority, its distinctive silhouette marking the presence of senior officers and elite formations across the Inner Sphere.
BMNightstar_NSR9FC.deployment: Built exclusively by General Motors at Kathil, this variant trades the devastating but ammunition-dependent Gauss rifles for a pair of LB 10-X autocannons capable of firing both standard and cluster munitions, granting greater tactical flexibility. The most significant change is the installation of a 380-rated XL engine, boosting the Nightstar's top speed to nearly sixty-five kilometers per hour, a substantial improvement that better aligns with Federated Suns mobile warfare doctrine. This speed comes at the cost of raw firepower, as the LB 10-X autocannons lack the sheer destructive power of the weapons they replace. The laser array is simplified to three standard medium lasers, and the reduction in heat sink count to thirteen is offset by the lower thermal demands of the revised weapons loadout. Four tons of CASE-protected ammunition provide reasonable battlefield endurance.

BMNightstar_NSR9SS.deployment: Originally developed by Norse-Storm Technologies for combat in the arenas of Solaris VII, this variant stands as a radical departure from the Nightstar's traditional stand-off role. The long-range Gauss rifles and PPC are stripped entirely, replaced by an LB 20-X autocannon in the right arm and an Ultra AC/20 in the left, two of the most devastating close-range ballistic weapons available. Three jump jets grant the ninety-five-ton 'Mech the ability to vault up to ninety meters, enabling it to close range rapidly and bring its massive autocannons to bear. Three medium pulse lasers and a small laser provide backup firepower. The sheer bulk of the weaponry necessitated the removal of both lower arm and hand actuators, and half a ton of armor was sacrificed to accommodate the jump jets. While initially conceived as an arena combatant, this variant has proven effective in urban and close-quarters combat situations where its overwhelming short-range firepower can be fully exploited.

BMNinjaTo_NJT2.overview:
The Ninja-To was introduced in 3062 by Independence Weaponry of Quentin as a dedicated C3 slave platform for the Draconis Combine Mustered Soldiery. Named for the straight-bladed sword favored by ninja in ancient Japan, the sixty-five-ton heavy BattleMech was designed to complement other C3-equipped designs in the Combine's growing roster of networked 'Mechs. Independence Weaponry, already established as the premiere experts in C3 computer integration for heavy Combine BattleMechs, positioned the Ninja-To as a fast, hard-hitting platform that could leverage shared targeting data to maximize its effectiveness within a networked lance.

The design's emphasis on speed over firepower was intentional, reflecting the Combine's doctrine that C3 network accuracy bonuses could transform a modestly armed 'Mech into a genuine threat at extended engagement ranges.
BMNinjaTo_NJT2.capabilities:
Weighing sixty-five tons, the Ninja-To features an extra-light Magna 390 XL engine that propels the 'Mech to a top speed of just over ninety-seven kilometers per hour, matching or exceeding many Clan medium 'Mechs of comparable mass. This remarkable speed comes at a cost, however, as the extralight engine makes the design vulnerable to destruction from side torso hits. The chassis employs Star League XT NJT Light Endo Steel construction, which lightens the frame and frees mass for weapons and armor. Twelve tons of Durallex Heavy armor with CASE protect the Ninja-To from enemy fire and internal ammunition explosions, providing reasonable survivability for a heavy 'Mech that prefers to engage at range.

The Ninja-To's armament centers on two Diverse Optics Sunbeam extended-range large lasers supplemented by two Diverse Optics ER medium lasers and a single Shigunga MRM-10 launcher. While this weapon load is modest for a sixty-five-ton design, the 'Mech's Garret T-19G communications system integrates a C3 slave unit that is the heart of the design philosophy. When linked to a C3 command network, the Ninja-To's MechWarrior can achieve accuracy at extended ranges that would otherwise be impossible, transforming limited firepower into a genuine threat. The design's twelve double-strength heat sinks are barely adequate, and heavy use of the primary weapons can quickly overtax the cooling system.
BMNinjaTo_NJT2.history:
The Ninja-To's genesis at Independence Weaponry traces directly to the Draconis Combine's aggressive adoption of C3 computer technology during the late 3050s. Independence Weaponry had already established itself as the leading manufacturer of C3-equipped heavy 'Mechs for the DCMS, producing designs like the Naginata, Shugenja, and Tai-sho. The Ninja-To was conceived to fill a specific gap in the Combine's C3 doctrine: a fast heavy platform that could exploit network targeting data while operating at the fringes of engagement ranges.

Production began at a modest rate in 3062, with Independence Weaponry contracted to provide the first three production runs exclusively to the DCMS. The initial shipments went to the Genyosha regiments, where both the Tai-sho and Shugenja were first assigned. Independence Weaponry executives indicated that once the supply of Ninja-Tos caught up with the existing C3 command units, the company intended to offer C3 command lance discount incentive packages combining the Shugenja, Tai-sho, Naginata, and Ninja-To as matched sets, giving customers the most of the C3 computer network advantage.

The Jihad disrupted these plans severely. Quentin fell under Word of Blake control, and the Independence Weaponry facility shifted to Blakist production priorities. During this period, the Combine turned to its mobile factory ships DCS Yamato and DCS Ryuu, jointly operated by Luthien Armor Works and Independence Weaponry, which maintained production of the NJT-3 and later developed the NJT-4 variant. These factory ships provided a vital alternative production source through the Jihad and into the early Republic era.

Following the Jihad, Quentin passed through Republic of the Sphere control before eventually returning to Combine hands, but the Independence Weaponry facility did not resume Ninja-To production. The destruction of the factory ships Yamato and Ryuu by the Ghost Bear fleet in 3099 eliminated the last remaining production line, effectively ending new manufacture of the design. Despite this, surviving Ninja-Tos remain in service across several Combine formations, their speed and C3 integration continuing to make them valued components of networked lances.
BMNinjaTo_NJT2.deployment: The base model mounts a pair of Diverse Optics Sunbeam extended-range large lasers as its primary armament, supplemented by two ER medium lasers and a Shigunga MRM-10 launcher for close-range engagements. This weapons mix provides flexibility across multiple range brackets, though the design's twelve double-strength heat sinks can be overtaxed by sustained fire. Twelve tons of Durallex Heavy armor with CASE offers solid protection, while the integrated C3 slave unit allows the MechWarrior to take full advantage of shared targeting data from a command unit. Introduced in 3062, this variant entered service exclusively with DCMS formations, initially equipping the elite Genyosha regiments.

BMNinjaTo_NJT3.overview:
The Ninja-To was introduced in 3062 by Independence Weaponry of Quentin as a dedicated C3 slave platform for the Draconis Combine Mustered Soldiery. Named for the straight-bladed sword favored by ninja in ancient Japan, the sixty-five-ton heavy BattleMech was designed to complement other C3-equipped designs in the Combine's growing roster of networked 'Mechs. Independence Weaponry, already established as the premiere experts in C3 computer integration for heavy Combine BattleMechs, positioned the Ninja-To as a fast, hard-hitting platform that could leverage shared targeting data to maximize its effectiveness within a networked lance.

The design's emphasis on speed over firepower was intentional, reflecting the Combine's doctrine that C3 network accuracy bonuses could transform a modestly armed 'Mech into a genuine threat at extended engagement ranges.
BMNinjaTo_NJT3.capabilities:
Weighing sixty-five tons, the Ninja-To features an extra-light Magna 390 XL engine that propels the 'Mech to a top speed of just over ninety-seven kilometers per hour, matching or exceeding many Clan medium 'Mechs of comparable mass. This remarkable speed comes at a cost, however, as the extralight engine makes the design vulnerable to destruction from side torso hits. The chassis employs Star League XT NJT Light Endo Steel construction, which lightens the frame and frees mass for weapons and armor. Twelve tons of Durallex Heavy armor with CASE protect the Ninja-To from enemy fire and internal ammunition explosions, providing reasonable survivability for a heavy 'Mech that prefers to engage at range.

The Ninja-To's armament centers on two Diverse Optics Sunbeam extended-range large lasers supplemented by two Diverse Optics ER medium lasers and a single Shigunga MRM-10 launcher. While this weapon load is modest for a sixty-five-ton design, the 'Mech's Garret T-19G communications system integrates a C3 slave unit that is the heart of the design philosophy. When linked to a C3 command network, the Ninja-To's MechWarrior can achieve accuracy at extended ranges that would otherwise be impossible, transforming limited firepower into a genuine threat. The design's twelve double-strength heat sinks are barely adequate, and heavy use of the primary weapons can quickly overtax the cooling system.
BMNinjaTo_NJT3.history:
The Ninja-To's genesis at Independence Weaponry traces directly to the Draconis Combine's aggressive adoption of C3 computer technology during the late 3050s. Independence Weaponry had already established itself as the leading manufacturer of C3-equipped heavy 'Mechs for the DCMS, producing designs like the Naginata, Shugenja, and Tai-sho. The Ninja-To was conceived to fill a specific gap in the Combine's C3 doctrine: a fast heavy platform that could exploit network targeting data while operating at the fringes of engagement ranges.

Production began at a modest rate in 3062, with Independence Weaponry contracted to provide the first three production runs exclusively to the DCMS. The initial shipments went to the Genyosha regiments, where both the Tai-sho and Shugenja were first assigned. Independence Weaponry executives indicated that once the supply of Ninja-Tos caught up with the existing C3 command units, the company intended to offer C3 command lance discount incentive packages combining the Shugenja, Tai-sho, Naginata, and Ninja-To as matched sets, giving customers the most of the C3 computer network advantage.

The Jihad disrupted these plans severely. Quentin fell under Word of Blake control, and the Independence Weaponry facility shifted to Blakist production priorities. During this period, the Combine turned to its mobile factory ships DCS Yamato and DCS Ryuu, jointly operated by Luthien Armor Works and Independence Weaponry, which maintained production of the NJT-3 and later developed the NJT-4 variant. These factory ships provided a vital alternative production source through the Jihad and into the early Republic era.

Following the Jihad, Quentin passed through Republic of the Sphere control before eventually returning to Combine hands, but the Independence Weaponry facility did not resume Ninja-To production. The destruction of the factory ships Yamato and Ryuu by the Ghost Bear fleet in 3099 eliminated the last remaining production line, effectively ending new manufacture of the design. Despite this, surviving Ninja-Tos remain in service across several Combine formations, their speed and C3 integration continuing to make them valued components of networked lances.
BMNinjaTo_NJT3.deployment: This variant is a straightforward weapons swap, trading both extended-range large lasers and the MRM-10 launcher for a pair of standard PPCs. While the particle projection cannons sacrifice some flexibility compared to the original mixed armament, they deliver significantly more raw damage per salvo and eliminate the ammunition dependency of the MRM system. The reduced overall energy draw also improves the heat management profile of the design. Introduced in 3068 during the opening stages of the Jihad, this variant was produced both at the Independence Weaponry plant on Quentin and aboard the Combine mobile factory ships Yamato and Ryuu, ensuring continued availability even as the Jihad disrupted conventional supply lines.
BMNinjaTo_NJT3.manufacturer: Independence Weaponry|DCS Yamato & DCS Ryuu (LAW & Independence Weaponry)

BMNoDachi_NDA1K.overview: The No-Dachi is a seventy-ton heavy BattleMech introduced in 3058 by the Cosby BattleMech Research Firm on Vega as the Draconis Combine's answer to the growing proliferation of melee-equipped BattleMechs fielded by the Federated Commonwealth. Named for the legendary oversized Japanese sword, the No-Dachi was designed to pair devastating close-combat capability with respectable ranged firepower. The samurai culture deeply ingrained in Combine MechWarriors made them resistant to the hatchets favored by Commonwealth designs, and the No-Dachi's sword offered a more elegant melee weapon befitting the Combine's warrior traditions. The design quickly became a fixture of frontline DCMS formations and remains in production well into the ilClan era.
BMNoDachi_NDA1K.capabilities:
The No-Dachi is built around its seven-meter katana-style sword, a weapon made truly devastating by the 'Mech's Triple Strength Myomer system. When running hot, the myomers dramatically increase the No-Dachi's striking power and boost its speed from 86 to 97 kilometers per hour, making it a fearsome opponent in close quarters. This heat dependency shapes the entire combat philosophy of the design, as pilots must carefully manage their thermal output to maximize myomer performance.

At range, the Lord's Light 2 extended-range PPC provides the primary long-range striking power, capable of softening targets as the No-Dachi closes the distance. The dual Shigunga MRM-20 racks deliver devastating medium-range barrages, though their inherent inaccuracy stands in stark contrast to the precision of the katana. A Guided Technologies SRM-2, Telos-4 SRM-4, and Diverse Optics medium laser round out the close-range arsenal, providing supplementary firepower and crucial heat generation to activate the myomers.

Riding on a Magna 350 XL engine, the No-Dachi achieves respectable speed for a seventy-ton design, though the extra-light engine's vulnerability to side torso hits serves as a significant weakness. Starshield A armor provides adequate protection, but pilots must be mindful that sustained exchanges of fire can expose the design's limitations before it reaches melee range.
BMNoDachi_NDA1K.history:
The No-Dachi's development traces back to the mid-3050s, when the Cosby Myomer Research Firm (then primarily a myomer component supplier) partnered with the Eleventh Legion of Vega to develop a new close-combat BattleMech. The Legion, known for its technical expertise and its famous former commander Theodore Kurita, provided Cosby with advanced technologies and research support. In exchange, Cosby agreed to allocate half of all No-Dachi production to the Legion's ranks.

The design entered service in 3058 and quickly became synonymous with the Legion of Vega. Through special arrangement with Cosby, the bulk of No-Dachis were assigned to the Eleventh Legion, though several battalions' worth were distributed to other front-line DCMS units by the time of the FedCom Civil War. The design's association with the Legion proved a double-edged sword; Sword of Light regiments and other prestigious formations largely avoided the No-Dachi, preferring to lobby for a melee-capable 'Mech untainted by the Legion's reputation.

When the Word of Blake launched its invasion of Vega during the Jihad, the Draconis Combine ordered Cosby to relocate its production facilities deeper into the Combine. The company moved to Kajikazawa in the Benjamin Military District, an impressive logistical feat accomplished during wartime. By 3079, production lines were running at capacity, though a shortage of shipping infrastructure on the formerly backwater world initially hampered distribution. The bulk of output during this period went to the Second Benjamin Regulars tasked with defending Kajikazawa and the company's facilities.

The relocation proved fortuitous, as the Kajikazawa facility received significant government funding to develop experimental technologies, ultimately producing the NDA-3X prototype. The No-Dachi's prominence continued into the Dark Age, with senior DCMS commanders continuing to favor the design for frontline service. The Kajikazawa facility remained active through the ilClan era, producing updated variants including the NDA-3S Lyran export model, ensuring the No-Dachi's continued service across multiple factions and eras.
BMNoDachi_NDA1K.deployment: The base model carries the No-Dachi's signature loadout of a seven-meter katana paired with an extended-range PPC, dual MRM-20 racks, an SRM-2, SRM-4, and medium laser. The Triple Strength Myomer system rewards aggressive heat management, boosting both striking power and speed when the 'Mech runs hot. This combination of ranged suppression and devastating melee capability established the template for all subsequent No-Dachi variants.
BMNoDachi_NDA1K.manufacturer: Cosby BattleMech and Myomer Research Firm

Produced at Cosby's Kajikazawa facility as a Lyran export model, this variant trades the traditional elegance of the sword for raw bludgeoning power, a philosophical shift that would horrify purist Combine MechWarriors but proved popular with Commonwealth buyers.
BMNoDachi_NDA3S.manufacturer: Cosby BattleMech and Myomer Research Firm

BMNoborinin_A.overview:
The Huntsman was originally developed by Clan Diamond Shark as a totemic OmniMech honoring their namesake predator, but before the design could enter full production, Clan Nova Cat won exclusive manufacturing rights through a Trial of Possession driven by the fierce rivalry between the two Clans' Merchant Castes. Entering production in 3049, the fifty-ton Huntsman quickly became the premier medium OmniMech of Clan Nova Cat, exemplifying the flexibility and adaptability that defined the OmniMech concept. Khan Severen Leoux contracted Clan Cloud Cobra's Brim Ironworks facility for additional manufacturing, ensuring sufficient production to equip Nova Cat frontline units in time for Operation Revival.

First encountered by Inner Sphere forces during the Battle of Luthien in 3052, a Draconis Combine intelligence officer designated the OmniMech "Nobori-nin" after the distinctive dorsal fin projection reminded him of the banners feudal samurai wore on their backs. The Huntsman has since spread well beyond its Nova Cat origins, serving with multiple Clans and finding renewed production under the Clan Protectorate on Asellus Australis.
BMNoborinin_A.capabilities:
Sturdy and stable, the Huntsman dedicates nearly half its mass to pod space, granting MechWarriors exceptional flexibility in loadout configuration. Built on a Mynx Type Medium Endo Steel chassis and powered by a 250-rated Consolidated extralight fusion engine, the design achieves a respectable top speed of eighty-six kilometers per hour. Five fixed Northrup Starlifters jump jets provide a one-hundred-fifty-meter leap capability, offsetting what some warriors consider a middling ground speed for a medium OmniMech. Nine tons of Alpha Compound ferro-fibrous armor provide protection comparable to many heavier designs, contributing to the Huntsman's reputation as the equal in raw survivability of numerous heavy 'Mechs taking the field.

The Primary configuration demonstrates the Huntsman's versatility with a broad weapons mix spanning all engagement ranges. An Ultra autocannon/2 and Artemis IV-enhanced LRM-10 provide long-range suppression, while four extended-range medium lasers and a Streak SRM-6 deliver devastating close-range firepower. An active probe, TAG spotting laser, and anti-missile system round out the electronics suite, making the Prime configuration an exceptionally capable scout and skirmisher. The twenty-three and a half tons of available pod space allow configurations ranging from heavy fire support to dedicated brawler loadouts, though warriors accustomed to faster medium designs occasionally chafe at the Huntsman's more measured pace.
BMNoborinin_A.history:
The Huntsman's origins lie in the intense commercial rivalry between the Merchant Castes of Clans Nova Cat and Diamond Shark, whose competition for resources and trade opportunities was among the fiercest in the Clan Homeworlds prior to Operation Revival. When the Nova Cats successfully trialed for exclusive production rights to the promising new Diamond Shark OmniMech, it became a long-standing point of irritation that their totemic shark design had become a quintessential Nova Cat machine. Khan Severen Leoux wisely contracted Clan Cloud Cobra's Brim Ironworks to supplement Nova Cat production, preserving the Clan's own industrial capacity for other priorities.

The Huntsman first saw combat against Inner Sphere forces during Operation Revival, where it appeared in the ranks of the 119th Nova Cat Striker Cluster at the Battle of Luthien. Throughout the Clan Invasion, the design remained almost exclusively a Nova Cat asset, prized for its flexibility across diverse opponents and battlefield conditions. In the years following the invasion, however, Clan Diamond Shark finally reclaimed the right to produce their totemic design, while Clan Cloud Cobra's long manufacturing partnership led to the sharing of schematics with Clan Star Adder. By the outbreak of the Jihad, multiple Clans fielded significant numbers of the Huntsman.

The Word of Blake Jihad proved devastating for Huntsman production. The Nova Cat facilities on Irece and Avon were both destroyed in 3071, severely curtailing the supply of new chassis. When a significant portion of the Clan Nova Cat Touman joined the Republic of the Sphere after the Jihad, Huntsmans began appearing in Republic Armed Forces livery, a sight that raised eyebrows among observers who recognized the distinctly Clan design in recent RAF operations.

The Second Combine-Dominion War further depleted Nova Cat Huntsman numbers, as combat losses outpaced the Clan's diminished ability to replace them. The establishment of the Clan Protectorate brought renewed hope for the design, with Clan Protectorate Arms on Asellus Australis placing the Huntsman back into production for use by the descendants of both Nova Cat and Sea Fox, serving as a symbol of new cooperation within the Protectorate. Meanwhile, Brim Ironworks has maintained continuous production throughout these upheavals, ensuring the Huntsman remains a common sight on battlefields across the Inner Sphere and Clan territories alike.
BMNoborinin_A.deployment: Alternate Configuration A pairs a pair of large pulse lasers with an LRM-10 and LB 2-X autocannon, creating a loadout equally effective at range and in close quarters. The heavy firepower and similarity to the Crossbow B configuration have made it a MechWarrior favorite, particularly among Clan Steel Viper warriors who appreciate the consistent damage output at all engagement distances. Two additional double heat sinks manage the significant thermal load generated by the pulse lasers.
BMNoborinin_A.manufacturer: Avon Alpha|Brim Ironworks|Irece Alpha|Clan Protectorate Arms

BMNoborinin_N.history:

By the outbreak of the Jihad, multiple Clans fielded significant numbers of the Huntsman.

BMNovaCat_A.overview:
The Nova Cat is a 70-ton Clan heavy OmniMech introduced in 3059, commissioned by Khan Severen Leroux of Clan Nova Cat following the Clan's devastating defeat at the Battle of Tukayyid. Designed to rebuild both the touman's fighting strength and the Clan's shattered morale, the Nova Cat was christened after the Clan's spiritual namesake, imbuing it with deep symbolic significance for its warriors. The design draws heavy inspiration from Clan Jade Falcon's Night Gyr, trading five tons of mass for equivalent pod capacity through efficient use of an Endo Steel chassis and XL engine.

First produced at Barcella Alpha in Clan space, production expanded almost immediately to the Irece Alpha facility in the Inner Sphere. This dual-site manufacturing proved critical when Clan Nova Cat was abjured by the other Clans, ensuring uninterrupted production. The design's combination of heavy armor, generous pod space, and straightforward maintenance requirements made it popular well beyond its parent Clan, spreading rapidly to numerous other Clan and Inner Sphere factions over the following decades.
BMNovaCat_A.capabilities:
Long regarded as a pocket assault OmniMech, the Nova Cat sacrifices speed for firepower and protection. Its Consolidated Fusion 280 XL engine propels the seventy-ton chassis at a modest 43 kph cruising speed and 65 kph maximum, slower than most Clan heavies but sufficient for fire support and direct engagement roles. With over half its tonnage dedicated to weapons, ammunition, and equipment, the 38 tons of available pod space rivals many assault OmniMechs, giving technicians extraordinary flexibility in tailoring loadouts to mission requirements.

The Mynx Type Heavy Endo Steel frame supports 13.5 tons of Alpha Compound Plate armor, approaching the maximum protection possible for this weight class. Combined with a Clan XL engine that remains operational even after side torso loss, the Nova Cat is exceptionally difficult to destroy. Straightforward internal construction using common Clan components ensures rapid field repairs and reconfigurations, a significant logistical advantage for units operating far from supply lines.

The Primary configuration exemplifies the design's philosophy with two ER PPCs and three ER Large Lasers, creating a withering long-range energy barrage. Twenty-five double heat sinks struggle to dissipate a full alpha strike, but the all-energy loadout allows extended independent operations without ammunition concerns, and disciplined fire grouping keeps the 'Mech combat-effective indefinitely.
BMNovaCat_A.history:
The Nova Cat's origins are inseparable from the crisis that gripped Clan Nova Cat after Tukayyid. The Clan's defeat in 3052 shook its warriors to the core, and Khan Severen Leroux's decision to commission a new OmniMech was as much about restoring spiritual confidence as rebuilding military capability. Production began at Barcella Alpha, the Nova Cat capital world, and expanded to the Irece Alpha plant in early 3059 as the Clan began establishing its presence in the Inner Sphere.

The Nova Cat first saw significant combat during Operation Bulldog in 3059, when Clan Nova Cat's warriors turned their new OmniMech against Clan Smoke Jaguar. When the 357th Assault Cluster took Dyev from the Draconis Combine, the versatility of several Nova Cats proved decisive, with configurations mounting heavy autocannons and cluster munitions devastating militia vehicles and infantry formations. The sight of the towering twelve-meter 'Mech stalking through battlefield smoke became a potent psychological weapon against defending forces.

The Clan's Abjuration following their alliance with the Second Star League scattered Nova Cats across multiple factions' arsenals. Several units were seized by Clan Smoke Jaguar forces when they captured a malfunctioning Nova Cat DropShip during the chaos surrounding the Clan's dissolution. Sources in the Periphery persistently reported sightings of machines resembling the Nova Cat, suggesting that salvaged or captured examples may have entered the arsenals of Clans that accepted Smoke Jaguar refugees. The design also spread through more conventional channels, with Clan Diamond Shark's acquisition of the Barcella Alpha facility during the Civil War era enabling broader commercial distribution.

The Jihad proved devastating for Nova Cat production. The Irece Alpha plant was destroyed in 3071 during the Word of Blake's assault on the Draconis Combine, and individual Nova Cats were documented fighting desperate engagements against Blakist forces on worlds like Luthien and Caph. Despite the death of Clan Nova Cat as a political entity, the Tiburon Khanate maintained the Irece factory after it was rebuilt in the 3090s, meeting continued demand that proved both expected and surprising. Salvaged Nova Cats became a fixture in the Rasalhague Dominion, where native warriors of the former Free Rasalhague Republic put them to effective use despite being shunned by their Ghost Bear overlords.

By the ilClan era, the Nova Cat OmniMech had long outlived its parent Clan. Production continued at Irece under Draconis Combine control, while the Barcella facility's ownership passed through multiple Clan hands. Among the warriors of the Clan Protectorate, Nova Cat OmniMechs remain highly prized assets that frequently change hands through Trials of Possession, a fitting legacy for a design born from one Clan's determination to endure.
BMNovaCat_A.deployment: The A configuration reconfigures the Nova Cat as a mobile skirmisher, equipping four ER Large Lasers linked to a targeting computer for enhanced accuracy. Six jump jets propel the seventy-ton chassis up to one hundred and twenty meters at a time, granting tactical mobility unusual for a 'Mech of this weight class. Fourteen additional double heat sinks keep thermal loads manageable, though sustained fire remains inadvisable. The combination of precision fire, jump capability, and the Nova Cat's heavy armor makes this configuration particularly dangerous in broken terrain where it can exploit elevation advantages while shrugging off return fire that would cripple lighter designs.

The design draws heavy inspiration from Clan Jade Falcon's Night Gyr, trading five tons of mass for equivalent pod capacity through efficient use of an Endo Steel chassis and XL engine.

First produced at Barcella Alpha in Clan space, production expanded almost immediately to the Irece Alpha facility in the Inner Sphere. This dual-site manufacturing proved critical when Clan Nova Cat was abjured by the other Clans, ensuring uninterrupted production. The design's combination of heavy armor, generous pod space, and straightforward maintenance requirements made it popular well beyond its parent Clan, spreading rapidly to numerous other Clan and Inner Sphere factions over the following decades.
BMNovaCat_E.capabilities:
Long regarded as a pocket assault OmniMech, the Nova Cat sacrifices speed for firepower and protection. Its Consolidated Fusion 280 XL engine propels the seventy-ton chassis at a modest 43 kph cruising speed and 65 kph maximum, slower than most Clan heavies but sufficient for fire support and direct engagement roles. With over half its tonnage dedicated to weapons, ammunition, and equipment, the 38 tons of available pod space rivals many assault OmniMechs, giving technicians extraordinary flexibility in tailoring loadouts to mission requirements.

The Mynx Type Heavy Endo Steel frame supports 13.5 tons of Alpha Compound Plate armor, approaching the maximum protection possible for this weight class. Combined with a Clan XL engine that remains operational even after side torso loss, the Nova Cat is exceptionally difficult to destroy. Straightforward internal construction using common Clan components ensures rapid field repairs and reconfigurations, a significant logistical advantage for units operating far from supply lines.

The Primary configuration exemplifies the design's philosophy with two ER PPCs and three ER Large Lasers, creating a withering long-range energy barrage. Twenty-five double heat sinks struggle to dissipate a full alpha strike, but the all-energy loadout allows extended independent operations without ammunition concerns, and disciplined fire grouping keeps the 'Mech combat-effective indefinitely.
BMNovaCat_E.history:
The Nova Cat's origins are inseparable from the crisis that gripped Clan Nova Cat after Tukayyid. The Clan's defeat in 3052 shook its warriors to the core, and Khan Severen Leroux's decision to commission a new OmniMech was as much about restoring spiritual confidence as rebuilding military capability. Production began at Barcella Alpha, the Nova Cat capital world, and expanded to the Irece Alpha plant in early 3059 as the Clan began establishing its presence in the Inner Sphere.

The Nova Cat first saw significant combat during Operation Bulldog in 3059, when Clan Nova Cat's warriors turned their new OmniMech against Clan Smoke Jaguar. When the 357th Assault Cluster took Dyev from the Draconis Combine, the versatility of several Nova Cats proved decisive, with configurations mounting heavy autocannons and cluster munitions devastating militia vehicles and infantry formations. The sight of the towering twelve-meter 'Mech stalking through battlefield smoke became a potent psychological weapon against defending forces.

The Clan's Abjuration following their alliance with the Second Star League scattered Nova Cats across multiple factions' arsenals. Several units were seized by Clan Smoke Jaguar forces when they captured a malfunctioning Nova Cat DropShip during the chaos surrounding the Clan's dissolution. Sources in the Periphery persistently reported sightings of machines resembling the Nova Cat, suggesting that salvaged or captured examples may have entered the arsenals of Clans that accepted Smoke Jaguar refugees. The design also spread through more conventional channels, with Clan Diamond Shark's acquisition of the Barcella Alpha facility during the Civil War era enabling broader commercial distribution.

The Jihad proved devastating for Nova Cat production. The Irece Alpha plant was destroyed in 3071 during the Word of Blake's assault on the Draconis Combine, and individual Nova Cats were documented fighting desperate engagements against Blakist forces on worlds like Luthien and Caph. Despite the death of Clan Nova Cat as a political entity, the Tiburon Khanate maintained the Irece factory after it was rebuilt in the 3090s, meeting continued demand that proved both expected and surprising. Salvaged Nova Cats became a fixture in the Rasalhague Dominion, where native warriors of the former Free Rasalhague Republic put them to effective use despite being shunned by their Ghost Bear overlords.

By the ilClan era, the Nova Cat OmniMech had long outlived its parent Clan. Production continued at Irece under Draconis Combine control, while the Barcella facility's ownership passed through multiple Clan hands. Among the warriors of the Clan Protectorate, Nova Cat OmniMechs remain highly prized assets that frequently change hands through Trials of Possession, a fitting legacy for a design born from one Clan's determination to endure.
BMNovaCat_E.deployment: Developed during the Civil War era, the E configuration leverages Advanced Tactical Missile technology to create a highly flexible brawler. Four ATM 9 launchers, each supplied with two tons of ammunition, can engage targets at any range by selecting between standard, extended-range, and high-explosive munitions. A single Large Pulse Laser provides accurate direct fire support to finish targets weakened by missile volleys. The ATM system's adaptability means this configuration can shift between long-range fire support and devastating close-range engagement as the tactical situation demands, though pilots must carefully manage their ammunition expenditure across the different munition types to maintain effectiveness throughout prolonged operations.

Twenty-five double heat sinks cannot fully manage the tremendous thermal output of a simultaneous discharge, requiring pilots to employ disciplined fire grouping to maintain combat effectiveness. The lack of jump jets limits tactical flexibility in rough terrain, but the configuration's devastating long-range firepower makes it an ideal anchor for defensive positions or massed fire engagements.

BMNyx_NX100.overview:
The Nyx is a thirty-ton light BattleMech originally conceived by Word of Blake engineers as a fast and capable reconnaissance platform during the Jihad. Recovered by Draconis Combine forces during the liberation of Quentin in 3077, the design was subsequently brought into production through a joint agreement between the DCMS and the Republic of the Sphere, with manufacturing split between Diplan 'MechYards on Aix-la-Chapelle and Krupp Armament Works on Terra.

Though less a revolutionary design than an efficient amalgamation of proven technologies, the Nyx has earned a solid reputation as a fast, capable scout 'Mech. Its extraordinary speed and integrated electronic warfare systems make it a natural fit for reconnaissance and pursuit operations, and steady production has ensured a growing presence across multiple military establishments.
BMNyx_NX100.capabilities:
The heart of the Nyx is its Pitban 300 XL fusion engine, an oversized powerplant that pushes the thirty-ton chassis to a remarkable 162 kilometers per hour. This extraordinary speed, combined with a Beagle Active Probe, makes the Nyx a natural scout platform capable of detecting hidden units and rapidly relaying battlefield intelligence. The Chariot Type I-B endo steel chassis keeps structural weight to a minimum, while five tons of Krupp 200 ferro-fibrous armor provides respectable protection for a design in the light weight class.

The weapon loadout is practical rather than inspired. A pair of Diverse Optics extended-range medium lasers mounted in the arms serve as the primary offensive weapons, effective at medium to long range. A Diverse Optics extended-range small laser supplements the energy weapons at close quarters, while a Holly SRM-6 launcher delivers additional punch during hit-and-run engagements. Ten double heat sinks manage the thermal load efficiently, allowing sustained fire without significant overheating concerns.

The Nyx's primary weakness lies in its reliance on the XL engine, which leaves it vulnerable to catastrophic shutdown from a single side torso breach. The design has also earned a reputation as being difficult to maintain in the field, a legacy of its Word of Blake origins and the scarcity of specialized components during the early years of production.
BMNyx_NX100.history:
The origins of the Nyx trace back to the Word of Blake's extensive military development programs during the Jihad. As the Blakists expanded their war machine through the late 3060s and into the 3070s, their engineers conceived the Nyx as a fast scout 'Mech that could outpace most opponents while providing real-time battlefield intelligence. The design reached the field testing stage at Independence Weaponry facilities on Quentin before the planet's liberation by Allied Coalition forces in 3077, where a complete set of technical documentation and a mostly functional prototype fell into Draconis Combine hands.

The captured materials were rushed to Diplan 'MechYards on Aix-la-Chapelle, where Combine engineers quickly recognized the design's potential but struggled with its construction requirements. Many critical components were highly specialized and available only from factories on Terra, still under Word of Blake control at the time. For nearly two years the project stalled, with engineers forced to work with whatever substitute components they could scrounge.

Terra's liberation in 3079 changed the equation dramatically. The Draconis Combine approached the nascent Republic of the Sphere, and with Diplan's engineering knowledge and Krupp Armament Works' access to Terra-based manufacturing, the two powers established a joint production agreement. The Nyx entered full production shortly before the Jihad's formal end, with both Aix-la-Chapelle and Terra serving as manufacturing sites.

Within the DCMS, the Nyx found an enthusiastic reception among the Sword of Light regiments, where its speed and electronic warfare capabilities complemented existing reconnaissance doctrine. The Republic of the Sphere issued the design to its own forces and distributed small numbers to Coalition allies that had helped liberate Terra, a gesture that was received with less than stellar enthusiasm from the Draconis Combine. As the design matured, Diplan 'MechYards expanded production to include a range of specialized variants, from the C3-networked NX-80C to the missile-armed NX-100 and the technologically advanced NX-110.

As the Republic retreated behind Fortress Republic and the Dark Age descended, the Nyx remained in steady production at Aix-la-Chapelle for the DCMS. The design's relatively modest logistical demands and proven reliability have ensured its continued service, even as more advanced designs have entered the battlefield. The recovery of additional Word of Blake design notes, including the radical lance-armed NX-90 concept, has provided Combine engineers with ongoing opportunities to refine and expand the Nyx family.
BMNyx_NX100.deployment: Introduced around 3095, this variant replaces the torso-mounted equipment of the original design with three small MML-3 launchers, providing flexible fire support through the launchers' ability to switch between LRM and SRM ammunition types. Each arm retains an extended-range medium laser for direct engagements. The advanced electronics suite is eliminated entirely, while protection is upgraded to heavy ferro-fibrous armor. This variant trades the Nyx's signature scouting role for a more conventional light fire-support platform capable of engaging targets at varying ranges.

Production has remained extremely limited, with most units believed to see use in Solaris VII arena combat rather than conventional military deployments.

BMOBakemono_OBKM10.overview:
The O-Bakemono is an eighty-ton assault BattleMech developed in 3057 by Luthien Armor Works as part of an ambitious program to reverse-engineer captured Clan OmniMech technology. Named after the Japanese term for "great goblin," the design is directly based on the Clan Wolf Naga mobile artillery platform. LAW's engineers sought to replicate the devastating dual Arrow IV artillery capability of their Clan counterpart, creating what many consider the ideal fire-support BattleMech for the Draconis Combine Mustered Soldiery.

While the Inner Sphere version necessarily made compromises compared to the original Clan design, the O-Bakemono delivers an impressive long-range artillery punch that few contemporary designs can match. Produced exclusively at Luthien Armor Works' facilities on Luthien, the design's specialized role and the scarcity of Arrow IV munitions have always confined its deployment to larger, more elite DCMS commands.
BMOBakemono_OBKM10.capabilities:
Though LAW managed to implement the dual Shigunga Arrow IV launching system that defines the Naga, significant concessions were required to achieve this within Inner Sphere technological limitations. The O-Bakemono actually mounts five additional tons of StarSlab/3 armor compared to its Clan ancestor and carries a slightly expanded secondary weapons array, including two Diverse Optics Type 20 medium lasers and a ChisComp 32 small laser for close-range defense. These gains come at the cost of reduced heat dissipation capacity and a notable reduction in top speed, reinforcing the persistent technological gap between the Inner Sphere and the Clans despite decades of reverse-engineering efforts.

The twin Arrow IV systems provide the O-Bakemono with an effective engagement range of up to three kilometers, allowing the 'Mech to remain well behind the front lines while delivering devastating artillery barrages onto targets designated by friendly spotters. The Hermes 320 XL engine provides a respectable top speed of 64 kph for an eighty-ton chassis, granting sufficient mobility to reposition between fire missions. CASE protection in the side torsos mitigates the risk posed by the large ammunition stores. However, the near-total reliance on Arrow IV systems and their specialized munitions creates significant logistical demands, and the limited secondary armament leaves the design acutely vulnerable should hostile forces close to direct combat range.
BMOBakemono_OBKM10.history:
The O-Bakemono was born from the technological windfall of the Clan Invasion. Following the critical Battle of Wolcott in 3049, which provided the Draconis Combine with pristine examples of Clan military technology, Luthien Armor Works was tasked with reverse-engineering captured OmniMech systems. While LAW successfully produced several OmniMech designs at their Guthry Island facility, the O-Bakemono represented a different approach, a dedicated Inner Sphere BattleMech designed to replicate a specific Clan capability rather than the OmniMech concept itself.

In an unusual move for the Draconis Combine (reminiscent of programs by other Great Houses such as House Steiner's initial deployment of the Wolfhound with the Kell Hounds) the O-Bakemono first saw operational deployment with Camacho's Caballeros, a mercenary unit. Chandrasekhar Kurita reportedly secured a prototype, with or without his cousin the Coordinator's direct consent, and handed it to the Caballeros for field testing on Towne in 3057. The design's effectiveness was quickly validated during these trials, and reports of its capabilities soon filtered back to the DCMS high command.

The O-Bakemono's artillery-focused loadout and the chronic scarcity of Arrow IV ammunition prevented it from achieving widespread deployment across the DCMS. Instead, it was concentrated in larger, more elite commands where its specialized fire support capabilities could be properly integrated into combined-arms formations. During the campaigns against Clan Smoke Jaguar, O-Bakemono units provided devastating long-range support, with their dual Arrow IV systems proving particularly effective when coordinated with forward spotters operating in the Assault Company's Support Lance formations.

The Jihad devastated Luthien Armor Works' production facilities when the main factory complex was destroyed by nuclear detonation in 3068, a catastrophe engineered by Black Dragon agents. With production of the original OBK-M10 halted indefinitely, Combine field technicians developed the M11 and M12 field-salvage variants to keep surviving chassis operational using more readily available components. These improvised modifications traded the design's signature artillery capability for cheaper, more maintainable medium-range missile systems, ensuring the O-Bakemono remained a viable combat asset even as its original production line lay in ruins. The proliferation of these field refits during and after the Jihad speaks to both the durability of the underlying chassis and the ingenuity of Combine technicians working under desperate conditions.
BMOBakemono_OBKM10.deployment: The base model mounts twin Shigunga Arrow IV artillery systems supported by a pair of Diverse Optics medium lasers and a ChisComp small laser for self-defense. Fourteen tons of StarSlab armor with CASE protection and a Hermes 320 XL engine provide adequate survivability and mobility for the artillery role. While the Arrow IV's three-kilometer engagement range keeps the 'Mech safely behind the front lines, the expensive and scarce nature of Arrow IV munitions limits this configuration to well-supplied elite formations within the DCMS.

In an unusual move for the Draconis Combine (reminiscent of programs by other Great Houses such as House Steiner's initial deployment of the Wolfhound with the Kell Hounds) the O-Bakemono first saw operational deployment with Camacho's Caballeros, a mercenary unit. Chandrasekhar Kurita reportedly secured a prototype, with or without his cousin the Coordinator's direct consent, and handed it to the Caballeros for field testing on Towne in 3057. The design's effectiveness was quickly validated during these trials, and reports of its capabilities soon filtered back to the DCMS high command.

The O-Bakemono's artillery-focused loadout and the chronic scarcity of Arrow IV ammunition prevented it from achieving widespread deployment across the DCMS. Instead, it was concentrated in larger, more elite commands where its specialized fire support capabilities could be properly integrated into combined-arms formations. During the campaigns against Clan Smoke Jaguar, O-Bakemono units provided devastating long-range support, with their dual Arrow IV systems proving particularly effective when coordinated with forward spotters operating in the Assault Company's Support Lance formations.

The Jihad devastated Luthien Armor Works' production facilities when the main factory complex was destroyed by nuclear detonation in 3068, a catastrophe engineered by Black Dragon agents. With production of the original OBK-M10 halted indefinitely, Combine field technicians developed the M11 and M12 field-salvage variants to keep surviving chassis operational using more readily available components. These improvised modifications traded the design's signature artillery capability for cheaper, more maintainable medium-range missile systems, ensuring the O-Bakemono remained a viable combat asset even as its original production line lay in ruins. The proliferation of these field refits during and after the Jihad speaks to both the durability of the underlying chassis and the ingenuity of Combine technicians working under desperate conditions.
BMOBakemono_OBKM11.deployment: Born from the brutal necessity of the Jihad, this field-salvage variant emerged when maintaining the original design's complex systems became untenable during heavy fighting on Luthien and elsewhere. The modification replaces the Hermes 320 XL engine with a more readily available Pitban 240 standard fusion engine, reducing top speed to 54 kph. More significantly, the costly Arrow IV systems and their scarce ammunition are stripped out entirely in favor of twin MRM-40 launchers, each backed by four tons of ammunition. Fourteen double heat sinks manage the thermal load while a C3 slave unit integrates the 'Mech into a lance-level targeting network, helping guide the massive volleys of missiles with greater accuracy. Though lacking the extreme range of the original, this variant offers devastating medium-range firepower using plentiful and cheap MRM munitions.

BMOBakemono_OBKM12.overview:
The O-Bakemono is an eighty-ton assault BattleMech developed in 3057 by Luthien Armor Works as part of an ambitious program to reverse-engineer captured Clan OmniMech technology. Named after the Japanese term for "great goblin," the design is directly based on the Clan Wolf Naga mobile artillery platform. LAW's engineers sought to replicate the devastating dual Arrow IV artillery capability of their Clan counterpart, creating what many consider the ideal fire-support BattleMech for the Draconis Combine Mustered Soldiery.

While the Inner Sphere version necessarily made compromises compared to the original Clan design, the O-Bakemono delivers an impressive long-range artillery punch that few contemporary designs can match. Produced exclusively at Luthien Armor Works' facilities on Luthien, the design's specialized role and the scarcity of Arrow IV munitions have always confined its deployment to larger, more elite DCMS commands.
BMOBakemono_OBKM12.capabilities:
Though LAW managed to implement the dual Shigunga Arrow IV launching system that defines the Naga, significant concessions were required to achieve this within Inner Sphere technological limitations. The O-Bakemono actually mounts five additional tons of StarSlab/3 armor compared to its Clan ancestor and carries a slightly expanded secondary weapons array, including two Diverse Optics Type 20 medium lasers and a ChisComp 32 small laser for close-range defense. These gains come at the cost of reduced heat dissipation capacity and a notable reduction in top speed, confirming the persistent technological gap between the Inner Sphere and the Clans despite decades of reverse-engineering efforts.

The twin Arrow IV systems provide the O-Bakemono with an effective engagement range of up to three kilometers, allowing the 'Mech to remain well behind the front lines while delivering devastating artillery barrages onto targets designated by friendly spotters. The Hermes 320 XL engine provides a respectable top speed of 64 kph for an eighty-ton chassis, granting sufficient mobility to reposition between fire missions. CASE protection in the side torsos mitigates the risk posed by the large ammunition stores. However, the near-total reliance on Arrow IV systems and their specialized munitions creates significant logistical demands, and the limited secondary armament leaves the design acutely vulnerable should hostile forces close to direct combat range.

BMOBakemono_OBKM12.deployment: A rarer modification of the already-scarce M11 field refit, this variant sacrifices two double heat sinks and two tons of missile ammunition to replace the C3 slave unit with a full C3 master computer. This change transforms the 'Mech from a network participant into a lance coordinator, capable of directing the combined fire of up to three other C3-equipped units. The reduced ammunition capacity and diminished heat management make this variant even more difficult to produce and maintain in the field than its M11 predecessor, significantly limiting its numbers.

BMOcelot.overview: The Ocelot is a thirty-five-ton Clan light BattleMech designed by Clan Nova Cat following their Abjuration and relocation to the Irece Prefecture of the Draconis Combine. Produced at the Irece Alpha facility beginning in 3067, the design was developed by a team of Nova Cat researchers and captured Smoke Jaguar scientists under the direction of Khan Santin West. The Ocelot represented Clan Nova Cat's determination to rebuild their touman with domestically produced BattleMechs rather than relying solely on OmniMech production or outside procurement. At thirty-five tons, the design fills the role of a fast, aggressive skirmisher capable of punishing opponents at medium range while using its mobility to avoid sustained engagements.
BMOcelot.capabilities:
The Ocelot's primary armament centers on a torso-mounted Model X heavy large laser, a weapon capable of devastating damage for a chassis of this weight class. The original design called for a shoulder mount similar to the Pack Hunter's weapon placement, but focusing difficulties with the heavy large laser forced the engineering team to relocate it to the main torso cavity with dedicated shock absorbers. This repositioning limits the weapon's firing arc, requiring pilots to twist the 'Mech's torso more aggressively than typical light designs, a tendency that becomes particularly pronounced during airborne evasive maneuvers when the design's center of gravity shifts toward the weapon.

Supporting the main gun, a pair of Series 2d extended-range medium lasers provide consistent mid-range firepower with an identical effective range envelope. A bank of fifteen double heat sinks manages the thermal load adequately under normal operations, though sustained fire combined with heavy jump jet use will eventually overwhelm the cooling system. To compensate for the chassis instability created by the heavy laser's mass, the designers implemented distinctive "stub wing" extensions that help maintain balance during the Ocelot's 180-meter jumps. An Irecian "Squealer" light active probe rounds out the sensor suite, ensuring pilots maintain situational awareness appropriate for the design's skirmisher role.
BMOcelot.history:
The Ocelot emerged from one of the most turbulent periods in Clan Nova Cat's history. Following the Clan's Abjuration and expulsion from Clan space, the Nova Cats settled in the Irece Prefecture of the Draconis Combine, bringing with them a group of former Smoke Jaguar scientists acquired as isorla during their flight. Khan Santin West recognized that rebuilding the Clan's military capabilities required domestic manufacturing capacity, and in the early 3060s he directed these scientists alongside Nova Cat researchers to develop new BattleMech designs at the Irece Alpha facility, itself built on the ruins of the former LexaTech Industries plant destroyed during the initial Clan invasion.

The Ocelot entered production in 3067, just as the Word of Blake Jihad was beginning to engulf the Inner Sphere. Despite the chaos of the era, the design saw rapid deployment across Clan Nova Cat's frontline forces. The Jihad took a severe toll on Irece Alpha's workforce, with the facility losing fifty-five percent of its workers and operating at only sixty-five percent capacity by 3079. However, production of the Ocelot and its variants continued throughout the conflict.

The design saw combat across multiple theaters during the Jihad, with Nova Cat forces deploying Ocelots in actions ranging from the failed 3072 attempt to liberate Luthien to various defensive engagements against Word of Blake forces. Individual Ocelots also found their way into Republic of the Sphere service during the early Dark Age, as some Nova Cat warriors brought their machines with them when joining the nascent state following the Jihad's conclusion.

The Irece Alpha facility suffered destruction during the Second Combine-Dominion War but was reconstructed during the 3120s, resuming production of the Ocelot and its variants. By the ilClan era, with Clan Nova Cat destroyed as a political entity, production continued under Draconis Combine authority, ensuring the design's continued availability to Combine forces.
BMOcelot.deployment: The base Ocelot configuration centers on a heavy large laser as its primary striking weapon, supported by extended-range medium lasers and backed by a light active probe for situational awareness. The standard configuration emphasizes the design's skirmisher role, encouraging pilots to use their jump jets to achieve favorable firing positions before delivering punishing volleys and withdrawing before heavier opponents can respond. Initial resistance from traditionalist MechWarriors who viewed a standard BattleMech as a step backward from OmniMech technology faded once the Ocelot demonstrated its reliability and combat effectiveness in frontline service.

Though initially tested by engineers at the Irece Alpha manufacturing plant, the modification's simplicity made it easily replicable in the field, and it was eventually adopted into regular factory production during the Jihad years.

The armament is rebuilt around an extended-range large laser paired with two heavy medium lasers, supplemented by a targeting computer for enhanced accuracy and an ECM suite for electronic warfare protection. These changes come at the cost of three double heat sinks, making heat management a more pressing concern during prolonged engagements. Rather than manufacturing the targeting computer and ECM suite domestically, Clan Nova Cat negotiated with Clan Diamond Shark to supply both systems in exchange for a percentage of Irece Alpha's industrial output.
