BMOcelot_4.deployment: Emerging during the Dark Age, this variant strips the original Ocelot's entire weapons suite and light active probe, replacing them with an all-pulse laser armament consisting of a Series 44h large pulse laser and a pair of Kolibri Delta Series medium pulse lasers. The shift to pulse technology dramatically improves the design's accuracy, addressing the heavy large laser's inherent imprecision that plagued the base model. While sacrificing some raw damage potential compared to the original configuration, the pulse laser suite provides more reliable damage output, particularly against fast-moving targets at closer ranges.

BMOmega_SHP5R.overview: The Omega is the first truly viable superheavy BattleMech ever produced, introduced in 3076 by Skobel MechWorks on Terra under Word of Blake direction. Weighing an unprecedented 150 tons, the Omega represents the culmination of centuries of failed attempts at superheavy construction, from the Terran Hegemony's early experiments through the infamous Matar. Standing half again as tall as the hundred-ton King Crab, the design proved that the superheavy concept could succeed where all previous efforts had failed. Close to thirty were manufactured before the fall of the Word of Blake, earning a fearsome reputation during their brief operational service in the final battles of the Jihad on Terra.
BMOmega_SHP5R.capabilities:
Powered by a Vlar 300 XL engine, the Omega achieves a maximum speed of just 32 kph, making it among the slowest 'Mechs to walk any battlefield. This deliberate sacrifice of mobility allows the design to carry twenty-seven tons of Aldis Plate armor reinforced with CASE II protection across the arms and torso sections, creating an extraordinarily resilient platform capable of absorbing tremendous punishment. The superheavy construction demanded a Heavy-Duty Gyro to manage the immense stresses placed on the chassis, adding weight but significantly improving the design's ability to remain standing under concentrated fire.

The Omega's primary armament consists of three M-7 Gauss Rifles distributed across the left torso, center torso, and right torso, a configuration made possible by the superheavy construction that allowed mounting a standard Inner Sphere Gauss Rifle with ammunition and CASE II in the center torso for the first time. Two Imperator Code Red LB 10-X Autocannons mounted in the arms provide flexible firepower through cluster or solid-shot ammunition selection. This weapons mix creates a devastating defensive emplacement and even a serviceable low-altitude anti-air platform.

Each Omega integrates an Improved C3 Computer into its communications suite, enabling the massive 'Mech to share targeting data across a network. Despite this technological sophistication, the Omega remains cumbersome and difficult to pilot, with the superheavy mass imposing severe limitations on tactical maneuverability.
BMOmega_SHP5R.history:
The quest to build a BattleMech exceeding one hundred tons stretches back to the late twenty-eighth century, when Terran Hegemony engineers first attempted superheavy construction. These early efforts met with repeated failure, and the concept was widely derided after Stefan Amaris commissioned the Matar during the Amaris Civil War. The Matar's engineering shortcomings earned it the lasting nickname "Amaris' Folly," though its underlying chassis and musculature research eventually found use in the Clans' Stone Rhino design. Despite these partial successes, no faction managed to produce a fully functional superheavy BattleMech until the Word of Blake turned its considerable resources toward the problem.

Working from Skobel MechWorks' facilities in Russia on Terra, Blakist engineers developed revolutionary solutions to the structural and mobility challenges that had defeated all previous designers. Their innovations in enhanced hybrid myomer fibers, oversized actuators, and a purpose-built superheavy endo-steel skeleton produced a chassis capable of supporting 150 tons of combat equipment. Close to thirty Omegas were manufactured beginning in 3076, though the design remained technically in its prototype phase throughout its operational life.

The majority of these machines were deployed in defense of Terra during Operation SCOUR, concentrated around the Devils Peak command post where Precentor Martial Cameron St. Jamais directed the Word of Blake's final resistance. Additional Omegas were sighted at Hilton Head Island and in Cairo. Combined with the Blakists' other unconventional assets (including drone 'Mechs, mobile defense platforms, and Land-Air 'Mechs) the Omegas contributed to fierce multi-front resistance during the last days of the Jihad. All engaged Omegas were publicly believed destroyed, and the superheavy manufacturing wing at Skobel was demolished during the liberation of Terra.

Unfinished Omega hulls even so survived within the Skobel complex. Following the establishment of the Republic of the Sphere, rebuilding Skobel MechWorks was given high priority, and Republic engineers used these surviving hulls as the foundation for their superheavy research program. Several SHP-5R models were completed with modifications necessitated by the loss of certain Blakist manufacturing techniques. At least one functional original Omega also survived on Solaris VII, where it was maintained by the administrators of the Ishiyama arena and occasionally deployed as a special hazard during assault 'Mech bouts. The hard-won lessons from the Omega program (along with those from the subsequent and less successful Orca prototype) ultimately contributed to the Republic's development of colossal tripod designs such as the Poseidon and Ares.
BMOmega_SHP5R.deployment: Developed by the Republic of the Sphere as part of its superheavy research program beginning around 3103, this variant was built from surviving SHP-X4 hulls recovered from the Skobel complex on Terra. Generally considered a downgrade from the original design, this variant replaces the advanced superheavy endo-steel skeleton with a standard superheavy structure, adding internal weight at the cost of available payload capacity. More significantly, the three M-7 Gauss Rifles were replaced with Heavy PPCs, eliminating the design's ammunition dependency but fundamentally altering its combat profile from a ballistic-focused platform to an energy-weapons combatant. These modifications reflect the Republic's inability to replicate certain Word of Blake technologies, particularly the specialized endo-steel construction techniques. The SHP-5R served as an important stepping stone in the Republic's broader superheavy development effort, contributing valuable operational data toward later colossal tripod programs.

BMOmen.overview: The Omen is an 85-ton Clan assault BattleMech designed by Clan Snow Raven and first produced in 3087 at the Snow Raven Industrial Complex Alpha on Dante. Conceived in the aftermath of the Jihad, the Omen was developed as a conventional BattleMech that could be manufactured more quickly and in greater numbers than an OmniMech design, addressing the severe losses suffered during the Wars of Reaving and the Jihad itself. The Omen fills the role of an all-purpose garrison assault 'Mech within the Raven Alliance touman, earning a solid reputation as a dependable anchor for second-line formations tasked with defending the Alliance's vast territorial holdings.
BMOmen.capabilities:
Built on a CSR Version 84.62 Standard chassis and powered by a Type 255 Extra-Light fusion engine, the Omen achieves a modest top speed of 54 km/h. While this makes it slow by Clan assault 'Mech standards, three Andoran Model JJ III jump jets compensate by providing 90 meters of tactical repositioning capability, allowing the 'Mech to exploit terrain advantages that would otherwise be inaccessible to a design of its weight class.

The Omen's weapon systems are designed for engagement across all range brackets. A Kolibri Delta Series Large Pulse Laser and a Type KOV LB 10-X Autocannon serve as the primary direct-fire weapons, capable of delivering accurate and sustained punishment at medium to long range. A Remer Series Alpha Deuce Advanced Tactical Missile-12 launcher provides exceptional tactical flexibility, with sufficient ammunition tonnage to carry a mix of warhead types suited to any combat situation. At closer ranges, paired Series 2d Extended Range Medium Lasers and 14a Medium Pulse Lasers give the Omen a devastating short-range punch. A head-mounted anti-missile system offers additional protection against incoming missile fire.

Defensively, the Omen carries sixteen and a half tons of Longanecker PlastiSteel standard armor with CASE-protected ammunition bins, making it exceptionally durable for a second-line design. The chief weakness lies in its limited heat dissipation, with only eighteen double heat sinks requiring MechWarriors to exercise careful fire discipline to avoid dangerous overheating.
BMOmen.history:
The Omen's development was driven by the Snow Ravens' precarious position following the Jihad. Having relocated the bulk of their forces to the Inner Sphere and merged politically with the Outworlds Alliance to form the Raven Alliance, the Clan found its ground forces stretched thin across a vast territory. The losses sustained during the Wars of Reaving and the Jihad itself had depleted the touman's BattleMech strength, particularly among the garrison and auxiliary Clusters responsible for defending Alliance space.

The Snow Raven scientist caste responded by developing a series of new second-line designs that could be built at the Clan's Dante production facilities without the extensive tooling and rare components demanded by OmniMech production. The Omen emerged alongside designs such as the Dark Crow and Goshawk II as part of this rebuilding effort. Production began in 3087, with the Twelfth Raven Garrison Cluster serving as the primary unit for field trials and operational testing of the new assault 'Mech.

Initial deliveries to auxiliary and garrison Clusters commenced in 3088, and production schedules projected that the Omen would reach sufficient numbers to restore full fighting strength to second-line formations by approximately 3095. The decision to restrict production exclusively to the Snow Raven Industrial Complex Alpha on Dante, rather than licensing the design to Outworlds Alliance manufacturers, reflected ongoing tensions within the Raven Alliance regarding the sharing of Clan military technology.

Through the Republic Era and into the Dark Age, the Omen became an increasingly common sight in Raven Alliance garrison forces. The introduction of the Omen 2 variant in 3141 demonstrated the Snow Ravens' continued investment in the design, adapting it with self-repair technology to improve battlefield survivability in the increasingly hostile strategic environment of the post-Blackout era. The Omen remains in active production as one of the Raven Alliance's principal second-line assault 'Mechs through the ilClan period.
BMOmen.deployment: The base Omen represents the standard production model that entered service in 3087. Designed as a garrison assault 'Mech for the Snow Raven touman, it balances firepower, armor protection, and limited jump capability to serve as the backbone of second-line Clusters. Its mix of ballistic, missile, energy, and pulse weapons gives it the versatility expected of a design intended to face threats ranging from pirate raids to full-scale Clan assaults without the luxury of choosing its engagements.

BMOmen_2.overview: The Omen is an 85-ton Clan assault BattleMech designed by Clan Snow Raven and first produced in 3087 at the Snow Raven Industrial Complex Alpha on Dante. Conceived in the aftermath of the Jihad, the Omen was developed as a conventional BattleMech that could be manufactured more quickly and in greater numbers than an OmniMech design, addressing the severe losses suffered during the Wars of Reaving and the Jihad itself. The Omen fills the role of an all-purpose garrison assault 'Mech within the Raven Alliance touman, earning a solid reputation as a dependable anchor for second-line formations tasked with defending the Alliance's vast territorial holdings.
BMOmen_2.capabilities:
Built on a CSR Version 84.62 Standard chassis and powered by a Type 255 Extra-Light fusion engine, the Omen achieves a modest top speed of 54 km/h. While this makes it slow by Clan assault 'Mech standards, three Andoran Model JJ III jump jets compensate by providing 90 meters of tactical repositioning capability, allowing the 'Mech to exploit terrain advantages that would otherwise be inaccessible to a design of its weight class.

The Omen's weapon systems are designed for engagement across all range brackets. A Kolibri Delta Series Large Pulse Laser and a Type KOV LB 10-X Autocannon serve as the primary direct-fire weapons, capable of delivering accurate and sustained punishment at medium to long range. A Remer Series Alpha Deuce Advanced Tactical Missile-12 launcher provides exceptional tactical flexibility, with sufficient ammunition tonnage to carry a mix of warhead types suited to any combat situation. At closer ranges, paired Series 2d Extended Range Medium Lasers and 14a Medium Pulse Lasers give the Omen a devastating short-range punch. A head-mounted anti-missile system offers additional protection against incoming missile fire.

Defensively, the Omen carries sixteen and a half tons of Longanecker PlastiSteel standard armor with CASE-protected ammunition bins, making it exceptionally durable for a second-line design. The chief weakness lies in its limited heat dissipation, with only eighteen double heat sinks requiring MechWarriors to exercise careful fire discipline to avoid dangerous overheating.
BMOmen_2.history:
The Omen's development was driven by the Snow Ravens' precarious position following the Jihad. Having relocated the bulk of their forces to the Inner Sphere and merged politically with the Outworlds Alliance to form the Raven Alliance, the Clan found its ground forces stretched thin across a vast territory. The losses sustained during the Wars of Reaving and the Jihad itself had depleted the touman's BattleMech strength, particularly among the garrison and auxiliary Clusters responsible for defending Alliance space.

The Snow Raven scientist caste responded by developing a series of new second-line designs that could be built at the Clan's Dante production facilities without the extensive tooling and rare components demanded by OmniMech production. Through the Republic Era and into the Dark Age, the Omen became an increasingly common sight in Raven Alliance garrison forces. The introduction of the Omen 2 variant in 3141 demonstrated the Snow Ravens' continued investment in the design, adapting it with self-repair technology to improve battlefield survivability in the increasingly hostile strategic environment of the post-Blackout era. The Omen remains in active production as one of the Raven Alliance's principal second-line assault 'Mechs through the ilClan period.
BMOmen_2.deployment: Introduced in 3141, this variant trades raw firepower for improved survivability through the addition of HarJel III self-repair systems in each side torso. To accommodate this technology, engineers downgraded the primary missile launcher and reduced its ammunition supply, while removing some of the secondary laser armament and several heat sinks. This refit reflects the Raven Alliance's growing emphasis on keeping 'Mechs operational in sustained engagements far from established supply lines, a practical consideration given the Alliance's vast territorial holdings and limited repair infrastructure.

BMOnager.overview: The Onager is a ninety-ton Clan assault BattleMech introduced in 3083 by Red Devil Industries on Pandora for Clan Jade Falcon. Named after a medieval siege engine, the design was developed to fill the Jade Falcon garrison clusters with a proper Clan-technology assault platform, replacing the captured Inner Sphere machines that had been pressed into service during the Jihad. Built around proven Clan technology, the Onager prioritized durability, ease of maintenance, and manufacturing simplicity over cutting-edge performance, making it well suited to the second-line formations it was intended to reinforce. The design served as a visible commitment to rebuilding the Falcon's defensive strength with purpose-built Clan hardware.
BMOnager.capabilities:
Built around a sturdy endo steel frame, the Onager is protected by fifteen tons of ferro-fibrous armor, giving the ninety-ton chassis substantial staying power in prolonged engagements. Its Consolidated 270-rated fusion engine deliberately sacrifices speed for reliability and ease of maintenance, propelling the 'Mech to a modest fifty-four kilometers per hour. This slow pace is offset by five improved jump jets that grant the Onager a hundred and fifty meters of jump capability, providing the mobility of a much lighter design and making it surprisingly effective in urban and broken terrain.

The Onager's primary long-range threat is a Type 0 Hyper-Assault Gauss 30 rifle mounted in the left arm, which delivers devastating cluster fire at extended ranges. As opponents close, the 'Mech brings a punishing array of short-range weapons to bear: twin Pattern J7 SRM-6 launchers exploit gaps torn open by the HAG, while a pair of Series 14a medium pulse lasers provide accurate energy fire. For anti-infantry work, two Raid micro pulse lasers and a Chi Series small pulse laser round out the arsenal. The design runs warm under sustained fire, as its twelve double heat sinks struggle to manage the full weapon suite simultaneously, forcing pilots to exercise fire discipline at close quarters.
BMOnager.history:
The Onager's development was a direct consequence of the devastation wrought by the Jihad on Clan Jade Falcon's touman. By the end of the conflict, the Falcon garrison clusters were severely depleted and still reliant on captured Inner Sphere BattleMechs to fill their ranks. Khan Samantha Clees, determined to rebuild the Clan's defensive strength with proper Clan-technology platforms, ordered the engineering team fresh off the Flamberge project to design a new assault 'Mech prioritizing production volume and low maintenance costs over raw performance.

The most controversial aspect of the Onager's creation was the decision to upgrade and expand the Red Devil Industries facilities on Pandora for its production. The factory had long operated under Merchant Factor Daniel's policy of segregating different production plants, but the expansion signaled a relaxation of this approach. Red Devil Industries, originally a Lyran manufacturer with a checkered reputation for quality, had been pressed into Jade Falcon service after Pandora's capture during the FedCom Civil War. The facility had weathered labor unrest and Jihad-era production shortfalls but remained the largest producer of second-line 'Mechs in the Jade Falcon Occupation Zone.

The first production Onagers were dispatched to Iota Galaxy for operational testing against pirates and Periphery raiders along the Falcon border. Against such opponents the design performed admirably, earning positive reviews from warriors who appreciated having a genuine Clan assault platform rather than a salvaged Inner Sphere machine. The 'Mech was subsequently allocated more broadly to fill out second-line formations, and many garrison warriors were grateful to replace their aging equipment with a purpose-built Clan design, even though it lacked the flexibility of an OmniMech.

By the Dark Age, the Onager had become a mainstay of Jade Falcon garrison forces. Reports indicated that Khan Clees had considered deploying Onager-equipped units on raids against rival Clans to further test the design against more capable opponents, though such operations had not materialized by the time Pandora's political situation shifted again. The introduction of the Onager 2 variant in 3137 demonstrated continued investment in the chassis, adapting it with heavier energy weapons and self-repair capability for the evolving battlefields of the Dark Age.
BMOnager.deployment: The base Onager configuration was initially dispatched to garrison clusters along the Jade Falcon border, where it replaced aging captured Inner Sphere designs in second-line formations. Garrison warriors appreciated having a genuine Clan assault platform capable of anchoring a defensive position, and the design saw steady deployment across Iota Galaxy and other second-line units throughout the Falcon Occupation Zone. By the Dark Age, the Onager had become a mainstay of Jade Falcon garrison forces, widely distributed among clusters tasked with holding the Clan's extensive border regions.

BMOnager_2.deployment: Introduced in 3137, the Onager 2 is a significant reworking of the original design's weapons philosophy. To accommodate this heavier energy loadout, the five improved jump jets were swapped for three standard jump jets, reducing jump capability to ninety meters but freeing critical weight and space. The most notable addition is HarJel II self-repair systems installed in both side torsos, giving the Onager 2 the ability to automatically seal breaches and stabilize internal damage during combat, significantly improving its survivability in sustained engagements.

BMOnslaught_SAOS.overview: The Onslaught is a seventy-five-ton heavy BattleMech produced by Solaris Arms, the small Solaris VII-based manufacturer known for designing arena-specific combat machines. Initially conceived as a technology test bed in the wake of the Clan Invasion, the Onslaught soon entered limited production and proved popular enough to keep the company afloat for years. Though mainstream manufacturers dismissed it as a limited-run novelty, the design earned a loyal following among Solaris stables and independent gladiators, establishing itself as one of the more recognizable heavy designs on the arena circuit. Over a hundred were built across the design's production life, with a distinctive culture of salvage rebuilds extending its presence well beyond original manufacturing numbers.
BMOnslaught_SAOS.capabilities:
The Onslaught's defining characteristic is its remarkable speed for a heavy 'Mech. Powered by a 375-rated XL fusion engine, the design achieves a cruising speed of fifty-four kilometers per hour and a maximum speed of eighty-six, performance figures that compare favorably with 'Mechs ten or twenty tons lighter. Five standard jump jets further enhance its mobility with a jump capacity of one hundred fifty meters, making the Onslaught one of the most agile heavy designs on the Solaris arena circuit.

The SA-OS2 mounts an experimental SA Light Autocannon/5 paired with an SA Large X-Pulse Laser as its primary weapons. Six Voelkers 200 machine guns provide effective anti-infantry capability and close-range supplemental fire, while two SureShot Mk VIa SRM-6 launchers deliver significant short-range punch. An experimental Angel ECM Suite integrated into the custom targeting system provides electronic warfare protection, including defense against Streak missile locks.

This speed and agility comes at a cost, however. The Onslaught's armor protection, while adequate, is hardly exceptional for a seventy-five-ton chassis. The reliance on an XL engine also creates a critical vulnerability to side torso damage, a trade-off that demands skilled piloting to mitigate in the unforgiving arena environment.
BMOnslaught_SAOS.history:
The Onslaught emerged during the technological ferment that followed the Clan Invasion, as Solaris Arms sought to capitalize on the flood of new technologies reaching the Inner Sphere's arenas. Designed as a platform to test and showcase experimental weapon systems, the design entered production in the early 3050s and quickly established itself as a competitive heavy contender in the Solaris VII arena circuit. More than one hundred Onslaughts were built over the design's decade and a half of production, with roughly forty-five remaining in active service by the mid-3060s.

Despite its niche origins, the Onslaught proved commercially viable enough to sustain Solaris Arms through the economic turbulence of the early 3060s, a period that nearly drove the small manufacturer into bankruptcy. The introduction of the SA-OS2 standard in 3062 and the subsequent SA-OS3 variant reinvigorated sales and secured the company's survival. Solaris Arms' strategy of offering upgrade kits that could bring older SA-OS models up to SA-OS2 specifications proved particularly shrewd, extending the service life of existing machines without requiring full new production.

The Onslaught's limited production numbers and the violent nature of arena combat have ensured a steady attrition rate, contributing to the proliferation of FrankenMech rebuilds that have become the design's most distinctive cultural feature. The practice of combining salvaged components from multiple destroyed Onslaughts into a single functioning machine became so widespread that it developed into a recognized tradition among Solaris stables and independent gladiators alike. These rebuilt machines often adopt combined names from their donor 'Mechs, further cementing the Onslaught's reputation as a uniquely Solarian creation.

During the Jihad, Solaris Arms' facility on Solaris VII suffered no capital or personnel losses and maintained full production capacity through at least 3072. The Onslaught continued to serve primarily in the arena circuit throughout this period, though the broader conflict disrupted the gladiatorial economy that sustained demand for the design.
BMOnslaught_SAOS.deployment: The original Onslaught was the design that established Solaris Arms' reputation as a viable heavy 'Mech manufacturer. Armed with an Ultra Autocannon/5 and a standard large laser as its primary weapons, supplemented by six machine guns and twin SRM-6 launchers, this variant was a competent arena combatant hampered by only twelve tons of armor protection. While its speed and maneuverability were exceptional for the weight class, its weapons made up less than half the 'Mech's total mass, leaving it outgunned by most contemporary heavy designs. The original model served as the foundation for all subsequent Onslaught development and remains the basis for many of the FrankenMech rebuilds that circulate on Solaris VII.

StarGuard CIII armor with CASE provides improved survivability over the original design.

BMOnslaught_SAOS3.deployment: This variant differs from the SA-OS2 through fundamental structural modifications that make it available only as a factory-built 'Mech rather than a field upgrade. The primary armament is reconfigured around an Ultra Autocannon/10 paired with a Medium X-Pulse Laser, trading the SA-OS2's longer engagement range for greater close-range firepower. The SA-OS3's distinct construction requirements mean that it cannot be produced from upgrade kits, requiring full new production from Solaris Arms' facility.

BMOrionIIC.overview: As Aleksandr Kerensky’s chosen BattleMech, the original Orion held a special place within the Clans, especially Clan Wolf. Out of respect for the Great Father, the Clans maintained the design for decades despite the invention of newer technologies. Behind the scenes, however, Clan Wolf was designing an updated version, as they saw it, neither of the great Kerenskys would have approved of blindly following tradition at the expense of military progress. The Orion IIC debuted early in the Golden Century but received little attention alongside the OmniMechs that were fast becoming standard frontline machines. Clan Wolf has jealously guarded the Orion IIC design, defending their exclusive right to it in Trials of Possession and refusing all proposed trades despite generous offers. Like the Kerensky bloodname heritages, Clan Wolf sees the Orion IIC as tied to their honor as guardians of Kerensky’s legacy.
BMOrionIIC.capabilities:
Produced before the advent of OmniMechs, the Orion IIC features many technological advancements preserved or developed by the Clans. Endo steel and ferro-fibrous construction materials lighten the design, allowing for a heavier weapons configuration, while double heat sinks manage thermal buildup effectively. The IIC upgrades the original Orion’s medium lasers to extended-range large lasers, particularly two different models, the result of a late design change in which a pulse laser was upgraded to an extended-range weapon. The older Series 6W laser was retained despite maintenance complications because it better matched the original design’s architecture.

A Clan-specification Omega 12-Coil Gauss rifle replaces the original autocannon, delivering devastating kinetic impacts without generating heat, while upgraded Type XX “Great Bow” LRM-20 and Offset Pattern K4 SRM-4 launchers provide comprehensive missile coverage. The resulting design delivers significantly more firepower than the Inner Sphere original while maintaining the same seventy-five-ton weight class, evidence of the efficiency of Clan manufacturing techniques.
BMOrionIIC.history:
The Orion IIC’s history is inseparable from Clan Wolf’s reverence for Aleksandr Kerensky. While other Clans moved rapidly toward OmniMech technology during the Golden Century, Clan Wolf’s scientists quietly redesigned the Orion to incorporate Clan technological advancements while preserving the spirit of Kerensky’s chosen mount. The IIC debuted early in the Golden Century at WC Aux Site #2 on Strana Mechty, produced in limited numbers exclusively for Clan Wolf’s use.

Clan Wolf has consistently defended its exclusive claim to the Orion IIC, winning Trials of Possession against other Clans who sought the design and refusing all trade proposals regardless of how generous the offers. This possessiveness mirrors the Wolf Clan’s guardianship of the Kerensky bloodname heritages, both are considered matters of honor central to the Clan’s identity.

Rather than assigning the Orion IIC to frontline units, Clan Wolf uses the design to reward officers in second-line Galaxies who are expected to advance to frontline assignments. Each Orion IIC is sent to its recipient “with the compliments of” Clan Wolf’s Khan or saKhan, a gesture of personal recognition that no officer has ever refused, even if it meant trading an assault-class BattleMech for the smaller heavy design.

A few Orion IICs traveled to the Inner Sphere with Phelan Kell’s Wolves-in-Exile, where they remain part of the exiled Clan’s second-line forces. Especially, no effort has been made to produce the Orion IIC outside Strana Mechty, a possible gesture of reconciliation toward the homeworld Clan Wolf. The Jihad-era Wars of Reaving disrupted Strana Mechty production, and a refit facility at W-7 Facilities on Weingarten was established to convert purchased Inner Sphere chassis to IIC specifications.
BMOrionIIC.deployment: Clan Wolf produces the standard Orion IIC in limited numbers at WC Aux Site #2 on Strana Mechty, with additional refits conducted at W-7 Facilities on Weingarten using purchased Inner Sphere chassis. The design’s Omega 12-Coil Gauss Rifle serves as the primary weapon, complemented by a Type XX “Great Bow” LRM-20 for ranged bombardment and two extended-range large lasers (the Series 6W and Series 7W) providing heavy energy firepower. An Offset Pattern K4 SRM launcher handles close-range engagements. The combination creates a versatile seventy-five-ton platform that outperforms the Inner Sphere original in virtually every engagement category.

BMOrion_C.overview: Commissioned by the Terran Hegemony in response to the expanding BattleMech arms race that followed Operation PROMETHEUS, the Orion was designed by General Mechanics on Mars as the Hegemony’s premier heavy attack BattleMech. First fielded in prototype form in 2456, the seventy-five-ton design has remained in continuous production for over half a millennium, making it one of the longest-serving BattleMech designs in history. Often called “a poor man’s Atlas,” the Orion earned lasting fame as the chosen mount of General Aleksandr Kerensky during his campaign to liberate Terra from Stefan Amaris, an image that made the Orion one of the most recognized BattleMechs in known space. Production shifted to Kali Yama Weapons Industries in the Free Worlds League after the fall of the Star League, and the Orion’s roomy, easily maintained chassis has proven remarkably adaptable to successive generations of weapons technology, ensuring its continued relevance across every major conflict of the last five centuries.
BMOrion_C.capabilities:
The Orion’s design philosophy emphasizes versatility through a balanced mix of ballistic, missile, and energy weapons systems, an approach that has kept the chassis competitive even as battlefield technology has evolved dramatically. The standard ON1-K mounts a KaliYama Class 10 Autocannon as its primary weapon, supplemented by a KaliYama Death Bloom LRM-15 launcher for ranged fire support, two Irian Weapons Works medium lasers, and an SRM-4 rack to exploit armor breaches at close range. Over fourteen tons of Valiant Lamellor armor provides protection sufficient for sustained frontline combat, while a Vlar 300 fusion engine delivers a respectable maximum speed of sixty-four kilometers per hour.

The chassis’s greatest strength lies in its adaptability. The roomy internal layout has readily accommodated every major technological advancement since the Star League era, from XL engines and double heat sinks to extended-range weaponry and advanced fire control systems. This flexibility has produced an extraordinary number of variants, from simple field refits that swap missile launchers to ground-up redesigns mounting Gauss rifles and experimental weapons. Any MechWarrior who can pilot one Orion can quickly adapt to virtually any variant, a logistical advantage that few other designs can match.
BMOrion_C.history:
The Orion’s origins trace to the earliest days of the BattleMech arms race. After the Lyran Commonwealth obtained BattleMech technology through Operation PROMETHEUS, the Terran Hegemony commissioned General Mechanics of Mars to develop a new heavy attack ’Mech. The first ON1-C prototype debuted in 2453 but was rejected by the Hegemony Armed Forces for insufficient firepower. General Mechanics returned to the drawing board, settling on a smaller engine to free mass for additional weapons. The third prototype (the ON1-H, incorporating the newly developed class-10 autocannon) finally won HAF approval in 2456.

The Orion served the Hegemony with distinction, but its defining moment came centuries later during the Amaris Civil War. General Aleksandr Kerensky chose an Orion as his personal BattleMech, piloting it through the liberation of Terra and the capture of Stefan Amaris. That olive-drab Orion became one of the most recognized machines in military history. When Kerensky departed on the Exodus, he abandoned the venerable ’Mech, which was eventually recovered by Combine salvage teams in the New Samarkand system and given to the young Theodore Kurita. Named “Revenant,” the machine served Theodore through the Fourth Succession War before reportedly being destroyed on Marfik.

Production shifted from the original Hesperus II and Mars facilities to Kali Yama Weapons Industries on Kalidasa and the Kali Yama/Alphard Trading Corporation joint venture on Kendall following the fall of the Star League. The Free Worlds League became the largest producer, fueling complaints that the Marik Militia received more than their fair share of new Orions. The Outreach Accords during the Clan Invasion opened League military exports to the other Great Houses, sparking a golden age for Kali Yama and the Alphard Trading Corporation.

The recovery of Star League technology in the late 3040s produced the ON1-M upgrade, trading the temperamental autocannon for a versatile LB 10-X and adding an XL engine. The plethora of field variants that followed (Artemis IV refits, MRM conversions, rotary autocannon upgrades, and light Gauss substitutions) testified to the chassis’s enduring adaptability. The ON2-M represented the first ground-up redesign, employing an endo steel frame, Gauss rifle, and Artemis-equipped LRM-15 to create what many consider the definitive modern Orion. Kali Yama’s ON3-M “Orion 3100” pushed the design further with Extended LRM technology, though declining military budgets limited initial sales.

When Clan Wolf captured Kalidasa, they converted the Kali Yama production lines to build the Orion C, a fitting tribute to Kerensky’s legacy that combined the proven Inner Sphere chassis with cutting-edge Clan weaponry.
BMOrion_C.deployment: When Clan Wolf captured the Kali Yama production facilities on Kalidasa, they resurrected the Orion as a successor to the Orion IIC, a fitting tribute to Kerensky’s legacy from the Clan that claims guardianship of it. Built on the ON2-M’s endo steel frame, the Orion C hides beneath thick ferro-lamellor armor and mounts Streak LRM-15s, ER pulse lasers, a Gauss rifle, and CASE II protection, cutting-edge Clan technology throughout. While some Wolf warriors question using non-Clan structural components, the decision to leverage existing manufacturing infrastructure reduced the strain on the Wolves’ industrial resources.

Often called “a poor man’s Atlas,” the Orion earned lasting fame as the chosen mount of General Aleksandr Kerensky during his campaign to liberate Terra from Stefan Amaris, an image that made the Orion one of the most recognized BattleMechs in known space. Production shifted to Kali Yama Weapons Industries in the Free Worlds League after the fall of the Star League, and the Orion’s roomy, easily maintained chassis has proven remarkably adaptable to successive generations of weapons technology, ensuring its continued relevance across every major conflict of the last five centuries.
BMOrion_ON1MA.capabilities:
The Orion’s design philosophy emphasizes versatility through a balanced mix of ballistic, missile, and energy weapons systems, an approach that has kept the chassis competitive even as battlefield technology has evolved dramatically. The standard ON1-K mounts a KaliYama Class 10 Autocannon as its primary weapon, supplemented by a KaliYama Death Bloom LRM-15 launcher for ranged fire support, two Irian Weapons Works medium lasers, and an SRM-4 rack to exploit armor breaches at close range. Over fourteen tons of Valiant Lamellor armor provides protection sufficient for sustained frontline combat, while a Vlar 300 fusion engine delivers a respectable maximum speed of sixty-four kilometers per hour.

The chassis’s greatest strength lies in its adaptability. The roomy internal layout has readily accommodated every major technological advancement since the Star League era, from XL engines and double heat sinks to extended-range weaponry and advanced fire control systems. This flexibility has produced an extraordinary number of variants, from simple field refits that swap missile launchers to ground-up redesigns mounting Gauss rifles and experimental weapons. Any MechWarrior who can pilot one Orion can quickly adapt to virtually any variant, a logistical advantage that few other designs can match.
BMOrion_ON1MA.history:
The Orion’s origins trace to the earliest days of the BattleMech arms race. After the Lyran Commonwealth obtained BattleMech technology through Operation PROMETHEUS, the Terran Hegemony commissioned General Mechanics of Mars to develop a new heavy attack ’Mech. The first ON1-C prototype debuted in 2453 but was rejected by the Hegemony Armed Forces for insufficient firepower. General Mechanics returned to the drawing board, settling on a smaller engine to free mass for additional weapons. The third prototype (the ON1-H, incorporating the newly developed class-10 autocannon) finally won HAF approval in 2456.

The Orion served the Hegemony with distinction, but its defining moment came centuries later during the Amaris Civil War. General Aleksandr Kerensky chose an Orion as his personal BattleMech, piloting it through the liberation of Terra and the capture of Stefan Amaris. That olive-drab Orion became one of the most recognized machines in military history. When Kerensky departed on the Exodus, he abandoned the venerable ’Mech, which was eventually recovered by Combine salvage teams in the New Samarkand system and given to the young Theodore Kurita. Named “Revenant,” the machine served Theodore through the Fourth Succession War before reportedly being destroyed on Marfik.

Production shifted from the original Hesperus II and Mars facilities to Kali Yama Weapons Industries on Kalidasa and the Kali Yama/Alphard Trading Corporation joint venture on Kendall following the fall of the Star League. The Free Worlds League became the largest producer, fueling complaints that the Marik Militia received more than their fair share of new Orions. The Outreach Accords during the Clan Invasion opened League military exports to the other Great Houses, sparking a golden age for Kali Yama and the Alphard Trading Corporation.

The recovery of Star League technology in the late 3040s produced the ON1-M upgrade, trading the temperamental autocannon for a versatile LB 10-X and adding an XL engine. The plethora of field variants that followed (Artemis IV refits, MRM conversions, rotary autocannon upgrades, and light Gauss substitutions) testified to the chassis’s enduring adaptability. The ON2-M represented the first ground-up redesign, employing an endo steel frame, Gauss rifle, and Artemis-equipped LRM-15 to create what many consider the definitive modern Orion. Kali Yama’s ON3-M “Orion 3100” pushed the design further with Extended LRM technology, though declining military budgets limited initial sales.

When Clan Wolf captured Kalidasa, they converted the Kali Yama production lines to build the Orion C, a fitting tribute to Kerensky’s legacy that combined the proven Inner Sphere chassis with cutting-edge Clan weaponry.
BMOrion_ON1MA.deployment: A common Artemis IV field refit of the ON1-M that appeared around 3052, this variant replaces the Narc Missile Beacon with Artemis IV fire control on the LRM-20, improving accuracy without requiring external targeting support. The SRM-4 is upgraded to an SRM-6, and medium pulse lasers replace the standard models for improved hit probability at short range. The LB 10-X autocannon and CASE protection are retained.

The Narc beacon system is retained for cooperative play, and the light Gauss rifle’s reduced bulk compared to a standard Gauss allows the variant to maintain generous ammunition supplies for extended engagements.

The MRM launchers’ lack of guidance systems is partially offset by the C3 network’s shared targeting data.

BMOrion_ON1VA.history:
The Orion’s origins trace to the earliest days of the BattleMech arms race. After the Lyran Commonwealth obtained BattleMech technology through Operation PROMETHEUS, the Terran Hegemony commissioned General Mechanics of Mars to develop a new heavy attack ’Mech. General Mechanics returned to the drawing board, settling on a smaller engine to free mass for additional weapons. The third prototype (the ON1-H, incorporating the newly developed class-10 autocannon) finally won HAF approval in 2456.

General Aleksandr Kerensky chose an Orion as his personal BattleMech, piloting it through the liberation of Terra and the capture of Stefan Amaris. That olive-drab Orion became one of the most recognized machines in military history. The Outreach Accords during the Clan Invasion opened League military exports to the other Great Houses, sparking a golden age for Kali Yama and the Alphard Trading Corporation.

The plethora of field variants that followed (Artemis IV refits, MRM conversions, rotary autocannon upgrades, and light Gauss substitutions) testified to the chassis’s enduring adaptability. The ON2-M represented the first ground-up redesign, employing an endo steel frame, Gauss rifle, and Artemis-equipped LRM-15 to create what many consider the definitive modern Orion. Kali Yama’s ON3-M “Orion 3100” pushed the design further with Extended LRM technology, though declining military budgets limited initial sales.

The resulting design is a devastating infighter that excels in urban or jungle combat where long-range missiles have limited effectiveness.

BMOrochi_OR2I.overview:
The Orochi is a ninety-ton assault BattleMech introduced in 3084 by Victory Industries on Marduk. Conceived as a modern successor to the venerable Longbow, the design emerged from the Draconis Combine Mustered Soldiery's post-Jihad recovery efforts as both a practical military need and a symbolic statement of the Combine's industrial resilience.

Though never produced in large numbers, the Orochi earned a reputation as a potent fire support platform capable of delivering concentrated strikes at range. Its presence in frontline formations signaled the Combine's continued investment in advanced assault-class designs despite the losses suffered during the Jihad and the formation of the Republic of the Sphere.
BMOrochi_OR2I.capabilities:
The Orochi builds upon the Longbow's fire support legacy while embracing a fundamentally different approach to indirect warfare. Where its predecessor relied on massed LRM volleys for area saturation, the Orochi mounts a pair of Telos ThunderShot Thunderbolt 20 launchers, each fed by three tons of ammunition. These weapons trade the Longbow's broad suppressive capability for concentrated, armor-penetrating strikes capable of threatening even the heaviest targets at range. The Thunderbolt missiles prove far more compact than equivalent Arrow IV artillery systems while delivering comparable focused damage.

Complementing the main armament, two Telos TargetLok-4 Streak SRM-4 launchers provide efficient close-range defense, ensuring no ammunition is wasted on missed shots. A single Victory 12E extended range small laser rounds out the weapon suite as a last-resort backup. The ninety-ton frame rides on a Hermes 360 XL engine, achieving a respectable sixty-four kilometers per hour for an assault 'Mech, though the extralight powerplant creates a significant vulnerability to side torso damage. Seventeen and a half tons of Starshield A armor provide substantial protection, while Longbow-derived shoulder actuators enable the iconic arm-flipping capability that maximizes the Orochi's firing arcs.
BMOrochi_OR2I.history:
The Orochi's development is inseparable from the Draconis Combine's broader post-Jihad industrial recovery. The Word of Blake's devastating campaign had shattered much of the Combine's military-industrial base, and the subsequent formation of the Republic of the Sphere stripped away several of its most productive worlds. Quentin alone cost the DCMS several modern and highly prized designs. The high command, anticipating these territorial losses even before the Republic's formal establishment, began shifting production capacity to surviving facilities across the realm.

Marduk's Victory Industries plant (formerly Norse BattleMech Works) had served the Combine for centuries, assembling Griffin and Wolverine variants along with components shipped across DCMS space. The factory received massive investment to expand its capabilities, with vast sums of money and labor directed toward necessary improvements. The Orochi was among the first new designs to emerge from the revitalized facility, a sign of the engineering talent Victory assembled on Marduk.

Initial fielding saw the Orochi distributed primarily to elite formations. The Sword of Light regiments received priority allocation as the design entered service, followed by other loyal formations such as the Dieron Regulars and Arkab legions. The design's high maintenance requirements and the specialized nature of its Thunderbolt launchers meant that overall production numbers remained modest, limiting the number of Orochi encountered in the field throughout the early Republic period.

The Combine's aggressive expansion into Federated Suns territory during the 3140s brought renewed strategic importance to the Orochi program. Victory Industries responded with the OR-3K variant, tailored for the evolving battlefield conditions of the Dark Age. As the ilClan era dawned and the political arena of the Inner Sphere continued to shift, the Orochi remained a visible symbol of Combine industrial capability, its presence in frontline units signaling both military investment and enduring technological ambition.
BMOrochi_OR2I.deployment: As the original production model introduced in 3084, this variant established the Orochi's role within the DCMS order of battle. Initial deployment prioritized the Sword of Light regiments and other elite formations, with limited production ensuring the design remained a prestige assignment throughout the early Republic era. Maintenance demands associated with the primary missile systems further constrained the number of units fielded, though those formations equipped with this variant consistently demonstrated the platform's value in dedicated fire support operations.

BMOsiris_OSR3D.overview:
The Osiris is a thirty-ton light BattleMech introduced in 3063 by Achernar BattleMechs, produced at their facility on New Avalon. Designed as a fast scout and harasser for the Armed Forces of the Federated Suns, the Osiris represented a major leap forward for Achernar, which had long relied on older designs like the Enforcer and Dervish. The design was developed in partnership with Fredonian Industrial Technologies, whose engineers drew explicit inspiration from the Clan Dragonfly OmniMech to produce an Inner Sphere machine capable of competing with Clan-era performance standards.

The Osiris earned a strong reputation as a capable light striker, with its combination of speed, energy firepower, and jump capability making it a valued asset in fast-moving engagements. Production continued through the Jihad and beyond, with manufacturing relocated to Cahokia after the New Avalon facility suffered devastating damage, ensuring the design remains a mainstay of Federated Suns light 'Mech formations into the ilClan era.
BMOsiris_OSR3D.capabilities:
The Osiris was explicitly modeled after the Clan Dragonfly OmniMech, and while Inner Sphere technological limitations forced certain compromises, the design maintains an identical top speed of 129 kilometers per hour through its Pharaoh 240 XL engine. Five Bright-Bloom extended-range medium lasers form the primary armament, providing devastating close-to-medium range firepower ideally suited to a fast raider operating far from supply lines. A Harpoon-6 SRM-6 launcher delivers supplementary short-range punch, while a single Double-Gun machine gun handles unarmored infantry threats. The designers prioritized offensive capability over the Dragonfly's superior jump performance, equipping the Osiris with only four Rawlings 61 jump jets for a 120-meter jump capacity, half that of its Clan-inspired predecessor.

Where the design suffers most is in protection. Just four and a half tons of StarGuard ferro-fibrous armor leaves the Osiris dangerously reliant on its speed and pilot skill to survive engagements. Heat management also demands careful attention, as the five extended-range lasers can quickly overwhelm the 'Mech's cooling capacity if fired aggressively. The Osiris excels in the hit-and-fade role it was designed for, but MechWarriors who allow themselves to be pinned down quickly discover its limitations.
BMOsiris_OSR3D.history:
The Osiris's development was intimately tied to the transformation of Achernar BattleMechs under CEO Paul LeBeau, who took the helm in 3058 with a promise to triple the company's profits within a decade. Achernar had long stagnated, relying almost entirely on its Enforcer and Dervish lines while competitors pushed ahead with new designs incorporating recovered and advanced technology. Even the updated Enforcer III failed to reverse the company's declining market relevance, and the AFFS Department of the Quartermaster ultimately forced Achernar into a humbling licensing arrangement with Kallon Industries on Talon.

LeBeau's decision to contract with Fredonian Industrial Technologies proved transformative. The F.I.T. engineers (already recognized for their work designing Inner Sphere 'Mechs capable of matching Clan designs) produced the Osiris as a direct response to the AFFS's need for light scouts and harassers. Drawing explicit inspiration from the Clan Dragonfly, the design entered production on New Avalon in early 3063, just as the simmering tensions of the FedCom Civil War were about to erupt into open conflict.

The timing proved both fortuitous and tragic. The Osiris saw extensive deployment throughout the Civil War, with production units rushed to the front lines during the fighting on New Avalon itself. The 'Mech's speed and firepower made it a valued asset in the fast-moving engagements that characterized the conflict, though its thin armor resulted in significant attrition among less experienced pilots.

The Jihad devastated Achernar's New Avalon facilities, with ninety-five percent of production lines either moved or damaged. Marshal of the Armies Jackson Davion ordered surface production shut down and planted false intelligence suggesting the main underground facility had been destroyed by orbital bombardment. This deception kept the Word of Blake from targeting Achernar directly, but the light 'Mech production wing still suffered catastrophic damage. After the Word of Blake was ejected from New Avalon, restoration of light 'Mech production became a top priority for AFFS High Command. A sizable government grant allowed Achernar to relocate the Osiris production line to a new facility on Cahokia, where production was restored by 3081.

The Cahokia plant has continued to produce the Osiris and its variants into the ilClan era, ensuring the design remains a mainstay of Federated Suns light 'Mech formations. The New Avalon facility, meanwhile, restored only four of its eight production lines after the Jihad, focusing on heavier designs and leaving Cahokia as the primary source for new Osiris production.
BMOsiris_OSR3D.deployment: The base production model entered service in February 3063 and quickly spread throughout the Armed Forces of the Federated Suns and the Lyran Alliance. The majority of those manufactured in the first four years of production remained within the Crucis March. During the grand assault on New Avalon, Osiris 'Mechs were assigned to combat units on the front lines as quickly as they could be produced, often before final assembly checks had been completed, evidence of the desperate need for capable light 'Mechs during the FedCom Civil War.

This reconfiguration transforms the Osiris from a hit-and-fade striker into a more mobile skirmisher, better able to exploit rough terrain and maintain distance from pursuing forces. The enhanced jump capability proved particularly valuable during the chaotic close-quarters engagements that characterized the latter stages of the Civil War.

BMOsiris_OSR5D.overview:
The Osiris is a thirty-ton light BattleMech introduced in 3063 by Achernar BattleMechs, produced at their facility on New Avalon. Designed as a fast scout and harasser for the Armed Forces of the Federated Suns, the Osiris represented a major leap forward for Achernar, which had long relied on older designs like the Enforcer and Dervish. The design was developed in partnership with Fredonian Industrial Technologies, whose engineers drew explicit inspiration from the Clan Dragonfly OmniMech to produce an Inner Sphere machine capable of competing with Clan-era performance standards.

The Osiris earned a strong reputation as a capable light striker, with its combination of speed, energy firepower, and jump capability making it a valued asset in fast-moving engagements. Production continued through the Jihad and beyond, with manufacturing relocated to Cahokia after the New Avalon facility suffered devastating damage, ensuring the design remains a mainstay of Federated Suns light 'Mech formations into the ilClan era.
BMOsiris_OSR5D.capabilities:
The Osiris was explicitly modeled after the Clan Dragonfly OmniMech, and while Inner Sphere technological limitations forced certain compromises, the design maintains an identical top speed of 129 kilometers per hour through its Pharaoh 240 XL engine. Five Bright-Bloom extended-range medium lasers form the primary armament, providing devastating close-to-medium range firepower ideally suited to a fast raider operating far from supply lines. A Harpoon-6 SRM-6 launcher delivers supplementary short-range punch, while a single Double-Gun machine gun handles unarmored infantry threats. The designers prioritized offensive capability over the Dragonfly's superior jump performance, equipping the Osiris with only four Rawlings 61 jump jets for a 120-meter jump capacity, half that of its Clan-inspired predecessor.

Where the design suffers most is in protection. Just four and a half tons of StarGuard ferro-fibrous armor leaves the Osiris dangerously reliant on its speed and pilot skill to survive engagements. Heat management also demands careful attention, as the five extended-range lasers can quickly overwhelm the 'Mech's cooling capacity if fired aggressively. The Osiris excels in the hit-and-fade role it was designed for, but MechWarriors who allow themselves to be pinned down quickly discover its limitations.
BMOsiris_OSR5D.history:
The Osiris's development was intimately tied to the transformation of Achernar BattleMechs under CEO Paul LeBeau, who took the helm in 3058 with a promise to triple the company's profits within a decade. Achernar had long stagnated, relying almost entirely on its Enforcer and Dervish lines while competitors pushed ahead with new designs incorporating recovered and advanced technology. Even the updated Enforcer III failed to reverse the company's declining market relevance, and the AFFS Department of the Quartermaster ultimately forced Achernar into a humbling licensing arrangement with Kallon Industries on Talon.

LeBeau's decision to contract with Fredonian Industrial Technologies proved transformative. The F.I.T. engineers (already recognized for their work designing Inner Sphere 'Mechs capable of matching Clan designs) produced the Osiris as a direct response to the AFFS's need for light scouts and harassers. Drawing explicit inspiration from the Clan Dragonfly, the design entered production on New Avalon in early 3063, just as the simmering tensions of the FedCom Civil War were about to erupt into open conflict.

The timing proved both fortuitous and tragic. The Osiris saw extensive deployment throughout the Civil War, with production units rushed to the front lines during the fighting on New Avalon itself. The 'Mech's speed and firepower made it a valued asset in the fast-moving engagements that characterized the conflict, though its thin armor resulted in significant attrition among less experienced pilots.

The Jihad devastated Achernar's New Avalon facilities, with ninety-five percent of production lines either moved or damaged. Marshal of the Armies Jackson Davion ordered surface production shut down and planted false intelligence suggesting the main underground facility had been destroyed by orbital bombardment. This deception kept the Word of Blake from targeting Achernar directly, but the light 'Mech production wing still suffered catastrophic damage. After the Word of Blake was ejected from New Avalon, restoration of light 'Mech production became a top priority for AFFS High Command. A sizable government grant allowed Achernar to relocate the Osiris production line to a new facility on Cahokia, where production was restored by 3081.

The Cahokia plant has continued to produce the Osiris and its variants into the ilClan era, ensuring the design remains a mainstay of Federated Suns light 'Mech formations. The New Avalon facility, meanwhile, restored only four of its eight production lines after the Jihad, focusing on heavier designs and leaving Cahokia as the primary source for new Osiris production.
BMOsiris_OSR5D.deployment: Developed in 3081 as part of the post-Jihad reconstruction effort at Achernar's new Cahokia facility, this variant serves as a radical departure from the original Osiris concept. All of the standard armament is replaced by a single heavy PPC, transforming the design into a light fire-support platform. An XL gyro and a smaller 210-rated XL engine reduce the top speed to approximately 110 kilometers per hour, while seven jump jets provide 210 meters of jump capability. The armor package shifts to light ferro-fibrous for improved protection within the reduced mass budget. The result trades the original's harasser role for a longer-ranged striking capability, allowing the Osiris to contribute meaningful firepower at distances where its thin armor is less of a liability.

BMOsprey_OSP15.overview:
The Osprey is a fifty-five-ton medium BattleMech originally designed in 2738 by Hollis Incorporated to fulfill a Star League Defense Force contract for a mobile, medium-weight fire support unit. When the primary contract was awarded to Blue Shot Weapons for their competing Lynx design, the Osprey was relegated to a limited production run for SLDF Royal units, serving in a specialized urban defense role. Fewer than a thousand were manufactured before the fall of the Star League, and the design was rendered virtually extinct during the Succession Wars.

The Osprey's fortunes changed dramatically during the Jihad when the Word of Blake commissioned Skobel MechWorks on Terra to revive the design for its Protectorate Militia forces. Massive production runs at Skobel and later at Achernar BattleMechs transformed the once-rare chassis into a frontline mainstay. Following the Jihad, both the Republic of the Sphere and the Capellan Confederation prioritized restarting Osprey production, ensuring the design's continued service well into the Dark Age and beyond.
BMOsprey_OSP15.capabilities:
Built around a dorsally mounted M-7 Gauss rifle, the Osprey delivers devastating long-range firepower unusual for a fifty-five-ton chassis. A Holly MML-7 rack supplements the Gauss rifle, providing flexible fire support with the ability to switch between long-range and short-range missile configurations depending on tactical needs. Two Diverse Optics ER medium lasers and an ER small laser round out the armament for close-quarters engagements. The design cleverly houses the small laser and a Beagle active probe in mountings identical to the medium laser assemblies, giving the visual impression of four arm-mounted lasers, a useful deception in urban combat scenarios.

To support this considerable weapons loadout on a medium chassis, the Osprey utilizes a Hollis Mk II Endo Steel frame and a DAV 220 XL extralight engine. While the extralight engine enables the necessary weight savings, it leaves the 'Mech vulnerable to catastrophic shutdown from torso breaches. Eleven tons of Durallex Heavy armor provides respectable protection, and CASE-protected ammunition bays in the torso mitigate the risk of internal explosions. Four Anderson Propulsion 25 jump jets compensate for the Osprey's modest ground speed of sixty-four kilometers per hour, granting the maneuverability essential for navigating the urban environments the design was built to fight in.
BMOsprey_OSP15.history:
During the Star League era, the Osprey was deployed in limited numbers, assigned to urban specialist units and Special Forces within the SLDF's Royal divisions. Designed by Hollis Incorporated on Corey, the 'Mech filled a niche role that the larger and more expensive Lynx could not, a mobile fire support platform optimized for the close confines of urban warfare. Fewer than a thousand were manufactured before the Star League's collapse, and the design saw limited but distinguished service in the defense of key urban centers across the Hegemony.

The Succession Wars proved devastating for the Osprey's survival. The few examples that escaped the Exodus were gradually lost to attrition over centuries of constant warfare, and without an active production line the design faded into obscurity. Only two examples were documented in the modern era, one discovered by a Federated Commonwealth mercenary unit in the 3020s, and a museum piece that would later serve as the prototype for the design's dramatic revival.

That revival began in the early 3070s when the Word of Blake, desperate for durable, high-firepower machines to equip its expanding Protectorate Militia, commissioned Skobel MechWorks on Terra to replicate the Osprey using ancient plans and the recovered museum specimen. The initial production run of OSP-25 models was quickly followed by the more comprehensive OSP-26 redesign, and both variants rolled off Skobel's assembly lines in significant numbers. The Word simultaneously established a second production line at the Achernar BattleMechs facility on Achernar, where old IndustrialMech lines were upgraded to produce the design.

The Osprey saw extensive combat during the closing stages of the Jihad. Images of a company of white Ospreys firing en masse to destroy a Wolf-in-Exile Daishi became a lasting symbol of the brutal battle to capture the Achernar complex. The Achernar facility itself was completely destroyed in 3077 when the Achernar Protectorate Militia refused to surrender to Stone's Coalition forces, fortifying the plant and forcing the allied task force to level the factory in order to root out the defenders. Though the factory was lost, the Coalition recovered several lances of intact Ospreys from the wreckage.

The nascent Republic of the Sphere was deeply impressed by the Osprey's durability and effectiveness in urban environments, and Victor Steiner-Davion personally designated the surviving Skobel production line on Terra as a priority for restoration. In the intervening years, a small but steady stream of Ospreys has continued to march off the line and into Republic Armed Forces frontline units. Seeing the renewed success of the design, Hollis Incorporated (the original manufacturer) retooled one of its Catapult production lines on Corey to produce the OSP-15E, a variant functionally identical to the OSP-25 that was quickly accepted by the Confederation Strategios. Capellan doctrine frequently pairs Ospreys with Catapults to form effective fire support teams.

The advantage of the OSP-26's MML system over the older LRM configuration was proven in a brief clash on Shipka, where two Ospreys from the Eighth Hastati Sentinels encountered a mixed Capellan Osprey/Catapult lance in broken terrain. Using the added short-range firepower of their MMLs, the two Hastati Ospreys destroyed both Capellan Catapults and one of the Capellan Ospreys in a running battle through the hills and gullies. By the Dark Age, the Osprey had firmly established itself as a valued fire support platform for both the Republic Armed Forces and the Capellan Confederation, a remarkable second life for a design that had been virtually extinct for centuries.
BMOsprey_OSP15.deployment: The original Star League-era model introduced in 2738, this variant mounted the same M-7 Gauss rifle found on all later models but paired it with an LRM-10 launcher and three standard Martell medium lasers. Lacking the Beagle active probe and advanced electronics of its successors, the design was straightforward but effective in its intended urban defense role. Assigned primarily to SLDF Royal units and Special Forces, fewer than a thousand were manufactured before the Star League's collapse, and the Succession Wars reduced the surviving population to a mere handful of machines.

This became the standard production model, manufactured at three facilities across the Inner Sphere and serving extensively with Word of Blake, Republic Armed Forces, and Capellan Confederation units.

BMOsprey_OSP26Lawrence.deployment: A customized field modification created in 3085 for a MechWarrior serving with the mercenary unit Lamenkov's Liability, this variant strips most of the standard armament in favor of a heavy PPC for long-range striking power, supplemented by two medium pulse lasers for improved accuracy at closer ranges. The MML-7 launcher and Beagle active probe were retained, but a C3 slave unit was added to enhance coordination with lancemates. Five improved jump jets replace the standard models, granting superior cross-country mobility, while a compact gyro frees internal space for the upgraded equipment.

BMOstroc_OSR2C.overview:
The Ostroc was designed in 2511 by Ostmann Industries as a dedicated urban combat platform for the Terran Hegemony's garrison forces. Distinguished by its low-slung walker-pod profile that would later inspire designs like the Stalker and Marauder, the Ostroc combined a silhouette comparable to the diminutive UrbanMech with the firepower expected of a heavy 'Mech. This unique combination made the design exceptionally difficult to target among the towers and debris of contested cityscapes.

Ostmann Industries' limited production capacity meant the Ostroc remained relatively rare throughout its service life, though the design's reputation for reliability and its interchangeable components with other Ost-series 'Mechs ensured its continued use across the Succession Wars and beyond. Multiple manufacturers eventually took up production, keeping the Ostroc relevant on battlefields well into the thirty-second century.
BMOstroc_OSR2C.capabilities:
The Ostroc's primary armament centers on twin Fuersturm-C large lasers mounted in the side torsos, providing effective medium-to-long range firepower without ammunition dependency. Secondary weapons include paired Fuersturm-b medium lasers and a single Totschlagen SRM-4 launcher, giving the design respectable close-range punch. This weapons mix allows the Ostroc to operate effectively as a guerrilla fighter, largely independent of supply lines that might be disrupted in urban combat zones.

The nineteen-ton Vlar 300 fusion engine propels the Ostroc to speeds of 86 kilometers per hour, making it fast for its weight class and capable of dictating engagement ranges against heavier opponents. Fifteen standard heat sinks provide adequate thermal management for sustained combat. Nine tons of Riese-475 armor offer reasonable protection, though the design's distinctive short arms receive minimal plating and are frequently lost in combat.

BMOstscout_OTT10CS.overview:
The Ostscout was designed for one purpose: scouting. Introduced in 2600 by Ostmann Industries, this 35-ton light 'Mech was built entirely around gathering intelligence and escaping danger. Its exceptional speed and maneuverability allow it to avoid trouble easily, though its minimal armament means it can only engage the lightest opponents with any hope of success. Enhanced sensor arrays and a high-resolution targeting and tracking system supply the Ostscout with a constant stream of data about its surroundings, while powerful narrow-band communications equipment allows it to report from deep inside enemy territory.

As demand for the design grew beyond Ostmann's production capacity, the company licensed Kong Interstellar Corporation to begin manufacturing in 2700, following a similar arrangement previously established for the Ostsol. The Ostscout became so valuable during the Succession Wars that commanders hoarded them like treasures, deploying them only for the most critical reconnaissance missions.
BMOstscout_OTT10CS.capabilities:
The Ostscout's primary feature is pure speed. Its VOX 280 fusion engine, typically mounted on designs twice its size, propels the 'Mech to a maximum speed of 129.6 kilometers per hour. Combined with a 240-meter jump capability provided by eight Ostmann Sct-A jump jets, only the Spider can match its maneuverability. This agility serves as the 'Mech's true protection, as the four-and-a-half tons of Durallex Light armor offers only modest defense against concentrated fire.

The Ostscout's combat capability is severely limited by design. A single Tronel II medium laser represents its entire offensive armament, mounted only after test pilots aggressively protested the original weaponless configuration. Ten heat sinks easily manage this minimal heat load, allowing the 'Mech to jump and fire simultaneously without overheating.

The true centerpiece of the design is its advanced sensor suite. The arm-mounted sensor arrays were installed outside the main chassis to avoid magnetohydrodynamic interference, with the 'Mech using its actuator systems to aim them. During maximum-intensity scanning, the Ostscout must move slowly while waving its arrays in seemingly random patterns, making it briefly vulnerable. However, if the first enemy salvo fails to cripple it, the 'Mech will almost certainly escape.
BMOstscout_OTT10CS.history:
Ostmann Industries built and sold the Ostscout starting in 2600 to fulfill many armies' need for a swift reconnaissance 'Mech. When demand outstripped their production capacity, rather than sacrifice their popular Ostroc line, Ostmann licensed Kong Interstellar to begin production in 2700. Kong continued building Ostscouts for a century until the destruction of their factory on Connaught in 2802 at the outset of the Succession Wars. Deprived of replacements, commanders began hoarding their Ostscouts, parceling them out only for special missions, and most pilots would not even attempt to engage enemy 'Mechs given the irreplaceable nature of the advanced sensor systems.

The Ostscout's battle history reads as a series of daring missions deep behind enemy lines. During the Rebellion of 3010, Janos Marik used Ostscouts extensively to gather information on rebel movements and strengths. In early September 3021, four Ostscouts were dropped over New Ivaarsen by Draconis Combine DropShips to scout landing sites for a Kurita invasion force, spending five weeks evading Davion patrols while accumulating critical intelligence. The most famous exploit came in 3024 during the "Thousand Kilometer Chase," when a Capellan Ostscout pilot evaded Smithson's Chinese Bandits for ten hours, accumulating enough intelligence to enable a successful Confederation counter-attack.

ComStar also utilized the Ostscout, and following the Clan Invasion and ComStar Schism, developed a new variant maintaining the original's capabilities while improving offensive and defensive profiles. Debuting successfully in 3064, nearly half of all Com Guard Ostscouts were upgraded within three years. However, it was soon discovered that both the Lyran Alliance and Word of Blake were fielding identical variants. The intelligence leak was traced to Dag Kesselring, former Precentor of the Sixty-sixth Division, who had passed information to both the Lyrans and Blakists.

Following the Jihad, the newborn Republic of the Sphere maintained production of upgraded Ostscout models from former Word of Blake factories on Terra, selling them to the Federated Suns and Lyran Commonwealth. During the Dark Age era, Kong Interstellar reestablished production and formed an alliance with Clan Sea Fox to produce variants incorporating stealth technology and Clan weaponry, while Robinson Standard BattleWorks began manufacturing models highly prized by the Draconis Combine.
BMOstscout_OTT10CS.deployment: The basis for the later 11J model, the 10CS was produced by Krupp Armament Works and Odin Manufacturing for ComStar and the Rasalhague Republic. Similar to the 11J but incrementally slower, it carries ER medium lasers in place of light PPCs and mounts a C3i computer instead of TAG. ComStar engineers designed this variant as a spotter for a Level II formation rather than an artillery battery, a role the Ostscout performed adequately for the Com Guards. Production continued in the Rasalhague Republic following its absorption by Clan Ghost Bear, with rumors suggesting the KungsArmé still receives new units.
