The variant saw allocation alongside the 200-B to the Word of Blake's most elite formations.

BMRaijin_RJN101A.overview:
The Raijin was designed as an all-purpose BattleMech to rearm Com Guard units following the Battle of Tukayyid in 3052. Precentor Martial Anastasius Focht wanted a design unfamiliar to both the Inner Sphere and the Clans, and Krupp Armament Works on Terra delivered. Entering production only six months after Tukayyid, the fifty-ton Raijin spread rapidly through the Com Guards, establishing itself as one of the most versatile medium 'Mechs in ComStar's arsenal.

The design's history proved turbulent, passing through the hands of ComStar, the Word of Blake, and ultimately the Draconis Combine as political upheavals repeatedly reshaped its production and deployment. Despite this complicated pedigree, the Raijin platform proved remarkably adaptable, spawning an entire family of medium 'Mechs that served multiple factions across radically different eras of warfare.
BMRaijin_RJN101A.capabilities:
The Raijin is built around a Vlar 300 XL engine, providing a top speed of 97.2 kilometers per hour for a fifty-ton chassis, placing it firmly among the fastest medium 'Mechs of its generation. Six Rawlings 60 jump jets grant an additional 180 meters of jump capability, giving the Raijin excellent tactical flexibility across varied terrain. Seven tons of Krupp 200 ferro-fibrous armor provide reasonable protection, though this can prove a liability in protracted engagements or close-quarters brawling where heavier opponents can exploit the relatively thin plating.

The primary armament centers on a Blankenburg 200 ER PPC for long-range engagement, supported by three Blankenburg Technologies medium pulse lasers for accurate close-range firepower. A Holly SRM-6 and Holly Streak SRM-2 round out the missile array, providing additional punch at shorter ranges while the Streak system conserves ammunition through its lock-on requirement. Ten double heat sinks manage the substantial thermal load, though sustained firing of the entire weapons suite generates considerable excess heat.

The original design especially featured a concealed one-shot SRM-6 bay intended to surprise opponents, though this was replaced with a standard rack for sustained combat utility in the production model. Early production runs also suffered from a jamming issue with the Streak launcher's loading mechanism, resolved through field modifications incorporated into later production.
BMRaijin_RJN101A.history:
The Raijin's origins lie in the aftermath of the Battle of Tukayyid in 3052, when ComStar's Com Guards suffered heavy casualties despite their strategic victory. Krupp Armament Works on Terra, operating from a facility rebuilt by Jerome Blake and mothballed for just such an emergency, produced the first Raijin in record time. The 'Mech initially equipped the Eighth Army's Eighty-Fifth and 167th Divisions, followed by the Eleventh Army stationed along the Federated Commonwealth-Clan Jade Falcon border.

The Word of Blake's seizure of Terra during Operation ODYSSEUS in 3058 transferred Krupp's production facilities to Blakist control. Blakist engineers acknowledged the Raijin's shortcomings and initiated the RJN-200 Raijin II upgrade program. ComStar, having lost its primary factory, turned to Independence Weaponry on Quentin in the Draconis Combine for continued production, receiving new variants designed to fill the gap left by Terra's loss.

Both production lines were eventually shuttered following the Blakist defeat in the Jihad and the disbanding of the Com Guards. The Raijin appeared destined for extinction until the 3120s, when Malcolm Buhl's Blessed Order secretly commissioned Independence Weaponry to manufacture new units for the reconstituted First Division. After the Draconis Combine seized Quentin from the Republic of the Sphere, the design's complicated pedigree was embraced rather than rejected, with Independence modifying and continuing production under Combine authority.

The Raijin's legacy thus spans ComStar, the Word of Blake, and ultimately the Draconis Combine, a journey that saw the design evolve from a post-Tukayyid stopgap into the foundation for an entire family of medium 'Mechs adapted to serve multiple factions across radically different eras of warfare.
BMRaijin_RJN101A.deployment: The original production model combines a Blankenburg ER PPC for long-range engagement with three medium pulse lasers, an SRM-6, and a Streak SRM-2 for close-range work. Designed for versatility rather than specialization, this variant reflected ComStar's need for a general-purpose combatant capable of filling multiple tactical roles within the Com Guards' reorganized divisions following the Battle of Tukayyid. Initially distributed to the Eighth and Eleventh Armies, the variant spread rapidly through the Com Guards before the loss of Terra disrupted production.

BMRakshasa_MDG1A.overview:
The Rakshasa is a seventy-five-ton heavy BattleMech introduced in 3055 by General Motors for the Federated Commonwealth. Named for the mythical creature that mimics the appearance and skills of its adversaries, the Rakshasa was engineered as one of the most ambitious Inner Sphere efforts to replicate the fearsome Clan Timber Wolf OmniMech, providing heavy formations with a platform that could match the general speed and weapons profile of its Clan counterpart.

While Inner Sphere technology of the era could not fully match Clan capabilities, the Rakshasa emerged as a capable heavy combatant in its own right. Its relatively straightforward construction and use of widely available components earned it a reputation for easy maintenance, though the design has struggled to escape an undeserved reputation for mediocrity that belies its actual combat record.
BMRakshasa_MDG1A.capabilities:
The Rakshasa achieves its mission profile through a combination of speed, firepower, and advanced construction techniques. A GM 375 XL engine propels the seventy-five-ton 'Mech to speeds of eighty-six kilometers per hour, matching the ground speed of the Timber Wolf it was designed to emulate. The use of endo steel internal structure and StarGuard ferro-fibrous armor maximizes available tonnage for weapons and equipment, providing near-maximum armor protection for its weight class.

The weapons array mirrors the Timber Wolf's general philosophy of combining long-range missile support with direct-fire energy weapons. Twin shoulder-mounted Federated LRM-10 racks, each linked to an Artemis IV fire control system, provide accurate indirect fire capability. A pair of ExoStar extended-range large lasers mounted in the arms deliver punishing damage at range, while two Martell medium lasers and a Martell medium pulse laser round out the close-combat armament.

This weapons mix generates considerable heat, representing the design's primary tactical limitation. The fifteen double heat sinks struggle to manage sustained fire from all weapons simultaneously, forcing MechWarriors to exercise careful fire discipline. The absence of jump jets further limits tactical flexibility, though the 'Mech's high ground speed partially compensates. A known weakness in the head armor has been noted by field commanders, requiring pilots to avoid prolonged exposure to concentrated headshots.
BMRakshasa_MDG1A.history:
The Rakshasa's origins trace to the aftermath of the Clan Invasion, when NAIS engineers spent five years studying salvaged Timber Wolf OmniMechs in an effort to reproduce the design's capabilities using Inner Sphere technology. The project faced significant challenges, as the technological gap between Inner Sphere and Clan manufacturing remained substantial throughout the 3050s. Yet, the team produced a workable design that, while clearly inferior to its Clan progenitor, offered a competitive platform by Inner Sphere standards.

The Rakshasa first saw combat shortly after its introduction in 3055, with initial combat trials proving promising. Early deployments included service with a joint FedCom-Clan Wolf task force formed to combat the Red Corsair in 3055, where Rakshasas assigned to the Kell Hounds performed well on Arc-Royal and Elyssa. Despite these successes, the design acquired an unfortunate reputation during Operation Guerrero two years later, when Rakshasas serving with the Eighth FedCom RCT were destroyed in engagements that had more to do with poor tactical circumstances than any inherent design flaw. The resulting criticism from senior officers unfairly tainted the 'Mech's reputation for years.

Production continued at the General Motors facility on Kathil, which became a critical battleground during the FedCom Civil War. The close-combat MDG-2A variant emerged during the height of the fighting for Kathil around 3064-3065, developed by resourceful technicians who adapted the design to meet the demands of the intense urban and close-quarters combat that characterized the struggle for the planet. The Rakshasa found a surprising following among Capellan March MechWarriors who appreciated the 2A's devastating short-range firepower.

Beyond its primary service with the Armed Forces of the Federated Suns, the Rakshasa gained a small but dedicated following on Solaris VII, where its combination of speed and firepower proved well-suited to arena combat. Individual Rakshasas have appeared in the service of the Draconis Combine and other states through battlefield salvage and the gray market, demonstrating the design's appeal beyond its nation of origin. Field refit packages developed during the Jihad era further extended the chassis's service life, ensuring the Rakshasa continues to see deployment across the Inner Sphere.
BMRakshasa_MDG1A.deployment: The base production model introduced in 3055, this variant established the Rakshasa's core design philosophy of emulating the Timber Wolf's weapons profile with Inner Sphere technology. Its combination of missile support and direct-fire energy weapons provides a versatile mix of engagement options at multiple ranges, supplemented by pulse and standard laser armament for close engagements. The 1A served primarily with Federated Commonwealth and later Federated Suns commands throughout the late thirty-first century.

BMRaptorII_RPT2X.overview:
The Raptor II is synonymous with the Void Signature System, a revolutionary stealth technology that renders the 'Mech effectively invisible to both electronic sensors and visual detection. Developed by the Word of Blake using research recovered from ComStar's Terra archives after Operation Odysseus in 3058, the forty-ton design married mimetic armor composites, chameleon-scale light polarization, and emission baffling into a single integrated package powered by an onboard ECM suite. First fielded as early as 3067, the Raptor II served as a premier infiltration and search-and-destroy platform throughout the Jihad.

Following the liberation of Terra, the Republic of the Sphere recovered the design specifications and restarted production at a classified facility, assigning all Raptor IIs exclusively to its most elite special forces units. The extreme secrecy surrounding the design, from classified manufacturers to the deliberate omission of ejection systems, highlights the lengths taken to prevent the Void Signature technology from falling into foreign hands.
BMRaptorII_RPT2X.capabilities:
The Raptor II is built on a Void Integrated endo steel chassis powered by a VOX 280 XL engine, achieving a base speed of 118 kilometers per hour with MASC providing burst speeds up to 151 kilometers per hour in the standard RPT-3X configuration. Seven and a half tons of specially shaped Void Integrated light ferro-fibrous armor bonded with mimetic composites provides moderate protection while maintaining the sensor-deflecting properties essential to the Void Signature System's operation. A Guardian ECM suite is integral to every production model, as it is required for VoidSig to function.

The RPT-3X mounts two Streak SRM-6 launchers and two ER medium lasers, providing efficient and accurate firepower for an infiltrator. The Streak systems ensure no wasted ammunition, while the extended-range lasers allow engagement at distances where the Raptor II's stealth makes return fire extremely difficult. A small cockpit and the deliberate omission of both CASE and an ejection system reflect the Republic's uncompromising approach to operational security: pilots are expected to escape or die, with capture considered unacceptable.

At a standstill, the Raptor II is virtually undetectable, capable of lurking at optimum engagement range before striking with lethal precision and vanishing before effective countermeasures can be mounted. This combination of stealth, speed, and focused firepower makes the Raptor II one of the most feared light-to-medium combatants on the modern battlefield.
BMRaptorII_RPT2X.history:
The origins of the Raptor II trace to the Word of Blake's seizure of Terra from ComStar during Operation Odysseus in 3058. Among the vast technological archives recovered were records of Star League-era stealth systems, including the Null Signature System and Chameleon Light Polarization Shield, technologies that had been largely forgotten or abandoned even by the Clans, who considered such systems dishonorable. The Blakists recognized the potential in these technologies and initiated a decade-long development program that culminated in 3070 with the Void Signature System, a synthesis that combined the fidelity of mimetic armor, the scale of chameleon technology, and the emission baffling of the Null Signature System.

Reports of invisible 'Mechs stalking the battlefields of the Inner Sphere began circulating as early as 3067, though most were dismissed as fantasy or propaganda. The RPT-2X and RPT-2X1 are considered to have been formally introduced by 3073, produced at a classified Blakist facility on Terra. These early models proved devastatingly effective during the Jihad, with Blakist Raptor IIs conducting raids and infiltration operations that left defenders unable to identify, let alone engage, their attackers. Multiple facilities were targeted by Raptor IIs during the conflict, with the surprise and destruction wrought by invisible attackers spreading fear far beyond the immediate tactical impact.

The Coalition's liberation of Terra saw the destruction of the Blakist production facility, but the development laboratory and design specifications survived intact. The Republic of the Sphere, under Devlin Stone's leadership, quickly recognized the strategic significance of VoidSig technology and prioritized the acquisition of all salvaged Raptor IIs. A standing order directed Republic Armed Forces officers to destroy any intact Raptor IIs found in the field rather than risk them falling into foreign hands. By 3084, the Republic had restarted production with the redesigned RPT-3X at a classified facility, with all units assigned exclusively to elite special forces.

Despite the Republic's efforts at containment, evidence emerged during the thirty-second century that some Raptor IIs had slipped beyond their control. Examples appeared among foreign powers and independent mercenary commands, with some reportedly serving as family 'Mechs passed down since the Jihad era. Units with functional Void Signature Systems remain high-priority targets for Republic intelligence services, reflecting the ongoing sensitivity surrounding this technology.
BMRaptorII_RPT2X.deployment: The original Word of Blake variant carries a single BattleMech taser backed by two medium variable speed pulse lasers. Introduced around 3073, this variant exploits the Void Signature and MASC systems to close to effective taser range before the target can react, allowing the pilot to disable enemy 'Mechs without destroying them. One fewer heat sink and half a ton less armor compared to the later RPT-3X reflect the Blakist prioritization of offensive capability over survivability. Unlike later Republic models, this variant retained CASE to protect the pilot.

These early models proved devastatingly effective during the Jihad, with Blakist Raptor IIs conducting raids and infiltration operations that left defenders unable to identify, let alone engage, their attackers. Multiple facilities were targeted by Raptor IIs during the conflict, with the surprise and destruction wrought by invisible attackers spreading fear far beyond the immediate tactical impact.

The Coalition's liberation of Terra saw the destruction of the Blakist production facility, but the development laboratory and design specifications survived intact. The Republic of the Sphere, under Devlin Stone's leadership, quickly recognized the strategic significance of VoidSig technology and prioritized the acquisition of all salvaged Raptor IIs. A standing order directed Republic Armed Forces officers to destroy any intact Raptor IIs found in the field rather than risk them falling into foreign hands. By 3084, the Republic had restarted production with the redesigned RPT-3X at a classified facility, with all units assigned exclusively to elite special forces.

Despite the Republic's efforts at containment, evidence emerged during the thirty-second century that some Raptor IIs had slipped beyond their control. Examples appeared among foreign powers and independent mercenary commands, with some reportedly serving as family 'Mechs passed down since the Jihad era. Units with functional Void Signature Systems remain high-priority targets for Republic intelligence services, reflecting the ongoing sensitivity surrounding this technology.
BMRaptorII_RPT2X2.deployment: A Dark Age-era refit of the original RPT-2X, this variant replaces the BattleMech taser with a TSEMP cannon. This upgrade trades the non-lethal capture capability of the taser for the TSEMP's ability to temporarily shut down enemy electronics and 'Mech systems entirely, making this variant a more lethal infiltration platform. Whether these refits were performed on existing captured RPT-2X chassis, newly manufactured frames, or some combination remains uncertain.

BMRaptorII_RPT3X.overview:
The Raptor II is synonymous with the Void Signature System, a revolutionary stealth technology that renders the 'Mech effectively invisible to both electronic sensors and visual detection. Developed by the Word of Blake using research recovered from ComStar's Terra archives after Operation Odysseus in 3058, the forty-ton design married mimetic armor composites, chameleon-scale light polarization, and emission baffling into a single integrated package powered by an onboard ECM suite. First fielded as early as 3067, the Raptor II served as a premier infiltration and search-and-destroy platform throughout the Jihad.

Following the liberation of Terra, the Republic of the Sphere recovered the design specifications and restarted production at a classified facility, assigning all Raptor IIs exclusively to its most elite special forces units. The extreme secrecy surrounding the design, from classified manufacturers to the deliberate omission of ejection systems, emphasizes the lengths taken to prevent the Void Signature technology from falling into foreign hands.
BMRaptorII_RPT3X.capabilities:
The Raptor II is built on a Void Integrated endo steel chassis powered by a VOX 280 XL engine, achieving a base speed of 118 kilometers per hour with MASC providing burst speeds up to 151 kilometers per hour in the standard RPT-3X configuration. Seven and a half tons of specially shaped Void Integrated light ferro-fibrous armor bonded with mimetic composites provides moderate protection while maintaining the sensor-deflecting properties essential to the Void Signature System's operation. A Guardian ECM suite is integral to every production model, as it is required for VoidSig to function.

The RPT-3X mounts two Streak SRM-6 launchers and two ER medium lasers, providing efficient and accurate firepower for an infiltrator. The Streak systems ensure no wasted ammunition, while the extended-range lasers allow engagement at distances where the Raptor II's stealth makes return fire extremely difficult. A small cockpit and the deliberate omission of both CASE and an ejection system reflect the Republic's uncompromising approach to operational security: pilots are expected to escape or die, with capture considered unacceptable.

At a standstill, the Raptor II is virtually undetectable, capable of lurking at optimum engagement range before striking with lethal precision and vanishing before effective countermeasures can be mounted. This combination of stealth, speed, and focused firepower makes the Raptor II one of the most feared light-to-medium combatants on the modern battlefield.

One heat sink is removed to accommodate the altered weapons array. The jump capability gives this variant superior maneuverability in terrain where the RPT-3X's MASC system would provide insufficient tactical advantage.

BMRaptor_RTX1BZ1.overview:
The Raptor holds the distinction of being the first Inner Sphere OmniMech ever produced. Designed by Luthien Armor Works as a proof of concept after months of studying Clan OmniMech salvage recovered from the Battle of Luthien in 3052, the twenty-five ton design validated that Inner Sphere engineers could replicate the modular technology that had given the Clans such a decisive advantage during the invasion. The Raptor filled the role of a light reconnaissance and fast strike platform, where its ability to rapidly reconfigure loadouts between missions proved invaluable to Draconis Combine commanders adjusting to the new reality of the Clan threat.

Though initially regarded with skepticism by traditionalists within the DCMS, Luthien Armor Works stood behind the design and eventually won over even its harshest critics. The Raptor became the premier light OmniMech of the Combine, and its prolific production saw it spread beyond Combine borders to become one of the most widely fielded Inner Sphere OmniMechs of its era.
BMRaptor_RTX1BZ1.capabilities:
The Raptor is built on an Alshain Type KR140 endo steel chassis powered by a weight-saving Omni 175 XL engine, giving the design a top speed of just under 119 kilometers per hour. This speed is the Raptor's primary defense, as three and a half tons of StarSlab/4 armor provides only modest protection against sustained fire. The trade-off is deliberate, maximizing the eleven and a half tons of pod space available for mission-specific loadouts, which represents an impressive proportion of the chassis's total mass.

The Prime configuration reflects a versatile combat philosophy, mounting three LRM-5 launchers for long-range harassment alongside two medium lasers and two small lasers for closer engagements. A pair of machine guns provides anti-infantry capability. This mix allows the Prime to contribute meaningfully at multiple range brackets while maintaining the speed to disengage when outmatched.

With seven distinct factory configurations and additional field variants, the Raptor demonstrates the flexibility that makes OmniMech technology so valued. Loadouts range from pure energy builds for extended operations to electronic warfare packages and even an underwater combat configuration, ensuring the Raptor can be tailored to virtually any light 'Mech mission profile.
BMRaptor_RTX1BZ1.history:
The Raptor's origins trace directly to the Battle of Luthien in January 3052, when the combined defense of the Combine capital against Clan Smoke Jaguar and Clan Nova Cat yielded significant quantities of Clan salvage. Luthien Armor Works engineers studied the captured OmniMech technology intensively, and by May 3052, just months after the battle, the first Raptors walked off the production line at the OmniMech Production Facility on Luthien. The very first units were assigned to the Dragon's Claws for testing, with additional Raptors sent to the Sword of Light, Genyosha, and Ghost regiments for further evaluation.

Acceptance within the DCMS was gradual. Many Combine soldiers, steeped in tradition, were slow to appreciate the advantages of an OmniMech that could swap its weapons between engagements. It took years for the standard Combine soldier to recognize the tactical flexibility the Raptor offered, but its performance during Operation Bulldog in 3059 and the Combine-Dominion War proved decisive in cementing the design's reputation. By the early 3060s, the Raptor was found in the regiments of every top-rated command within the Combine.

The Raptor's success saw it proliferate beyond Combine boundaries, becoming available to allied states and even appearing in mercenary commands. The design's "Easy to Maintain" reputation made it popular with units that lacked dedicated OmniMech maintenance facilities, as the Raptor proved more forgiving of improvised repair work than many of its contemporaries.

Production at Luthien Armor Works continued through the Civil War era, but the facility ceased Raptor production during the Jihad when the Word of Blake's assault on Luthien devastated much of the planet's industrial capacity. While LAW survived and eventually resumed other production lines, Raptor manufacturing was not restarted, leaving surviving units increasingly reliant on salvage and aftermarket parts to remain operational.
BMRaptor_RTX1BZ1.deployment: The Prime configuration represents the Raptor's most balanced loadout, combining three LRM-5 launchers for standoff fire with two medium lasers, two small lasers, and two machine guns for closer engagements. This versatile weapons mix enables the Prime to serve as a screening unit, light skirmisher, or anti-infantry platform depending on the tactical situation, making it the most commonly fielded configuration in general DCMS service.

The Raptor C is designed to overwhelm opponents with concentrated laser fire during rapid attack runs, relying on its speed to break contact before return fire can find its mark.

BMRaptor_RTX1OD.overview:
The Raptor holds the distinction of being the first Inner Sphere OmniMech ever produced. Designed by Luthien Armor Works as a proof of concept after months of studying Clan OmniMech salvage recovered from the Battle of Luthien in 3052, the twenty-five ton design validated that Inner Sphere engineers could replicate the modular technology that had given the Clans such a decisive advantage during the invasion. The Raptor filled the role of a light reconnaissance and fast strike platform, where its ability to rapidly reconfigure loadouts between missions proved invaluable to Draconis Combine commanders adjusting to the new reality of the Clan threat.

Though initially regarded with skepticism by traditionalists within the DCMS, Luthien Armor Works stood behind the design and eventually won over even its harshest critics. The Raptor became the premier light OmniMech of the Combine, and its prolific production saw it spread beyond Combine borders to become one of the most widely fielded Inner Sphere OmniMechs of its era.
BMRaptor_RTX1OD.capabilities:
The Raptor is built on an Alshain Type KR140 endo steel chassis powered by a weight-saving Omni 175 XL engine, giving the design a top speed of just under 119 kilometers per hour. This speed is the Raptor's primary defense, as three and a half tons of StarSlab/4 armor provides only modest protection against sustained fire. The trade-off is deliberate, maximizing the eleven and a half tons of pod space available for mission-specific loadouts, which represents an impressive proportion of the chassis's total mass.

The Prime configuration reflects a versatile combat philosophy, mounting three LRM-5 launchers for long-range harassment alongside two medium lasers and two small lasers for closer engagements. A pair of machine guns provides anti-infantry capability. This mix allows the Prime to contribute meaningfully at multiple range brackets while maintaining the speed to disengage when outmatched.

With seven distinct factory configurations and additional field variants, the Raptor demonstrates the flexibility that makes OmniMech technology so valued. Loadouts range from pure energy builds for extended operations to electronic warfare packages and even an underwater combat configuration, ensuring the Raptor can be tailored to virtually any light 'Mech mission profile.
BMRaptor_RTX1OD.history:
The Raptor's origins trace directly to the Battle of Luthien in January 3052, when the combined defense of the Combine capital against Clan Smoke Jaguar and Clan Nova Cat yielded significant quantities of Clan salvage. Luthien Armor Works engineers studied the captured OmniMech technology intensively, and by May 3052, just months after the battle, the first Raptors walked off the production line at the OmniMech Production Facility on Luthien. The very first units were assigned to the Dragon's Claws for testing, with additional Raptors sent to the Sword of Light, Genyosha, and Ghost regiments for further evaluation.

Acceptance within the DCMS was gradual. Many Combine soldiers, steeped in tradition, were slow to appreciate the advantages of an OmniMech that could swap its weapons between engagements. It took years for the standard Combine soldier to recognize the tactical flexibility the Raptor offered, but its performance during Operation Bulldog in 3059 and the Combine-Dominion War proved decisive in cementing the design's reputation. By the early 3060s, the Raptor was found in the regiments of every top-rated command within the Combine.

The Raptor's success saw it proliferate beyond Combine boundaries, becoming available to allied states and even appearing in mercenary commands. The design's "Easy to Maintain" reputation made it popular with units that lacked dedicated OmniMech maintenance facilities, as the Raptor proved more forgiving of improvised repair work than many of its contemporaries.

Production at Luthien Armor Works continued through the Civil War era, but the facility ceased Raptor production during the Jihad when the Word of Blake's assault on Luthien devastated much of the planet's industrial capacity. While LAW survived and eventually resumed other production lines, Raptor manufacturing was not restarted, leaving surviving units increasingly reliant on salvage and aftermarket parts to remain operational.
BMRaptor_RTX1OD.deployment: Alternate Configuration D fills an electronic warfare and reconnaissance role, carrying TAG, a Beagle active probe, and a C3 slave unit alongside a modest combat loadout of three Streak SRM-2 launchers, two small lasers, and two machine guns. The combination makes the Raptor D an excellent point 'Mech for C3-equipped lances, capable of detecting hidden units, designating targets for artillery, and sharing precise targeting data with networked allies.

BMRavenII_RVN5X.overview: The Raven II is the next generation of the Capellan Confederation's iconic Raven electronic warfare BattleMech, introduced in 3123 by Hellespont 'Mech Works on Sian. Developed from the experimental Jihad-era RVN-3X Raven X prototype, the Raven II advances the concept further than any previous model, increasing the chassis weight to forty tons to accommodate improved speed, heavier armor, and a more potent weapon suite. This weight increase pushes the design into the medium 'Mech class, making it a significantly more capable platform than its thirty-five ton predecessor while retaining the electronic warfare focus that has defined the Raven lineage for over a century.
BMRavenII_RVN5X.capabilities:
The Raven II is built on a lightweight Hellespont Type R2 endo steel skeleton, with a VOX 280 XL engine providing a top speed of nearly one hundred nineteen kilometers per hour. This exceptional speed, combined with seven tons of Hellespont Lite stealth armor powered by an Angel ECM suite, makes the Raven II extraordinarily difficult to detect and track. A Bloodhound Active Probe provides advanced sensor capability that surpasses the Beagle system used by earlier Raven models.

The most distinctive addition to the Raven II's arsenal is the Firmir Hypnos Tight-Stream Electromagnetic Pulse cannon, capable of shutting down enemy 'Mechs entirely. This weapon shifts the Raven II's role from passive electronic support toward active scout hunting and line-breaking operations. Pilots must exercise caution with repeated TSEMP firings, however, as the weapon's energy discharge can interfere with the Raven II's own sensitive electronics.

Supplementary armament includes a pair of Firmir Improved ER medium lasers and a Doombud MML-5 launcher fed by two ammunition bays. The absence of CASE protection for the missile ammunition in the left torso represents the design's most significant vulnerability, demanding that pilots prioritize avoiding critical hits to that location.
BMRavenII_RVN5X.history:
The Raven II's development traces directly to the Raven X prototype that Hellespont Industrials unveiled in 3078 during the Jihad. That experimental design demonstrated the potential for mounting cutting-edge electronics and weapons on the Raven platform, but the Strategios ultimately declined to approve it for full production due to concerns about its fragility and the prototype nature of its technology. The lessons learned from the Raven X program, however, informed the development of what became the Raven II.

When the Raven II entered service in 3123, many observers believed the original Raven's days were numbered. This proved premature, as Hellespont also introduced the updated RVN-5L Raven variant in 3125, designed specifically to work in tandem with the Raven II. The pairing of the lighter 5L as a spotter and electronic warfare support unit alongside the heavier, more combat-capable Raven II created a synergistic team greater than either design alone.

The Raven II saw extensive deployment during Operation Celestial Reward, where Dynasty Guard units used the 'Mech to devastating effect during the seizure of Avigait from the First Syrtis Fusiliers. Raven IIs from several battalions were deployed in augmented scouting lances, with orders to locate and pin down planetary militia forces. The 'Mech's superior speed and electronics proved instrumental in discovering and eliminating militia ambushes, and its TSEMP cannon disrupted enemy C3 networks while shutting down key Davion commanders' 'Mechs.

The Confederation has positioned the Raven II as a cornerstone of its reconnaissance and electronic warfare doctrine for the ilClan era, building on over a century of Raven development to field what may be the most capable dedicated EW platform in the Inner Sphere.
BMRavenII_RVN5X.deployment: The sole production variant of the Raven II mounts the full suite of next-generation electronic warfare equipment inherited from the Raven X prototype, including the Angel ECM suite and Bloodhound Active Probe, combined with the devastating Firmir Hypnos TSEMP cannon. The Ceres Metals Model 777 communications system integrates seamlessly with the Angel ECM, while the Apple Churchill 3000 targeting system works in concert with the Bloodhound probe to provide unmatched battlefield awareness. Ten double heat sinks manage the thermal load from the energy weapons and TSEMP system.

BMRaven_RVN1X.overview:
The Raven is a thirty-five ton electronic warfare BattleMech developed by the Capellan Confederation, with the first prototype, the RVN-1X, entering service in 3024. Wedged between the Free Worlds League and Federated Suns, the diminutive Confederation was desperately searching for force multipliers at the close of the Third Succession War. One ambitious research program attempted to recreate the sophisticated electronic warfare technology of the long-lost Star League era. While the resulting Ceres Arms Electronic Warfare X-1 equipment was a technical success, the seven-and-a-half ton package proved too bulky to install on any existing BattleMech chassis.

Rather than abandon a promising technology, Chancellor Maximillian Liao directed Hellespont Industries to develop an entirely new design built around the electronics. The resulting Raven was one of the first truly original BattleMech designs produced in centuries, though the prototype would not live up to its ambitious expectations until the recovery of lostech allowed Hellespont 'Mech Works to produce the definitive RVN-3L model in the late 3040s.
BMRaven_RVN1X.capabilities:
The production RVN-3L Raven is built around the most comprehensive electronic warfare suite available to any Inner Sphere light 'Mech of its era. The Apple Churchill consortium provides the complete electronics package, including a Guardian ECM suite to blanket friendly units with electronic jamming, a Beagle Active Probe to locate hidden enemies, Target Acquisition Gear for designating artillery targets, and a Narc Missile Beacon to improve allied missile accuracy. A Ceres Metals Model 666 communications system integrates these disparate systems into a cohesive electronic warfare platform.

A Hermes 210 XL engine provides a respectable top speed of ninety-seven kilometers per hour, while four and a half tons of Hellespont Lite ferro-fibrous armor offers reasonable protection for a design never intended to see direct combat. The Raven's offensive armament is deliberately modest, consisting of a Harpoon-6 SRM-6 launcher and a pair of Ceres Arms medium lasers. CASE protection in the left torso mitigates the risk of ammunition explosions.

The Raven's design philosophy accepts that any mission requiring direct engagement stands as a tactical failure. Its true value lies in electronic countermeasures, target designation, and sensor operations conducted from standoff range. When forced into combat, the 'Mech's light armor and limited firepower make survival dependent on speed and the hope that reinforcements arrive quickly.
BMRaven_RVN1X.history:
The Raven's combat debut came during the Fourth Succession War, when prototype RVN-1X models were pressed into service against the Federated Suns. Deployed at the battalion level as temporary additions to command lances, these early Ravens provided electronic warfare support to Capellan formations, but the primitive EW equipment could not provide a sufficient edge to influence the course of engagements. Many Ravens were captured by Davion forces during the conflict, with some sent to the New Avalon Institute of Science for reverse engineering while others were retained by the units that seized them.

One of the Raven's earliest notable missions involved providing electronic cover for Capellan units participating in Operation Intruders Communion. BMRazorback_RZK10S.overview:
The Razorback is a thirty-ton light BattleMech introduced by Bowie Industries in 3063, representing the massive defense corporation's first foray into light 'Mech design after generations of producing exclusively heavy chassis. Built at the company's Carlisle manufacturing facility, the Razorback was developed to compete in an Inner Sphere market that had shifted decisively toward newer designs incorporating recovered Star League technology.

The design debuted in prototype form in mid-3063 and entered final production just months later, its full testing period cut short by the eruption of the FedCom Civil War. The Razorback has since proven itself a reliable and versatile light combatant, seeing widespread service across the Lyran Commonwealth and beyond.
BMRazorback_RZK10S.capabilities:
The Razorback fills a middle ground in light BattleMech design, combining long-range firepower with effective short-range punch. Its primary weapon, a Defiance Model 6 extended-range large laser, provides accurate fire at considerable distances, while a Defiance Trak-Shot II Streak SRM-4 launcher delivers reliable close-range damage. Four Coventry Light Autogun machine guns round out the armament, making the design particularly lethal against conventional infantry and useful for exploiting breaches in enemy armor.

While the Razorback is far from the fastest light 'Mech in existence, its Defiance 180 light fusion engine propels the design at speeds sufficient to keep pace with most light combat elements. This allows MechWarriors to provide ranged covering fire while faster units close with the enemy or withdraw. The use of a light engine rather than an extra-light model gives the Razorback a notable survivability advantage, as a side torso breach will not result in catastrophic engine failure.

Durallex Super Medium ferro-fibrous armor provides solid protection for a 'Mech of its tonnage, and the inclusion of CASE ensures that an ammunition explosion in the missile or machine gun bins will not destroy the entire machine. The Razorback's general reliance on ballistic and missile weaponry means it rarely encounters overheating issues under normal combat conditions, though this comes at the cost of ammunition dependency.
BMRazorback_RZK10S.history:
The Razorback's development was driven by economic necessity rather than military doctrine. Throughout the Succession Wars and beyond, Bowie Industries had built its reputation on heavy BattleMechs like the Archer and Marauder, produced at facilities on Alarion, Carlisle, and Wyatt. The post-Clan Invasion era saw a surge in military procurement that temporarily sustained these legacy production lines, but by the late 3050s the market had shifted decisively toward newer designs incorporating recovered Star League technology.

Bowie's decision to develop a light BattleMech in 3060 represented a fundamental strategic pivot for the centuries-old corporation. The Razorback entered service just as the FedCom Civil War erupted, creating immediate demand for combat replacements on all sides of the conflict. The Carlisle production facility ran at capacity throughout the war, with Bowie shipping 'Mechs directly to the LAAF Quartermaster Corps. Several shipments were diverted by officers loyal to Victor Steiner-Davion, though nearly all Razorbacks remained within Lyran Alliance territory. The first production run especially found its way into Katherine-loyal units stationed in the Federated Suns.

The Jihad proved both devastating and transformative for the Razorback program. Word of Blake attacks destroyed the Bowie facility on Alarion entirely and nuclear strikes devastated the Wyatt plant in 3068, leaving Carlisle as Bowie's primary surviving manufacturing center. The fall of Hesperus II cut off Bowie's main weapons supplier, directly spawning the all-energy RZK-9T variant and forcing the company to become more self-sufficient in component sourcing. Despite operating at reduced capacity, the Carlisle plant continued production throughout the conflict.

Following the Jihad, the Razorback saw wider distribution across the Inner Sphere. The design found service with the Federated Suns, Free Worlds League successor states, the Free Rasalhague Republic, the Marian Hegemony, and the Republic of the Sphere, in addition to numerous mercenary commands. Continued production through the Dark Age and into the ilClan era, particularly of the proven RZK-9T and the newer tenth-series variants, ensured a steady supply to Lyran forces and their trading partners.
BMRazorback_RZK10S.deployment: Introduced in 3079 following the devastation of the Jihad, this variant incorporates several weight-saving technologies to expand the Razorback's tactical flexibility. An XL gyro and small cockpit free tonnage for a snub-nose PPC as the primary weapon, backed by a five-tube multi-missile launcher with two tons of ammunition and a pair of extended-range small lasers. The addition of a Beagle active probe enhances the design's reconnaissance capability, making this variant well-suited for scouting operations where firepower and detection ability must be balanced.

BMRazorback_RZK10T.overview:
The Razorback is a thirty-ton light BattleMech introduced by Bowie Industries in 3063, representing the massive defense corporation's first foray into light 'Mech design after generations of producing exclusively heavy chassis. Built at the company's Carlisle manufacturing facility, the Razorback was developed to compete in an Inner Sphere market that had shifted decisively toward newer designs incorporating recovered Star League technology.

The design debuted in prototype form in mid-3063 and entered final production just months later, its full testing period cut short by the eruption of the FedCom Civil War. The Razorback has since proven itself a reliable and versatile light combatant, seeing widespread service across the Lyran Commonwealth and beyond.
BMRazorback_RZK10T.capabilities:
The Razorback fills a middle ground in light BattleMech design, combining long-range firepower with effective short-range punch. Its primary weapon, a Defiance Model 6 extended-range large laser, provides accurate fire at considerable distances, while a Defiance Trak-Shot II Streak SRM-4 launcher delivers reliable close-range damage. Four Coventry Light Autogun machine guns round out the armament, making the design particularly lethal against conventional infantry and useful for exploiting breaches in enemy armor.

While the Razorback is far from the fastest light 'Mech in existence, its Defiance 180 light fusion engine propels the design at speeds sufficient to keep pace with most light combat elements. This allows MechWarriors to provide ranged covering fire while faster units close with the enemy or withdraw. The use of a light engine rather than an extra-light model gives the Razorback a notable survivability advantage, as a side torso breach will not result in catastrophic engine failure.

Durallex Super Medium ferro-fibrous armor provides solid protection for a 'Mech of its tonnage, and the inclusion of CASE ensures that an ammunition explosion in the missile or machine gun bins will not destroy the entire machine. The Razorback's general reliance on ballistic and missile weaponry means it rarely encounters overheating issues under normal combat conditions, though this comes at the cost of ammunition dependency.
BMRazorback_RZK10T.history:
The Razorback's development was driven by economic necessity rather than military doctrine. Throughout the Succession Wars and beyond, Bowie Industries had built its reputation on heavy BattleMechs like the Archer and Marauder, produced at facilities on Alarion, Carlisle, and Wyatt. The post-Clan Invasion era saw a surge in military procurement that temporarily sustained these legacy production lines, but by the late 3050s the market had shifted decisively toward newer designs incorporating recovered Star League technology.

Bowie's decision to develop a light BattleMech in 3060 represented a fundamental strategic pivot for the centuries-old corporation. The Razorback entered service just as the FedCom Civil War erupted, creating immediate demand for combat replacements on all sides of the conflict. The Carlisle production facility ran at capacity throughout the war, with Bowie shipping 'Mechs directly to the LAAF Quartermaster Corps. Several shipments were diverted by officers loyal to Victor Steiner-Davion, though nearly all Razorbacks remained within Lyran Alliance territory. The first production run particularly found its way into Katherine-loyal units stationed in the Federated Suns.

The Jihad proved both devastating and transformative for the Razorback program. Word of Blake attacks destroyed the Bowie facility on Alarion entirely and nuclear strikes devastated the Wyatt plant in 3068, leaving Carlisle as Bowie's primary surviving manufacturing center. The fall of Hesperus II cut off Bowie's main weapons supplier, directly spawning the all-energy RZK-9T variant and forcing the company to become more self-sufficient in component sourcing. Despite operating at reduced capacity, the Carlisle plant continued production throughout the conflict.

Following the Jihad, the Razorback saw wider distribution across the Inner Sphere. The design found service with the Federated Suns, Free Worlds League successor states, the Free Rasalhague Republic, the Marian Hegemony, and the Republic of the Sphere, in addition to numerous mercenary commands. Continued production through the Dark Age and into the ilClan era, particularly of the proven RZK-9T and the newer tenth-series variants, ensured a steady supply to Lyran forces and their trading partners.
BMRazorback_RZK10T.deployment: Developed in 3071 during the Jihad, this variant stands as a complete rebuild of the Razorback from the ground up. An extra-light fusion engine replaces the original light engine, boosting top speed to over one hundred and ten kilometers per hour. Endo steel internal structure and standard ferro-fibrous armor maintain protection levels while freeing the weight needed for the dramatic speed increase. Armed with a heavy PPC and four extended-range small lasers, this variant sacrifices the versatility of earlier models for raw speed and striking power, making it an effective raider and harasser on the modern battlefield.

BMRedShift_RDS2A.overview: The Red Shift was introduced in 3062 as the first BattleMech produced by Leopard Armor, a venerable Terran vehicle manufacturer that transitioned to BattleMech production under the Word of Blake. Primarily conceived as a TAG spotter for combined-arms formations reliant on Arrow IV artillery, the twenty-ton design filled a critical tactical niche within the Word of Blake Militia. The Red Shift's development was driven by the need to complement Leopard Armor's own Padilla Heavy Artillery Tank, creating an integrated targeting and fire support partnership. Despite its narrow specialization, the Red Shift proved effective enough to see widespread distribution across the Militia, establishing Leopard Armor as a capable BattleMech manufacturer.
BMRedShift_RDS2A.capabilities:
The Red Shift's design philosophy centers entirely around its TAG targeting system, making it one of the few light BattleMechs purpose-built as an artillery spotter. A GM 180 XL extralight engine drives the twenty-ton chassis to speeds exceeding 150 kilometers per hour, giving it the agility to reach forward observation positions and evade enemy fire. The Leopard Mark I endo steel frame saves critical weight that is allocated to four tons of StarSlab/1 ferro-fibrous armor, providing impressive protection for a design in its weight class.

The Guardian ECM suite serves a dual purpose, shielding both the Red Shift and the Padilla artillery vehicles it supports from advanced electronic warfare systems such as Artemis IV and C3 networks. For self-defense, two Tronel XII medium pulse lasers provide accurate close-range firepower, their enhanced tracking capability proving particularly effective against other fast-moving light 'Mechs and vehicles. Ten double heat sinks manage waste heat efficiently, allowing the MechWarrior to fire both lasers while maintaining full speed.

The design's primary weakness lies in its narrow mission profile, as the Red Shift contributes relatively little direct firepower to engagements where artillery support is unavailable or unnecessary.
BMRedShift_RDS2A.history:
The Red Shift's origins are deeply intertwined with the Word of Blake's consolidation of power on Terra. When the Blakists seized control of the Terran system from ComStar in the late 3050s, Leopard Armor, a venerable vehicle manufacturer based in North Africa, simply transferred its contracts to the new regime. The company had maintained a long history of producing combat vehicles for both the Terran Hegemony and ComStar, including the Demon, Rhino, and Padilla Heavy Artillery Tank.

Following the restart of Padilla production for the Word of Blake Militia around 3058, Leopard Armor's design team undertook the ambitious challenge of developing a BattleMech specifically to complement the heavy artillery tank. The result was the Red Shift, which entered production in 3062 as the company's first foray into BattleMech manufacturing. The design's emphasis on TAG spotting for Arrow IV artillery systems reflected a deliberate effort to recreate combined-arms tactics dating back to the original Star League era.

The Red Shift saw rapid deployment across the Word of Blake Militia, with every division receiving at least some examples of the design. During the Jihad, Red Shifts served on numerous fronts, often operating in tandem with Padilla batteries. On Outreach in 3068, a Red Shift gained notoriety harassing Wolf's Dragoons guerrilla forces during the Second Battle of Outreach, directing artillery fire and leading defenders into ambushes throughout the campaign.

Production of all Red Shift variants ceased with the destruction of the Word of Blake during the Jihad's conclusion. The Leopard Armor facility on Terra subsequently fell under Republic of the Sphere control, but Red Shift production was not resumed. Surviving examples became increasingly rare in the post-Jihad era, though the design's specialized nature meant few operators had reason to seek them out without access to Arrow IV-equipped support vehicles.
BMRedShift_RDS2A.deployment: This variant serves as the baseline production model of the Red Shift, entering service in 3062 with the Word of Blake Militia. This configuration was typically assigned alongside Padilla Heavy Artillery Tanks or other Arrow IV-equipped units, where its combination of spotting capability and electronic protection proved most effective. In some cases, Red Shifts were attached to missile-heavy formations, as the Word of Blake had access to the Free Worlds League's semi-guided warhead technology, allowing the design's TAG system to enhance indirect fire accuracy beyond its primary artillery-spotting role.

BMRedShift_RDS3A.deployment: Developed in 3068 during the opening stages of the Jihad, this variant is a significant reimagining of the Red Shift concept. This transformation converts the design from an artillery spotter into a networked direct-combat platform, capable of sharing targeting data across an entire C3i-equipped formation while delivering substantially greater firepower at longer ranges.

BMRevenant_UBM2R.overview:
The Revenant is a 30-ton quadrupedal drone BattleMech with origins rooted in the Word of Blake's desperate final defense of Terra during the Jihad. First appearing in 3075, the original UBM-1A was an autonomous unmanned 'Mech produced at the Devil's Peak Production Site, designed to bolster ground defenses against the allied coalition assault on the Terran system. Controlled by a robotic cockpit rather than a human pilot, the Revenant filled the role of a cheap, expendable sentry capable of engaging infantry and light armor in large numbers.

The concept was later recovered and refined by the Republic of the Sphere into the UBM-2R series, transforming a crude Blakist weapon into a practical, inexpensive defensive asset. The Revenant represents one of the few successful implementations of fully autonomous BattleMech technology in the post-Jihad era.
BMRevenant_UBM2R.capabilities:
The Revenant is slower than most modern light 'Mechs, with its GM 180 engine providing a top speed of only 97 kph, but compensates with durability that belies its weight class. Built on a Spectre IV-Gamma endo steel frame, the UBM-2R mounts a respectable amount of Strasbourg Armaments Type 3 standard armor for a 30-ton design, allowing it to absorb considerable punishment and still return to base. The lack of jump jets limits its tactical flexibility in rough terrain, though its quad configuration provides superior stability on uneven ground.

The primary UBM-2R configuration carries four Martell extended range medium lasers paired with four MainFire light machine guns, giving the drone effective anti-infantry and anti-armor capability at medium range. The laser-heavy loadout eliminates ammunition dependency for its primary weapons, an important consideration for an autonomous unit operating without logistical support. While the Revenant cannot match dedicated combat 'Mechs in a stand-up fight, its combination of toughness, low production cost, and drone operation makes it ideally suited for nighttime patrols, sentry duty, and raiding operations where risking a human pilot would be unacceptable.
BMRevenant_UBM2R.history:
The Revenant's origins trace to the final, desperate years of the Jihad, when the Word of Blake began fielding autonomous drone 'Mechs to supplement their dwindling conventional forces defending the Terran system. In 3075, allied coalition forces first encountered the quadrupedal drones during the assault on Terra, Mars, and Luna. Intelligence operatives initially could not identify the source of the unfamiliar unmanned BattleMechs, and it was not until coalition troops overran Cameron St. Jamais' command post at Devil's Peak in North America that the manufacturing facility was discovered. The Revenant was the most numerous of at least three robotic 'Mech designs produced at the site.

Despite being deployed in significant numbers, the Revenant proved to be more of a nuisance than a genuine threat. Its erratic behavior under ECM exposure and complete disregard for tactical principles made individual drones easy to dispatch. However, the sheer volume of Revenants, combined with their unfamiliar quadrupedal design, occasionally gave coalition attackers pause and forced them to divert resources from more critical objectives. The fighting at Devil's Peak ultimately destroyed the production lines, and a Word of Blake computer virus erased all design schematics and programming specifications, seemingly ending the program.

The concept was not forgotten, however. ComStar had experimented with similar drone technology alongside programs like the Celerity before the organization's disarmament, and the Republic of the Sphere inherited both the research and the recovered Blakist hardware. Following the activation of Fortress Republic in 3136, Republic Armed Forces scientists at the Manufacturing Center Providence on Terra began developing the UBM-2R series, replacing the original's crude robotic cockpit with a more capable Drone Operating System. Production began around 3139, yielding a family of specialized variants optimized for different tactical roles.

Within the Fortress, Revenants have served on a number of RAF raids against hostile forces, exploiting the advantage that enemies who have not faced drone 'Mechs since the Jihad have no idea what they are confronting. Elements of the XIV Principes have deployed Revenants in spoiling attacks, where mixed formations of combat and fire support variants have successfully raided Capellan Confederation resupply points and engaged hovertank companies under cover of darkness. The drones' willingness to execute anti-capture protocols and their indifference to personal risk have made them particularly effective in night raids and operations where the loss of a human pilot would be strategically unacceptable.
BMRevenant_UBM2R.deployment: This variant represents the Republic of the Sphere's successful reverse-engineering of the Blakist drone concept. Introduced around 3139 from the RAF Manufacturing Center Providence on Terra, the redesign replaces the original's crude robotic cockpit with a more sophisticated Drone Operating System and upgrades the chassis to the Spectre IV-Gamma endo steel frame. The armament is standardized to four extended range medium lasers and four light machine guns, providing a reliable anti-personnel and medium-range engagement platform. RAF theorists expect the design to excel as a nighttime raider and sentry-walker, and its low cost makes it feasible to deploy on almost every Republic world within the Fortress.

BMRevenant_UBM2R2.history:

BMRiflemanIIC.overview:
The Rifleman IIC represents the culmination of nearly two centuries of Clan trial and error to perfect the venerable Rifleman chassis. Where the Inner Sphere design epitomized a "best compromise" of weapons and armor that never fully satisfied its critics, the Clans examined the problem from a fresh perspective and largely resolved the overheating and armor deficiencies inherent in the original. By adding five tons of mass and incorporating superior Clan technology, engineers created a platform that finally delivered on the Rifleman's anti-aircraft promise.

An ancient rebuild of an already ancient design, the Rifleman IIC has soldiered on throughout the centuries. The 'Mech serves with most Clans (a notable exception being Clan Wolf, which prefers the Glass Spider) and has found markets among several Inner Sphere powers. Mountain Wolf BattleMechs on Alpheratz recently began building the design for the Raven Alliance Military Corps, demonstrating the continued demand for this proven anti-aircraft platform. Its simplicity is matched only by its effectiveness, and new variants continue to debut as manufacturers explore different weapon configurations while maintaining the core air-denial mission.
BMRiflemanIIC.capabilities:
Visually, the Clan Rifleman looks nothing like the traditional outline Inner Sphere MechWarriors recognize. Like its smaller brother, it mounts a large rotating radar array over its head, but the IIC variant's sensor package is mounted much higher, with twin box-like appendages fitted on either side of the central support pylon. Close analysis of battlefield scans revealed this unusual configuration operates as a phased array acting in tandem with the main array, though the full benefits of this arrangement warrant further study. The sophisticated GH D5j targeting system with integrated Active Probe can switch rapidly between ground engagements and the fluid realm of aerospace combat, providing protection against fighter strikes without compromising offensive capability.

The standard configuration mounts four Kolibri Delta Series Large Pulse Lasers, offering simple, accurate firepower that requires no ammunition supply. MechWarriors who have faced the Rifleman IIC report that it is impossible to close quickly enough with this 'Mech, as it will often strip an opponent's armor before they can reach close-combat range. A single Series 1b ER Small Laser serves as a backup weapon. Nineteen double heat sinks keep heat mostly in check, though pilots should employ volley fire during sustained engagements. Three "Highlifter" 44 jump jets propel the sixty-five-ton chassis up to ninety meters per leap, providing tactical mobility the original Rifleman never possessed. Eleven tons of Forging Z5 ferro-fibrous armor on a CCo-B Endo Steel frame maximizes protection, and many garrison MechWarriors appreciate the extra cockpit protection provided by the well-armored sensor package that forms the design's distinctive "helmet."
BMRiflemanIIC.history:
The Rifleman IIC was first observed as part of Clan Nova Cat forces during the initial invasion, but has since been seen in all the Clans with which the Inner Sphere has come into contact. The 'Mech forms a common sight in Clan garrison units, serving as the first line of defense against air attack. The main variant on the Rifleman IIC appeared first with the Smoke Jaguar Clan and has since been spotted among other garrison forces. Designated the IIC 2, this version takes a more conservative approach to the anti-aircraft role, using a larger 260-rated engine to retain standard Rifleman performance while eliminating the ferro-fibrous armor in favor of two additional tons of standard plating. Four Ultra Autocannon/2s with 135 rounds of ammunition stored in CASE-fitted torso sections provide formidable sustained firepower.

Clan Cloud Cobra upgraded their aging Rifleman IICs following the surprise invasion of Huntress, introducing the IIC 3 variant in early 3062 with Heavy Large Lasers that deliver a nasty surprise to enemies expecting the standard pulse configuration. Mountain Wolf BattleMechs' newly refurbished factory on Alpheratz began building the base design for the Alliance Military Corps, giving second-line units access to Clan technologies against pirates and border threats. When bandits struck Prinis Prime using local collaborators to disable AMC aerospace contingents, a lance of new Rifleman IICs appeared and rendered the pirate command lance to slag in moments. Similar actions on Suianheer and Risin have sent clear signals to opportunists along the Alliance border.

The Diamond Sharks collaborated with Federated Suns interests to develop the IIC 8, whose ECM capabilities and 86 kph speed proved troublesome for Inner Sphere defenders on New Earth during the Jihad. An unusual action occurred on Ballalaba, where Marian Hegemony forces fought to stave off a Canopian counterattack. One century of IV Prima, under Centurion Wozniak's command, held off repeated charges by the Second Canopian Light Horse for several days using archaic Rifleman IICs that were nonetheless cutting-edge for the tech-limited Marian forces. Wozniak's Stand became a heavily propagandized bright spot during an otherwise bleak period for the Hegemony, and a daring nighttime raid later freed the centurion from Canopian captors.

Clan Nova Cat introduced the IIC 7 in 3078 with heavy lasers and plasma cannons linked to a targeting computer, while Star Adder's IIC 6 mounting twin HAG-30s reportedly remained in the Clan Homeworlds and may be apocryphal. The Raven Alliance's recent IIC 9 variant uses coolant pods to handle alpha strike heat with reflective armor providing protection against energy weapons, while their IIC 10 mounts ProtoMech autocannons in a curious short-range configuration that analysts consider a conceptual failure. Both the Draconis Combine and Duchy of Oriente have acquired various Rifleman IIC models in small numbers, ensuring this ancient Clan design continues finding new markets throughout the Inner Sphere.
BMRiflemanIIC.deployment: The base Rifleman IIC emerged in 2845 as a Clan upgrade of captured SLDF Riflemen, adding five tons to the chassis and incorporating advanced Clan technology. Four Large Pulse Lasers provide devastating accuracy against both ground targets and aerospace assets, with the pulse technology proving particularly effective for anti-aircraft work. An ER Small Laser offers token close-range backup. Nineteen double heat sinks manage the considerable thermal load, though pilots must employ volley fire during sustained engagements. Three jump jets compensate for the reduced ground speed, providing ninety meters of tactical repositioning capability. Maximum ferro-fibrous armor protection and an Active Probe round out this formidable fire support platform.

Each arm carries a Series 7K ER Large Laser paired with twin Series-9 AP Gauss Rifles for combined-arms engagement, while Type VI Streak SRM-6 launchers in each torso provide additional close-range firepower. A head-mounted ECM Suite disrupts enemy targeting networks, and five jump jets enable one hundred fifty meter leaps. This configuration transforms the traditional fire support platform into an aggressive skirmisher capable of rapid repositioning and precision strikes.

BMRiflemanII_RFL3N2.overview:
The Rifleman II emerged from the Star League Defense Force's Royal program in 2773, representing a dramatic reimagining of Kallon Industries' venerable anti-aircraft platform. By adding twenty tons to the chassis weight and incorporating the most advanced technologies available, SLDF engineers transformed a capable fire-support 'Mech into a devastating assault-weight weapons platform. The design served exclusively with Royal units, never seeing widespread distribution before the Exodus.

When General Kerensky led the SLDF into exile, the Rifleman II accompanied them, disappearing from the Inner Sphere entirely. Rumors persisted throughout the Succession Wars of advanced Rifleman variants hidden in Periphery caches or carried by fortunate mercenary commands, but no confirmed sightings occurred for centuries. The most persistent legend involved the infamous Gray Noton, whose "Legend-Killer" Rifleman dominated the Solaris VII arenas, whispers suggested he had discovered an abandoned Rifleman II during his Periphery mercenary days and disguised it as a standard model to maintain his competitive advantage.
BMRiflemanII_RFL3N2.capabilities:
The Rifleman II builds upon its predecessor's anti-aircraft excellence while addressing nearly every weakness that plagued the original design. An Endo Steel internal structure and Extralight fusion engine free sufficient weight for twelve tons of standard armor, a sixty percent improvement over the RFL-3N. The weapons array replaces the original's mixed armament with paired LB 10-X autocannons and Large Pulse Lasers, one of each mounted in the distinctive arm assemblies. This combination provides devastating firepower against both aerial and ground targets, with the cluster ammunition option offering particular effectiveness against fast-moving aircraft.

Fourteen double heat sinks manage the thermal load far more effectively than the original's ten single units, enabling sustained fire that the RFL-3N could never achieve. A Beagle Active Probe enhances the already-exceptional sensor capabilities, allowing pilots to detect hidden enemies and coordinate with friendly forces. Torso-mounted medium lasers provide close-range backup. The only significant drawback is the XL engine's vulnerability to side torso damage, a trade-off the Royal engineers deemed acceptable given the design's intended role engaging enemies at range rather than brawling in close quarters.
BMRiflemanII_RFL3N2.history:
The Rifleman II served exclusively with SLDF Royal regiments during its brief Inner Sphere deployment, participating in the final campaigns against Stefan Amaris's forces on Terra. These elite units employed the design's superior firepower and sensor capabilities to devastating effect during the liberation, though the chaos of the conflict left few detailed records of specific engagements. When Kerensky called the Exodus, virtually every Rifleman II accompanied the departing fleet.

For three centuries, the Rifleman II existed only in fragmentary records and persistent rumors. The legend of Gray Noton's "Legend-Killer" kept speculation alive, with theories ranging from a lucky cache discovery to secret ComStar assistance. Noton himself never confirmed or denied piloting anything other than a standard Rifleman, and his unsolved murder in 3027 ensured the truth died with him. Various record sheets have attempted to reconstruct possible configurations, but whether any accurately represent the actual "Legend-Killer" remains unknown.

Technical Readout data recovered after the Clan Invasion finally confirmed the Rifleman II's specifications, though the design remains extraordinarily rare in the Inner Sphere. The Clans presumably retained some examples during their centuries of isolation, potentially incorporating the design into their touman or using it as a basis for the Rifleman IIC development. Any surviving Inner Sphere examples would be priceless relics of the Star League era, though none have been definitively authenticated since the rediscovery of the design's technical specifications.
BMRiflemanII_RFL3N2.deployment: This variant emerged in 2773 as part of the SLDF Royal Command's equipment upgrade program, representing the ultimate expression of the Rifleman's anti-aircraft design philosophy. Twenty additional tons allowed comprehensive modernization: Endo Steel construction supported a Pitban 320 XL engine, while twelve tons of Kallon Royalstar armor finally gave the chassis adequate battlefield protection. Each arm mounted an LB 10-X autocannon paired with a Large Pulse Laser, devastatingly effective against aerospace assets and ground targets alike. Torso-mounted medium lasers and a Beagle Active Probe rounded out the configuration. Fourteen double heat sinks managed the thermal load effectively. The design saw limited service during the Amaris Civil War before being lost with the Exodus fleet, remaining unknown to the Inner Sphere until rediscovery in the post-Jihad era.
