BMTalon_TLN5V.overview:
The Talon was first deployed in 2670 to provide light BattleMech companies with much-needed long-range firepower. Star League High Command was so impressed by the design during combat trials in 2669 that they immediately ordered full production, and sales to the SLDF quickly surpassed all other light BattleMechs. Commonly paired with the lighter Mongoose, the Talon provided covering fire should the reconnaissance unit encounter something it could not handle on its own.

Rendered extinct during the Succession Wars, the Talon was absent from the battlefield for over two centuries before Blackstone BattleMechs restarted production on Inarcs in 3056. The once-popular design quickly reestablished itself as a valued asset in light formations, earning renewed respect for its combination of speed and long-range hitting power.
BMTalon_TLN5V.capabilities:
The Talon combines impressive speed with heavy long-range firepower, a rare combination in the light weight class. An Edasich Motors 280-rated extra-light engine propels the thirty-five ton machine to a maximum speed of nearly 130 kilometers per hour, allowing it to keep pace with virtually any reconnaissance unit. Blackstone markets the design as being able to outrun anything it cannot outgun.

The primary weapon is a Lord's Light-2 extended-range PPC, giving the Talon an engagement range approaching 700 meters. For close-range defense, a pair of ChisComp 39 medium lasers mounted on the left arm provide adequate firepower against other light 'Mechs. Seven and a half tons of Kallon Light Shield A standard armor give the Talon excellent protection for its weight class, enough durability to weather return fire while withdrawing from unfavorable engagements.

The design sacrifices jump capability entirely, relying on raw speed for maneuverability. The absence of jump jets can leave the Talon vulnerable in rough terrain, but on open ground its combination of speed, reach, and staying power make it a formidable opponent for anything in its weight class.
BMTalon_TLN5V.history:
The Talon first saw action shortly after its introduction in 2670 and quickly proved itself invaluable to light 'Mech companies across the Star League Defense Force. Its long-range firepower filled a critical gap that had long plagued light formations, which traditionally relied on speed and numbers rather than hitting power. By the late Star League era, the Talon was among the most ordered light BattleMechs in SLDF service.

The TLN-5W upgrade in 2760 initially saw distribution restricted to Royal units. The Amaris Civil War changed this, with the TLN-5V distributed widely among regular SLDF formations and the upgraded TLN-5W seeing frontline service for the first time. Following the Exodus, every Successor State sought to acquire Talons as fast as they could be manufactured. Commanders attempted to replicate the original SLDF lance tactic of deploying three Talons alongside a Mongoose for headhunting and supply disruption behind enemy lines, substituting a Spector to flush out enemy commanders when Mongooses were unavailable.

The harshness of the Succession Wars proved too great for the design's survival. Production at the Briden BattleMechs Unlimited facility on Errai never kept pace with losses during the First Succession War. When several tactical nuclear strikes destroyed the factory in 2815, the Talon's fate was sealed. The last operational example was stripped for parts around 2830 to keep a House Kurita light lance functional.

The Inner Sphere would not see another Talon for over two centuries. In 3056, Blackstone BattleMechs announced they had secured production rights and restarted manufacturing at their facility on Inarcs. Sent to the Clan occupation zone border, the reborn Talon first saw combat during the Jade Falcon invasion of Coventry, where reports of its performance were highly favorable. During the FedCom Civil War, elements of the Seventh Crucis Lancers damaged Blackstone's production lines on Inarcs in 3065, though they returned to full capacity by late 3066.

Following the Civil War, the Lyran Alliance opened the Talon for export, recognizing that most Lyran units preferred traditional heavier formations. The Federated Suns and mercenary units absorbed much of the demand, while ComStar, the Free Rasalhague Republic, and the Draconis Combine acquired lances for evaluation. A few of these combined-arms lances have been spotted along the Jade Falcon border, though no command has fielded Talons in the numbers the original SLDF once did. Blackstone continued developing new variants through the Jihad and into the Dark Age, keeping the venerable design relevant with successive technological improvements.
BMTalon_TLN5V.deployment: The original Talon introduced in 2670, this variant mounts a standard PPC rather than the extended-range model found on later variants. While lacking the reach of the TLN-5W, the standard particle projector cannon still provides formidable long-range firepower for a light 'Mech. The simpler weapon system produces slightly less heat, allowing the MechWarrior to fire all weapons while running without significant overheating concerns. Produced at the Briden BattleMechs Unlimited facility on Errai during the Star League era, this variant was distributed widely among regular SLDF formations and saw extensive service during the Amaris Civil War before attrition and the destruction of its production facility ended its run.

BMTalon_TLN5W.deployment: This variant represents the upgraded Royal variant introduced in 2760, replacing the standard PPC with a Lord's Light-2 extended-range model. This upgrade extended the Talon's engagement envelope to nearly 700 meters, making it one of the longest-ranged light 'Mechs in existence. Initially reserved for Royal units, this variant was distributed more broadly during the Amaris Civil War. When Blackstone BattleMechs restarted Talon production on Inarcs in 3056, this variant was chosen as the standard production model, fielding the superior variant from the outset.

BMTalon_TLN5Z.overview:

Star League High Command was so impressed by the design during combat trials in 2669 that they immediately ordered full production, and sales to the SLDF quickly surpassed all other light BattleMechs. Commonly paired with the lighter Mongoose, the Talon provided covering fire should the reconnaissance unit encounter something it could not handle on its own.

Rendered extinct during the Succession Wars, the Talon was absent from the battlefield for over two centuries before Blackstone BattleMechs restarted production on Inarcs in 3056. The once-popular design quickly reestablished itself as a valued asset in light formations, earning renewed respect for its combination of speed and long-range hitting power.
BMTalon_TLN5Z.capabilities:
The Talon combines impressive speed with heavy long-range firepower, a rare combination in the light weight class. An Edasich Motors 280-rated extra-light engine propels the thirty-five ton machine to a maximum speed of nearly 130 kilometers per hour, allowing it to keep pace with virtually any reconnaissance unit. Blackstone markets the design as being able to outrun anything it cannot outgun.

The primary weapon is a Lord's Light-2 extended-range PPC, giving the Talon an engagement range approaching 700 meters. For close-range defense, a pair of ChisComp 39 medium lasers mounted on the left arm provide adequate firepower against other light 'Mechs. Seven and a half tons of Kallon Light Shield A standard armor give the Talon excellent protection for its weight class, enough durability to weather return fire while withdrawing from unfavorable engagements.

The design sacrifices jump capability entirely, relying on raw speed for maneuverability. The absence of jump jets can leave the Talon vulnerable in rough terrain, but on open ground its combination of speed, reach, and staying power make it a formidable opponent for anything in its weight class.
BMTalon_TLN5Z.history:
The Talon first saw action shortly after its introduction in 2670 and quickly proved itself invaluable to light 'Mech companies across the Star League Defense Force. Its long-range firepower filled a critical gap that had long plagued light formations, which traditionally relied on speed and numbers rather than hitting power. By the late Star League era, the Talon was among the most ordered light BattleMechs in SLDF service.

The TLN-5W upgrade in 2760 initially saw distribution restricted to Royal units. The Amaris Civil War changed this, with the TLN-5V distributed widely among regular SLDF formations and the upgraded TLN-5W seeing frontline service for the first time. Following the Exodus, every Successor State sought to acquire Talons as fast as they could be manufactured. Commanders attempted to replicate the original SLDF lance tactic of deploying three Talons alongside a Mongoose for headhunting and supply disruption behind enemy lines, substituting a Spector to flush out enemy commanders when Mongooses were unavailable.

The harshness of the Succession Wars proved too great for the design's survival. Production at the Briden BattleMechs Unlimited facility on Errai never kept pace with losses during the First Succession War. When several tactical nuclear strikes destroyed the factory in 2815, the Talon's fate was sealed. The last operational example was stripped for parts around 2830 to keep a House Kurita light lance functional.

The Inner Sphere would not see another Talon for over two centuries. In 3056, Blackstone BattleMechs announced they had secured production rights and restarted manufacturing at their facility on Inarcs. Sent to the Clan occupation zone border, the reborn Talon first saw combat during the Jade Falcon invasion of Coventry, where reports of its performance were highly favorable. During the FedCom Civil War, elements of the Seventh Crucis Lancers damaged Blackstone's production lines on Inarcs in 3065, though they returned to full capacity by late 3066.

Following the Civil War, the Lyran Alliance opened the Talon for export, recognizing that most Lyran units preferred traditional heavier formations. The Federated Suns and mercenary units absorbed much of the demand, while ComStar, the Free Rasalhague Republic, and the Draconis Combine acquired lances for evaluation. A few of these combined-arms lances have been spotted along the Jade Falcon border, though no command has fielded Talons in the numbers the original SLDF once did. Blackstone continued developing new variants through the Jihad and into the Dark Age, keeping the venerable design relevant with successive technological improvements.
BMTalon_TLN5Z.deployment: Introduced around 3062, this variant pushes the Talon's long-range engagement concept further. Blackstone replaced the extra-light engine with a 245-rated light fusion engine, trading some top speed for improved survivability against torso penetration. The entire weapons payload was redesigned around a pair of arm-mounted extended-range large lasers, giving the variant dual long-range striking capability. Ferro-fibrous armor and an endo steel chassis recover weight for the new loadout, though the loss of a heat sink forces careful heat management when both lasers fire simultaneously. A C3 slave unit allows this variant to share targeting data within a lance network. Initially intended for exclusive Lyran Alliance sale, the variant proved unpopular with Lyran commands, and intense lobbying led Blackstone to export it to the Draconis Combine and Federated Suns.

BMTalon_TLN6W.deployment: This variant stands as a Jihad-era redesign entering production around 3076. BMTarantula_ZPH1.overview:
The success of the GOL-3M Goliath prompted Corean Enterprises to take another look at four-legged 'Mech designs in the early 3050s. Seeking to avoid the problems shown by the poorly regarded Scorpion, Corean's designers on Stewart settled on an entirely new purpose for the quad chassis, creating a light reconnaissance platform rather than attempting another assault or fire support design. Introduced in 3054, the Tarantula became the first four-legged BattleMech to mount jump jets, a distinction that set it apart from all previous quad designs.

Produced at Corean Enterprises' facility on Stewart for the Free Worlds League, the Tarantula would eventually prove its worth and help spark a broader renaissance in four-legged 'Mech development during the 3060s.
BMTarantula_ZPH1.capabilities:
Corean designers took advantage of the stability and maneuverability provided by a quad chassis to build an extremely agile recon 'Mech. Built on a Corean IX Standard chassis with a massive Nissan 200 XL engine, the Tarantula achieves a top speed approaching 130 km/h. Eight Rawlings 75 jump jets propel the 'Mech up to 240 meters, allowing it to navigate rough terrain with ease. The resulting design combines the squat, four-legged look of the Scorpion with the sleek lines of the Mercury, offering a noticeably comfortable ride with improved stability and handling that serve as key factors in winning pilots over to the unusual design.

The Tarantula's weapons complement is light but well suited to its role. A pair of Magna Mk II medium lasers mounted in pods on the upper surface provide most of its striking power, backed by a Hovertec Streak SRM-2 in the center torso for exploiting weak spots in enemy armor. Protected by four and a half tons of StarSlab/2 armor, the Tarantula carries roughly three-quarters of its theoretical maximum protection. While this leaves the design vulnerable to concentrated fire, its extraordinary speed makes it capable of avoiding most damage, and once a pilot grows accustomed to the different feel of a four-legged 'Mech, the Tarantula proves clearly superior to bipedal 'Mechs of similar specifications.
BMTarantula_ZPH1.history:
The Tarantula's early service was marked by deep resistance from the MechWarrior community. Quadrupedal designs carried a strong stigma among pilots, and the Tarantula initially had to be assigned on a voluntary basis. Corean Enterprises launched a comprehensive marketing campaign that included promotional holovids, battle footage with MechWarrior testimonials, and even donated machines to appropriate units. Despite these efforts, the Tarantula was far ahead of its time, and only the broader quad renaissance of the 3060s, which produced designs like the Sirocco and the Barghest, enabled it to find wider acceptance.

The turning point for the Tarantula came through an unlikely source. The wild exploits of the Seventeenth Recon Regiment in the Draconis Combine drew attention to the new ZPH-4A variant, pushing it to an unexpectedly large market: the Draconis Combine Mustered Soldiery. The DCMS High Command grudgingly accepted the Tarantula's potency and assigned machines to well-known units such as the Legion of Vega and the Proserpina Hussars. Corean Enterprises was happy to exploit the irony that an undisciplined mercenary group had created demand for the design within House Kurita's generally anti-mercenary military culture.

The Tarantula's production history reflects the turbulent politics of Stewart itself. The Corean Enterprises MacAdams-Suharno facility remained under Free Worlds League control through the Clan Invasion and Civil War eras, producing successive variants as demand grew. During the Jihad, the Word of Blake seized control of Stewart and its factories. Following the liberation, the Republic of the Sphere administered the world before it eventually declared independence during the Dark Age. By the ilClan era, Clan Wolf had claimed Stewart, though Tarantula production had largely ceased by then.

Perhaps the Tarantula's most significant legacy was unintentional. When Clan Cloud Cobra scientists acquired the remains of an Inner Sphere Tarantula, they used it as the basis for their own quad design, the Stalking Spider. This Clan reinterpretation of the Tarantula concept proved that the fundamental design philosophy behind Corean's four-legged scout was sound, even if it took a Clan engineering team to fully exploit its potential.
BMTarantula_ZPH1.deployment: The base ZPH-1 model represents the original Tarantula design as it entered production in 3054. Optimized purely for reconnaissance, its combination of extreme speed, exceptional jump capability, and energy-based primary weapons allows for extended operations without resupply. The quad chassis provides a remarkably stable firing platform even at high speeds, making the Tarantula effective at harassing heavier opponents while remaining difficult to pin down.

By the ilClan era, Clan Wolf had claimed Stewart, though Tarantula production had largely ceased by then.

Perhaps the Tarantula's most significant legacy was unintentional. When Clan Cloud Cobra scientists acquired the remains of an Inner Sphere Tarantula, they used it as the basis for their own quad design, the Stalking Spider. This Clan reinterpretation of the Tarantula concept proved that the fundamental design philosophy behind Corean's four-legged scout was sound, even if it took a Clan engineering team to fully exploit its potential.
BMTarantula_ZPH5A.deployment: A Dark Age era field refit based on the ZPH-4A, this variant replaces the extended-range PPC with an extended-range large laser and upgrades the C3 slave unit to a C3 boosted slave for improved networking range. The MASC system and armor protection of the 4A are retained, maintaining the fast sniper role while adapting to the networking requirements of Republic and post-Republic era combined-arms formations. As a field modification rather than a factory variant, the 5A has appeared across multiple successor states wherever Tarantulas and the necessary components are available.

BMTarge_TRG1N.overview:
The Targe was introduced in 3081 by Cosara Weaponries on Northwind, designed to fill a reconnaissance and cavalry role within the fledgling Republic Armed Forces. Named after the round shield carried by the Scottish Highlanders of ancient Terra, the forty-ton medium BattleMech was born from Cosara's ambition to move beyond their reputation for solid but unremarkable designs like the Crab and Black Watch.

The resulting design was hamstrung by compromises between speed, protection, and firepower, earning the Targe a lackluster reputation that limited sales largely to the Northwind Highlanders. Cosara would produce a few hundred units before reassigning its assembly lines to civilian production, though development of improved variants continued across the Republic era.
BMTarge_TRG1N.capabilities:
The Targe is built around a Pitban 320 Light fusion engine, providing a cruising speed of 86 kph and a top speed of 129 kph. When the MASC system is engaged, the 'Mech can briefly exceed 170 kph, making it one of the fastest medium designs in the Republic arsenal. Cosara selected the light engine over a more fragile extralight model to improve battlefield survivability, though this choice consumed nearly half the 'Mech's total tonnage. A small cockpit further saves weight at the expense of pilot comfort.

To maximize the limited weight remaining for protection, the design team selected Valiant Lamellor Special heavy ferro-fibrous armor, squeezing the most coverage possible from five tons of plating. Ten double heat sinks easily manage the modest heat output of the weapons array.

The armament reflects the compromises forced by the engine and MASC installation. A Shigunga MRM-10 launcher serves as the primary weapon, supplemented by three Diverse Optics extended-range small lasers. A single ton of missile ammunition provides adequate endurance for scouting engagements, protected by CASE in the event of a detonation. While underarmed for its weight class, the Targe relies on speed and hit-and-run tactics rather than sustained firepower exchanges.

BMTarge_TRG1N.history:
The Targe's development began in the aftermath of the Jihad when Northwind joined the Republic of the Sphere. Cosara Weaponries, eager to supply the new state's military and rehabilitate its reputation after Northwind's occupation by the Word of Blake, conducted an extensive analysis of Republic Armed Forces needs. The resulting design specifications were ambitious, calling for a medium 'Mech with burst speeds exceeding 160 kph and missile-based armament, but the compromises required to meet those specifications produced a design that satisfied the letter of the requirements while falling short of expectations.

Production commenced in 3081, but sales proved disappointing from the outset. The RAF procurement office, while acknowledging the design met its stated requirements, found the Targe's limited firepower insufficient for front-line service. The Northwind Highlanders became the primary operators, purchasing the bulk of Cosara's output more from institutional loyalty to their homeworld manufacturer than tactical enthusiasm. The Targe was found most frequently in Highlander formations, generally assigned to scouting and counter-reconnaissance duties where its exceptional speed could be leveraged. Pilots developed a strafing tactic, approaching targets at high speed, firing at close range, and engaging MASC to escape before opponents could effectively return fire.

Cosara attempted to revitalize interest with the TRG-2N in 3084, addressing the most common complaints about the design's armament. While the upgraded variant performed well in simulations and dry runs, concerns about ammunition placement near the MASC system dampened enthusiasm among potential buyers. The Quartermaster's Office initiated an investigation into the safety issue, further stalling procurement.

By the early thirty-second century, the Targe had been largely relegated to second-line duties and garrison postings. The TRG-3M, introduced in 3109, represented a significant redesign that embraced the extralight engine Cosara had originally rejected. While a more capable platform overall, the Targe's poor reputation and the Bad Reputation quirk that followed the chassis continued to hamper sales across the remaining Republic era and into the ilClan period, leaving the design a footnote in Cosara's otherwise respectable catalog.
BMTarge_TRG1N.deployment: The baseline Targe represents Cosara Weaponries' original vision for a fast medium scout and cavalry 'Mech. Armed with a Shigunga MRM-10 and three Diverse Optics extended-range small lasers, the design prioritizes speed over firepower, relying on MASC-assisted bursts to close with targets, deliver fire at short range, and disengage before opponents can respond effectively. Five tons of heavy ferro-fibrous armor with CASE provides reasonable protection for a design of its weight. The variant has found its greatest success among Northwind Highlander cavalry units, where its speed complements the formation's aggressive tactical doctrine.

BMTempest_C.overview: The Tempest is a sixty-five-ton heavy BattleMech designed by Irian BattleMechs Unlimited as a replacement for the aging Thunderbolt in Free Worlds League service. Originating in the late 3040s and relying on little advanced technology, the Clan Invasion and resulting research and development effort led to radical modifications, and the production model fielded in 3055 bore little resemblance to the initial concept. Irian BattleMechs Unlimited produces the Tempest at facilities on both Irian and Angell II, and the design has earned a reputation as a versatile and well-balanced heavy combatant that has proven difficult to improve upon. Combat operations have prompted the creation of several variants as both field modifications and factory-built options.
BMTempest_C.capabilities:
The Tempest's primary armament centers on a Zeus Slingshot Gauss rifle, delivering devastating long-range firepower without generating waste heat. A Sutel Precision Line large pulse laser supplements this at medium to long ranges, while three Diplan M3 medium lasers and an Irian Weapons Works 60mm SRM-6 rack provide punishing close-range firepower. The Gauss rifle carries two tons of ammunition for sixteen rounds of fire, and the SRM-6 has one ton of ammunition providing fifteen salvos.

The original design concept called for twin PPCs, but Irian designers replaced this configuration with the Gauss rifle and large pulse laser combination for the production model. Four Chilton 465 jump jets grant the Tempest a one hundred twenty meter jump capability, allowing it to keep pace with many lighter 'Mechs despite a mediocre cruising speed of forty-three kilometers per hour. Fine-tuning and testing on Irian's varied landscapes led the manufacturer to claim the Tempest operates across any terrain without loss of capability, an assertion the League military has tested on several occasions. Twelve tons of Maximillian 100 armor provide respectable protection for a sixty-five ton chassis, though the lack of CASE leaves the XL engine vulnerable to catastrophic ammunition explosions.
BMTempest_C.history:
The Tempest's origins trace to the late 3040s, when Irian BattleMechs Unlimited began developing a replacement for the venerable Thunderbolt in Free Worlds League service. The project initially used little advanced technology, but the shock of the Clan Invasion in 3049 prompted massive investment in research and development across the Inner Sphere. The Tempest design was radically overhauled to incorporate newly recovered Star League-era technologies, and the production TMP-3M that rolled off the Irian assembly line in 3055 was fundamentally different from the original prototype.

The Tempest's introduction immediately created friction within the Free Worlds League's defense industry. When Earthwerks attempted to market their updated TDR-9M Thunderbolt variant, Irian BattleMechs Unlimited lobbied the League Central Coordination and Command to halt new Thunderbolt production, arguing the Tempest rendered further Thunderbolt development unnecessary. The resulting corporate dispute was only resolved when the Word of Blake brokered a compromise, pitting the two designs against each other in a combat trial to determine which would supply the Blakist military.

Free Worlds military strategists embraced the Tempest, deploying it throughout the FWLM in formations that deliberately echoed Star League Defense Force doctrine. Lance- and company-sized Tempest units, often paired with the lighter Shadow Hawk, created flexible strike forces capable of rapid offensive and defensive operations. The largest concentrations served in the Marik Militias, Free Worlds Legions, and Fusiliers of Oriente. The design made its greatest impression in the Sirian Lancers, where its balance of firepower and agility proved vital during Operation Guerrero and the subsequent liberation of Sirius and Procyon.

The Jihad devastated the Tempest's production infrastructure. The Irian facility fell under Word of Blake control, and while production continued under Blakist oversight, many Free Worlds League units found themselves cut off from spare parts and replacement chassis. The establishment of the Angell II production line by Irian Technologies helped offset this loss, though the facility did not reach operational capacity until 3077. Following the Jihad, the Republic of the Sphere assumed control of both facilities, allegedly taking the Irian line offline during the 3090s, though production reportedly continued in secret.

The collapse of the Republic and the reformation of the Free Worlds League saw Irian BattleMechs Unlimited regain control of its production lines. Regarded as a difficult design to improve upon, it took until the 3130s for a formal successor variant to debut. New variants including the TMP-4M and the Clan Protectorate-backed Tempest C emerged during the Dark Age, demonstrating the design's continued relevance more than eight decades after its introduction.
BMTempest_C.deployment: Produced under the auspices of the Clan Protectorate, the Tempest C melds the proven Inner Sphere chassis and armor with a mix of Inner Sphere and Clan-specification weaponry. A Clan-grade large pulse laser and Gauss rifle replace their Inner Sphere counterparts in the arm mounts, while three standard medium lasers are retained. An ATM-9 launcher mounted in the left torso provides tactical flexibility through its variable ammunition types, though only two tons of ammunition somewhat limit this advantage. As with all previous Tempest designs, no CASE has been fitted, a persistent vulnerability that Clan warriors have noted with some disapproval.

BMTempest_TMP3MA.capabilities:
The Tempest's primary armament centers on a Zeus Slingshot Gauss rifle, delivering devastating long-range firepower without generating waste heat. A Sutel Precision Line large pulse laser supplements this at medium to long ranges, while three Diplan M3 medium lasers and an Irian Weapons Works 60mm SRM-6 rack provide punishing close-range firepower. The Gauss rifle carries two tons of ammunition for sixteen rounds of fire, and the SRM-6 has one ton of ammunition providing fifteen salvos.

The original design concept called for twin PPCs, but Irian designers replaced this configuration with the Gauss rifle and large pulse laser combination for the production model. Four Chilton 465 jump jets grant the Tempest a one hundred twenty meter jump capability, allowing it to keep pace with many lighter 'Mechs despite a mediocre cruising speed of forty-three kilometers per hour. Fine-tuning and testing on Irian's varied landscapes led the manufacturer to claim the Tempest operates across any terrain without loss of capability, an assertion the League military has tested on several occasions. Twelve tons of Maximillian 100 armor provide respectable protection for a sixty-five ton chassis, though the lack of CASE leaves the XL engine vulnerable to catastrophic ammunition explosions.

BMTemplarIII_TLR2O.overview:
The Templar III is a Dark Age era eighty-five ton assault OmniMech produced by General Motors for the Federated Suns. Introduced around 3100, it was designed as a direct replacement for the original Templar after the destruction of Kallon Industries' factory on Talon during the Jihad eliminated production of the first-generation design. General Motors established a new production line on New Valencia to continue the Templar legacy with updated technologies.

Like its predecessor, the Templar III serves primarily as a command 'Mech for AFFS assault formations. The design incorporates advanced equipment across its alternate configurations, giving field commanders significant tactical flexibility while maintaining the assault-weight presence that made the original Templar an effective formation anchor.
BMTemplarIII_TLR2O.capabilities:
The most significant change from the original Templar is the Templar III's adoption of a GM 340 Light engine in place of the KalTek 340 Extralight. This substantially improves survivability by eliminating the vulnerability to side torso destruction that plagued the original design, though it comes at the cost of reduced pod space, dropping from forty tons to twenty-nine. The Kallon Type XX Endo Steel chassis and StarGuard CIV armor maintain the same level of protection as the predecessor, and a Heavy-Duty Gyro improves stability under fire.

The primary configuration draws comparison to the proven WHM-8D Warhammer loadout, mounting twin ER PPCs as its primary armament alongside extended-range medium and small lasers. A four-tube short-range missile launcher provides supplementary close-range firepower, with CASE protecting the ammunition. A targeting computer links all energy weapons for improved accuracy, while four additional double heat sinks manage the considerable thermal output of the energy-heavy weapons suite.

While the reduced pod capacity limits the Templar III's ability to mount the heaviest weapon loadouts, the improved chassis durability ensures it can remain in the fight longer. Several configurations take advantage of advanced and Clan-specification technologies to maximize firepower within the tighter weight budget, making the Templar III a more resilient, if somewhat less versatile, successor to the original.
BMTemplarIII_TLR2O.history:
The Templar III's development grew directly from the ashes of the Jihad. With the Kallon Industries factory on Talon destroyed by the Word of Blake, the Federated Suns lost its only production source for the original Templar. General Motors on New Valencia, already producing the Pendragon, a limited-production design loosely based on the Templar chassis, leveraged their familiarity with the platform to develop a modernized successor. Production of the Templar III began around 3100, establishing New Valencia as the new center of Templar-lineage manufacturing.

The Templar III quickly became a popular command 'Mech for AFFS company and battalion commanders, appearing regularly in assault lances throughout Federated Suns frontline formations. During the Capellan invasion campaigns of the Dark Age, lances of Templar IIIs proved effective in combined arms operations. In one notable engagement on Spica in late 3144, a lance of three Templar IIIs and a Salamander inflicted significant casualties on a Capellan 'Mech company, using ER PPCs and targeting computers to devastating effect while channeling the enemy through minefields and narrow streets.

The Templar III's influence extended beyond the Federated Suns. When General Motors resumed Victor production in the 3080s, they redesigned that venerable assault 'Mech to share many components with the Templar III, creating manufacturing efficiencies on New Valencia. Additionally, the custom configuration piloted by the First Prince demonstrated the platform's ability to accept Clan-specification weaponry, producing a significantly more lethal variant that served through the critical campaigns of the late 3140s and into the ilClan era.
BMTemplarIII_TLR2O.deployment: The primary configuration draws heavily from the proven WHM-8D Warhammer weapons loadout, mounting twin ER PPCs as its main armament alongside extended-range medium and small lasers. A four-tube short-range missile launcher provides supplementary close-range firepower, with CASE protecting the ammunition store. All energy weapons are linked to a targeting computer for enhanced accuracy, and four additional double heat sinks manage the heavy thermal output.

BMTemplar_TLR1O.overview:
The Templar was the first unique Federated Suns OmniMech, an eighty-five ton assault design produced by Kallon Industries and introduced in 3062. Commissioned to address the Federated Suns' lack of an indigenous OmniMech design, the Templar was intended to replace aging designs like the Awesome and Victor in frontline units.

Built around proven off-the-shelf components to reduce costs and speed development, the design offered a generous forty tons of pod space for mission-specific configurations, establishing itself as a powerful and versatile command platform for AFFS assault formations. Though production was eventually disrupted, the Templar proved durable enough to remain in active service well beyond its original production run.
BMTemplar_TLR1O.capabilities:
The Templar is built on a lightweight Kallon Type XIX Endo Steel chassis and powered by a KalTek 340 Extralight engine, achieving a respectable top speed of sixty-four kilometers per hour for its weight class. Sixteen and a half tons of Starshield A armor provide excellent protection, while CASE in the right torso mitigates ammunition explosion risks. BMTemplar_TLR1OG.capabilities:
The Templar is built on a lightweight Kallon Type XIX Endo Steel chassis and powered by a KalTek 340 Extralight engine, achieving a respectable top speed of sixty-four kilometers per hour for its weight class. BMTemplar_TLR1OG.history:
The Templar's origins trace directly to the political tensions within the Federated Commonwealth following the Great Refusal in 3060. While both Archon-Prince Victor Steiner-Davion and his sister Archon Katrina dismissed calls for OmniMech development on economic grounds, Field Marshal Duke George Hasek of the Capellan March took matters into his own hands. Hasek directly commissioned Kallon Industries on Talon, a moon of Wernke, to develop the design, backing the project with his own considerable personal fortune. The resulting 'Mech entered production in 3062, just as the FedCom Civil War was erupting.

With House Hasek as the driving force behind its creation, the Templar's initial distribution was heavily weighted toward Capellan March formations. The first units off Kallon's production lines were routed to the Syrtis Fusiliers, with subsequent production runs reaching units such as the Federated Suns Armored Cavalry and the Davion Assault Guards. Throughout the Civil War, Hasek's loyalists ensured these powerful OmniMechs were directed exclusively to units opposing Archon Katrina, particularly excluding Loyalist commands from receiving any. The Twenty-Second Avalon Hussars received several during their defense of Talon, though this alone proved insufficient to secure victory.

The Word of Blake Jihad dealt a catastrophic blow to the Templar program when the Kallon Industries factory on Talon was vaporized, halting all production. The design's intended rise as a flagship AFFS assault 'Mech was set back by decades. General Motors, having obtained access to the Templar's design data through Operation MUSE RED, eventually established production on New Valencia, though they chose to develop a modernized successor rather than restart the original line.

During the Republic era, the Republic Institute of Strategic Combat developed the experimental ORISC configuration, fitting stored Templar chassis with RISC Repeating TSEMP weapons and other volatile experimental technology. The Republic of the Sphere and its wartime Exarch deployed these in false-flag operations under AFFS colors against the Capellan Confederation and Draconis Combine. When Julian Davion visited Terra in 3146, nearly all stored ORISC equipment packages were included in supplies provided to the AFFS, where they saw continued use until every piece of the experimental gear was destroyed through combat, wear, or self-detonation by the end of the 3140s.

Despite the loss of its original production line, surviving Templars remained in AFFS service throughout the Dark Age and into the ilClan era, valued for their durability, flexibility, and the Easy to Maintain quirk that kept aging chassis operational far beyond their expected service life. The Blessed Order's revived First Division also operated a modified configuration, the BLO variant, incorporating improved C3 networking to coordinate their reformed ComStar forces.
BMTemplar_TLR1OG.deployment: Alternate Configuration G appears designed for long-range direct fire support or anti-aircraft duties, mounting three LB 2-X autocannons alongside an ER PPC and Light Gauss Rifle. A C3 slave unit enables the sharing of targeting data with lancemates, enhancing the collective accuracy of the formation while the configuration provides sustained suppressive fire at extended ranges.

The first units off Kallon's production lines were routed to the Syrtis Fusiliers, with subsequent production runs reaching units such as the Federated Suns Armored Cavalry and the Davion Assault Guards. Throughout the Civil War, Hasek's loyalists ensured these powerful OmniMechs were directed exclusively to units opposing Archon Katrina, especially excluding Loyalist commands from receiving any. The Twenty-Second Avalon Hussars received several during their defense of Talon, though this alone proved insufficient to secure victory.

The Word of Blake Jihad dealt a catastrophic blow to the Templar program when the Kallon Industries factory on Talon was vaporized, halting all production. The design's intended rise as a flagship AFFS assault 'Mech was set back by decades. General Motors, having obtained access to the Templar's design data through Operation MUSE RED, eventually established production on New Valencia, though they chose to develop a modernized successor rather than restart the original line.

During the Republic era, the Republic Institute of Strategic Combat developed the experimental ORISC configuration, fitting stored Templar chassis with RISC Repeating TSEMP weapons and other volatile experimental technology. The Republic of the Sphere and its wartime Exarch deployed these in false-flag operations under AFFS colors against the Capellan Confederation and Draconis Combine. When Julian Davion visited Terra in 3146, nearly all stored ORISC equipment packages were included in supplies provided to the AFFS, where they saw continued use until every piece of the experimental gear was destroyed through combat, wear, or self-detonation by the end of the 3140s.

Despite the loss of its original production line, surviving Templars remained in AFFS service throughout the Dark Age and into the ilClan era, valued for their durability, flexibility, and the Easy to Maintain quirk that kept aging chassis operational far beyond their expected service life. The Blessed Order's revived First Division also operated a modified configuration, the BLO variant, incorporating improved C3 networking to coordinate their reformed ComStar forces.
BMTemplar_TLR1OU.deployment: Alternate Configuration U is specifically designed for underwater operations, equipped with four Underwater Maneuvering Units and a BattleMech HarJel System to prevent hull breaches. Offensive armament includes a large pulse laser, three medium pulse lasers, an SRT-6 and LRT-10 torpedo launcher for submerged combat. A C3 slave unit maintains coordination with friendly forces in the limited-visibility underwater environment.

BMTenshi_TN10O.overview: The Tenshi, whose name translates to "Angel" in Japanese, is a 95-ton assault OmniMech introduced in 3101 by Luthien Armor Works for the Draconis Combine Mustered Soldiery. Designed to be manufactured entirely from Combine-sourced technologies and materials, the Tenshi represented LAW's first foray into OmniMech production for the DCMS. Conceived during a period of covert rearmament following the Jihad, the design answered the Combine's need for a domestically produced assault-weight platform that did not rely on foreign supply chains. A common sight among the Dragon's assault formations, the Tenshi fills the heavy end of the weight spectrum with a flexible platform capable of adapting to multiple battlefield roles through its substantial modular pod system.
BMTenshi_TN10O.capabilities:
The Tenshi was Luthien Armor Works' first OmniMech platform to incorporate several advanced technologies that had entered production in the decades preceding the Jihad. Built on an Endo-Composite internal structure and powered by a Hermes 285 Light fusion engine, the design achieves a remarkable 48 tons of pod capacity, roughly half its total weight. This impressive payload comes at the cost of speed, with a maximum velocity of only 54 kilometers per hour, especially slower than many comparable assault designs of the era. A Compact Gyro saves additional internal volume, while 18.5 tons of Mitchell Argon Standard armor provides exceptional protection across all locations.

The Tenshi is somewhat labor-intensive to reconfigure due to its complex pod linkage system, making rapid battlefield swaps impractical during time-sensitive operations. This logistical burden is the design's most significant drawback, requiring dedicated technical teams and extended maintenance windows that can strain a formation's operational tempo during fast-moving campaigns.
BMTenshi_TN10O.history:
The Tenshi emerged from Luthien Armor Works as part of a deliberate and covert program to reconstitute the Draconis Combine's shattered military in the aftermath of the Jihad. While publicly adhering to Devlin Stone's disarmament agreements, the Combine quietly pursued new BattleMech projects that would achieve two purposes: manufacture designs using Combine-centric technologies, and rapidly rebuild its decimated 'Mech regiments. Older machines were cycled down to planetary militias to maintain the appearance of compliance while new hardware flowed to frontline units.

The DCMS initially assigned the first Tenshis to the Ghost Regiments, a deliberate choice rooted in both pragmatism and politics. The Ghost Regiments' lower profile within the DCMS meant that should the Tenshi prove a tactical failure, much as the Daboku had nearly a century earlier, the embarrassment would be contained within less prestigious formations. Ghost pilots, however, quickly embraced the new OmniMech and realized its battlefield potential.

In 3103, the Tenshi saw one of its earliest significant engagements when the First Ghost dropped two lances of the assault 'Mechs on the Ghost Bear Dominion world of Grumium. The raiding force struck directly at a weapons stockpile, blasting through a Striker Star before encountering heavier resistance from a Dominion Nova of the First Freemen Cluster. When the Bear commander refused a Trial of Possession, the Ghosts employed massed firepower to devastating effect, cutting down Clan 'Mechs while absorbing heavy return fire. Six of the eight Tenshis survived the engagement and returned to the Combine along with several hundred tons of captured Clan technology, a significant haul that validated the design's combat worthiness.

By the mid-thirty-second century, the Tenshi had become a common sight among the Dragon's frontline 'Mech regiments. At least one full assault company within the Sixteenth Galedon Regulars fielded the type exclusively, demonstrating growing production numbers and the DCMS' deepening confidence in the design. The Tenshi's combination of heavy armor, massive pod capacity, and the flexibility inherent to OmniMech technology ensured its continued prominence within Combine formations as tensions escalated across the Inner Sphere.
BMTenshi_TN10O.deployment: The Primary configuration establishes the Tenshi as a long-range fire support platform. Its arm-mounted Gauss rifle delivers punishing kinetic strikes at extreme distances, supported by a battery of five Light PPCs that can maintain withering suppressive fire. A Targeting Computer enhances the accuracy of all direct-fire weapons, while a Guardian ECM suite disrupts enemy targeting systems and missile locks. A Supercharger fitted in the center torso allows brief surges of speed for repositioning between engagements, and paired Rocket Launcher 10s in the legs provide a final close-range deterrent.

BMTenshi_TN10OR.deployment: The R configuration employs a mix of Inner Sphere and Clan technologies to create a long-range indirect fire support platform. Twin Extended Long-Range Missile 20 launchers backed by six tons of ammunition can saturate targets at extreme distances well beyond the reach of most conventional weapons. Five Clan-manufactured ER Medium Lasers provide accurate backup firepower at closer ranges, giving this variant some protection against units that manage to close the distance. This configuration transforms the Tenshi from a direct-combat assault 'Mech into a bombardment platform best employed behind friendly lines.

BMTessen_TSN1C.overview:
Named for the traditional Japanese war fan, the Tessen is a fifty-ton medium BattleMech originally conceived through a joint venture between the Draconis Combine Mustered Soldiery and ComStar's Com Guard. Begun in the early 3050s, the project was meant to create a fast, well-armored heavy scout capable of operating deep behind enemy lines. Philosophical and technological differences between the two partners led to the project's abandonment in 3055, and the design languished unfinished until ComStar revived it as a platform for their improved C3 computer system. Certified combat-ready in 3061, the Tessen entered full-scale production at Independence Weaponry on Quentin.

Despite its networking capabilities, the Tessen earned a reputation for being overspecialized, drawing criticism from analysts who questioned its suitability for independent scouting operations. The design has nonetheless served with distinction in formations that leverage its force-multiplying potential, from ComStar's Com Guards through the Republic Armed Forces era and beyond.
BMTessen_TSN1C.capabilities:
Built on a lightweight Endo Steel chassis and powered by a Vlar 300 XL engine, the Tessen achieves a top speed of 97 km/h, making it one of the faster medium 'Mechs in its weight class. Nine tons of Durallex ferro-fibrous armor provide respectable protection for a scout platform, while CASE protects against catastrophic ammunition explosions. The design's defining feature is its improved C3 computer, which allows the Tessen to share targeting data with up to five other C3i-equipped units, forming a powerful networked combat element.

The Tessen's armament reflects its role as a spotter and force multiplier rather than a standalone combatant. A Lord's Light extended-range PPC provides long-range striking power, while a single Diverse Optics medium pulse laser serves as backup for close engagements. The Series II Pragma improved Narc missile beacon allows the Tessen to designate targets for missile-equipped lancemates, and an integrated TAG laser designator enables it to call in Arrow IV artillery strikes. This sensor and targeting suite makes the Tessen lethal as part of a coordinated unit, though critics note the light weapons loadout and absence of jump jets leave it vulnerable when operating independently.
BMTessen_TSN1C.history:
The Tessen's origins reflect the brief period of cooperation between the Draconis Combine and ComStar following the Battle of Tukayyid in 3052. Inspired in part by the success of the Phoenix Hawk PXH-1bC's energy weapon and Narc beacon combination during that decisive engagement, engineers from both factions envisioned a purpose-built heavy scout that could leverage emerging network-centric warfare technologies. Work proceeded at Independence Weaponry on Quentin, but fundamental disagreements over technology compatibility, particularly regarding command-and-control systems, caused the project to collapse in 3055.

ComStar revived the design in the late 3050s when their technicians completed the improved C3 computer. Seeking a test platform for the new system, they returned to the unfinished Tessen, constructing six prototypes for extensive field trials. These trials took place on Tukayyid against a wide variety of simulated Clan opponents and tactics, and by June 3061 the design was certified combat-ready. Production began at Independence Weaponry, with the DCMS offered half the initial production run. The Combine declined, arguing that ComStar's C3 improved technology was incompatible with the standard C3 systems already deployed throughout their forces. This led directly to the development of the TSN-C3 variant fitted with a conventional C3 slave.

The Tessen's most notable early deployment came with ComStar's Eighty-third Division based on Bryant, known as the White Cyclones. This unit employed Tessens as scouts and harassers, using the 'Mech's networking capabilities to devastating effect against Blakist raiding parties, forcing the enemy to withdraw. The fall of Quentin to the Word of Blake during the Jihad disrupted production significantly, and the factory's eventual liberation saw it pass to Republic of the Sphere control.

The TSN-1Cr field refit, originally developed in 3069 using captured Blakist equipment, was later formalized as a production variant to replace the increasingly scarce C3i components. Independence Weaponry continued Tessen production through the Republic era and into the Dark Age, with the factory eventually returning to Draconis Combine ownership as the Republic contracted. The chassis also attracted the attention of Solaris VII arena stables, where custom variants appeared in gladiatorial combat by the 3130s.
BMTessen_TSN1C.deployment: The base production model carries the design's signature improved C3 computer alongside a Lord's Light extended-range PPC, Diverse Optics medium pulse laser, Series II Pragma improved Narc missile beacon, and TAG laser designator. This configuration epitomizes the Tessen's role as a networked spotter, trading standalone firepower for the ability to dramatically enhance the combat effectiveness of an entire C3i-connected lance. Nine tons of Durallex ferro-fibrous armor with CASE provide solid protection for a medium scout, though the absence of jump jets limits the 'Mech's tactical flexibility in broken terrain.

Independence Weaponry continued Tessen production through the Republic era and into the Dark Age, with the factory eventually returning to Draconis Combine ownership as the Republic contracted. The chassis also attracted the attention of Solaris VII arena stables, where custom variants appeared in gladiatorial combat by the 3130s.
BMTessen_TSNC3.deployment: Introduced in 3062, this variant was developed after the Draconis Combine declined the initial production run, citing the C3 improved technology's incompatibility with their existing C3 networks. The modification replaces the C3i computer with a conventional C3 slave unit, allowing the Tessen to integrate into standard Combine lance formations. The weight savings from this swap permitted the addition of a second medium pulse laser, giving the variant marginally improved close-range firepower while retaining the iNarc beacon and TAG designator for target marking duties.

BMTessen_TSNC3M.overview:
Named for the traditional Japanese war fan, the Tessen is a fifty-ton medium BattleMech originally conceived through a joint venture between the Draconis Combine Mustered Soldiery and ComStar's Com Guard. Begun in the early 3050s, the project was meant to create a fast, well-armored heavy scout capable of operating deep behind enemy lines. Philosophical and technological differences between the two partners led to the project's abandonment in 3055, and the design languished unfinished until ComStar revived it as a platform for their improved C3 computer system. Certified combat-ready in 3061, the Tessen entered full-scale production at Independence Weaponry on Quentin.

Despite its networking capabilities, the Tessen earned a reputation for being overspecialized, drawing criticism from analysts who questioned its suitability for independent scouting operations. The design has nonetheless served with distinction in formations that leverage its force-multiplying potential, from ComStar's Com Guards through the Republic Armed Forces era and beyond.
BMTessen_TSNC3M.capabilities:
Built on a lightweight Endo Steel chassis and powered by a Vlar 300 XL engine, the Tessen achieves a top speed of 97 km/h, making it one of the faster medium 'Mechs in its weight class. Nine tons of Durallex ferro-fibrous armor provide respectable protection for a scout platform, while CASE protects against catastrophic ammunition explosions. The design's defining feature is its improved C3 computer, which allows the Tessen to share targeting data with up to five other C3i-equipped units, forming a powerful networked combat element.

The Tessen's armament reflects its role as a spotter and force multiplier rather than a standalone combatant. A Lord's Light extended-range PPC provides long-range striking power, while a single Diverse Optics medium pulse laser serves as backup for close engagements. The Series II Pragma improved Narc missile beacon allows the Tessen to designate targets for missile-equipped lancemates, and an integrated TAG laser designator enables it to call in Arrow IV artillery strikes. This sensor and targeting suite makes the Tessen lethal as part of a coordinated unit, though critics note the light weapons loadout and absence of jump jets leave it vulnerable when operating independently.
BMTessen_TSNC3M.history:
The Tessen's origins reflect the brief period of cooperation between the Draconis Combine and ComStar following the Battle of Tukayyid in 3052. Inspired in part by the success of the Phoenix Hawk PXH-1bC's energy weapon and Narc beacon combination during that crucial engagement, engineers from both factions envisioned a purpose-built heavy scout that could leverage emerging network-centric warfare technologies. Work proceeded at Independence Weaponry on Quentin, but fundamental disagreements over technology compatibility, particularly regarding command-and-control systems, caused the project to collapse in 3055.

ComStar revived the design in the late 3050s when their technicians completed the improved C3 computer. Seeking a test platform for the new system, they returned to the unfinished Tessen, constructing six prototypes for extensive field trials. These trials took place on Tukayyid against a wide variety of simulated Clan opponents and tactics, and by June 3061 the design was certified combat-ready. Production began at Independence Weaponry, with the DCMS offered half the initial production run. The Combine declined, arguing that ComStar's C3 improved technology was incompatible with the standard C3 systems already deployed throughout their forces. This led directly to the development of the TSN-C3 variant fitted with a conventional C3 slave.

The Tessen's most notable early deployment came with ComStar's Eighty-third Division based on Bryant, known as the White Cyclones. This unit employed Tessens as scouts and harassers, using the 'Mech's networking capabilities to devastating effect against Blakist raiding parties, forcing the enemy to withdraw. The fall of Quentin to the Word of Blake during the Jihad disrupted production significantly, and the factory's eventual liberation saw it pass to Republic of the Sphere control.

Independence Weaponry continued Tessen production through the Republic era and into the Dark Age, with the factory eventually returning to Draconis Combine ownership as the Republic contracted. The chassis also attracted the attention of Solaris VII arena stables, where custom variants appeared in gladiatorial combat by the 3130s.
BMTessen_TSNC3M.deployment: Introduced in 3077 during the Jihad, this variant strips the medium pulse laser, iNarc launcher, and TAG system, replacing them with a C3 master computer that allows the Tessen to serve as a command node for an entire C3 network. A Snub-Nose PPC provides additional close-range punch alongside the retained ER PPC, and a small pulse laser serves as a last-ditch defensive weapon. The addition of a MASC system allows brief bursts of speed up to 120 km/h, transforming the Tessen from a dedicated spotter into a fast command platform capable of keeping pace with lighter elements while coordinating their fire.

BMThanatos_TNS4S.overview:
The Thanatos was developed by StarCorps Industries as a seventy-five ton OmniMech intended to emulate the Clan Summoner. After years of producing licensed OmniMechs from Luthien Armor Works on four worlds in the Federated Commonwealth and St. Ives Compact, StarCorps had gained sufficient expertise to design their own Omni-technology platforms by 3060. When neither the LAAF nor the AFFS expressed interest in another OmniMech design, citing high costs and the availability of existing models, StarCorps converted the Thanatos into a standard BattleMech. This pragmatic decision won contracts from both militaries beginning in 3061.

Produced at StarCorps facilities on Crofton and Loburg, the Thanatos filled the role of a heavy cavalry platform, offering a blend of speed, firepower, and electronic warfare capability that kept it in production through the Jihad, Dark Age, and into the ilClan era.
BMThanatos_TNS4S.capabilities:
Taking design cues from the Clan Thor, the Thanatos is built on a StarFrame Heavy Endo Steel chassis and powered by a PlasmaStar 375 Extra Light engine, giving it a top speed of 86 kph, fast for a heavy BattleMech. Five Audi-Fokker Mark IV jump jets provide an additional 150 meters of jumping capability. The internal components and electronics systems are heavily reinforced and stabilized, giving the chassis excellent resistance to rough terrain and combat impacts. Thirteen tons of Durallex Heavy armor provide solid protection for its weight class, though the extra-light engine remains a vulnerability if either side torso is breached.

The weapons array is weighted toward medium and short range engagements. A Defiance Model 6 extended-range large laser provides long-range reach, while a Shigunga MRM-20 launcher and two Defiance Model XII extended-range medium lasers deliver punishing firepower at closer ranges. A RAMTech 800P medium pulse laser adds accurate close-range fire. A Guardian ECM suite disrupts enemy electronics, while a C3 slave unit dramatically improves accuracy when operating as part of a networked lance.

systems.label: Communications

BMThanatos_TNS4S.history:
The Thanatos traces its origins to StarCorps Industries' experience producing licensed OmniMechs from Luthien Armor Works. By 3060, StarCorps was manufacturing Black Hawk KUs, Avatars, and Sunders across four worlds, building the institutional knowledge necessary to design their own Omni-technology platforms. The Thanatos emerged alongside the Manteuffel OmniVehicle as the first fruits of this initiative. When neither the LAAF nor the AFFS expressed interest in the OmniMech version, StarCorps converted it into a standard BattleMech, a decision that proved shrewd, winning contracts from both militaries that carried production from 3061 into the next decade.

The Thanatos found its niche in heavy cavalry formations, operating alongside similarly fast designs like the Argus, Barghest, Falconer, and Rakshasa. It displaced aging Quickdraws in units such as the First Federated Suns Armored Cavalry and the Alliance Jaegers. StarCorps also marketed the design to mercenary commands, with buyers ranging from the prestigious Eridani Light Horse to smaller outfits.

Production survived the Jihad at both the Crofton and Loburg facilities. The Jihad era produced the TNS-6T refit, which replaced the original's missile and laser loadout with a snub-nose PPC and multi-missile launcher. Both factories began producing the -6T as a standard model during the 3080s, with Loburg also offering the CASE II-equipped TNS-6S2 subvariant.

During the Dark Age, the Thanatos continued to serve the Armed Forces of the Federated Suns and the Lyran Commonwealth Armed Forces. In 3146, Republic Armed Forces technicians developed an upgraded variant using Clan-specification weapons during a stopover on Terra. These specifications were passed to StarCorps on Crofton, which began producing the TNS-7D for the AFFS, featuring an all-ClanTech weapons suite that dramatically improved the design's reach and accuracy. StarCorps subsequently offered the TNS-7D2 subvariant, trading electronic warfare capability for an Artemis V fire-control system.

Though some observers considered the Thanatos as never quite fulfilling the potential StarCorps originally envisioned, the design proved durable and adaptable enough to remain in continuous production for nearly a century, proof of the soundness of its underlying chassis and the flexibility of its weapon bays.
BMThanatos_TNS4S.deployment: The base TNS-4S mounts a Shigunga MRM-20 launcher, a Defiance Model 6 extended-range large laser, two Defiance Model XII extended-range medium lasers, and a RAMTech 800P medium pulse laser, providing a weapons suite that excels at medium and short range. A Guardian ECM suite and C3 slave unit offer electronic warfare capability and networked fire coordination. Introduced in 3061, this variant was produced at StarCorps facilities on both Crofton and Loburg, serving primarily with the LAAF and AFFS.

BMThorII_A.overview: The Grand Summoner is a seventy-ton Clan OmniMech introduced in 3093 by Clan Jade Falcon as a direct replacement for the venerable Summoner. Produced by the Eagle Craft Group at their facility on Erewhon, the Grand Summoner was designed to address the aging Summoner's limitations while preserving the proven mobility and firepower balance that had made its predecessor a mainstay of Clan heavy cavalry formations for over two centuries. The design quickly spread beyond its Jade Falcon origins through inter-Clan trade, finding particular favor among the Inner Sphere Clans' warrior castes. Known to Inner Sphere intelligence services by the reporting name Thor II, the Grand Summoner has established itself as a reliable and versatile frontline OmniMech favored by junior grade officers for independent operations.
BMThorII_A.capabilities:
The Grand Summoner retains the same Magna 350 XL engine as its predecessor, maintaining the same top speed of eighty-six kilometers per hour that made the original Summoner effective in fast-moving engagements. The critical improvement lies in the adoption of an Olivetti T4 Endo Steel internal structure combined with the conversion of the Summoner's fixed jump jets to pod-mounted equipment, freeing thirty and a half tons of pod space compared to the original's twenty-two and a half. Compound Beta ferro-fibrous armor provides marginally better protection than the original Summoner, adding half a ton of additional coverage across the design.

The Grand Summoner's Model J-D 067 communications system is a standout feature that has elevated the design beyond a simple heavy cavalry platform. Capable of supporting three times the number of simultaneous connections compared to competing systems such as the Alpha-com, the 067 can also cut through standard ECM interference when operating at maximum power, making the Grand Summoner a natural command platform despite not being originally intended for that role. The Hawkeye 58 targeting and tracking system, while highly accurate, requires recalibration whenever the OmniMech's pod configuration is changed, briefly leaving the 'Mech unable to employ its weapons during the process.
BMThorII_A.history:
The Grand Summoner emerged from Clan Jade Falcon's recognition that the Summoner, while still serviceable, was showing its age after more than two centuries of continuous production. The Eagle Craft Group's Erewhon facility began production in 3093, and the Jade Falcons treated the new design as a symbol of Clan pride from its very first chassis. The inaugural Grand Summoner, bearing serial number JF000-01A, was mounted on a ceremonial dais at the Erewhon factory complex gate rather than being deployed to a frontline unit. Each year, the Jade Falcon Khan selects one Cluster to be honored for distinguished service, and JF000-01A is repainted in that Cluster's parade colors. The Third Falcon Talon Cluster holds the distinction of being selected five times, more than any other formation.

The design's proliferation beyond Clan Jade Falcon came through the inter-Clan trade networks that characterized the post-Jihad era. Other Inner Sphere Clans readily adopted the Grand Summoner, recognizing its advantages over the original Summoner design. Though the largest concentrations of Grand Summoners remained within the Jade Falcon touman, the design became a common sight in the formations of allied and rival Clans alike.

One of the Grand Summoner's most celebrated engagements occurred on Feltre in 3097, when Clan Wolf Star Colonel Jess Calvert challenged Clan Diamond Shark's Swimmer Khanate to a Trial of Possession for the entire Beta Aimag. Aggressive bidding reduced each side's forces to a single Cluster. The Diamond Sharks selected the Swordtooth Canyons as the trial grounds, a labyrinth of ravines, dead ends, and heavy electromagnetic interference that degraded communications and tracking systems. The fighting quickly devolved into small-unit actions where the Grand Summoner's superior communications suite proved decisive, allowing Diamond Shark Stars to maintain coordination while Wolf forces struggled with disrupted signals. The Diamond Sharks' victory in this trial cemented the Grand Summoner's reputation as a design that could turn difficult terrain from a liability into an advantage.
BMThorII_A.deployment: Alternate Configuration A mirrors the original Summoner's Prime configuration in concept, pairing direct-fire weapons with missile support. An ER PPC and LB 10-X autocannon occupy the right and left arms respectively, providing flexible engagement options at range with the autocannon's ability to switch between solid and cluster munitions. Twin LRM launchers in the side torsos, an LRM-15 and an LRM-5, deliver sustained indirect fire support. Five jump jets round out the configuration, making it well-suited for MechWarriors who prefer the traditional Summoner combat doctrine of mobile fire support with jump-assisted positioning.

BMThor_A.overview:
The Summoner, designated Thor by Inner Sphere forces, is a 70-ton Clan OmniMech introduced in 2872 by Clan Jade Falcon. The design emerged shortly after the Jade Falcons became the first Clan to win OmniMech technology from Clan Coyote in 2863, making the Summoner one of the earliest second-generation OmniMechs ever produced. Jade Falcon engineers combined technology derived from the Coyote Warlock OmniMech with captured Thresher BattleMech chassis to create a versatile heavy platform capable of filling multiple battlefield roles.

Produced primarily by the Eagle Craft Group and other Clan manufacturers, the Summoner became a signature design of the Jade Falcon touman and one of the most widely recognized Clan OmniMechs in the Inner Sphere. Its combination of speed, firepower, and jump capability has kept it in continuous production for nearly three centuries, earning it the distinction of being one of the longest-serving OmniMechs in existence.
BMThor_A.capabilities:
The Summoner achieves its remarkable versatility through a balanced combination of speed, firepower, and protection. Powered by a Redline 350 XL engine, the seventy-ton chassis reaches speeds of just over eighty-six kilometers per hour, while five permanently mounted JF Standard jump jets provide a jump capability of one hundred and fifty meters. This combination of ground speed and jump capability gives the Summoner mobility that rivals many medium OmniMechs, allowing it to dictate engagement ranges and exploit terrain to an unusual degree for a heavy design.

Nine and a half tons of J63-3E Ferro Fibrous armor provide respectable protection for the chassis weight, though the design sacrifices maximum armor coverage to preserve its generous twenty-two and a half tons of pod space. In its Primary configuration, the Summoner carries an ER PPC in the right arm for devastating long-range strikes, an LB 10-X Autocannon in the left arm for flexible direct fire, and an LRM-15 in the left torso for indirect fire support. This combination of energy, ballistic, and missile weaponry allows a single Summoner to engage effectively across all range brackets.

The fixed jump jets represent both a strength and a design constraint. While they ensure every configuration benefits from superior tactical mobility, they consume tonnage and critical space that cannot be reallocated, limiting the pod space available compared to competing heavy OmniMechs that mount jump jets as pod equipment. This trade-off has proven acceptable in practice, as the Summoner's consistent mobility across all configurations remains one of its defining tactical advantages.
BMThor_A.history:
The Summoner's history is inextricably linked to the rise of Clan Jade Falcon as a military power. When the Jade Falcons won OmniMech technology from Clan Coyote in 2863, they moved quickly to develop their own designs. The Summoner was among the first results, entering production at Eagle Craft Group facilities on Ironhold and rapidly becoming the backbone of Falcon heavy OmniMech forces. St. Louis MechWorks on Niles, operating under Clan Hell's Horses control, established a parallel production line that ensured the design's availability beyond Falcon territory. Kindraa Kline of Clan Fire Mandrill also maintained limited production at their facility on Dagda, though in far smaller numbers.

During Operation REVIVAL, the Summoner was three times as common in Jade Falcon units as in any other Clan's forces, and it was during this campaign that Victor Steiner-Davion assigned the reporting name Thor after his personal encounter with the design on Trellwan. The name proved fitting, the combination of a PPC's lightning and an autocannon's thunder made an indelible impression on Inner Sphere commanders. A Clan Coyote adage born of the Invasion warned that encountering a Falcon outside a Summoner, Hellbringer, or Kit Fox warranted doubling one's caution, sign of how thoroughly the design defined Jade Falcon tactical doctrine.

The Wars of Reaving reshaped the Summoner's production sphere dramatically. The Ghost Bear facility on Bearclaw, which had produced Summoners since the design's early years, passed to Clan Snow Raven and later to Clan Stone Lion as alliances and absorptions shifted Clan territories. The Fire Mandrill facility on Dagda fell under Clan Goliath Scorpion and then Clan Star Adder control. Meanwhile, the Jade Falcon factory on Vantaa was destroyed when the planet was rendered uninhabitable during fighting between the Hell's Horses and Ice Hellions in 3072.

In the Inner Sphere occupation zones, the Jade Falcons expanded Summoner production through Eagle Craft Group operations on Erewhon and mobile factory assets, while Olivetti Weaponry on Sudeten briefly hosted a production line during the Jihad era. The Hell's Horses, having long maintained production on Niles through St. Louis MechWorks, added a new line at Svarstaad Industriplex Gamma after capturing that world. This proved prescient, as the Jade Falcons increasingly shifted their heavy OmniMech production to the Grand Summoner during the Dark Age, leaving the Hell's Horses as the primary champions of the original design.

By 3150, the Summoner had served continuously for nearly three centuries, an almost unmatched record for any OmniMech. Clan Hell's Horses embraced the design for both training and front-line service, introducing new configurations that incorporated modern weapons technology while retaining the chassis's proven mobility and reliability. The Hell's Horses' continued investment ensured that the Summoner remained a relevant battlefield presence well into the ilClan era, even as newer designs increasingly dominated the rosters of other Clans.
BMThor_A.deployment: Alternate Configuration A shifts the Summoner toward a more focused engagement profile. A Gauss rifle serves as the primary weapon, delivering devastating long-range kinetic strikes without generating waste heat. A Large Pulse Laser provides accurate intermediate-range firepower, while an SRM-6 launcher adds close-range punch for finishing engagements. This configuration trades the Prime's versatility for superior damage projection at range, making it particularly effective in open terrain where the Gauss rifle's reach can be fully exploited.
