BMTiTsang_TSG9J.deployment: Introduced around 3060, this variant addresses the base Ti Ts'ang's most significant tactical limitation: an inability to engage targets beyond medium range. An extended-range medium laser from each torso, two extended-range small lasers from the left arm, the TAG designator, and one double heat sink are removed to make room for an extended-range large laser mounted in the center torso. While the reduced laser array generates less waste heat, potentially delaying triple-strength myomer activation, the ability to threaten opponents at long range gives pilots greater flexibility in choosing when and how to close for melee combat.

BMTianZong_TNZN1.overview:
The Tian-Zong was introduced in 3090 as a dedicated command BattleMech for the Capellan Confederation Armed Forces. Developed by Hellespont 'Mech Works on Sian in cooperation with the Capellan Science Foundation, the design was originally intended as a mobile fire support platform for the Confederation's shadow lances. Combining potent Gauss-based firepower with sophisticated stealth technology and an advanced command and control suite, the Tian-Zong quickly exceeded its intended role. Its exceptional electronics allow battalion-level coordination while its stealthy profile makes it difficult to engage at range, earning it a reputation as one of the most dangerous heavy command 'Mechs in the Inner Sphere.

The design became the preferred mount of elite formations including the Death Commandos and Warrior Houses, serving as the Capellan Confederation's premier command 'Mech for over half a century. Ongoing production at Hellespont 'Mech Works has ensured a steady supply of upgraded variants incorporating the latest advances in Capellan military science.
BMTianZong_TNZN1.capabilities:
The Tian-Zong's combination of stealth armor, electronic warfare capabilities, and devastating firepower makes it a formidable opponent at any range. Its Hellespont Lite II stealth armor works in concert with an Angel ECM suite, rendering the 'Mech extremely difficult to detect and target. This is a critical advantage for a design meant to operate on the flanks and behind enemy lines with shadow lances. The paired Mydron Concussor Gauss rifles deliver crushing long-range firepower without generating appreciable heat, while the Ceres Arms Striker light particle projection cannons provide accurate medium-range support. This weapons mix allows sustained engagement without taxing the 'Mech's heat management systems, leaving its pilot free to concentrate on battlefield coordination.

The Rawlings 300 XL engine propels the seventy-five-ton chassis to a respectable top speed of 64 kph, adequate for keeping pace with medium 'Mech formations. The endo-composite internal structure saves weight allocated to the heavy armor protection and weapons payload. However, the design's reliance on an extralight engine creates vulnerability in the side torsos, and its lack of jump jets limits tactical flexibility in close terrain. The small cockpit fitted to later production variants also increases pilot fatigue during prolonged engagements.
BMTianZong_TNZN1.history:
The Tian-Zong entered production in 3090 at Hellespont 'Mech Works on Sian, quickly earning its place as the Capellan Confederation's foremost command 'Mech. Originally conceived for shadow lance operations, its combination of stealth, firepower, and command electronics made it irresistible to elite formations. The Death Commandos and Warrior Houses adopted the design almost immediately, and within a decade the Tian-Zong had become synonymous with Capellan heavy command assets.

During the siege of Victoria by Armed Forces of the Federated Suns, Warrior House Kamata demonstrated the Tian-Zong's devastating potential. Using stolen encryption keys, a force comprised principally of Tian-Zongs slipped behind enemy lines during a unit rotation between battered elements of the Sixth Syrtis Fusiliers and the reconstituted Forty-second Avalon Hussars. The Warrior House maneuvered two companies of shadow lances into a gap in the Davion lines, catching the AFFS regiments mid-rotation. Their combined volley felled a full company of 'Mechs, while a second volley disabled or destroyed another dozen. Both regiments broke and ran before regrouping for a counterattack, by which time the Warrior House had withdrawn behind cover.

On Arboris, elements of the First McCarron's Armored Cavalry used the Tian-Zong to delay a company of Hastati Sentinels. Commanding a single shadow lance and a platoon of light tanks, a Capellan officer used convenient weather and varying engagement ranges to repeatedly ambush the Sentinels' patrols, throwing them off-guard each time. This resourceful use of the Tian-Zong's stealth and command capabilities tied down a significantly larger force for weeks until additional Capellan troops arrived.

During Operation Tiamat in 3149, the Fifth McCarron's Armored Cavalry teamed with Warrior House Imarra to capture Liberty. On the island of Dendez, Tian-Zong pilots of the Fifth MAC held defensive positions against a Republic Armed Forces unit identified as Stone's Fury. Despite being surprised by advanced RISC weaponry, the Tian-Zong's firepower proved decisive in several engagements, with Silver Bullet Gauss rifle shards piercing enemy cockpits at close range.

By the ilClan era, Hellespont 'Mech Works had introduced a new generation of Tian-Zong variants leveraging the Capellan Confederation's success in replicating the Star League-era Chameleon light polarization shield. These newer models traded stealth armor for lighter protection combined with the Chameleon system, freeing weight for heavier weaponry and, in some variants, jump capability. The acquisition of Clan-grade weapons through trade with the Skate Khanate further expanded the Tian-Zong's tactical versatility, ensuring the design's continued relevance on the battlefields of the thirty-second century.
BMTianZong_TNZN1.deployment: The original Tian-Zong introduced in 3090, this variant established the design's reputation as a lethal shadow lance command platform. Armed with paired Mydron Concussor Gauss rifles and two extended-range medium lasers, it carries an additional ton of Gauss ammunition and two extra double heat sinks compared to later production models. The standard cockpit provides better pilot comfort for extended operations, though this came at the cost of internal volume that later variants would reclaim with a small cockpit. The combination of heavy Gauss firepower and energy weapons backed by stealth armor and an Angel ECM suite made the design instantly popular with Capellan elite formations.

Replacing the standard Gauss rifles with a pair of light Gauss rifles and swapping the energy weapons for extended-range large lasers, it trades raw hitting power for a more versatile engagement envelope. The lighter Gauss weapons reduce the severity of ammunition explosions while still delivering accurate long-range fire, and the extended-range large lasers provide sustained energy firepower without ammunition dependency. Like the original, it retains the standard cockpit and stealth armor suite.

These light PPCs provide greater damage output at medium range than their laser predecessors, though the reduced Gauss ammunition supply of three tons demands more disciplined fire. The small cockpit is considered an acceptable trade-off for a command 'Mech expected to operate behind the main battle line.

BMTiburon.overview: The Tiburon is a 35-ton Clan light BattleMech produced by Trellshire Heavy Industries on Twycross for Clan Sea Fox. Named for a large Terran shark found in the Caribbean, the design evokes the Clan's predatory heritage dating back to their Diamond Shark identity. First entering service in 3099, the Tiburon was developed during a period when the Clan was transforming from a decimated, centralized military power into a nomadic, spacefaring society of warrior-merchants. Unlike most Sea Fox military hardware, the Tiburon was not offered for sale to other factions, remaining exclusively in the hands of Sea Fox warriors. Fast and well-armed for its weight class, the design fills both scout and attack roles within Sea Fox light Stars across the Khanates.
BMTiburon.capabilities:
The Tiburon packs considerable firepower into a compact frame. Four Series 6b extended-range medium lasers provide its primary striking power, split between both arms, while a pair of Series 6c extended-range small lasers and two Pattern Alpha SRM-2 launchers offer additional close-range punch. All lasers are linked to the Multi-Spread 9 targeting computer, significantly improving accuracy and making the Tiburon a dangerous opponent in any engagement. In keeping with Clan Sea Fox's mercantile tendencies, most of the Tiburon's weapons are concealed behind retractable panels, giving the design a deceptively nonaggressive appearance until the moment of engagement.

A Watchdog CEWS integrated with the Able-Seven Sensor Suite gives the Tiburon powerful electronic warfare capabilities, disrupting enemy targeting and communications while extending the pilot's detection range. Built on an NCIA Type N endo steel frame and powered by a Standard 245 XL engine, the Tiburon reaches speeds near 120 km/h, outrunning most BattleMechs it encounters. Alpha Compound ferro-fibrous armor provides solid protection for a light design, and a CASE II system ensures that an ammunition explosion from the SRM reloads will not destroy the BattleMech outright. The design trades jump capability for raw speed and firepower, leaving it vulnerable if terrain prevents it from using its mobility advantage.
BMTiburon.history:
The Tiburon emerged from Clan Sea Fox's transformation during the early thirty-second century. As the Clan abandoned fixed territorial holdings in favor of a nomadic, trade-based existence among the stars, new military hardware was needed to reflect this shift in doctrine. The former Diamond Sharks, recently renamed Clan Sea Fox, commissioned Trellshire Heavy Industries on Twycross to develop a fast, lethal BattleMech suited for the hit-and-run engagements that would characterize their new way of life.

The Twycross facility had a long and turbulent history before the Tiburon entered production. Originally a Lyran Commonwealth factory producing Stalkers, BattleMasters, and Riflemen, the plant passed through the hands of the Federated Commonwealth, Clan Steel Viper, and Clan Jade Falcon before the Diamond Sharks secured control during the Civil War era. The factory suffered significant damage during the Bloody Tricentennial attacks of late 3080, but the Clan invested heavily in rebuilding the facility. By the time production began in 3099, the refurbished plant had become a key asset in the Clan's military-industrial portfolio.

The Tiburon's exclusivity to Sea Fox warriors was unusual for a Clan that made its fortune selling military goods to any willing buyer. This policy reflected the Clan's desire to maintain a technological edge over its trading partners and potential adversaries. In an era when most Sea Fox military encounters involved Trials of Possession with other Clans seeking to take goods by force rather than commerce, the Tiburon's combination of speed, electronic warfare capability, and concentrated firepower proved invaluable. The design saw widespread deployment across all five Khanates, becoming a staple of light formations. By the ilClan era, the Alyina Mercantile League had assumed oversight of the Twycross production line, continuing to supply Sea Fox forces with this exclusive design.
BMTiburon.deployment:
The Tiburon is common in Sea Fox light Stars, appearing among warrior-merchants across all five Khanates. The retractable weapon panels only deploy when the pilot commits to engagement, allowing the Tiburon to move through populated areas and trade corridors without provoking alarm. This feature proves particularly valuable in the Clan's mercantile operations, where warrior-merchants often conduct business in potentially hostile environments.

In September 3135, Epsilon Aimag deployed Tiburons during operations against pirates threatening the Spina Khanate's assets between the Rim Commonality and the Regulan Fiefs. OvKhan Gar Labov moved his Aimag to the Kogl system under cover of a trade mission, using merchant contacts and the Watch to locate a pirate base in the Duchy of Tamarind-Abbey. Labov led two Sea Fox Clusters to the base, sending his heavier forces against the pirate defenders while personally leading lighter, faster BattleMechs around the defenders' flank. The survivors and the base surrendered, and evidence recovered implicated senior Kogl government officials in the piracy, allowing Epsilon Aimag to negotiate favorable trading concessions.

BMTitanII_TI2P.overview:
The Titan II is a hundred-ton assault BattleMech produced by Kressly WarWorks on Epsilon Eridani for the Word of Blake's Protectorate Militia. First identified by the Successor States in 3071, the Titan II is a more faithful modernization of the original Star League-era Titan prototype than the heavily modified Grand Titan that preceded it. Where Vining Engineering and Salvage Team had used the recovered Titan specifications as a jumping-off point for an entirely new design, Kressly's engineers hewed much closer to the original concept.

Although it shares a lineage with the Vining-designed Grand Titan, the Titan II is emphatically not that 'Mech. Built using standard construction technologies throughout (a standard engine, standard internal structure, and conventional armor) the Titan II eschews the weight-saving but fragile technologies favored by many modern designs. This approach reflects its intended role as a garrison 'Mech for the Protectorate Militia, where reliability and ease of production take precedence over cutting-edge performance.
BMTitanII_TI2P.capabilities:
The Titan II retains the same Vlar 300 standard fusion engine and nineteen tons of Kressly Stoneskin 50 armor as its Star League-era ancestor, maintaining the original's philosophy of rugged survivability over speed. At fifty-four kilometers per hour, the Titan II relies on its heavy armor and firepower to dominate engagements rather than maneuver around opponents. The Kressly TIA-Infused chassis provides a solid foundation without resorting to expensive endo steel construction.

The weapons loadout modernizes the Titan concept with contemporary systems. A Blankenburg "Divine Wrath" Heavy PPC serves as the primary long-range weapon, backed by four Diplan M3-XR extended-range medium lasers that provide effective firepower at intermediate distances. A ZT Triple Fire Streak SRM-6 and twin Helga Series nine-tube multi-missile launchers handle close-range work, with the Streak system ensuring that every missile fired finds its target. Eighteen double heat sinks generally keep the Titan II operating within acceptable thermal limits. Particularly absent from the design are the advanced C3 computer networks and other sophisticated electronics that characterize most Word of Blake military hardware, a deliberate omission that suggests the Protectorate is reserving its best technology for more elite formations.
BMTitanII_TI2P.history:
The Titan II's genesis lies in the Word of Blake's expansion of its Protectorate Militia during the early 3070s. As the Blakists consolidated control over their occupied worlds, they required large numbers of garrison 'Mechs that could be produced quickly and maintained by less experienced technicians. Kressly WarWorks on Epsilon Eridani, by then operating under Word of Blake authority, was directed to resurrect the original Titan specifications and produce an updated version suited to garrison duty.

The Titan II appeared on the battlefield in 3071, deployed primarily to Protectorate Militia forces garrisoning the worlds around Terra. While individual Titan IIs were occasionally spotted among Word of Blake Militia forces engaging coalition troops across the Inner Sphere, none were ever confirmed in service with the elite Manei Domini Shadow Divisions. This exclusion from the Word's most capable formations reinforced assessments that the Titan II was built for the Protectorate's second-line forces, with the Word's Precentor Martial restricting the best equipment for more devoted commands.

Following the fall of the Word of Blake, Kressly WarWorks continued production of the Titan II under new ownership. The factory on Epsilon Eridani transitioned through Republic of the Sphere control and continued manufacturing the design through the Dark Age, with the Titan II finding new buyers among the successor states that emerged from the Republic's fragmentation.
BMTitanII_TI2P.deployment: The base TI-2P is the standard production model designed for Protectorate Militia garrison duty. Its combination of a Heavy PPC, extended-range medium lasers, multi-missile launchers, and a Streak SRM-6 provides effective firepower at all engagement ranges, while the heavily armored standard-engine design allows it to absorb significant punishment before being forced from the field. The deliberate exclusion of advanced electronics and weight-saving technologies keeps production costs manageable and simplifies maintenance for garrison technicians.

BMTitanII_TI2PA.overview:
The Titan II is a hundred-ton assault BattleMech produced by Kressly WarWorks on Epsilon Eridani for the Word of Blake's Protectorate Militia. First identified by the Successor States in 3071, the Titan II serves as a more faithful modernization of the original Star League-era Titan prototype than the heavily modified Grand Titan that preceded it. Where Vining Engineering and Salvage Team had used the recovered Titan specifications as a jumping-off point for an entirely new design, Kressly's engineers hewed much closer to the original concept.

Although it shares a lineage with the Vining-designed Grand Titan, the Titan II is emphatically not that 'Mech. Built using standard construction technologies throughout (a standard engine, standard internal structure, and conventional armor) the Titan II eschews the weight-saving but fragile technologies favored by many modern designs. This approach reflects its intended role as a garrison 'Mech for the Protectorate Militia, where reliability and ease of production take precedence over cutting-edge performance.
BMTitanII_TI2PA.capabilities:
The Titan II retains the same Vlar 300 standard fusion engine and nineteen tons of Kressly Stoneskin 50 armor as its Star League-era ancestor, maintaining the original's philosophy of rugged survivability over speed. At fifty-four kilometers per hour, the Titan II relies on its heavy armor and firepower to dominate engagements rather than maneuver around opponents. The Kressly TIA-Infused chassis provides a solid foundation without resorting to expensive endo steel construction.

The weapons loadout modernizes the Titan concept with contemporary systems. A Blankenburg "Divine Wrath" Heavy PPC serves as the primary long-range weapon, backed by four Diplan M3-XR extended-range medium lasers that provide effective firepower at intermediate distances. A ZT Triple Fire Streak SRM-6 and twin Helga Series nine-tube multi-missile launchers handle close-range work, with the Streak system ensuring that every missile fired finds its target. Eighteen double heat sinks generally keep the Titan II operating within acceptable thermal limits. Especially absent from the design are the advanced C3 computer networks and other sophisticated electronics that characterize most Word of Blake military hardware, a deliberate omission that suggests the Protectorate is reserving its best technology for more elite formations.
BMTitanII_TI2PA.history:
The Titan II's genesis lies in the Word of Blake's expansion of its Protectorate Militia during the early 3070s. As the Blakists consolidated control over their occupied worlds, they required large numbers of garrison 'Mechs that could be produced quickly and maintained by less experienced technicians. Kressly WarWorks on Epsilon Eridani, by then operating under Word of Blake authority, was directed to resurrect the original Titan specifications and produce an updated version suited to garrison duty.

The Titan II appeared on the battlefield in 3071, deployed primarily to Protectorate Militia forces garrisoning the worlds around Terra. While individual Titan IIs were occasionally spotted among Word of Blake Militia forces engaging coalition troops across the Inner Sphere, none were ever confirmed in service with the elite Manei Domini Shadow Divisions. This exclusion from the Word's most capable formations reinforced assessments that the Titan II was built for the Protectorate's second-line forces, with the Word's Precentor Martial restricting the best equipment for more devoted commands.

Following the fall of the Word of Blake, Kressly WarWorks continued production of the Titan II under new ownership. The factory on Epsilon Eridani transitioned through Republic of the Sphere control and continued manufacturing the design through the Dark Age, with the Titan II finding new buyers among the successor states that emerged from the Republic's fragmentation.
BMTitanII_TI2PA.deployment: This variant is an anti-insurgent and urban combat configuration developed for internal security operations within the Protectorate. The Heavy PPC and missile systems are replaced with a pair of plasma rifles capable of suppressing both 'Mechs and infantry, four standard medium lasers, and two four-gun machine gun arrays mounted in machine gun arrays for devastating anti-personnel firepower. The addition of a Beagle active probe allows this variant to detect hidden vehicles and 'Mechs in urban environments, while the Streak SRM-6 is retained for heavier targets.

BMTitan_TI1A.overview:
The Titan is a hundred-ton assault BattleMech prototype originally designed for the Star League Defense Force in 2765, intended to serve as a devastating close-range brawler. Developed by Blankenburg Technologies on Terra, the design never advanced beyond prototype testing before the upheaval of the Amaris Civil War halted all further development. The specifications that General Aleksandr Kerensky himself reviewed reportedly influenced his later commissioning of the Devastator to address perceived shortcomings in the Titan concept.

The Titan's legacy far outlived its brief prototype phase. Recovered by Federated Suns forces in 3023, the original specifications inspired both the radically redesigned Grand Titan produced by Earthwerks and the more faithful Titan II built by Kressly WarWorks for the Word of Blake. Centuries after its initial development, the Titan itself was finally brought into limited production during the Dark Age era.
BMTitan_TI1A.capabilities:
Weighing in at a full hundred tons, the Titan was designed around a Vlar 300 standard fusion engine that limits its top speed to fifty-four kilometers per hour. While slow even by assault 'Mech standards, the use of a standard engine provides exceptional survivability, as the 'Mech can continue operating even after catastrophic torso damage. Nineteen tons of standard armor give the Titan formidable protection across its frame.

The original armament centers on twin PPCs providing long-range striking power, supplemented by six medium lasers and a battery of short-range missiles (four SRM-4 launchers and an SRM-6) for devastating close-range salvos. This weapon mix reflects a brawler philosophy that demands the pilot close to effective range to bring the full arsenal to bear. The twenty-two single heat sinks proved insufficient for sustained fire with all weapons, forcing MechWarriors to carefully manage their engagement profile. Despite these heat management challenges, the Titan's combination of rugged construction and heavy firepower represented a sound assault platform that simply arrived at the wrong moment in history.
BMTitan_TI1A.history:
The Titan's origins trace to the final years of the Star League, when Blankenburg Technologies on Terra developed the prototype to specifications reviewed by General Aleksandr Kerensky himself. The design was intended to fill an assault 'Mech role emphasizing close-range dominance, but the onset of the Amaris Civil War in 2766 disrupted all further development. The prototype facilities were either destroyed or abandoned during the conflict, and the Titan was consigned to history as another promising design lost to the chaos of the era.

The design resurfaced when Armed Forces of the Federated Suns forces recovered the original specifications in 3023. The New Avalon Institute of Science reportedly conducted limited experiments with the design, producing a small number of prototypes, though full-scale production was never attempted. The recovered data proved more valuable as inspiration than as a production blueprint, Vining Engineering and Salvage Team used it as the foundation for the Grand Titan, while the Word of Blake later directed Kressly WarWorks to produce the more faithful Titan II.

The Titan itself finally entered limited production during the Dark Age era, when Kressly WarWorks applied the original NAIS-derived specifications to their production line on Epsilon Eridani, manufacturing updated variants for the Republic Armed Forces. These modernized versions incorporated double heat sinks and CASE protection while retaining the core design philosophy that had made the original prototype appealing to Kerensky's engineers over two centuries earlier.
BMTitan_TI1A.deployment: The original TI-1A represents the Star League-era prototype as designed in 2765. Armed with two PPCs, six medium lasers, four SRM-4 launchers, and a single SRM-6, the design emphasizes overwhelming firepower at the expense of heat management. Its twenty-two single heat sinks cannot adequately cool a full alpha strike, requiring disciplined fire selection from the pilot. Though never reaching mass production, this variant's specifications were preserved and would serve as the foundation for multiple successor designs centuries later.

BMTomahawkII_A.overview: The Tomahawk II is a 100-ton assault OmniMech produced by Clan Wolf beginning in 3088. Developed as the fully realized production version of the earlier prototype Tomahawk, the Tomahawk II incorporates significant structural improvements that maximize available tonnage for weapons and armor. Initially manufactured at the W-7 Facilities on Weingarten and later at Earthwerks-FWL on Keystone following the Wolf Empire's relocation, the design benefits from mature manufacturing processes refined over decades. The Tomahawk II represents one of the most formidable assault platforms fielded by any faction during the thirty-second century. Few assault 'Mechs in either the Inner Sphere or Clan inventories can match its combination of firepower, protection, and operational flexibility, establishing the design as a prestige unit within Clan Wolf's touman.
BMTomahawkII_A.capabilities:
The Tomahawk II achieves its devastating combat capability through a carefully optimized chassis design. The DSAM Endo 10-Composite internal structure saves critical tonnage compared to the prototype's standard skeleton, freeing weight for the design's impressive 56 tons of available pod space. A Starfire 300 XL engine propels the hundred-ton assault 'Mech to a maximum speed of 54 kilometers per hour, while nineteen tons of Advanced/3 armor provides near-maximum protection for an assault-class platform. The chassis is supported by Khan Series communications and Build 4 MadCat targeting systems, ensuring reliable command integration and weapons accuracy.

The Primary configuration demonstrates the Tomahawk II's offensive philosophy with a pair of Hyper-Assault Gauss 30 rifles, among the most powerful kinetic weapons available in the Clan arsenal. Three extended-range large lasers and two medium pulse lasers supplement the main battery, creating overlapping fields of fire from extreme to close range. CASE II protects the ammunition stores against catastrophic detonation. The design's principal weakness is its lack of mobility, without jump jets in most configurations and limited ground speed, the Tomahawk II depends on friendly forces to prevent flanking maneuvers and must be deployed with careful attention to terrain and tactical positioning. The design also carries a known fault in its ejection system that presents a concern for pilots under combat conditions.
BMTomahawkII_A.history:
Full production of the Tomahawk II commenced in 3088 at the W-7 Facilities on Weingarten, where Clan Wolf established dedicated manufacturing lines following the Jihad. The superior facilities available at the W-7 complex, already responsible for other key Clan Wolf designs, enabled the integration of the endo-composite structure and advanced electronics that had been absent from the prototype Tomahawk. A significant number of Tomahawk IIs entered service before Clan Wolf's migration from its occupation zone in the late 3130s.

When Clan Wolf relocated to former Free Worlds League space to establish the Wolf Empire, the Weingarten production line was necessarily abandoned. Unlike some other designs that required extensive retooling, the Tomahawk II was able to resume production relatively quickly at the Earthwerks-FWL facilities on Keystone, a sign of both the design's manufacturing maturity and the capabilities of the Earthwerks complex. Clan Hell's Horses also gained access to the Tomahawk II through decades of Trials with Clan Wolf, fielding the design alongside their own assault assets.

The Tomahawk II's most dramatic moment came during the invasion of Tharkad in 3143. Galaxy Commander Alaric Ward of Beta Galaxy deployed a Binary of elite Tomahawk II pilots against the Second Royal Guards defending the Nagelring military academy. On 13 July, the Binary shattered two companies of heavy and assault Lyran machines in two hours of intense combat, suffering the loss of only a single Tomahawk II. The engagement effectively broke Lyran resistance at the Nagelring and demonstrated the Tomahawk II's ability to dominate the battlefield against even the most determined opposition.

The invasion of Tharkad cemented the Tomahawk II's reputation as one of the most feared assault platforms in the Inner Sphere. With production secured on Keystone under Wolf Empire control, the design continues to serve as the premier assault OmniMech in the Clan Wolf touman, a symbol of the technological superiority that Clan Wolf has long cultivated.
BMTomahawkII_A.deployment: Alternate Configuration A focuses on precision anti-materiel and anti-aircraft capability through paired LB 10-X autocannons and four AP Gauss rifles mounted in the arms. The cluster munitions capability of the LB-X weapons makes this configuration particularly effective against conventional aircraft and light vehicles, while AP Gauss rifles provide pinpoint anti-infantry and anti-battle armor fire. Paired large and medium pulse lasers in the side torsos deliver accurate energy fire, complemented by a head-mounted ER large laser. CASE II protects the autocannon ammunition, and seven additional double heat sinks manage thermal loads.

Five additional double heat sinks manage the weapons' considerable thermal output. This configuration was the primary armament used during the assault on the Nagelring during the 3143 invasion of Tharkad.

BMTomahawk_A.overview: The Tomahawk is a 100-ton assault-class OmniMech designed by Clan Wolf in 3065. Conceived as a next-generation heavy assault platform to complement the Clan's existing stable of frontline OmniMechs, the Tomahawk represented an ambitious attempt to create the most devastating battlefield unit available to any military force. Several prototypes were constructed and tested by Omega Galaxy, demonstrating impressive firepower potential despite persistent system errors and integration issues that plagued early production models. The design was never approved for serial production, with the onset of the Jihad and the subsequent loss of Clan Wolf's Homeworld manufacturing infrastructure effectively ending the prototype program. The Tomahawk nonetheless served as the direct predecessor to the mass-produced Tomahawk II, which incorporated significant structural improvements to resolve the original design's shortcomings.
BMTomahawk_A.capabilities:
The Tomahawk was designed to deliver overwhelming firepower from a heavily armored assault chassis. Built around a standard internal structure and powered by a 300-rated extra-light fusion engine, the design achieves a maximum speed of 54 kilometers per hour, adequate for an assault platform intended to anchor battle lines rather than pursue lighter opponents. The chassis provides 56 tons of available pod space, offering tremendous flexibility in weapons configuration across its various loadouts.

The Primary configuration exemplifies the design's intent, mounting paired Gauss rifles and extended-range large lasers in the arms for devastating long-range engagements, supplemented by medium pulse lasers and Streak SRM-4 launchers for close defense. An anti-missile system and ECM suite provide additional protection and electronic warfare capability. The Tomahawk's lack of endo-composite structure, later addressed in its successor, means the design carries slightly less armor protection than might otherwise be possible, though this compromise was acceptable given the prototype's role as a proof-of-concept platform. The absence of jump jets limits tactical mobility, requiring careful positioning to maximize the design's formidable direct-fire capability.
BMTomahawk_A.history:
The Tomahawk's origins trace to Clan Wolf's drive for battlefield supremacy in the mid-thirty-first century. By 3065, Clan Wolf had established a prototype program at the W-7 Facilities on Tranquil in the Clan Homeworlds, producing a small number of test units for evaluation by Omega Galaxy. Early trials revealed significant promise alongside persistent technical difficulties, system errors and integration gremlins prevented the design from being cleared for frontline deployment despite its impressive combat performance during field testing.

One of the first prototypes saw combat in a Circle of Equals on Tamar in September 3065, successfully defeating a Summoner despite the acknowledged system issues. The same prototype subsequently deployed with Omega Galaxy to Novo Cressidas in the Star's End system in April 3064, demonstrating the design's combat potential in an operational environment. These deployments provided valuable data that would later inform the development of the improved Tomahawk II.

The onset of the Jihad proved catastrophic for the Tomahawk program. Clan Wolf's attention and resources were diverted to more pressing matters, and the eventual loss of Homeworld manufacturing infrastructure effectively terminated any possibility of serial production. The design remained in prototype status, its small number of operational units gradually lost to combat attrition. Following the Jihad, Clan Wolf's engineers revisited the Tomahawk concept, incorporating endo-composite structure and other improvements that culminated in the Tomahawk II, a design that would finally realize the original Tomahawk's potential as a dominant assault platform.
BMTomahawk_A.deployment: Alternate Configuration A transforms the Tomahawk into a devastating close-range combatant. Twin Ultra Class 20 autocannons mounted in the arms deliver punishing bursts of fire capable of crippling most opponents in a single engagement, with the arm-mounted design allowing rear-arc fire when flipped. Three medium pulse lasers, two Streak SRM-6 launchers, and an extended-range large laser provide supporting firepower across multiple range brackets. The configuration's reliance on ammunition-dependent weapons creates a logistics dependency that limits extended operations.

BMToro_TRA6.overview:
The Toro holds the distinction of being the Taurian Concordat's first indigenous BattleMech. Developed in 2481 by the government-run Taurus WarWorks, the design was based on captured Capellan Firebees and won a competition among three Taurian defense contractors to build the Concordat's first home-sourced 'Mech. Intended as a light fire-support platform, the Toro was designed to engage conventional targets and work alongside TDF infantry forces to isolate and destroy enemy BattleMechs. Its comparatively low cost allowed entire battalions to be equipped quickly, giving the Taurian Defense Force a significant boost in capability during the Age of War.

Few BattleMech designs carry as much symbolic weight as the Toro. Its legacy as the Concordat's first 'Mech and its association with the Reunification War have made it an enduring icon of Taurian independence and self-reliance, inspiring fierce loyalty among Taurian citizens across centuries.
BMToro_TRA6.capabilities:
The TR-A-6 Toro is built around a long-range engagement doctrine favored by the Taurian Defense Force. Its primary weapon, a Taurus WarWorks particle projector cannon, delivers punishing fire at extended ranges, while twin Delta Dart LRM-5 launchers provide sustained indirect fire support. Two tons of missile ammunition allow flexibility in payload selection and keep the 'Mech operational through protracted engagements, a quantity some League and House observers considered excessive. The Toro lacks meaningful close-range firepower, a deliberate design choice reflecting Taurian tactical philosophy. Formations of Toros compensate for this vulnerability by deploying in staggered lines, ensuring at least a portion of the formation can bring weapons to bear at optimal range.

Powered by a Magna 175 fusion engine, the Toro reaches a top speed of 86 kilometers per hour, above average for medium 'Mechs of its era and sufficient to maintain standoff distance against heavier opponents. Six and a half tons of Ecto-Mineral Armorplate 2 provide respectable protection for a light design. The infamously cramped cockpit is a legacy of the Toro's primitive origins, a compromise Taurus WarWorks never fully resolved despite multiple redesigns over the course of the design's long production history.
BMToro_TRA6.history:
The origins of the Toro trace back to a period of relative peace in the Taurian Concordat beginning around 2425. Under the leadership of Protector Amanda Calderon and her successors, the Concordat pursued a strategy of non-interference backed by superior firepower. When the Federated Suns debuted its BattleAxe in 2459, Taurian agents spent two decades acquiring key BattleMech technologies, culminating in the capture of several Capellan Firebees in 2475. Three Taurian defense contractors competed for the procurement contract, with Taurus WarWorks winning thanks to its close ties to Concordat intelligence services and government backing. The first prototype walked out of Taurus WarWorks' labs in August 2481, and first-generation models reached the TDF less than two years later.

The early TR-A-1 model operated with distinction and was consistently upgraded as newer technologies became available. By the time the TR-A-6 entered production, the Toro had become the backbone of the TDF's BattleMech forces. The Taurian Defense Force fielded the Toro in large numbers and in almost every independent unit, going so far as deploying entire battalions of the design. Though the Concordat did not export the BattleMech, it found its way into Capellan and Federated Suns ranks through battlefield salvage.

The Reunification War proved devastating for the Toro and its legacy. The Star League initially salvaged captured Toros, but after the design became reviled by SLDF troops, they began publicly destroying any salvaged units to boost morale. Some Striker regiments organized destruction derbies where Toros were propped up to allow MechWarriors to knock them down with charge attacks or fire from above. As the war escalated, some units began executing prisoners of war in these spectacles. Few Toros survived the Reunification War, and only one endured as a historical artifact through the Star League era. The TR-A-6 was the last model produced before the Star League closed and dismantled all manufacturing sites in 2598, hoping the destruction of the Toro would be instrumental in reducing Taurian nationalism.

When the Concordat was free of the Star League once again, there was heated debate about whether to rebuild a Toro factory. In a pragmatic decision, it was concluded that continuing to produce 'Mechs they already had access to was more sensible than wasting resources resurrecting a design that had not walked in almost two centuries. The Toro remained dormant through the Succession Wars, the Clan Invasion, and the Civil War, surviving only as a cultural icon and symbol of Taurian defiance.

The Jihad changed everything. The dissemination of the Hegemony Memory Core made retrotech manufacturing feasible again, and the desperate need for any operational BattleMechs spurred multiple factions to revive the primitive TR-A-1 design. Patriotic citizens of the Concordat funded Liberty Arms on Jamestown, while Taurus Territorial Industries converted a WorkMech line on Illiushin. Even the Federated Suns saw retrotech Toro production, with Iroquois Machinery Limited on Shawnee and the newly founded Coalition Armory on Filtvelt building primitive models for March and planetary militias. The Magistracy of Canopus joined through Bermuda Combat Systems on Booker, and the Calderon Protectorate's Protectorate Arms Conglomerate on Diik began its own production run.

In the decades following the Jihad, the Toro evolved beyond its retrotech revival. The Calderon Protectorate, eager to prove its industrial capabilities, developed the TR-B-9 variant with modern technologies sourced from Federated Suns consultants and allied Periphery realms. This new Toro Bravo became a point of pride for the Protectorate and a sore point for the Concordat, which viewed it as a provocation. Relations between the two Taurian successor states reached a low point around 3111, with border skirmishes highlighting the Toro Bravo's surprising effectiveness. By 3144, diplomatic negotiations between the Concordat and Protectorate led to the jointly developed TR-B-12, touted as a symbol of reunification. Coalition Armory on Filtvelt also upgraded its production line to modern technology, producing the TR-A-6 for the Filtvelt Coalition, while Colonial Tractors on Fronc began manufacturing for the Fronc Reaches.
BMToro_TRA6.deployment: This variant represents the final evolution of the original Toro line, replacing the primitive systems of earlier models with a modern chassis frame, standard fusion engine, and upgraded armament. The large laser and SRM launchers gave way to a particle projector cannon and paired LRM-5 racks, shifting the design firmly into a long-range fire support role. Taurus WarWorks produced this variant until the Star League dismantled the factory in 2598. The variant was reintroduced during the Dark Age by Coalition Armory on Filtvelt after upgrading their retrotech production line to modern technology, and by Protectorate Arms Conglomerate on Diik, providing the Filtvelt Coalition and Calderon Protectorate with a proven, affordable light 'Mech design.
BMToro_TRA6.manufacturer: Coalition Armory, Inc.|Protectorate Arms Conglomerate (Formerly Protectorate Defense Conglomerate)|Taurus WarWorks

BMToyama_TYM1A.overview: The Toyama is a seventy-five-ton heavy BattleMech produced for the Word of Blake at the Gibson Federated BattleMechs facilities beginning in 3057. Named for Conrad Toyama, the founder of the Blakist religion and successor to Jerome Blake as Primus of ComStar, the design carried strong ideological significance for its operators. Intended as a multi-purpose 'Mech capable of operating independently of supply lines for extended periods, the Toyama became one of the most recognizable heavy designs fielded by the Blakist Militia. A second production line at the Lantren Corporation on Bryant supplemented Gibson's output during the Jihad. Its strong association with the Word of Blake has left the design with a lasting stigma in the post-Jihad era, and no faction has attempted to resume production.
BMToyama_TYM1A.capabilities:
Designed for versatility and endurance, the Toyama carries an impressive mix of weapons systems covering all engagement ranges. A pair of Diverse Optics Sunbeam extended-range large lasers mounted in the right arm provide devastating long-range firepower, while an Imperator Code Red LB 10-X autocannon in the left arm offers flexibility through both standard and cluster munitions. A Doombud LRM-20 launcher in the torso adds indirect fire capability, with two full tons of ammunition allowing the pilot to carry a mix of warhead types tailored to the mission at hand. Three Magna Mark II medium lasers clustered in the torso provide additional close-range firepower, though their effective range is limited.

The Toyama is built on a lightweight Endo Steel chassis powered by a Vlar 300 XL engine, giving it a top speed of sixty-five kilometers per hour, adequate for keeping pace with most heavy 'Mech formations. Twelve tons of Durallex Heavy armor provide substantial protection for its weight class. A Guardian ECM suite mounted in the right torso disrupts enemy electronic warfare systems, though the original design's planned anti-missile system was ultimately sacrificed to accommodate the larger LRM launcher.
BMToyama_TYM1A.history:
The Toyama was the product of an unusual collaboration. Unlike many Word of Blake designs produced in-house, the 'Mech was the work of a military technology consultant at the Free Worlds League's Heliopolis design labs. As part of an arrangement with Captain-General Thomas Marik, the design was passed to the Word of Blake, who named it for Conrad Toyama, the successor to Jerome Blake as Primus of ComStar and the acknowledged founder of the Blakist religion. Gibson Federated BattleMechs put the design into production in early 3057.

The Toyama first saw combat with the Word of Blake Militia during the late 3050s. Plans to deploy several Toyamas to the Atrean Dragoons were postponed when the Word of Blake launched Operation Odysseus in 3058, during which Blakist Militia troops masquerading as the mercenary 21st Centauri Lancers infiltrated and sabotaged ComStar's defenses on Terra. At least four Toyamas were used during that operation, marking the design's baptism of fire.

Following the seizure of Terra, the Toyama became increasingly common among Blakist forces. Gibson Federated BattleMechs, a division of Free Worlds Defense Industries, ramped up production at their facilities on Gibson throughout the Civil War era. By the time of the Jihad, the Word of Blake had established a second production line at the Lantren Corporation facility on Bryant, which intelligence analysts had long suspected based on the volume of new Toyamas appearing in combat zones far exceeding projected output from Gibson alone.

During the Jihad, both factories operated at full capacity producing the original TYM-1A along with newly developed variants incorporating advanced technologies. The Gibson facility produced all three known variants, while the Bryant line focused on the TYM-1A and the advanced TYM-1C. Word of Blake engineers on Gibson continued refining the design throughout the conflict, producing machines that combined increased durability with devastating firepower.

The destruction wrought during the Jihad brought Toyama production to a permanent halt. Both the Gibson and Bryant facilities ceased operations during or shortly after the conflict, and no faction has resumed manufacturing of the design. Surviving Toyamas remain in service with various successor states and mercenary commands that captured them during the Jihad, but the 'Mech's strong association with the Word of Blake has discouraged any attempts to revive production.
BMToyama_TYM1A.deployment: The original TYM-1A was deployed exclusively with the Word of Blake Militia from its introduction in 3057. Its combination of energy weapons, autocannon, missiles, and electronic warfare equipment made it well suited to the independent operations that Word of Blake units frequently conducted. The base configuration saw extensive service during Operation Odysseus and throughout the Jihad, where it became one of the most common heavy 'Mechs in Blakist formations.
BMToyama_TYM1A.manufacturer: Gibson Federated BattleMechs (A Division of Free Worlds Defense Industries)|Lantren Corporation

BMToyama_TYM1B.deployment: Introduced in 3070, this variant serves as a significant redesign driven by combat experience during the Jihad. The fragile extralight engine is replaced with a more durable Vlar light engine, dramatically improving survivability. The entire weapons complement is overhauled, replacing the autocannon and large lasers with Blankenburg particle projection cannons, two light and one heavy, weapons originally developed by the Draconis Combine but acquired through Blakist channels. The LRM launcher is downsized to a fifteen-tube rack, while the medium lasers give way to extended-range models. A C3i computer replaces the Guardian ECM suite, enabling the Toyama to participate in enhanced tactical networks. A compact gyro frees additional tonnage used to increase armor protection.
BMToyama_TYM1B.manufacturer: Gibson Federated BattleMechs (A Division of Free Worlds Defense Industries)

A pair of Diverse Optics Sunbeam extended-range large lasers mounted in the right arm provide devastating long-range firepower, while an Imperator Code Red LB 10-X autocannon in the left arm offers flexibility through both standard and cluster munitions. A Doombud LRM-20 launcher in the torso adds indirect fire capability, with two full tons of ammunition allowing the pilot to carry a mix of warhead types tailored to the mission at hand. Three Magna Mark II medium lasers clustered in the torso provide additional close-range firepower, though their effective range is limited.

The Toyama is built on a lightweight Endo Steel chassis powered by a Vlar 300 XL engine, giving it a top speed of sixty-five kilometers per hour, adequate for keeping pace with most heavy 'Mech formations. Twelve tons of Durallex Heavy armor provide substantial protection for its weight class. A Guardian ECM suite mounted in the right torso disrupts enemy electronic warfare systems, though the original design's planned anti-missile system was ultimately sacrificed to accommodate the larger LRM launcher.
BMToyama_TYM1C.history:
The Toyama was the product of an unusual collaboration. Unlike many Word of Blake designs produced in-house, the 'Mech was the work of a military technology consultant at the Free Worlds League's Heliopolis design labs. As part of an arrangement with Captain-General Thomas Marik, the design was passed to the Word of Blake, who named it for Conrad Toyama, the successor to Jerome Blake as Primus of ComStar and the acknowledged founder of the Blakist religion. Gibson Federated BattleMechs put the design into production in early 3057.

The Toyama first saw combat with the Word of Blake Militia during the late 3050s. Plans to deploy several Toyamas to the Atrean Dragoons were postponed when the Word of Blake launched Operation Odysseus in 3058, during which Blakist Militia troops masquerading as the mercenary 21st Centauri Lancers infiltrated and sabotaged ComStar's defenses on Terra. At least four Toyamas were used during that operation, marking the design's baptism of fire.

Following the seizure of Terra, the Toyama became increasingly common among Blakist forces. Gibson Federated BattleMechs, a division of Free Worlds Defense Industries, ramped up production at their facilities on Gibson throughout the Civil War era. By the time of the Jihad, the Word of Blake had established a second production line at the Lantren Corporation facility on Bryant, which intelligence analysts had long suspected based on the volume of new Toyamas appearing in combat zones far exceeding projected output from Gibson alone.

During the Jihad, both factories operated at full capacity producing the original TYM-1A along with newly developed variants incorporating advanced technologies. The Gibson facility produced all three known variants, while the Bryant line focused on the TYM-1A and the advanced TYM-1C. Word of Blake engineers on Gibson continued refining the design throughout the conflict, producing machines that combined increased durability with devastating firepower.

The destruction wrought during the Jihad brought Toyama production to a permanent halt. Both the Gibson and Bryant facilities ceased operations during or shortly after the conflict, and no faction has resumed manufacturing of the design. Surviving Toyamas remain in service with various successor states and mercenary commands that captured them during the Jihad, but the 'Mech's strong association with the Word of Blake has discouraged any attempts to revive production.
BMToyama_TYM1C.deployment: Emerging in 3072, this variant reconfigures the Toyama as a dedicated fire support platform. The most dramatic change is the replacement of the LB 10-X autocannon with a devastating M-2 Gauss rifle, giving the 'Mech tremendous long-range striking power. The large lasers are removed in favor of two Blankenburg medium variable-speed pulse lasers, which offer flexible accuracy at shorter ranges. The Doombud LRM-20 is retained but enhanced with an Artemis IV fire control system for improved missile accuracy, with ammunition bins now protected by CASE equipment. An XL gyro and upgraded Durallex Guardian heavy ferro-fibrous armor round out the extensive modifications, while a C3i computer links this variant into Blakist tactical networks.
BMToyama_TYM1C.manufacturer: Gibson Federated BattleMechs (A Division of Free Worlds Defense Industries)|Lantren Corporation

BMTrebaruna_TRXB.overview:
The Trebaruna is a ninety-five ton quad assault BattleMech whose origins trace back to the Word of Blake Protectorate. Plans for the design were discovered in Blakist databases seized during the Coalition assault on Terra, with partially decrypted information suggesting the 'Mech was developed from stolen Free Rasalhague Republic drafts. The Blakists had planned to begin production in 3078, but scrapped the project as Coalition forces closed the noose around Terra. Though much of the captured data was available to all Coalition partners, only three nations elected to put the Trebaruna into production. The Republic of the Sphere fielded the design first in 3081, followed closely by the Marik-Stewart Commonwealth and the Capellan Confederation.

Named for an ancient goddess of battle, protection, and death, the Trebaruna serves as a resilient long-range fire support platform. Its unusual quad chassis configuration provides exceptional stability for its heavy armament, and the design has earned a reputation as a durable command vehicle capable of anchoring defensive positions.
BMTrebaruna_TRXB.capabilities:
The Trebaruna is an incredibly resilient design. Sixteen tons of Durallex Heavy armor protect the Pitban 285 standard fusion engine at its heart. Forgoing an extralight engine saves precious space in the cramped confines of the quadruped chassis and provides excellent survivability in the event of side torso destruction. Where many modern assault machines are rendered functional kills after losing a side torso, the Trebaruna is barely slowed.

Firepower is modest for an assault-class machine but carefully selected for sustained engagement. The Imperator Dragon's Fire Gauss rifle serves as the primary weapon, a reliable and low-maintenance system with a solid record on the Atlas and Orion. Two tons of ammunition stored in a rapid-feed magazine below the breach keep the weapon firing, while CASE protection mitigates the risk of a catastrophic ammunition explosion. Backing up the main gun is a trio of Moscovia light particle projection cannons, providing consistent energy-based firepower at range.

An Orion Suretrak XVII targeting computer significantly enhances the value of these armaments. Four Chilton 950 improved jump jets give the Trebaruna a 120-meter jump range, a remarkable capability for a ninety-five ton machine. The Hartford JEQ-5 communications system includes all standard features expected in a battalion or regimental command platform.
BMTrebaruna_TRXB.history:
The Trebaruna's history begins not with its production, but with its theft. The original design specifications were apparently pilfered from Free Rasalhague Republic military archives, though this claim remains uncorroborated. What is known is that Word of Blake engineers on Terra refined the concept into a production-ready assault quad, intending it as a command platform for Protectorate Militia and Word of Blake Militia formations. When the allied Coalition closed in on Terra in 3078, the Blakists abandoned the Trebaruna project to focus resources on strategic weaponry for their final defense.

Following the liberation of Terra, Coalition intelligence teams discovered the complete production plans in seized Blakist databases. The data was shared among the allied nations, though the Federated Suns, Draconis Combine, and Lyran Commonwealth all chose not to develop the design. The Republic of the Sphere, building its Republic Armed Forces from scratch, was eager for new designs untainted by Succession Wars-era politics and brought the Trebaruna into production at Kressly WarWorks on Epsilon Eridani in 3081. The Marik-Stewart Commonwealth followed suit at Earthwerks-FWL on Keystone, and the Capellan Confederation established production at Ceres Metals Industries on St. Ives.

The Trebaruna has served in all three nations' frontline formations since its introduction. In the Republic Armed Forces, it deployed with the Hastati Sentinels and Principes Guards, where its quad chassis and heavy armor made it a favored command vehicle. The Marik-Stewart Commonwealth produced the TR-XJ variant at Keystone and sold examples to other former Free Worlds League states where relations permitted. House Liao fielded the largest number of TR-XLs in the St. Ives Armored Cavalry, and the design has appeared in the forces of multiple Warrior Houses.

As the Dark Age deepened, the Trebaruna remained in continuous production across all three factory sites. Changes in political ownership affected the Keystone facility, which passed from Marik-Stewart Commonwealth control to Clan Wolf during the ilClan era. The design's proven reliability and straightforward logistics ensured demand remained steady through the turbulent decades following the collapse of the HPG network and the rise of Fortress Republic.
BMTrebaruna_TRXB.deployment: The base TR-XB represents the original Blakist design as refined by Coalition engineers, combining a primary ballistic weapon with energy-based secondary armament and an advanced targeting computer for exceptional long-range accuracy. Produced at all three factory sites, this variant's standard fusion engine and generous armor protection give the design outstanding survivability, while improved jump jets provide tactical flexibility uncommon in machines of this weight class. The configuration has proven popular as a command vehicle, with its combination of resilience and precision fire making it well suited to anchoring defensive formations.

BMTrebaruna_TRXH.deployment: Introduced in 3115, this variant is a specialized siege variant built around more than twenty-five tons of hardened armor, enabling it to shrug off withering volumes of enemy fire that would cripple lighter designs. The internal structure uses a composite skeleton to save weight, though this comes at the cost of fragile internal components that are more susceptible to critical damage. The primary armament is an improved heavy Gauss rifle, delivering devastating kinetic impacts at extreme range. A turret-mounted extended-range particle projection cannon provides secondary firepower with a wide field of fire, compensating for the quad chassis's limited torso rotation. Produced at all three factory sites, this variant serves in formations requiring a heavy assault platform capable of absorbing sustained punishment while advancing on fortified positions.

This variant replaces the trio of Moscovia light particle cannons with a brace of snub-nose particle projection cannons, trading long-range output for devastating close-range firepower. A double-strength heat sink is added to manage the increased thermal load. The Orion Suretrak targeting computer is removed in favor of a Spillman Multitrack 8 tracking system, a solid piece of technology that lacks the Suretrak's enhanced precision but frees weight for two additional tons of armor and an upgrade to light ferro-fibrous protection.

A light fusion engine frees the necessary weight for seventeen and a half tons of standard armor, making this variant one of the most heavily protected variants in the family.

BMTrebuchet_TBT3C.overview:
The Trebuchet was one of a handful of BattleMech designs produced during the final years of the Star League, first walking off Corean Enterprises' assembly lines in 2780 for the SLDF. Originally designated the TBT-3C and equipped with advanced technology including an extralight engine, Artemis IV fire control, and double heat sinks, the design served as a medium fire support platform intended to operate as part of a well-balanced lance rather than independently. The devastation of the First Succession War forced Corean to redesign the 'Mech without lostech components, producing the simplified TBT-5N in 2799 that would become the standard production model.

Renowned for its effective blend of long-range missile fire and short-range laser support, the Trebuchet became an almost exclusive staple of the Free Worlds League during the Succession Wars, its surviving manufacturing sites on Stewart and Kalidasa falling within League territory. The design's reputation for easy maintenance and reliable performance ensured its continued production across multiple centuries and manufacturers.
BMTrebuchet_TBT3C.capabilities:
Designed to serve as part of a well-balanced lance, the Trebuchet relies on an effective combination of good mobility and a weapons load that blends long-range missile support with close-in laser firepower. The primary armament consists of twin Zeus LRM-15 launchers, one mounted in the right torso and one in the left arm, capable of softening enemy formations at ranges beyond effective return fire. Three Magna Mk II medium lasers (two in the right arm and one in the left) provide credible close-range defense and discourage lighter 'Mechs from attempting interception.

The Magna 250 fusion engine drives the fifty-ton chassis to a respectable 86 kilometers per hour, adequate for keeping pace with most fire support formations. Seven and a half tons of Starshield armor provides reasonable protection for the weight class, though dedicated brawlers will outmatch the Trebuchet in sustained close combat. Ten heat sinks manage thermal output adequately when firing lasers at cruising speed, and the chassis has earned a reputation for easy maintenance and quick reloading of its torso-mounted weaponry.

The design's greatest weakness is endurance. Each LRM launcher carries only a single ton of ammunition, providing barely a minute of continuous fire before the Trebuchet must rely solely on its lasers, where it finds itself outgunned compared to dedicated close-combat 'Mechs of similar tonnage. This limited ammunition supply reflects the design philosophy of operating near friendly supply lines rather than on extended independent patrols.
BMTrebuchet_TBT3C.history:
The Trebuchet's origins trace to the twilight of the Star League, entering production in 2780 at Corean Enterprises' facilities during the brief period between Terra's liberation from Stefan Amaris and Aleksandr Kerensky's Exodus. The original TBT-3C was a sophisticated design featuring an extralight engine, Artemis IV-equipped LRM launchers, and double heat sinks, but the attrition of the First Succession War quickly rendered these advanced components irreplaceable. By 2799, Corean had redesigned the chassis as the simplified TBT-5N, sacrificing capability for manufacturability.

The Free Worlds League became the Trebuchet's primary operator during the Succession Wars, a consequence of geography rather than exclusive licensing, Corean's surviving MacAdams-Suharno plant on Stewart and Kali Yama's facilities on Kalidasa both fell within League borders. ComStar's records incorrectly suggested Corean ceased Trebuchet production in 2845, but in truth the MacAdams-Suharno facility maintained an average output of eight units annually throughout the Third Succession War. The confusion likely arose from the destruction of Corean's corporate headquarters and primary factory on Ramen II by Capellan forces that same year, after which the company relocated its headquarters to New Avalon.

The FWLM developed distinctive tactical doctrines around the Trebuchet, frequently pairing it with the heavier Archer for fire support operations. The Regulan Hussars perfected a siege lance configuration comprising an Archer, two Trebuchets, and a Centurion that proved devastatingly effective. Despite its Free Worlds origins, the design found its way into service with every Great House during the Succession Wars, serving with distinction in nearly every major operation and spawning variants to meet diverse tactical needs.

The technological renaissance of the 3030s proved transformative for the Trebuchet program. Kali Yama Weapons Industries and Irian BattleMechs Unlimited both began production, and upgraded variants incorporating recovered Star League technology debuted in the years preceding the Clan Invasion. The TBT-7M reintroduced endo-steel construction, an XL engine, and jump capability that the simplified 5N series had abandoned decades earlier. No fewer than three manufacturers produced the upgraded model, reflecting both the design's proven value and the expanding industrial base of the Inner Sphere.

The Trebuchet continued evolving through subsequent conflicts. House Kurita's adoption of MRM technology spawned field-refitted variants, while Kali Yama's TBT-8B of 3071 attempted to blend the best characteristics of every preceding model into a single chassis. The Word of Blake's use of advanced Trebuchet variants during the Jihad added a darker chapter to the design's distinguished service record. As late as the Dark Age era, Tvastar Enterprises on Regulus produced advanced models incorporating Clan-grade weaponry, demonstrating the enduring viability of a chassis concept first conceived in the dying days of the Star League.
BMTrebuchet_TBT3C.deployment: The original Trebuchet produced for the Star League Defense Force mounted a formidable array of advanced technology. A 300-rated extralight engine provided the same ground speed as later models while freeing tonnage for an endo-steel chassis, Artemis IV fire control on both LRM-15 launchers, CASE ammunition protection, four medium lasers, and double heat sinks. The 3C represented the design at its technological peak, but the rapid decline of the Succession Wars rendered its advanced components impossible to replace or manufacture. Corean Enterprises was forced to abandon the model before the end of the First Succession War, redesigning the chassis around more readily available components.

The primary armament consists of twin Zeus LRM-15 launchers, one mounted in the right torso and one in the left arm, capable of softening enemy formations at ranges beyond effective return fire. Three Magna Mk II medium lasers (two in the right arm and one in the left) provide credible close-range defense and discourage lighter 'Mechs from attempting interception.

The Magna 250 fusion engine drives the fifty-ton chassis to a respectable 86 kilometers per hour, adequate for keeping pace with most fire support formations. Ten heat sinks manage thermal output adequately when firing lasers at cruising speed, and the chassis has earned a reputation for easy maintenance and quick reloading of its torso-mounted weaponry.

The design's greatest weakness is endurance. Each LRM launcher carries only a single ton of ammunition, providing barely a minute of continuous fire before the Trebuchet must rely solely on its lasers, where it finds itself outgunned compared to dedicated close-combat 'Mechs of similar tonnage. This limited ammunition supply reflects the design philosophy of operating near friendly supply lines rather than on extended independent patrols.

Thirteen double heat sinks attempted to manage the considerable thermal load, though pilots must exercise careful heat discipline to avoid overwhelming the cooling system during sustained engagements.

BMTrebuchet_TBT9K.overview:
The Trebuchet was one of a handful of BattleMech designs produced during the final years of the Star League, first walking off Corean Enterprises' assembly lines in 2780 for the SLDF. Originally designated the TBT-3C and equipped with advanced technology including an extralight engine, Artemis IV fire control, and double heat sinks, the design served as a medium fire support platform intended to operate as part of a well-balanced lance rather than independently. The devastation of the First Succession War forced Corean to redesign the 'Mech without lostech components, producing the simplified TBT-5N in 2799 that would become the standard production model.

Renowned for its effective blend of long-range missile fire and short-range laser support, the Trebuchet became an almost exclusive staple of the Free Worlds League during the Succession Wars, its surviving manufacturing sites on Stewart and Kalidasa falling within League territory. The design's reputation for easy maintenance and reliable performance ensured its continued production across multiple centuries and manufacturers.
BMTrebuchet_TBT9K.capabilities:
Designed to serve as part of a well-balanced lance, the Trebuchet relies on an effective combination of good mobility and a weapons load that blends long-range missile support with close-in laser firepower. The primary armament consists of twin Zeus LRM-15 launchers, one mounted in the right torso and one in the left arm, capable of softening enemy formations at ranges beyond effective return fire. Three Magna Mk II medium lasers (two in the right arm and one in the left) provide credible close-range defense and discourage lighter 'Mechs from attempting interception.

The Magna 250 fusion engine drives the fifty-ton chassis to a respectable 86 kilometers per hour, adequate for keeping pace with most fire support formations. Seven and a half tons of Starshield armor provides reasonable protection for the weight class, though dedicated brawlers will outmatch the Trebuchet in sustained close combat. Ten heat sinks manage thermal output adequately when firing lasers at cruising speed, and the chassis has earned a reputation for easy maintenance and quick reloading of its torso-mounted weaponry.

The design's greatest weakness is endurance. Each LRM launcher carries only a single ton of ammunition, providing barely a minute of continuous fire before the Trebuchet must rely solely on its lasers, where it finds itself outgunned compared to dedicated close-combat 'Mechs of similar tonnage. This limited ammunition supply reflects the design philosophy of operating near friendly supply lines rather than on extended independent patrols.
BMTrebuchet_TBT9K.history:
The Trebuchet's origins trace to the twilight of the Star League, entering production in 2780 at Corean Enterprises' facilities during the brief period between Terra's liberation from Stefan Amaris and Aleksandr Kerensky's Exodus. The original TBT-3C was a sophisticated design featuring an extralight engine, Artemis IV-equipped LRM launchers, and double heat sinks, but the attrition of the First Succession War quickly rendered these advanced components irreplaceable. By 2799, Corean had redesigned the chassis as the simplified TBT-5N, sacrificing capability for manufacturability.

The Free Worlds League became the Trebuchet's primary operator during the Succession Wars, a consequence of geography rather than exclusive licensing, Corean's surviving MacAdams-Suharno plant on Stewart and Kali Yama's facilities on Kalidasa both fell within League borders. ComStar's records incorrectly suggested Corean ceased Trebuchet production in 2845, but in truth the MacAdams-Suharno facility maintained an average output of eight units annually throughout the Third Succession War. The confusion likely arose from the destruction of Corean's corporate headquarters and primary factory on Ramen II by Capellan forces that same year, after which the company relocated its headquarters to New Avalon.

The FWLM developed distinctive tactical doctrines around the Trebuchet, frequently pairing it with the heavier Archer for fire support operations. The Regulan Hussars perfected a siege lance configuration comprising an Archer, two Trebuchets, and a Centurion that proved devastatingly effective. Despite its Free Worlds origins, the design found its way into service with every Great House during the Succession Wars, serving with distinction in nearly every major operation and spawning variants to meet diverse tactical needs.

The technological renaissance of the 3030s proved transformative for the Trebuchet program. Kali Yama Weapons Industries and Irian BattleMechs Unlimited both began production, and upgraded variants incorporating recovered Star League technology debuted in the years preceding the Clan Invasion. The TBT-7M reintroduced endo-steel construction, an XL engine, and jump capability that the simplified 5N series had abandoned decades earlier. No fewer than three manufacturers produced the upgraded model, reflecting both the design's proven value and the expanding industrial base of the Inner Sphere.

The Trebuchet continued evolving through subsequent conflicts. House Kurita's adoption of MRM technology spawned field-refitted variants, while Kali Yama's TBT-8B of 3071 attempted to blend the best characteristics of every preceding model into a single chassis. The Word of Blake's use of advanced Trebuchet variants during the Jihad added a darker chapter to the design's distinguished service record. As late as the Dark Age era, Tvastar Enterprises on Regulus produced advanced models incorporating Clan-grade weaponry, demonstrating the enduring viability of a chassis concept first conceived in the dying days of the Star League.
BMTrebuchet_TBT9K.deployment: A field modification of the TBT-7M with a distinctly Kuritan character, the 9K reflects the Draconis Combine's embrace of MRM technology. The LRM launchers were replaced with twin MRM-20 launchers fed by three tons of shared ammunition, delivering devastating medium-range salvos that sacrifice the precision of guided missiles for sheer volume of fire. The right arm medium lasers gave way to twin medium pulse lasers for improved accuracy in close combat, while the original left arm medium laser was retained. A C3 slave unit in the left torso integrates the 9K into the Combine's networked combat doctrine, sharing targeting telemetry across the lance. Jump capability from the base 7M was preserved, maintaining the variant's tactical flexibility.

BMTrebuchet_TBT9R.deployment: Introduced during the Dark Age era, the 9R represents the most technologically advanced production Trebuchet to date.
